the rent and taxes were remitted for the five commanderies of Lǒngyòu that had suffered from banditry.
Loans of grain were provided to those who could not support themselves.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Jǐngdù, Prince of Chéngyáng, passed away.
An imperial edict stated:
“Since the beginning of Tàishǐ,
all important affairs have been compiled and recorded in the imperial archives,
and copies made.
Henceforth, whenever such affairs occur,
they should be continually compiled as a regular practice.”
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Jùn, Prince of Rǔyīn, was appointed General Who Guards the West and Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yōng and Liáng two prefectures.
In the ninth month,
Dàyuān presented blood-sweating horses,
and Yānqí came to offer tribute of local products.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
the Emperor visited the Bìyōng,
and performed the Ceremony of Village Archery and Feasting.
The Grand Master of Ceremonies, scholars, and students were granted silk, oxen, and wine, each according to their rank.
The imperial son Jiǎn was established as Prince of Rǔnán.
In the twelfth month,
Sūn Xiù, Supervisor of Xiàkǒu and Former General of Wú, led his troops to surrender.
He was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and granted the honors of opening an administration and holding the three ducal offices,
and enfeoffed as Duke of Kuàijī.
On the *wùchén* day,
the office of General Who Guards the Army was reinstated.
In the spring of the seventh year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the first month,
the crown prince was capped,
and princes and dukes and those below them were granted silk, each according to their rank.
Liú Měng, a Xiongnú chieftain, rebelled and crossed the frontier.
In the third month,
Sūn Hào led his troops towards Shòuyáng.
The Grand Marshal Wàng was dispatched to garrison north of the Huái River to resist him.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
〔一三〕Péi Xiù, Minister of Works and Duke of Jùlù, passed away.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Wáng Yè, Central Protector of the Army, was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance and Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
Guī, Prince of Gāoyáng, was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance and Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
Hé Chóng, a subordinate general of Sūn Xiù, led five thousand troops to surrender.
In summer, fourth month,
Dǒng Yuán, Administrator of Jiǔzhēn, was attacked by Yú Fàn, a general of Wú.
His army was defeated,
and he died.
Hu barbarians from Běidì attacked Jīnchéng.
Qiān Hóng, Inspector of Liángzhōu, went to suppress them.
The various barbarians rebelled from within
and besieged Hóng at Qīngshān.
Hóng's army was defeated,
and he died.
In the fifth month,
the imperial son Xiàn was established as Prince of Chéngyáng.
There was a famine in Yōng, Liáng, and Qín three prefectures.
An amnesty was granted to those in its territory sentenced to death and below.
In the intercalary month,
a great ritual for rain was performed,
and the imperial kitchen reduced its dishes.
An imperial edict ordered that the three commanderies of Jiāozhǐ and the commanderies of Nánzhōng
should not be levied with this year's household taxes.
In the sixth month,
an imperial edict ordered all high officials and below to recommend one general each.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Wàng, Grand Marshal and Prince of Yìyáng, passed away.
There was heavy and continuous rain.
The Yī, Luò, and Hé rivers overflowed,
washing away over four thousand households,
and killing over three hundred people.
An imperial edict ordered relief, loans, and coffins to be provided.
In autumn, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the seventh month,
Jiǎ Chōng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qín and Liáng two prefectures.
Táo Huáng and other generals of Wú besieged Jiāozhǐ.
Yáng Jì, Administrator, along with Máo Jǐng, Administrator of Yùlín, and the three commanderies including Rìnán, surrendered to Wú.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the eighth month,
Wèi Guàn, General Who Attacks the East, was appointed General Who Attacks the North and Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yōuzhōu.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Xiàn, Prince of Chéngyáng, passed away.
Níngzhōu was established by dividing the four commanderies of Nánzhōng from Yìzhōu.
A partial amnesty was granted to those in the four commanderies sentenced to death and below.
In winter, on the *dīngchǒu* day of the tenth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīngsì* day of the eleventh month,
Jī Shǔ, Duke of Wèi, passed away.
In the twelfth month,
there was heavy snow.
The office of Central Leader of the Army was abolished,
and combined with the Central Inspector of the Northern Army.
Zhèng Mào, Grand Master of Guanglu, was appointed Minister of Works.
In the spring of the eighth year, first month,
Hé Zhēn, Supervising Military Inspector, attacked Liú Měng of the Xiongnú,
defeating him repeatedly.
Lǐ Kè, chieftain of the Left Division, killed Měng and surrendered.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor plowed the sacrificial field.
On the *yǐhài* day of the second month,
the carving of patterns and weaving of brocade, which were illegal, were prohibited.
On the *rénchén* day,
Fú, Grand Tutor and Prince of Ānpíng, passed away.
An imperial edict ordered all officials, internal and external, to recommend three individuals each suitable for appointment to frontier commanderies.
The Emperor discussed affairs with Huángfǔ Táo, Right General.
Táo argued with the Emperor.
Zhèng Huī, Palace Attendant, submitted a memorial requesting his punishment.
The Emperor said:
“Speaking frankly and directly
is what I expect from those around me.
A ruler often suffers from flattery,
so how can a dissenting minister be a detriment?
Huī's overstepping his bounds and making a baseless accusation
is not my intention.”
Thereupon, Huī was dismissed from office.
In summer, fourth month,
the office of General of the Rear was established,
to complete the four generals' offices.
In the sixth month,
Zhāng Hóng, a staff officer from Yìzhōu, falsely accused his Inspector Huángfǔ Yàn of rebellion,
killed him,
and sent his head to the capital.
Hóng was executed,
and his three clans exterminated.
On the *rénchén* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict restored the land tax to the four commanderies of Lǒngyòu that had suffered from banditry.
In autumn, seventh month,
Jiǎ Chōng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Minister of Works.
In the ninth month,
Bù Chǎn, Dū of Xīlíng in Wú, came to surrender.
He was appointed Wèi Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī,
and enfeoffed as Yídū Gōng.
Lù Kàng, a general from Wú, attacked Chǎn.
Yáng Hù, Chēqí Jiāngjūn, was dispatched to lead troops out of Jiānglíng.
Yáng Zhào, Cǐshǐ of Jīngzhōu, met Chǎn at Xīlíng,
and Xú Yìn, Jiānjūn of Bādōng, attacked Jiànpíng to rescue Chǎn.
In winter, on the first day of the tenth month, Xīnwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twelfth month,
Zhào attacked Kàng,
but failed and returned.
Chǎn's city fell,
and he was captured by Kàng.
In the ninth year, in spring, on the Xīnyǒu day of the first month,
Zhèng Mào, Sīkōng and Mìlíng Hóu, passed away.
On the Guǐsì day of the second month,
Shí Bāo, Sītú and Lèlíng Gōng, passed away.
Lóng, Ānpíng Tínghóu, was established as Ānpíng Wáng.
In the third month,
Royal Prince Zhī was established as Dōnghǎi Wáng.
In summer, on the Wùchén day, the first day of the fourth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
Hé Zēng, Tàibǎo, was appointed to oversee the Sītú office.
On the Yǐwèi day of the sixth month,
Zhī, Dōnghǎi Wáng, passed away.
In autumn, on the Dīngyǒu day, the first day of the seventh month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Lǔ Shú, a Wú general, besieged Yìyáng.
Wáng Hún, Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn, defeated him.
The offices of Wǔguān Zuǒyòu Zhōnglángjiāng, Hóngxùn Tàipú, Wèiwèi, and Dàchángqiú were abolished.
The Xiānbēi raided Guǎngníng,
killing and abducting five thousand people.
An imperial edict ordered the selection of daughters of dukes, ministers, and below to fill the Six Palaces,
and until the selection was complete,
marriages were temporarily prohibited.
In winter, on the Xīnsì day of the tenth month,
an edict stated that if parents did not marry off their daughters by the age of seventeen,
senior officials should arrange their marriages.
On the Dīngyǒu day of the eleventh month,
the Emperor reviewed all the armies at Xuānwǔ Guān,
and the review concluded on the Jiǎchén day.
In the tenth year, in spring, on the Xīnhài day of the first month,
the Emperor ploughed the ceremonial field.
In the intercalary month, on the Guǐyǒu day,
Zhèng Chōng, Tàifù and Shòuguāng Gōng, passed away.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
Guī, Gāoyáng Wáng, passed away.
On the Gēngchén day,
Guī, Tàiyuán Wáng, passed away.
On the Dīnghài day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The distinction between嫡 and庶 (primary and secondary wives and their children)
is to differentiate between high and low,
and to clarify nobility and lowliness.
However, in recent times,
many have indulged in inner favorites,
elevating them to the positions of empresses and consorts,
disrupting the order of seniority.
From now on,
concubines and bondmaids are not to be appointed as primary wives."
In the second month,
five commanderies of Yōuzhōu were separated to establish Píngzhōu.
On the Guǐhài day of the third month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer, on the Jǐwèi day of the fourth month,
Xún Yǐ, Tàiwèi and Línhuái Gōng, passed away.
On the Guǐsì day of the sixth month,
the Emperor personally heard lawsuits at Tīngsòng Guān and released many prisoners.
Many were pardoned and released.
This summer,
there was a great locust plague.
In autumn, on the Bǐngyín day of the seventh month,
Empress Yáng passed away.
On the Rénwǔ day,
Mèng Tài, Pínglǔ Jiāng from Wú, and Wáng Sì, Piānjiāngjūn, led their troops to surrender.
In the eighth month,
the barbarians of Liángzhōu raided Jīnchéng and other commanderies.
Jùn, Zhènxī Jiāngjūn and Rǔyīn Wáng, attacked them,
beheading their chieftain Qǐwénní and others.
On the Wùshēn day,
Empress Yuán was buried at Jùnyáng Líng.
On the Guǐhài day of the ninth month,
Chén Qiān, Dàjiāngjūn, was made Tàiwèi.
The Wú city of Zhǐlǐ was attacked and captured,
and Zhuāng Yòu, Lìxìn Xiàowèi of Wú, was captured.
Sūn Zūn and Lǐ Chéng, Wú generals, led troops to raid Jiāngxià.
Jī Xǐ, Tàishǒu, attacked and defeated them.
A bridge was built over the Hé at Fùpíng Jīn.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
a stone bridge was built at the Qīlǐ Jiàn to the east of the city.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
the Emperor reviewed all the armies
at Xuānwǔ Guān.
In the twelfth month,
a comet appeared in Zhěn.
The office of Jiètián Lìng was established.
Jī, son of Tàiyuán Wáng, was established as Gāoyáng Wáng.
Yán Cōng, Wēiběi Jiāngjūn of Wú, Yán Zhěng, Yángwēi Jiāngjūn, and Zhū Mǎi, Piānjiāngjūn, came to surrender.
This year,
the southern mountains of Shǎn were excavated,
and the Hé was diverted,
flowing eastward into the Luò,
to facilitate water transport.
In the first year of Xiánníng, in spring, on the Wùwǔ day, the first day of the first month,
there was a general amnesty,
and the reign era was changed.
In the second month,
because many officers and soldiers had already married,
households with five daughters were granted tax exemption.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
because Xià Sù, the former Yè Lìng, had a reputation for integrity,
he was bestowed with one hundred hù of grain.
Due to meager salaries,
dukes, ministers, and below were bestowed with varying amounts of silk.
The rebellious barbarian Shùjīnéng sent a hostage and requested to surrender.
In summer, in the fifth month,
there were strong winds in Xiàpī and Guǎnglíng,
uprooting trees
and destroying dwellings.
In the sixth month,
Lìwēi of the Xiānbēi sent his son to offer tribute.
People from Wú raided Jiāngxià.
Mǎ Xún, Wǔjǐ Xiàowèi of the Western Regions, attacked rebellious Xiānbēi,
defeated them,
and beheaded their chieftain.
On the Wùshēn day,
the office of Tàizǐ Zhānshì was established.
In autumn, on the Jiǎshēn day, the last day of the seventh month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Locusts infested the commanderies and states.
On the Rén Yín day of the eighth month,
Wén, son of Pèi Wáng, passed away.

The former Tàifù Zhèng Chōng, Tàiwèi Xún Yǐ, Sītú Shí Bāo, Sīkōng Péi Xiù, Piàojì Jiāngjūn Wáng Shěn, Ānpíng Xiàn Wáng Fú, and others, as well as Tàibǎo Hé Zēng, Sīkōng Jiǎ Chōng, Tàiwèi Chén Qiān, Zhōngshū Jiān Xún Xù, Píngnán Jiāngjūn Yáng Hù, Qí Wáng Yōu, and others, were all listed for inscription and offerings.
On the Jiǎzǐ day of the ninth month,
locusts infested Qīngzhōu,
and Xúzhōu experienced severe flooding.
In winter, on the Yǐyǒu day of the tenth month,
Yīn, Chángshān Wáng, passed away.
On the Guǐsì day,
Quán, Péngchéng Wáng, passed away.
On the Guǐhài day of the eleventh month,
there was a grand review at Xuānwǔ Guān,
lasting until the Jǐsì day.
On the Dīnghài day of the twelfth month,
Emperor Xuān's temple name was posthumously changed to Gāozǔ,
Emperor Jǐng's to Shìzōng,
and Emperor Wén's to Tàizǔ.
This month, there was a great plague,
and more than half of the population in Luòyáng died.
Péi Wěi was enfeoffed as Jùlù Gōng.
In the second year, in spring, in the first month,
court was suspended due to the epidemic.
All scattered officials down to soldiers were bestowed with varying amounts of silk.
On the Bǐngxū day of the second month,
Hóng, Héjiān Wáng, passed away.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
amnesty was granted for sentences of five years or less.
Eight nations of the Eastern Yi submitted.
Barbarians in Bìngzhōu violated the frontier.
Hú Fèn, Jiānbìngzhōu Zhūjūnshì, attacked and defeated them.
Previously,
Yǐn Qú, Tàishǒu of Dùnhuáng, had died.
The province appointed Liáng Chéng, Lìng of Dùnhuáng, to act as Tàishǒu.
Lìnghú Fēng, Yìláng, deposed Chéng
and took charge of the commandery himself.
After Fēng died,
his younger brother Hóng succeeded him.
At this point,
Yáng Xīn, Cǐshǐ of Liángzhōu, beheaded Hóng
and sent his head to Luòyáng.
Before this,
the Emperor had been unwell,
and when he recovered,
officials offered congratulations.
An imperial edict stated:
"Every time I recall the recent deaths due to the plague,
I feel mournful.
How can I enjoy my personal rest
and forget the hardships and suffering of the people?
All congratulatory rituals are to be cancelled."
In summer, in the fifth month,
Jùn, Zhènxī Dàjiāngjūn and Rǔyīn Wáng, attacked the Northern Hu,
beheading their chieftain Tùdūn.
The Guózǐ Xué (National Academy) was established.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
there was a great sacrifice for rain.
In the *guǐchǒu* day of the sixth month,
lychees were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
[(15)] a comet (bèi) appeared in the asterism Dī.
There had been a drought since spring,
and it was not until this month that rain finally fell.
Wú's Jingxià Inspector Sūn Kǎi (孫楷) led his troops to surrender,
and was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chēqí Jiāngjūn),
and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dānyáng (Dānyáng Hóu).
Two white dragons were seen in a well in Xīnxīng.
In the seventh month of autumn,
a comet appeared in the asterism Dàjiǎo.
Wú's Línpíng Lake (Línpíng Hú), which had been blocked since the end of the Hàn dynasty,
now opened on its own.
The elders passed down a saying:
"When this lake is blocked,
the world is in chaos;
when this lake opens,
the world is at peace."
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Ānpíng Prince Lóng (隆) passed away.
Seventeen states of the Eastern Yi (Dōngyí) submitted and became内附 (nèifù).
Hénán (Hénán) and Wèijùn (Wèijùn) suffered severe floods,
killing over a hundred people.
An imperial edict ordered that coffins be provided.
The Xiānbēi (Xiānbēi) led by Āluóduō (阿羅多) and others raided the border,
and the Western Regions (Xīyù) Wùjǐ Commandant Mǎ Xún (馬循) attacked them,
beheading over four thousand,
and capturing over nine thousand alive.
They then surrendered.
On the *gēngchén* day of the eighth month,
Hédōng (Hédōng) and Píngyáng (Píngyáng) experienced an earthquake.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Grand Tutor (Tàibǎo) Hé Zēng (何曾) was appointed Grand Preceptor (Tàifù),
Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi) Chén Qiān (陳騫) was appointed Grand Marshal (Dà Sīmǎ),
Minister of Works (Sīkōng) Jiǎ Chōng (賈充) was appointed Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi),
and General-in-chief Who Guards the Army (Zhènjūn Dàjiāngjūn) Qí Prince Yōu (攸) was appointed Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
A comet appeared in the asterism Tàiwēi,
and in the ninth month, it appeared again in Yì.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Grand Granary (Tàicāng) was built east of the city,
and the Ever-Normal Granaries (Chángpíngcāng) were built in the east and west markets.
In the intercalary month,
the five commanderies of Jīngzhōu (Jīngzhōu) suffered floods,
displacing over four thousand households.
In the tenth month of winter,
Rǔyīn Prince Jùn (駿) was appointed General-in-chief Who Conquers the West (Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn),
and General Who Pacifies the South (Píngnán Jiāngjūn) Yáng Hù (羊祜) was appointed General-in-chief Who Conquers the South (Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn).
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Empress Yáng (楊氏) was enthroned.
A general amnesty was declared,
and kings, dukes, and below, as well as orphans, widows, and the lonely, were granted gifts of varying amounts.
In the eleventh month,
two white dragons were seen in Liángguó (Liángguó).
In the twelfth month,
the recluse Huángfǔ Mì (皇甫謐) of Āndìng (Āndìng) was summoned to be Aide to the Heir Apparent (Tàizǐ Zhōngshùzǐ),
and the Empress's father, General-in-chief Who Guards the Army (Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn) Yáng Jùn (楊駿), was enfeoffed as Marquis of Línjìn (Línjìn Hóu).
In this month,
the Inspector of Píngzhōu (Píngzhōu), Fù Xún (傅詢), and the former Grand Administrator of Guǎngpíng (Guǎngpíng), Méng Huán (孟桓), were praised for their integrity.
Xún (詢) was granted two hundred bolts of silk,
and Huán (桓) one hundred bolts.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day, the first day of the first month of spring in the third year,
there was a solar eclipse.
Imperial Prince Yù (裕) was established as Shǐpíng Prince,
and Dūn (敦), the brother of Ānpíng Mù Prince Lóng (隆), was established as Ānpíng Prince.
An imperial edict stated:
"The imperial clan and imperial relatives
are the branches and leaves of the state.
We desire them to lead by virtue and righteousness,
and serve as models for the world.
However, those who can maintain prudent conduct while in wealth and nobility are few.
Shào Mùgōng (召穆公) gathered his brothers and composed the poem Tangdì (唐棣),
which is why the Jī clan (姬氏) has maintained its lineage for a hundred generations.
Now, We appoint General Who Guards the Army (Wèijiāngjūn) and Fúfēng Prince Liàng (亮) as the宗師 (Zōngshī, Master of the Clan).
All matters that should be implemented
are to be consulted with the Zōngshī."
On the *gēngyín* day,
Shǐpíng Prince Yù (裕) passed away.
A comet appeared in the west.
General-in-chief Who Conquers the North (Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn) Wèi Guàn (衞瓘) was sent to attack the Xiānbēi (Xiānbēi) leader Lì Wēi (力微).
In the third month,
the Commander of Pacifying the Barbarians (Pínglǔ Hùjūn) Wén Shú (文淑) attacked the rebellious barbarians Shù Jīnéng (樹機能) and others,
[(17)] and defeated them all.
A comet appeared in the asterism Wèi.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor intended to hunt pheasants,
but stopped out of concern for damaging the wheat seedlings.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the fifth month of summer,
Wú generals Shào Kǎi (邵凱) and Xià Xiáng (夏祥) led over seven thousand troops to surrender.
In the sixth month,
the eight commanderies of Yì (Yì) and Liáng (Liáng) suffered floods,
killing over three hundred people,
and submerging official granaries and separate storehouses.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Commander-in-chief of All Military Affairs in Yùzhōu (Yùzhōu Zhū Jūnshì) Wáng Hún (王渾) was appointed Commander-in-chief of All Military Affairs in Yángzhōu (Yángzhōu Zhū Jūnshì).
Zhōngshān Prince Mù (睦) was stripped of his title for a crime and demoted to Marquis of Dānshuǐ (Dānshuǐ Hóu).
On the *guǐhài* day of the eighth month,
Fúfēng Prince Liàng (亮) was transferred to be Rǔnán Prince,
Dōngguǎn Prince Zhòu (伷) to be Lángyé Prince,
Rǔyīn Prince Jùn (駿) to be Fúfēng Prince,
Lángyé Prince Lún (倫) to be Zhào Prince,
Bóhǎi Prince Fǔ (輔) to be Tàiyuán Prince,
Tàiyuán Prince Yóng (顒) to be Héjiān Prince,
Běihǎi Prince Líng (陵) to be Rènchéng Prince,
Chén Prince Bīn (斌) to be Xīhé Prince,
Rǔnán Prince Jiǎn (柬) to be Nányáng Prince,
Jìnán Prince Dān (耽) to be Zhōngshān Prince,
and Héjiān Prince Wēi (威) to be Zhāngwǔ Prince.
Imperial Prince Wěi (瑋) was established as Shǐpíng Prince,
Yǔn (允) as Púyáng Prince,
Gāi (該) as Xīndū Prince,
Xiá (遐) as Qīnghé Prince,
and Marquis of Jùpíng (Jùpíng Hóu) Yáng Hù (羊祜) as Marquis of Nánchéng (Nánchéng Hóu).
Rǔnán Prince Liàng (亮) was appointed General-in-chief Who Guards the South (Zhènnán Dàjiāngjūn).
There was a great wind that uprooted trees,
and it was severely cold and icy.
[(19)] Five commanderies and states experienced hoarfrost,
damaging grain.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the ninth month,
Left General (Zuǒ Jiāngjūn) Hú Fèn (胡奮) was appointed Commander-in-chief of All Military Affairs North of the Jiāng River (Jiāngběi Zhū Jūnshì).
The seven provinces of Yǎn (Yǎn), Yù (Yù), Xú (Xú), Qīng (Qīng), Jīng (Jīng), Yì (Yì), and Liáng (Liáng) suffered great floods,
damaging the autumn harvest.
An imperial edict ordered relief distribution.
Qí Prince's son Ruí (蕤) was established as Liáodōng Prince,
and Zàn (贊) as Guǎnghàn Prince.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the eleventh month of winter,
the Emperor personally reviewed a grand parade at Xuānwǔ Guān (Xuānwǔ Guān),
until the *rénchén* day.
In the twelfth month,
Wú general Sūn Shèn (孫慎) entered Jiāngxià (Jiāngxià) and Rǔnán (Rǔnán),
plundering over a thousand households before departing.
In this year,
northwestern barbarians, including the Xiānbēi (Xiānbēi), Xiōngnú (Xiōngnú), Five Streams Man (Wǔxīmán), and three Eastern Yi (Dōngyí) states, totalling over ten groups,
[(20)] each led their tribal people and communities to submit and become内附 (nèifù).
On the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the first month of spring in the fourth year,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the third month,
Minister (Shàngshū) Left Attendant (Zuǒ Púshè) Lú Qīn (盧欽) passed away.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Minister (Shàngshū) Right Attendant (Yòu Púshè) Shān Tāo (山濤) was appointed Minister (Shàngshū) Left Attendant (Zuǒ Púshè).
[(21)] Six Eastern Yi (Dōngyí) states came to offer tribute.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Chīyóu Banner (Chīyóu Qí) was seen in the asterism Dōngjǐng.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the sixth month,
Yīnpíng (Yīnpíng) and Guǎngwǔ (Guǎngwǔ) experienced an earthquake,
and on the *jiǎzǐ* day, it shook again.
The Inspector of Liángzhōu (Liángzhōu), Yáng Xīn (楊欣), battled with the barbarians Ruòluó Bánéng (若羅拔能) and others in Wǔwēi (Wǔwēi),
suffering a defeat,
and died.
Empress Hóngxùn (Hóngxùn Huánghòu) Yáng (楊氏) passed away.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the seventh month of autumn,
Empress Jǐngxiàn (Jǐngxiàn Huánghòu) Yáng (楊氏) was interred together with the emperor at Jùnpíng Líng (Jùnpíng Líng).
On the *gēngyín* day,
Gāoyáng Prince Jī (緝) passed away.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Fànyáng Prince Suī (綏) passed away.
Twenty commanderies and states in Jīng (Jīng) and Yáng (Yáng) all suffered great floods.
In the ninth month,
Grand Preceptor (Tàifù) Hé Zēng (何曾) was appointed Grand Tutor (Tàizǎi).
On the *xīnsì* day,
Minister (Shàngshū) Lǐ Yìn (李胤) was appointed Minister of Education (Sītú).
In the tenth month of winter,
General-in-chief Who Conquers the North (Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn) Wèi Guàn (衞瓘) was appointed Minister (Shàngshū) Lǐng (Lǐng).
The Inspector of Yángzhōu (Yángzhōu), Yīng Chuò (應綽), attacked Wú's Wǎnchéng (Wǎnchéng),
beheading five thousand,
and burning one million eight hundred thousand *hú* of grain and rice.
On the *xīnsì* day of the eleventh month,
Imperial Physician (Tàiyī) Sīmǎ Chéng Jù (程據) presented a pheasant-feather coat.
The Emperor, considering it an extravagant and unusual garment forbidden by ritual,
burned it in front of the palace hall.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an edict commanded that anyone, internal or external, who dared to commit such an offense would be punished.
Wú's General Who Displays Martial Prowess (Zhāowǔ Jiāngjūn) Liú Fān (劉翻) and General Who Inspires Martial Prowess (Lìwǔ Jiāngjūn) Zǔ Shǐ (祖始) came to surrender.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Minister (Shàngshū) Dù Yù (杜預) was appointed Commander-in-chief of All Military Affairs in Jīngzhōu (Jīngzhōu Zhū Jūnshì).
General-in-chief Who Conquers the South (Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn) Yáng Hù (羊祜) passed away.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the twelfth month,
Xīhé Prince Bīn (斌) passed away.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Grand Tutor (Tàizǎi) Lánglíng Duke Hé Zēng (何曾) passed away.
In this year,
nine Eastern Yi (Dōngyí) states submitted and became内附 (nèifù).
In the first month of spring in the fifth year,
the barbarian leader Shù Jīnéng (樹機能) attacked and captured Liángzhōu (Liángzhōu).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Commander of Pacifying the Barbarians (Tǎolǔ Hùjūn) and Grand Administrator of Wǔwēi (Wǔwēi Tàishǒu) Mǎ Lóng (馬隆) was sent to attack him.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the second month,
a white qilin was seen in Píngyuán (Píngyuán).
In the third month,
the Xiōngnú (Xiōngnú) Commander (Dūdū) Bá Yìxū (拔弈虛) led his tribes to submit to civilization.
On the *yǐhài* day,
due to famine among the people,
the imperial meals were reduced by half.
A comet appeared in the asterism Liǔ.
In the summer, fourth month,
a comet again appeared in the asterism Nǚyù.
There was a general amnesty,
and the commoner hostages of Bùqǔdū and below were released.
On the Dīnghài day,
hail fell in eight commanderies and kingdoms,
〔二二〕damaging the autumn crops
and destroying the homes of the common people.
In the autumn, seventh month,
a comet appeared in the Zǐgōng asterism.
On the ninth month Jiǎwǔ day,
a Qílín was seen in Hénán.
In the winter, tenth month Wùyín day,
Dúyōng and others, the remaining Qú Dūdū of the Xiōngnú, led their tribes to submit.
A man from Jí Jùn, Bùzhǔn, excavated the tomb of Wèi Xiāng Wáng,
〔二三〕and obtained over 100,000 words of ancient texts on bamboo slips in Xiǎozhuàn script,
which were stored in the secret archive.
In the eleventh month,
a grand expedition was launched to attack Wú.
Zhèn Jūn Jiāngjūn, Lángyá Wáng Zhòu was dispatched to exit Tútúzhōng;
〔二四〕Ān Dōng Jiāngjūn Wáng Hún exited Jiāngxī;
Jiàn Wēi Jiāngjūn Wáng Róng exited Wǔchāng;
Píng Nán Jiāngjūn Hú Fèn exited Xiàkǒu;
Zhèn Nán Dà Jiāngjūn Dù Yù exited Jiānglíng;
Lóng Xiáng Jiāngjūn Wáng Jùn and Guǎng Wǔ Jiāngjūn Táng Bīn led the troops from Bāshǔ downstream along the Jiāng,
totaling over 200,000 on the east and west fronts.
Tàiwèi Jiǎ Chōng was made Grand Commander,
with Xíng Guàn Jūn Jiāngjūn Yáng Jì as his deputy,
to command all the armies.
In the twelfth month,
Mǎ Lóng attacked the rebellious Rú Shùjīnéng,
inflicted a great defeat,
and slew him.
Liángzhōu was pacified.
The Sùshèn came to offer Hú shǐ and stone arrowheads.
In the spring of Tàikāng first year, first month Jǐchǒu first day,
five-colored qi crowned the sun.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
Wáng Hún conquered Wú's Xúnyáng, Làixiāng, and other cities,
capturing Wú Wǔ Wēi Jiāngjūn Zhōu Xīng.
In the second month Wùwǔ day,
Wáng Jùn, Táng Bīn, and others conquered Dānyáng City.
On the Gēngshēn day,
they also conquered Xīlíng,
killing Xīlíng Dūdū, Zhèn Jūn Jiāngjūn Liú Xiàn,
〔二五〕Zhēng Nán Jiāngjūn Chéng Qú,
and Xīlíng Jiān Zhèng Guǎng.
On the Rénxū day,
Jùn also conquered Yídào Lexiāng City,
killing Yídào Jiān Lù Yàn and Shuǐ Jūn Dūdū Lù Jǐng.
On the Jiǎxū day,
Dù Yù conquered Jiānglíng,
beheading Wú Jiānglíng Dū Wǔ Yán;
〔二六〕Píng Nán Jiāngjūn Hú Fèn conquered Jiāng'ān.
Thereupon, all the armies advanced,
and the garrisons of Lexiāng and Jīngmén successively surrendered.
On the Yǐhài day,
Jùn was made Dūdū of the military affairs of Yì and Liáng provinces.
Another imperial edict was issued, stating:
"Jùn and Bīn are to proceed east downstream,
sweeping Bāqiū,
and together with Hú Fèn and Wáng Róng, pacify Xiàkǒu and Wǔchāng.
They are to continue rapidly downstream,
proceeding directly to Líng,
and with Fèn and Róng, consider what is appropriate.
Dù Yù shall pacify Líng and Guì,
and gather allegiance in Héngyáng.
Once the main army has passed,
the southern border of Jīngzhōu should be pacified by merely passing a dispatch.
Yù should allocate 10,000 men to Jùn,
and 7,000 to Bīn.
Once Xiàkǒu is pacified,
Fèn should allocate 7,000 men to Jùn.
Once Wǔchāng is settled,
Róng should add 6,000 men to Bīn.
Tàiwèi Chōng is to move his encampment to Xiàng,
to oversee all fronts."
Jùn advanced, defeated Xiàkǒu and Wǔchāng,
and then sailed east downstream,
pacifying all places he reached.
Wáng Hún and Zhōu Jùn fought Wú Chéngxiàng Zhāng Tì at Bǎnbqiáo,
inflicting a great defeat,
and beheaded Tì and his generals Sūn Zhèn and Shěn Yíng.
Their heads were sent to Luòyáng.
Sūn Hào, in dire straits, requested to surrender,
sending his imperial seal and ribbon to Lángyá Wáng Zhòu.
On the third month Rénrín day,
Wáng Jùn arrived with his fleet at Shítou in Jiànyè.
〔二七〕Sūn Hào was greatly terrified,
bound himself with rope, rode in a plain carriage with a coffin,
and surrendered at the army gate.
Jùn, holding the imperial envoy's staff, untied him and burned the coffin,
and sent him to the capital.
His maps and records were seized.
Four provinces,
forty-three commanderies,
three hundred thirteen counties,
523,000 households,
32,000 officials,
230,000 soldiers,
and 2,300,000 people (men and women) were taken.
Their governors and administrators, from then on, were those appointed by Wú.
Their harsh policies were abolished,
and they were shown simplicity and ease,
which greatly pleased the people of Wú.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
〔二八〕there was a general amnesty,
the era name was changed,
there was a grand feast for five days,
and orphans, the elderly, and the impoverished were given relief.
In the summer, fourth month,
hail fell in Hédōng and Gāopíng,
damaging the autumn crops.
Jiān Shìzhōng Zhāng Cè and Huángmén Shìláng Zhū Zhèn were dispatched to tour Yángyuè,
to comfort the newly surrendered.
A white Qílín was seen in Dùnqīu.
Hail fell in Sānhé, Wèi Jùn, and Hóngnóng,
damaging the winter wheat.
On the fifth month Xīnhài day,
Sūn Hào was enfeoffed as Guīmìng Hóu.
His crown prince was appointed Zhōngláng,
and his sons were appointed Lángzhōng.
Former distinguished figures of Wú
were promoted according to their talent.
The families of Sūn's great generals who died in battle were moved to Shòuyáng.
Generals and officials who crossed the Jiāng were granted ten years of tax exemption,
and common people and artisans twenty years.
On the Bǐngyín day,
〔二九〕the Emperor presided over a grand assembly,
led Hào to ascend the hall,
and all the officials shouted "Long live the Emperor!"
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Ēnlù wine was offered in the Tàimiào.
Hail fell in six commanderies and kingdoms,
damaging the autumn crops.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
an edict ordered all soldiers aged sixty and above to be dismissed and return home.
On the Gēngchén day,
Wáng Jùn was appointed Fǔguó Dà Jiāngjūn and Xiāngyáng Hóu;
Dù Yù was appointed Dāngyáng Hóu;
Wáng Róng was appointed Ānfēng Hóu;
Táng Bīn was appointed Shàngyōng Hóu;
Jiǎ Chōng, Lángyá Wáng Zhòu, and others received increased enfeoffments.
Thereupon, merits were assessed and enfeoffments granted,
and silk was bestowed upon dukes, ministers, and others, with varying amounts.
In the sixth month Dīngchǒu day,
the office of Yì Jūn Xiàowèi was first established.
Mù, the Dānshuǐ Hóu, was enfeoffed as Gāoyáng Wáng.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
ten states of the Eastern Yí submitted.
In the autumn, seventh month,
the barbarian Kēchéngní raided Xīpíng and Hàowěi,
killing over three hundred people, including the Dū Jiāng.
Twenty states of the Eastern Yí came to pay tribute.
On the Gēngyín day,
Shàngshū Wèi Shū was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
In the eighth month,
the former division of Chēshī sent a son to serve as a hostage.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the imperial younger brother Yánzuò was enfeoffed as Lèpíng Wáng.
Three white dragons were seen in Yǒngchāng.
In the ninth month,
the officials, seeing the unification of All Under Heaven,
repeatedly requested the fengshan sacrifices,
but the Emperor modestly refused.
In the winter, tenth month Dīngsì day,
the tax exemption for families with five daughters was abolished.
On the twelfth month Wùchén day,
Guǎnghàn Wáng Zàn passed away.
In the second year, spring, second month,
earthquakes occurred in Huáinán and Dānyáng.
On the third month Bǐngshēn day,
Ānpíng Wáng Dūn passed away.
Dukes, princes, and others were granted varying numbers of Wú captives.
An edict ordered the selection of 5,000 of Sūn Hào's concubines and entertainers to enter the palace.
Five states of the Eastern Yí came to pay tribute.
In the summer, sixth month,
five states of the Eastern Yí submitted.
Hail fell in sixteen commanderies and kingdoms,
strong winds uprooted trees,
and destroyed the homes of the common people.
Jiāngxià and Tàishān flooded,
sweeping away over three hundred households.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Shàngdǎng again suffered from violent storms and hail,
damaging the autumn crops.
In the eighth month,
a comet appeared in the asterism Zhāng.
In the winter, tenth month,
Xiānbēi Mùróng Wěi raided Chānglí.
In the eleventh month Rénrín day,
Dà Sīmǎ Chén Qiān passed away.
A comet appeared in the asterism Xuānyuán.
The Xiānbēi raided Liáoxī,
and Píngzhōu Cìshǐ Xiānyú Yīng attacked and defeated them.
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Qínzhōu was abolished
and merged into Yōngzhōu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zhāng Huà, Grand Minister of Works, was made Grand Controller of all military affairs in Yōuzhōu.
In the third month,
Yán Xún, General Who Pacifies the North, defeated Mùróng Cuì of the Xiānbēi at Chānglí,
killing and wounding tens of thousands of people.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Jiǎ Chōng, Grand Commandant and Duke of Lǔ, passed away.
In the intercalary month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Lǐ Yìn, Minister of Education and Marquis of Guǎnglù, passed away.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
two white dragons were seen in Jǐnán.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
〔三一〕the governors of Píngzhōu and Níngzhōu were ordered to submit reports to the court only once every three years.
In the ninth month,
twenty-nine Eastern Yi states submitted and assimilated,
offering their local products.
The former Wú generals Guǎn Gōng and Bó Fèng raised an army and rebelled,
attacking and harming the magistrate of Jiànyè,
and then besieged Yángzhōu.
Jī Xǐ, the Governor of Xúzhōu, suppressed them.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Sīkōng Qí Wáng Yōu was made Grand Minister of War and Controller of all military affairs in Qīngzhōu.
Zhòu, General Who Guards the East and Prince of Lángxié, was made General Who Stabilizes the Army.
〔三二〕Liàng, Prince of Rǔnán, was made Grand Commandant.
Shān Tāo, Grand Master of Guanglu, was made Minister of Education.
Wèi Guàn, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Sīkōng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an edict was issued that those areas with severe floods or droughts should be exempt from paying land taxes.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
〔三三〕Wèi Shū, Right Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
Huǎng, Prince of Xiàpí, was made Right Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Shān Tāo, Minister of Education, passed away.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Shí, Marquis of Chánglètíng, was enfeoffed as Prince of Běihǎi.
In the third month, on the day Xīnchǒu, the first day of the month,
〔三四〕there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Qí Wáng Yōu, Grand Minister of War, passed away.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Líng, Prince of Rènchéng, passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Zhòu, Grand General and Prince of Lángxié, passed away.
Ruí, Prince of Liáodōng, was transferred to be Prince of Dōnglái.
In the sixth month,
the ceremonial ranks of the nine ministers were increased.
Over two thousand households of the Zāngkē Láo submitted.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Huǎng, Right Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat and Prince of Xiàpí, was made Grand Controller of all military affairs in Qīngzhōu.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Yǎnzhōu experienced a great flood,
and its land taxes were remitted.
In the eighth month,
the state of Shànshàn sent a son to serve at court,
and he was granted the title of Marquis Guīyì.
Tài, Prince of Lǒngxī, was made Right Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Gāi, Prince of Xīndū, passed away.
Wèi Shū, Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat, was made Minister of Education.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
a grand military parade was held at Xuānwǔguān.
In this year,
Hénèi and Jīngzhōu, and Yángzhōu experienced great floods.
In the fifth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Jǐhài,
two green dragons were seen in the well of the Imperial Armory.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Diàn, a son of the Prince of Nángōng, was enfeoffed as Prince of Chánglè.
〔三五〕On the day Rénchén,
there was an earthquake.
In summer, in the fourth month,
the waters in the ponds of Rènchéng and Lǔguó turned red like blood.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the beam of Emperor Xuān's ancestral temple broke.
In the sixth month,
the Huángshā Prison was first established.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
Huī, an imperial prince, passed away.
Rènchéng, Liángguó, and Zhōngshān experienced hail,
damaging the autumn harvest.
The household tax quota for the entire empire was reduced by one-third.
In the ninth month,
Nán'ān experienced strong winds that broke trees.
Five commanderies and states experienced great floods.
Frost fell,
damaging the autumn harvest.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Fǔ, Prince of Tàiyuán, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Línyì and Dàqín each sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the intercalary month,
Dù Yù, General Who Guards the South and Marquis of Dāngyáng, passed away.
In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Jiǎshēn, the first day of the month,
〔三六〕because of continuous years of poor harvests,
rents and outstanding debts were remitted.
On the day Wùchén,
Wáng Hún, General Who Conquers the South, was made Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat.
Chǔ Sì, Grand Minister of Works, was made Grand Controller of all military affairs in Yángzhōu.
Yáng Jì was made Grand Controller of all military affairs in Jīngzhōu.
In the third month,
six commanderies and states experienced frost,
damaging mulberry trees and wheat.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Fúnán and ten other states came to offer tribute.
Over four thousand households of Cānlí submitted.
Four commanderies and states experienced drought,
and ten experienced great floods,
destroying people's homes.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Bāxī experienced an earthquake.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngxū, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The common people's contributions of silk floss and silk fabric were reduced by one-third.
A white dragon was seen in Jīngzhào.
Wáng Jùn, General Who Guards the Army, was made General Who Stabilizes the Army.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Liú Kāng, Duke of Shānyáng, passed away.
In winter, in the tenth month,
a mountain collapsed in Nán'ān,
and water gushed out.
A bipedal beast was captured in Nányáng Commandery.
The states of Qiūcí and Yānqí sent sons to serve at court.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
a grand military parade was held at Xuānwǔguān,
and it concluded after ten days.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wáng Jùn, General Who Stabilizes the Army and Marquis of Xiāngyáng, passed away.
In the seventh year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Jiǎyín, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict stated:
"In recent years, calamities and strange phenomena have occurred repeatedly.
There have been three solar eclipses,
earthquakes, and mountain collapses.
The state's misfortunes
are indeed due to me.
Let all dukes, ministers, and grand officers submit sealed memorials,
fully explaining the reasons,
and hide nothing."
In summer, in the fifth month,
thirteen commanderies and states experienced drought.
Mùróng Cuì of the Xiānbēi raided Liáodōng.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
a mountain collapsed in Zhūtí,
and Jiànwéi experienced an earthquake.
In the eighth month,
eleven Eastern Yi states submitted.
Jīngzhào experienced an earthquake.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
Jùn, General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Fúfēng, passed away.
Eight commanderies and states experienced great floods.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Tài, Prince of Lǒngxī, was made Grand Controller of all military affairs in Guānzhōng.
In the twelfth month,
attendant imperial censors were sent to inspect the commanderies affected by floods.
Two hundred and seventy imperial concubines, court entertainers, and others of lower rank were sent home from the imperial harem.
It was first decreed that high ministers might observe a three-year mourning period.
On the day Jǐhài,
Héyīn experienced a rain of red snow over an area of two qǐng.
In this year,
Fúnán and twenty-one other states, and Mǎhán and eleven other states sent envoys to offer tribute.
In the eighth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Wùshēn, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The main hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple collapsed.
In the third month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Línshāng Tower shook.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Qíguó and Tiānshuǐ experienced frost,
〔三七〕damaging the wheat.
In the sixth month,
Lǔguó experienced strong winds
that uprooted trees
and destroyed people's homes.
Eight commanderies and states experienced great floods.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the ground of the Front Palace collapsed,
several zhàng deep,
and a broken boat was found within.
In the eighth month,
two Eastern Yi states submitted.
In the ninth month,
the Imperial Ancestral Temple was rebuilt.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Lǐ Fēng, an official of Pínggù county in Nánkāng, rebelled,
gathering a crowd and attacking commanderies and counties.
He proclaimed himself general.
In the eleventh month,
Xiāo Fǔ, magistrate of Hǎi'ān, gathered a crowd and rebelled.
In the twelfth month,
Jiǎng Dí (蔣迪) of Wúxìng (吳興) gathered a party and rebelled.
They besieged Yángxiàn (陽羨) County.
The provincial and commandery authorities pursued and suppressed them,
and they were all executed.
Fúnán (扶南) of the southern Yi and Kāngjū (康居) State of the Western Regions each sent envoys to offer tribute.
In this year,
five commanderies and kingdoms experienced earthquakes.
In the first month, spring of the ninth year, on the day Rénshēn (壬申), the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict stated:
“The foundation of flourishing transformation
lies in fair governance and righteous judgments.
The Two-Thousand-Picul chief officials are unable to diligently care for the hidden sufferings of the people,
but instead lightly harbor private grievances,
giving rise to extended legal cases and punishments.
Moreover, many are greedy and corrupt,
troubling and disturbing the populace.
Therefore, instruct the Inspectors and Two-Thousand-Picul officials to rectify their impurity and corruption,
and to promote those who are public-minded and pure.
The relevant authorities shall deliberate on their demotion or promotion.
Order all officials, both within and outside the capital, to recommend the pure and capable,
and to elevate the humble and unadorned.”
Four commanderies in Jiāngdōng (江東) experienced earthquakes.
In the second month,
Hú Fèn (胡奮), Minister of the Right and Marquis of Yángxià (陽夏), passed away.
Zhū Zhěng (朱整), a Minister, was appointed Minister of the Right.
On the day Dīngchǒu (丁丑) in the third month,
the Empress personally performed the mulberry ceremony in the western suburb.
Silk was bestowed with varying grades.
On the day Rénchén (壬辰),
the two She (社) altars were first combined into one.
In the fourth month, summer,
eight commanderies and kingdoms south of the river experienced earthquakes;
frost fell in Lǒngxī (隴西),
damaging the over-wintering wheat.
In the fifth month,
Qí (奇), Prince of Yìyáng (義陽), was found guilty
and demoted to Marquis of Sānzòng (三縱) Pavilion.
An imperial edict ordered all officials, both within and outside the capital, to recommend talented prefects and magistrates.
On the day Gēngzǐ (庚子), the first day of the month in the sixth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Wēi (威), Prince of Zhāngwǔ (章武), was transferred to be Prince of Yìyáng (義陽).
Thirty-two commanderies and kingdoms experienced a great drought,
damaging the wheat.
On the day Rénzǐ (壬子) in the eighth month, autumn,
stars fell like rain.
An imperial edict ordered that all minor criminal cases below five years' imprisonment in commanderies and kingdoms be resolved and dispatched,
with no lingering common lawsuits.
In the ninth month,
seven states of the Eastern Yi presented themselves to the Commandant and submitted.
Twenty-four commanderies and kingdoms suffered from locusts.
On the day Guǐmǎo (癸卯) in the twelfth month, winter,
Yīng (英), son of Hóng (洪), Prince Píng (平) of Héjiān (河間), was established as Prince of Zhāngwǔ (章武).
〔三八〕On the day Wùshēn (戊申),
a green dragon and a yellow dragon each appeared in the state of Lǔ (魯).
In the fourth month, summer of the tenth year,
Liú Xiāo (劉霄), Administrator of Jīngzhào (京兆), and Liáng Liǔ (梁柳), Administrator of Yángpíng (陽平), were each granted a thousand hu (斛) of grain for their administrative achievements.
Eight commanderies and kingdoms experienced frost.
The Grand Ancestral Temple was completed.
On the day Yǐsì (乙巳),
the spirit tablets were moved to the new temple.
The Emperor welcomed them on the roadside,
and then performed the comprehensive ancestral sacrifice.
There was a great amnesty,
and civil and military officials were promoted one rank,
those who worked on the temple two ranks.
On the day Dīngwèi (丁未),
Zhū Zhěng (朱整), Minister of the Right and Marquis of Guǎngxìng (廣興), passed away.
On the day Guǐchǒu (癸丑),
Chóngxián (崇賢) Hall suffered a fire.
In the fifth month,
Mùróng Kuì (慕容廆) of the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) surrendered,
and eleven states of the Eastern Yi submitted.
On the day Gēngzǐ (庚zǐ) in the sixth month,
Liú Jǐn (劉瑾), Duke of Shānyáng (山陽), passed away.
The two She (社) altars were re-established.
On the day Rénzǐ (壬zǐ) in the tenth month, winter,
Chéng (承), Prince of Nángōng (南宮), was transferred to be Prince of Wǔyì (武邑).
On the day Bǐngchén (丙辰) in the eleventh month,
Xún Xù (荀勖), Acting Minister of the Left and Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left, passed away.
The Emperor recovered from his illness,
and bestowed silk upon princes, dukes, and others with varying grades.
The鞠 (Jú) chamber of Hánzhāng (含章) Hall caught fire.
On the day Jiǎshēn (甲shēn),
Liàng (亮), Prince of Rǔnán (汝南), was appointed Grand Marshal, Grand Commander, and Acting Grand Axe-Bearer.
Jiǎn (柬), Prince of Nányáng (南陽), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qín (秦).
Wěi (瑋), Prince of Shǐpíng (始平), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Chǔ (楚).
Yǔn (允), Prince of Púyáng (濮陽), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Huáinán (淮南).
All were granted temporary credentials and enfeoffed in their states,
each commanding the military affairs of a方 (fāng) province.
The imperial prince was established as Prince of Chángshā (長沙).
Yǐng (穎) was established as Prince of Chéngdū (成都).
Yàn (晏) was established as Prince of Wú (吳).
Chì (熾) was established as Prince of Yùzhāng (豫章).
Yǎn (演) was established as Prince of Dài (代).
The imperial grandson Yù (遹) was established as Prince of Guǎnglíng (廣陵).
Dí (迪), son of the Prince of Púyáng (濮陽), was established as Prince of Hàn (漢).
Yí (儀), son of the Prince of Shǐpíng (始平), was established as Prince of Pílíng (毗陵).
Yàng (羕), second son of the Prince of Rǔnán (汝南), was established as Duke of Xīyáng (西陽).
Chàng (暢), Prince of Fúfēng (扶風), was transferred to be Prince of Shùnyáng (順陽).
Xīn (歆), younger brother of Chàng (暢), was established as Duke of Xīnyě (新野).
Dàn (澹), younger brother of Jìn (覲), Prince of Lángyá (琅邪), was established as Duke of Dōngwǔ (東武).
Yáo (繇) was established as Duke of Dōng'ān (東安).
Cuǐ (漼) was established as Duke of Guǎnglíng (廣陵).
Juǎn (卷) was established as Duke of Dōngguǎn (東莞).
The titles of the prime ministers of the various princely states were changed to Intendants.
On the day Gēngyín (庚寅) in the twelfth month,
〔三九〕the beam of the Grand Ancestral Temple broke.
In this year,
more than thirty distant states of the Eastern Yi and more than twenty states of the Southwest Yi came to offer tribute.
One hundred thousand men and women of the barbarian Xīkē (奚軻) surrendered.
In the first month, spring of the first year of Tàixī (太熙), on the day Xīnyǒu (辛酉), the first day of the month,
the reign title was changed.
On the day Jǐsì (己sì),
Wáng Hún (王渾), Minister of the Left, was appointed Minister over the Masses.
Wèi Guàn (衞瓘), Minister of Works, was appointed Grand Tutor.
On the day Xīnchǒu (辛丑) in the second month,
seven states of the Eastern Yi paid tribute.
Jìn (覲), Prince of Lángyá (琅邪), passed away.
On the day Jiǎzǐ (甲zǐ) in the third month,
Shí Jiàn (石鑒), Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Right, was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Xīnchǒu (辛丑) in the fourth month, summer,

Yáng Jùn (楊駿), Imperial Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Grand Commandant, Grand Commander of All Military Forces within and without the Capital, and Supervisor of the Affairs of the Secretariat.
On the day Jǐyǒu (己yǒu),
the Emperor passed away in Hánzhāng (含章) Hall.
He was fifty-five years old.
He was buried in Jùnyáng (峻陽) Mausoleum,
and his temple name was Shìzǔ (世祖).
Dì’s yǔliàng was magnanimous and generous;
in everything he did, he always aimed for benevolence and forgiveness.
He accepted upright counsel
without ever showing displeasure to anyone.
He was discerning and skilled in strategy,
capable of making crucial decisions,
and thus was able to pacify the myriad states
and bring tranquility to the four quarters.
Following the extravagance and corruption of the Wèi dynasty,
the common people longed for the ancient virtues.
So, he encouraged them with reverence and frugality,
and cultivated in them moderation of desires.
Officials once reported that the blue silk halter of the imperial oxen had snapped.
An imperial decree ordered that it be replaced with blue hemp.
When holding court, he was lenient and generous,
and his laws and regulations were consistent.
After Gāoyáng Xǔ Yǔn had been killed by Wén Dì,
Yǔn’s son, Qí, became Tàichángchéng.
When Dì was about to perform a ceremony at the Tàimiào,
the court deliberated, arguing that Qí came from a family that had suffered harm,
and they did not wish him to be close to the emperor.
They requested that he be sent out to serve as Zhǎngshǐ.
Dì then recalled Yǔn’s long-held reputation,
praised Qí’s talent,
and promoted him to Cíbùláng.
Contemporary opinion lauded his broad-mindedness.
After the conquest of Wú,
the realm was at peace,
and he gradually grew lax in governance
and indulged in excursions and banquets.
He favored his empress’s relatives,
and his intimate nobles wielded power.
Old retainers were not given sole appointments,
and established regulations were disregarded and abolished.
Requests and entreaties became common practice.
By his later years,
he knew that Huì Dì was incapable of bearing the burden of rule,
but he relied on the sagacity of the imperial grandson.
Thus, he had no intention of deposing him.
He also worried that since the grandson was not born of Jiǎ Hòu,
he would eventually face danger and ruin.
Therefore, he conspired with his trusted confidants about the succession.
Many suggestions were put forward,
and for a long time, no decision was made.
Eventually, Wáng Yòu’s plan was adopted:
Qín Wáng Jiǎn, the empress’s younger brother and the crown prince’s mother’s brother, was dispatched to oversee Guānzhōng,
while Chǔ Wáng Wěi and Huáinán Wáng Yǔn were sent to guard crucial strategic points
to strengthen the imperial house.
Fearing pressure from the Yáng clan,
he further appointed Yòu as Běijūnzhōnghóu
to command the imperial guards.
Later, he fell ill and lingered on,
until he was critically ill.
The founding heroes who assisted him in establishing the dynasty
had all passed away earlier.
The assembled officials were bewildered,
and had no course of action.
When Dì showed a slight improvement,
an imperial edict was issued appointing Rǔnán Wáng Liàng to assist in government.
It also intended to have several famous young court officials assist him,
but Yáng Jùn secretly withheld the decree.
Dì soon relapsed into confusion.
Empress Yáng immediately issued an edict appointing Jùn to assist in government
and urged Liàng to set out.
Dì soon had a brief moment of lucidity
and asked if Rǔnán Wáng had arrived,
intending to see him
and entrust matters to him.
Those around him replied that he had not yet arrived.
Dì then became critically ill again.
The chaos in the central court
truly began here.
A decree states: Wǔ Huáng inherited the foundation,
and was greatly entrusted with the mandate of Heaven.
He wielded the imperial power and governed the realm,
spreading his transforming influence and guiding the people.
He replaced hardship with ease,
and chaos with order.
He abolished the tribute of silk and fine fabrics,
and removed the embellishments of carvings.
He curbed extravagant customs to encourage frugality,
and halted corrupt trends to restore simple honesty.
He genuinely appreciated direct speech,
and carefully selected and promoted talent.
Liú Yì and Péi Kǎi were tolerated for their straightforwardness,
and Jī Sháo and Xǔ Qí were not discarded despite being from the families of his enemies.
He governed people with benevolence,
and gained the support of the masses through his leniency.
His grand strategy and magnanimity
were truly those of an emperor.
At that time, the people were harmonious and customs peaceful,
families were prosperous and people content.
He diligently cultivated military prowess,
and desired to expand the frontiers.
He made divine calculations from the depths of his heart,
and decisively executed grand strategies against prevailing opinions.
Mǎ Lóng campaigned in the west,
Wáng Jùn campaigned in the south.
The armies did not linger long,
the Xūn Lǔ vanished without a trace.
Without bloody battle,
Yáng and Yuè became desolate ruins.
He opened what previous generations had not opened,
and subjugated what former kings had not subjugated.
Auspicious signs appeared,
and moral education was solemn and clear.
The work of Heaven and man was accomplished;
the imperial enterprise was great.
Although he declined the Fēng and Shàn rites,
his heart of arrogance and complacency
arose from this.
Seeing the vastness of his territory,
he believed it would be secure for ten thousand generations;
observing the peace of the realm,
he believed it would be permanently ordered for a thousand years.
He did not know that by dwelling in vastness and contemplating narrowness,
vastness could be long-lasting;
and by residing in order and forgetting danger,
order would not be permanent.
Furthermore, he made improper choices in establishing his successor,
and entrusted power to the wrong people.
His intention was to achieve lasting peace,
but his actions foreshadowed disaster and chaos.
This is like someone wishing to go to Yuè
pointing to the desert as their path,
or someone wanting to climb a mountain
crossing by boat to find their way.
The destination becomes more distant,
the desired outcome increasingly difficult.
North and south are entirely different,
high and low are opposite.
To achieve their goal,
would it not be difficult?
Moreover, he had a newly established, easily disturbed foundation,
yet lacked long-term security and the foresight to prevent removal.
Thus, Jiǎ Chōng, a treacherous scoundrel,
harbored wicked ambitions and wielded power;
Yáng Jùn, a jackal and wolf,
nurtured sinister intentions and monopolized regency.
When the imperial carriage made its late departure (the emperor died),
and the mourning period was not yet complete,
the loyal frontier princes turned against their kin and became estranged,
their converging armies vying to destroy their own roots.
The pillars of the state turned their loyalty into deceit,
gathering followers and asserting their authority.
In fewer than a few years,
the fundamental order was plunged into great chaos,
the whole realm was in turmoil,
and the imperial ancestral temple was displaced.
The imperial Way and royal policies
reverted to the customs of tattooed barbarians;
the divine land and its registered population
became a land of uncivilized people with unbound hair.
Abandoning what was great to empower others,
and concealing what was minor to rely on himself,
he became a laughingstock to the world.
What was the reason for this?
It was truly due to a lack of prudence at the beginning,
which led to suffering in the end.
Moreover, a wise father knows his son;
a discerning ruler knows his ministers.
If a son is unworthy, the family perishes;
if a minister is disloyal, the state falls into chaos.
A chaotic state cannot be secure;
a ruined family cannot be preserved whole.
Therefore, the gentleman prevents evil at its beginning,
and the sage checks it at its inception.
Yet Shìzǔ was deluded by Xún Xù’s treacherous schemes,
and confused by Wáng Hún’s deceitful plans.
His mind was repeatedly swayed by popular opinion,
and his decisions were not based on his own designs.
Yuánhǎi should have been eliminated but was not,
which ultimately led to the disruption of the central land.
Huì Dì could have been deposed but was not,
which eventually caused the overthrow of the great foundation.
Indeed, saving one person is a minor virtue;
rescuing the entire realm is a major achievement.
Abandoning one son is a small act of cruelty;
securing the state and its altars is a great act of filial piety.
How much more so to inherit an enterprise built over three generations,
only to allow two undeserving successors to destroy it?
This is what is called valuing minor virtues over major achievements,
and fearing small cruelties while neglecting great filial piety.
Is the Way of the sages and worthies truly like this?
Although he started well,
he deviated from a good end in his later years.
Thus, diligent historians cannot help but feel sorrow and indignation.
Jiàokāojì
Dìjì Dìsì Huì Dì
Xiàohuì Huángdì, given name Zhōng,
courtesy name Zhèngdù,
was Wǔ Dì’s second son.
In the third year of Tàishǐ,
he was established as the crown prince,
at that time nine years old.
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu, of the first year of Tàixī,
Emperor Wǔ died.
On this day,
the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne,
granted a general amnesty,
and changed the era name to Yǒngxī.
He honored Empress Yáng as the Empress Dowager,
and established his consort, Lady Jiǎ, as Empress.
In the summer, in the fifth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Emperor Wǔ was buried at Jùnyáng Líng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
all officials in the empire were promoted one rank,
those involved in the funeral affairs two ranks.
Rent and taxes were remitted for one year,
and all officials of 2,000 shí or above were enfeoffed as Marquis within the Pass (Guānzhōng Hóu).
Tàiwèi Yáng Jùn was appointed Tàifù,
to assist in governing.
In the autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Guǎngl陵 Wáng Yù was established as Crown Prince.
Zhōngshū Jiān Hé Shào was appointed Crown Prince's Tàishī,
Lìbù Shàngshū Wáng Róng as Crown Prince's Tàifù,
and Wèijiāngjūn Yáng Jì as Crown Prince's Tàibǎo.
Nánzhōnglángjiāng Shí Chóng, Shèshēng Xiàowèi Hú Yì, Chángshuǐ Xiàowèi Zhào Jùn, and Yángliè Jiāngjūn Zhào Huān were dispatched with garrison troops to four directions.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Sīkōng Shí Jiàn was appointed Tàiwèi,
and former Zhènī Xī Jiāngjūn, Lǒngxī Wáng Tàì, was appointed Sīkōng.
In the spring, in the first month, on the day Yǐyǒu, the first day of the month, of the first year of Yǒngpíng,
the Emperor held court,
but no music was played.
An imperial edict stated:
"I have unfortunately encountered misfortune since my youth,
immersed in sorrow and sickness.
Relying on the lingering spirits of my ancestors,
and the loyal and virtuous prime ministers,
I, a humble person, have been entrusted to rule over the multitude of lords.
Ignorant of the Great Way,
and unclear in instruction,
I am apprehensive and fearful,
vigilant as if facing a severe illness.
At the time of my profound grief,
the three chief ministers, my limbs and backbone,
considering the importance of the altars of soil and grain,
followed the ancient ritual of 'aiding the wing-chamber' [i.e., enthroning the new emperor],
still wishing to perpetually uphold the system of the late Emperor,
hence the designation of Yǒngxī.
However, days and months have passed,
and the new year has arrived.
To initiate a new era and change the record [of years]
is an old practice of ritual.
Therefore, the second year of Yǒngxī shall be changed to the first year of Yǒngpíng."
Another edict stipulated that imperial relatives and all officials were not permitted to visit the mausoleum.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Crown Prince came of age (guàn).
On the day Dīngwèi,
he made an appearance at the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In the second month, on the day Jiǎyín,
kings, dukes, and officials below them were granted silk in varying amounts.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Zhènnán Jiāngjūn Chǔ Wáng Wěi and Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn Huáinán Wáng Yǔn came to court.
On the day Wùyín,
the office of Bìshū Jiān was re-established.
In the third month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Tàifù Yáng Jùn was executed.
His brother Wèijiāngjūn Yáng Yáo,
Crown Prince Tàibǎo Jì,
Zhōnghùjūn Zhāng Shào,
Sǎnjì Chángshì Duàn Guǎng and Yáng Miǎo,
Zuǒ Jiāngjūn Liú Yù,
Hénán Yǐn Lǐ Bīn,
Zhōngshū Lìng Jiǎng Jùn,
Dōngyí Xiàowèi Wén Shú,
and Shàngshū Wǔ Mào
all had their three kindreds exterminated.
On the day Rénchén,
a general amnesty was granted,
and the era name was changed.
Empress Jiǎ falsely issued an edict to depose the Empress Dowager as a commoner,
and she was exiled to Jīnyōng Chéng.
This was announced to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.
The Empress Dowager's mother, Lady Páng, was executed.
On the day Rényín,
Dàsīmǎ, Rǔnán Wáng Liàng, was summoned to be Tàizǎi,
to assist in governing with Tàibǎo Wèi Guàn.
Qín Wáng Jiǎn was appointed Dàjiāngjūn,
Dōngpíng Wáng Máo as Fǔjūn Dàjiāngjūn,
Zhènnán Jiāngjūn, Chǔ Wáng Wěi as Wèijiāngjūn,
leading the Beìjūn Zhōnghòu,
Xiàpí Wáng Huǎng as Shàngshū Lìng,
and Dōng'ān Gōng Yáo as Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè,
and promoted to be Dōng'ān Wáng.
One thousand eighty-one people were appointed as Dūjiāng Hóu.
On the day Gēngxū,
Dōng'ān Wáng Yáo and Dōngpíng Wáng Máo were dismissed,
and Yáo was exiled to Dàifāng.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Zhēngdōng Jiāngjūn, Liáng Wáng Róng, was appointed Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn, and Dūdū Guānxī Zhūjūnshì.
Crown Prince Shǎofù Ruǎn Tǎn was appointed Píngdōng Jiāngjūn, and Jiān Qīng Xú Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì.
On the day Jǐsì,
Crown Prince Tàifù Wáng Róng was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Pílíng Wáng Guǐ died.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the household taxes of silk floss and plain silk throughout the empire were abolished.
Filial and fraternal individuals, those of old age, widows, widowers, orphans, those without children, and diligent farmers were granted silk,
three bolts per person.
In the sixth month,
Empress Jiǎ falsely issued an edict making Chǔ Wáng Wěi kill Tàizǎi, Rǔnán Wáng Liàng,
and Tàibǎo, Zīyáng Gōng Wèi Guàn.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
because Wěi had presumptuously harmed Liàng and Guàn,
he was executed.
A partial amnesty was granted in Luòyáng.
Guǎngl陵 Wáng Shī Liú Shí was appointed Crown Prince Tàibǎo,
and Sīkōng, Lǒngxī Wáng Tàì, oversaw the affairs of the Secretariat (Lù Shàngshū Shì).
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
ten commanderies from Yángzhōu and Jīngzhōu were separated to form Jiāngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Zhào Wáng Lún was appointed Zhēngdōng Jiāngjūn, and Dūdū Xú Yǎn Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì;
Héjiān Wáng Yōng as Běizhōnglángjiāng,
to garrison Yè;
and Crown Prince Tàishī Hé Shào as Dūdū Yùzhōu Zhūjūnshì,
to garrison Xǔchāng.
Chángshā Wáng was relocated and enfeoffed as Chángshān Wáng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Xīyáng Gōng Yàng was promoted in noble rank to Wáng.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Lǒngxī Shìzǐ Yuè was established as Dōnghǎi Wáng.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Dàjiāngjūn, Qín Wáng Jiǎn, died.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn, Liáng Wáng Róng, was summoned to be Wèijiāngjūn, overseeing the affairs of the Secretariat.
Zhào Wáng Lún was appointed Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn, and Dūdū Yōng Liáng Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì.
In the winter, in the twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In this year,
seventeen states of the Eastern Yi and twenty-four tribes of the Southern Yi all came to the Xiàowèi to pledge allegiance.
In the spring, in the second month, on the day Jǐyǒu, of the second year,
Empress Jiǎ assassinated the Empress Dowager in Jīnyōng Chéng.
In the autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
a general amnesty was granted.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Zhōngshān Wáng Dān died.
In the winter, in the eleventh month,
there was a great plague.
In this year,
hail fell in Pèiguó,
damaging the wheat.
In the summer, in the fourth month, of the third year,
hail fell in Xíngyáng.
In the sixth month,
hail fell in Hóngnóng Jùn,
three chí deep.
In the winter, in the tenth month,
Tàiyuán Wáng Hóng died.
In the spring, in the first month, on the day Dīngyǒu, the first day of the month, of the fourth year,
Shìzhōng, Tàiwèi, Ānchāng Gōng Shí Jiàn died.
In the summer, in the fifth month,
a mountain shifted in Shǔjùn.
In Huáinán, Shòuchūn, there was a great flood.
Mountains collapsed and the ground sank,
destroying city offices and people's houses.
The Xiōngnú Hǎo Sàn rebelled,
attacking Shàngdǎng,
and killed the chief officials.
In the sixth month,
the ground in Shòuchūn shook violently,
killing over twenty families.
In Shàngyōng Jùn, a mountain collapsed,
killing over twenty people.
In the autumn, in the eighth month,
Hǎo Sàn led his followers to surrender,
but Fēngyì Dūwèi killed him.
In Shànggǔ Jūyōng and Shàngyōng, the ground cracked and sank,
and spring water gushed out,
causing some deaths.
There was a great famine.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
an amnesty was granted to regions affected by natural disasters.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
a straight-tailed comet (wǎngshǐ) appeared in the northeast and extended across the sky.
In this year,
there were eight earthquakes in the capital and various commanderies and states.
In the summer, in the fourth month, of the fifth year,
a comet was seen in the west,
blazing near Kuí (Andromeda),
and reaching Xuānyuán (Leo).
In the sixth month,
there was an earthquake in Jīnchéng.
Hail fell in Dōnghǎi,
five cùn deep.
In the autumn, in the seventh month,
a fierce storm occurred in Xiàpí,
destroying houses.
In the ninth month,
great winds occurred in Yànmén, Xīnxīng, Tàiyuán, and Shàngdǎng,
damaging crops.
In winter, tenth month,
the military arsenal caught fire,
burning treasures of successive generations.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐng-xū* day,
a new military arsenal was built,
and weapons were largely refurbished.
In Dānyáng, there was a hailstorm.
A rock was born in Yínián Lǐ of the capital.
This year,
there were great floods in the six provinces of Jīng, Yáng, Yǎn, Yù, Qīng, and Xú.
An imperial edict ordered censors to tour the affected areas and provide relief loans.
In the sixth year, in spring, first month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Sīkōng, the King of Xiàpī, Huǎng, passed away.
Zhāng Huà, the Zhongshū Jiān, was appointed Sīkōng.
Tàiwèi, the King of Lǒngxī, Tàiz, was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
Wèi Jiāngjūn, the King of Liáng, Róng, was appointed Tàizǐ Tàibǎo.
On the *dīng-chǒu* day,
there was an earthquake.
In the third month,
frost fell in Dōnghǎi,
damaging mulberry trees and wheat.
In Lǚ Xiàn of Péngchéng, blood flowed
for over a hundred paces east and west.
In summer, fourth month,
there was a great wind.
In the fifth month,
there were great floods in Jīng and Yáng provinces.
Hǎo Sǎn's younger brother Dù Yuán of the Xiōngnú, along with the Mǎlán Qiāng of Fēngyì and Běidì, and the Lúshuǐ Hú, rebelled,
attacking Běidì.
The Grand Administrator Zhāng Sǔn died there.
The Grand Administrator of Fēngyì, Ōuyáng Jiàn, fought against Dù Yuán,
and Jiàn was defeated.
Zhēng Xī Dà Jiāngjūn, the King of Zhào, Lún, was recalled and made Chēqí Jiāngjūn.
Tàizǐ Tàibǎo, the King of Liáng, Róng, was appointed Zhēng Xī Dà Jiāngjūn and Dūdū Yōng Liáng Èr Zhōu Zhū Jūnshì,
to guard Guānzhōng.
In autumn, eighth month,
the Inspector of Yōng Province, Xiè Xì, was again defeated by Dù Yuán.
The Dī and Qiāng of Qín and Yōng all rebelled,
proclaiming the Dī chieftain Qí Wànnián as emperor,
and besieged Jīngyáng.
In winter, tenth month, on the *yǐ-wèi* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Yōng and Liáng provinces.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐng-zǐ* day,
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Xiàhóu Jùn and
Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn Zhōu Chǔ were dispatched to attack Wànnián.
The King of Liáng, Róng, encamped at Hǎozhì.
Guānzhōng suffered from famine,
and a great plague.
In the seventh year, in spring, first month, on the *guǐ-chǒu* day,
Zhōu Chǔ fought Qí Wànnián at Liùmò.
The imperial army was defeated,
and Chǔ died there.
In summer, fifth month,
there was a hailstorm in Lǔguó.
In autumn, seventh month,
there was a plague in Yōng and Liáng provinces.
There was a great drought,
frost fell,
killing the autumn crops.
Guānzhōng suffered from famine,
a *hú* of rice cost ten thousand cash.
An imperial edict permitted the sale of family members.
On the *dīng-chǒu* day,
Sītú, the Duke of Jīnglíng, Wáng Hún, passed away.
In the ninth month,
Shàngshū Yòu Púyè Wáng Róng was appointed Sītú,
and Tàizǐ Tàishī Hé Shào was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
In the eighth year, in spring, first month, on the *bǐng-chén* day,
there was an earthquake.
An imperial edict ordered granaries to be opened
to provide relief to the starving people of Yōng Province.
In the third month, on the *rén-xū* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In summer, fifth month,
the stone at Jiāoméi broke into two.
In autumn, ninth month,
there were great floods in the five provinces of Jīng, Yù, Yáng, Xú, and Jì.
Yōng Province had a good harvest.
In the ninth year, in spring, first month,
Zuǒ Jīnú Jiāngjūn Mèng Guān attacked the Dī,
fighting at Zhōngtíng,
and greatly defeated them,
capturing Qí Wànnián.
Zhēng Xī Dà Jiāngjūn, the King of Liáng, Róng, was summoned to record Shàngshū affairs.
Běi Zhōngláng Jiāng, the King of Héjiān, Yóng, was appointed Zhèn Xī Jiāngjūn,
to guard Guānzhōng;
the King of Chéngdū, Yǐng, was appointed Zhèn Běi Dà Jiāngjūn,
to guard Yè.
In summer, fourth month,
Zhāng Chéngjī and others from Yè spread seditious rumors and appointed officials,
gathering several thousand followers.
The commanderies and counties arrested them,
and they were all executed.
In the sixth month, on the *wù-xū* day,
Tàiwèi, the King of Lǒngxī, Tài, passed away.
In autumn, eighth month,
Shàngshū Péi Wěi was appointed Shàngshū Púyè.
In winter, eleventh month, on the first day, *jiǎ-zǐ*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the capital, there was a great wind,
destroying houses and breaking trees.
In the twelfth month, on the *rén-xū* day,
Crown Prince Yù was deposed as a commoner,
and his three sons were imprisoned in Jīnyǒng Chéng.
The Crown Prince's mother, Lady Xiè, was killed.
In the first year of Yǒngkāng, in spring, first month, on the first day, *guǐ-hài*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the era name was changed.
On the *jǐ-mǎo* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *bǐng-zǐ* day,
the Imperial Grandson Zàng died.
In the second month, on the *dīng-yǒu* day,
there was a great wind,
flying sand and uprooting trees.
In the third month,
blood rained in Wèishì,
and an ominous star appeared in the south.
On the *guǐ-wèi* day,
Empress Jiǎ, by forged imperial edict, murdered the commoner Yù in Xǔchāng.
In summer, fourth month, on the *xīn-mǎo* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *guǐ-sì* day,
the King of Liáng, Róng, and the King of Zhào, Lún, by forged imperial edict, deposed Empress Jiǎ as a commoner.
Sīkōng Zhāng Huà and Shàngshū Púyè Péi Wěi were both murdered,
and Shìzhōng Jiǎ Mì and dozens of his partisans were all executed.
On the *jiǎ-wǔ* day,
Lún, by forged imperial edict, proclaimed a general amnesty,
appointing himself Xiàngguó and Dūdū Zhōng Wài Zhū Jūn,
following the precedent of Xuān Wén's assistance to Wèi.
The former Crown Prince's position was posthumously restored.
On the *dīng-yǒu* day,
the King of Liáng, Róng, was appointed Tàizǎi.
Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū Hé Shào was appointed Sītú.
Yòu Guānglù Dàfū Liú Shí was appointed Sīkōng.
The King of Huáinán, Yǔn, was appointed Piàojí Jiāngjūn.
On the *jǐ-hài* day,
the King of Zhào, Lún, by forged imperial edict, murdered the commoner Jiǎ in Jīnyǒng Chéng.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐ-sì* day,
Imperial Grandson Zàng was established as Imperial Grand Prince,
and Shàng as the King of Xiāngyáng.
In the sixth month, on the *rén-yín* day,
Crown Prince Mǐnhuái was buried at Xiǎnpíng Líng.
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn, the King of Qīnghé, Xiá, passed away.
On the *guǐ-mǎo* day,
the marker of Chóngyáng Líng was shaken.
In autumn, eighth month,
the King of Huáinán, Yǔn, raised an army to attack the King of Zhào, Lún,
but did not succeed.
Yǔn and his two sons, King of Qín Yù and King of Hàn Dí, were all murdered.
A partial amnesty was granted to Luòyáng.
Píng Dōng Jiāngjūn, the King of Péngchéng, Zhí, passed away.
The King of Wú, Yàn, was re-enfeoffed as the King of Bīntú Xiàn.
The King of Qí, Jiǒng, was appointed Píng Dōng Jiāngjūn,
to guard Xǔchāng;
Guānglù Dàfū Chén Zhǔn was appointed Tàiwèi and Lù Shàngshū Shì.
In the ninth month,
Sītú was changed to Chéngxiàng,
and the King of Liáng, Róng, was appointed to the post.
In winter, tenth month,
yellow fog filled the four directions.
In the eleventh month, on the *wù-wǔ* day,
a great wind carried sand and stones,
stopping only after six days.
On the *jiǎ-zǐ* day,
Empress Yáng was established.
A general amnesty was proclaimed,
and a grand feast for three days.
In the twelfth month,
a comet appeared in the east.
The Inspector of Yì Province, Zhào Xìn, and the refugee Lǐ Xiáng from Luèyáng murdered the Grand Administrator of Chéngdū Gěng Shèng,
the Grand Administrator of Jiànwéi Lǐ Mì, the Grand Administrator of Wénshān Huò Gù, and the Colonel of Xīyí Chén Zǒng,
and revolted, occupying Chéngdū.
In the first year of Yǒngníng, in spring, first month, on the *yǐ-chǒu* day,
the King of Zhào, Lún, usurped the imperial throne.
On the *bǐng-yín* day,
the Emperor was moved to Jīnyǒng Chéng,
and styled Tàishàng Huáng.
Jīnyǒng was renamed Yǒngchāng Gōng.
Imperial Grand Prince Zàng was deposed as the King of Púyáng.
The five planets traversed the sky,
moving irregularly.
On the *guǐ-yǒu* day,
Lún murdered the King of Púyáng, Zàng.
The refugee Lǐ Tè from Luèyáng killed Zhào Xìn,
and sent his head to the capital.
In the third month,
General Who Pacifies the East, Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏), raised an army to punish Lún (倫).
〔一一〕He sent a proclamation to the various prefectures and commanderies,
and encamped at Yángzhái (陽翟).
General Who Conquers the North, Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎),
General Who Conquers the West, Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒),
Chángshān Wáng (常山王),
Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Yì (豫州刺史李毅),
〔一二〕Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Yàn (兗州刺史王彥),
Southern Central Protector, Xīnyě Gōng Xīn (新野公歆),
all raised armies in response,
numbering several hundred thousand men.
Lún (倫) dispatched his generals Lǘ Hé (閭和) out of Yīquē (伊闕),
Zhāng Hóng (張泓) and Sūn Fǔ (孫輔) out of Èbǎn (堮坂) to resist Jiǒng (冏),
and Sūn Huì (孫會), Shì Yī (士猗), and Xǔ Chāo (許超) out of Huángqiáo (黃橋) to resist Yǐng (穎).
When Yǐng’s (穎) generals Zhào Xiāng (趙驤) and Shí Chāo (石超) fought at Jùshuǐ (湨水),
Huì (會) and the others were greatly defeated,
abandoned their army, and fled.
In the intercalary month, on the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer, the fourth month,
the Jupiter star was seen in daytime.
Jiǒng’s (冏) generals Hé Xù (何勖) and Lú Bō (盧播) attacked Zhāng Hóng (張泓) at Yángzhái (陽翟),
greatly defeating him,
and beheading Sūn Fǔ (孫輔) and others.
On the *xīnyǒu* (辛酉) day,
Left Guard General Wáng Yú (王輿), along with Shàngshū (尚書) and Huáilíng Wáng Cuǐ (淮陵王漼), led troops into the palace,
captured Lún’s (倫) partisans Sūn Xiù (孫秀), Sūn Huì (孫會), Xǔ Chāo (許超), Shì Yī (士猗), Luò Xiū (駱休), etc.,
and executed them all.
They pursued Lún (倫) back to his residence.
On that same day, the imperial carriage was restored.
The assembled officials kowtowed and apologized for their transgressions.
The Emperor said,
“This is not the fault of you, my lords.”
On the *guǐhài* (癸亥) day,
an imperial edict stated:
“I, being without virtue,
have inherited the imperial lineage.
Far away, I could not glorify the great enterprise and
pacify the four directions;
nearby, I could not clarify the punishments and awe,
or suppress treachery and villainy,
to the extent that the rebellious minister Sūn Xiù (孫秀) dared to unleash his evil cruelty,
spying on the royal house,
and thus serving Zhào Wáng Lún (趙王倫) to usurp the heavenly throne.
General-in-Chief Who Guards the East, Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏),
General Who Conquers the North, Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎),
General Who Conquers the West, Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒),
all with their illustrious virtue and close kinship,
their loyal strategies clearly demonstrated,
first established a great plan
to rescue the nation from calamity.
Shàngshū Cuǐ (漼) jointly formulated the great scheme.
Left Guard General Wáng Yú (王輿), along with the various high officials,
collaborated in the strategies,
personally commanded their own camps,
and executed Xiù (秀) and his two sons.
The former Zhào Wáng Lún (趙王倫) was misled by Xiù (秀).
He and his sons have already gone to Jīnyōng (金墉) to welcome me from my confinement in the palace,
and turned the chariot towards Chānghé (閶闔).
How can I alone enjoy this good fortune?
The imperial ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain truly relied on them.”
Thereupon, a great amnesty was declared,
the reign era was changed,
orphans and widows were granted five *hú* of grain,
and there was a great feast for five days.
Zhào Wáng Lún (趙王倫), Yìyáng Wáng Wēi (義陽王威), Jiǔmén Hóu Zhì (九門侯質) and others, as well as Lún’s (倫) partisans, were executed.
In the fifth month,
Xiāngyáng Wáng Shàng (襄陽王尚) was made Imperial Grandson.
In the sixth month, on the *wùchén* (戊辰) day,
a great amnesty was declared,
and officials were promoted two grades.
Bīntú Wáng Yàn (賓徒王晏) was re-enfeoffed as Wú Wáng (吳王).
On the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
Dōnglái Wáng Ruí (東萊王蕤) and Left Guard General Wáng Yú (王輿) plotted to depose Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏).
The plot was exposed,
Ruí (蕤) was deposed as a commoner,
Yú (輿) was executed,
and his three ancestral clans were exterminated.
On the *jiǎxū* (甲戌) day,
Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏) was made Grand Minister of War and Overall Commander of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Capital,
Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎) was made Grand General and Director of the Department of State Affairs,
and Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒) was made Grand Commandant.
The position of Chancellor was abolished,
