and the office of Minister of Education was re-established.
On the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day,
Liáng Wáng Róng (梁王肜) was made Grand Tutor,
and concurrently Minister of Education.
Qí Wáng Jiǒng’s (齊王冏) meritorious officials Gě Yú (葛旟) was enfeoffed as Mǒupíng Gōng (牟平公),
Lù Jì (路季) as Xiǎohuáng Gōng (小黃公),
〔一三〕Wèi Yì (衞毅) as Píngyīn Gōng (平陰公),
Liú Zhēn (劉真) as Ānxiāng Gōng (安鄉公),
and Hán Tài (韓泰) as Fēngqiū Gōng (封丘公).
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* (甲午) day,
Wú Wáng Yàn’s (吳王晏) son Guó (國) was made Hàn Wáng (漢王).
〔一四〕Chángshān Wáng (常山王) was re-enfeoffed as Chángshā Wáng (長沙王).
In the eighth month,
a great amnesty was declared.
On the *wùchén* (戊辰) day,
those exiled to the borders were pardoned.
Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Luó Shàng (益州刺史羅尚) attacked the Qiāng (羌),
and defeated them.
On the *jǐsì* (己巳) day,
Nánpíng Wáng Xiáng (南平王祥) was transferred and made Yídū Wáng (宜都王).
Xiàpí Wáng Wěi (下邳王韡) died.
〔一五〕Dōngpíng Wáng Máo (東平王楙) was made General Who Pacifies the East,
〔一六〕and Overall Commander of All Military Affairs in Xúzhōu (徐州).
In the ninth month,
Dōng'ān Wáng Yáo (東安王繇) was posthumously restored to his title.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
〔一七〕Chǔ Wáng Wěi’s (楚王瑋) son Fàn (範) was enfeoffed as Xiāngyáng Wáng (襄陽王).
In winter, the tenth month,
the refugee Lǐ Tè (李特) rebelled in Shǔ (蜀).
In the twelfth month,
Sīkōng Hé Shào (司空何劭) died.
〔一八〕Qí Wáng Jiǒng’s (齊王冏) son Bīng (冰) was enfeoffed as Lè'ān Wáng (樂安王),
Yīng (英) as Jìyáng Wáng (濟陽王),
and Chāo (超) as Huáinán Wáng (淮南王).
In this year,
twelve commanderies and states experienced drought, and six experienced locust infestations.
In the first year of Tàiyán (太安), spring, the first month, on the *gēngzǐ* (庚子) day,
General Who Guards the East, Qiáo Wáng Suí (譙王隨), died.
In the third month, on the *guǐmǎo* (癸卯) day,
an amnesty was granted to the four prefectures of Sī (司), Jì (冀), Yǎn (兗), and Yù (豫).
Imperial Grandson Shàng (尚) died.
In summer, the fourth month,
a comet was seen in daytime.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
Court Attendant, Grand Tutor, concurrently Minister of Education, Liáng Wáng Róng (梁王肜), died.
Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Liú Shí (劉寔) was made Grand Mentor.
Grand Commandant Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒) dispatched his general Yá Bó (衙博) to attack Lǐ Tè (李特) in Shǔ (蜀),
but was defeated by Tè (特).
Tè (特) then captured Zǐtóng (梓潼) and Bāxī (巴西),
killed Guǎnghàn Tàishǒu Zhāng Wēi (廣漢太守張微),
and proclaimed himself Grand General.
〔一九〕On the *guǐmǎo* (癸卯) day,
Qīnghé Wáng Xiá’s (清河王遐) son Tán (覃) was made Imperial Heir,
orphans and widows were granted silk,
and there was a great feast for five days.
Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏) was made Grand Preceptor,
and Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越) was made Minister of Works.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the four prefectures of Yǎn (兗), Yù (豫), Xú (徐), and Jì (冀) suffered great floods.
In winter, the tenth month,
there was an earthquake.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day,
Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒) memorialized that Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏) was coveting the imperial regalia
and harbored intentions of disloyalty towards the ruler.
He, along with Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎), Xīnyě Wáng Xīn (新野王歆), and Fányáng Wáng Xiāo (范陽王虓), assembled at Luòyáng (洛陽),
requesting to depose Jiǒng (冏) and send him back to his residence.
Chángshā Wáng (長沙王) took the imperial carriage and encamped at the Nánzhǐchēmén (南止車門),
attacked Jiǒng (冏),
killed him,
imprisoned all his sons in Jīnyōng Chéng (金墉城),
and deposed Jiǒng’s (冏) younger brother Běihǎi Wáng Shí (北海王寔).
A great amnesty was declared,
and the reign era was changed.
Chángshā Wáng (長沙王) was made Grand Commandant and Overall Commander of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Capital.
Dōnglái Wáng Ruí’s (東萊王蕤) son Zhào (炤) was enfeoffed as Qí Wáng (齊王).
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the *jiǎzǐ* (甲子) day, the first day of the lunar month,
〔二一〕pardons were granted for crimes punishable by five years of imprisonment.
In the third month,
Lǐ Tè (李特) attacked and captured Yìzhōu (益州).
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Sòng Dài (荊州刺史宋岱) attacked Tè (特),
beheaded him,
〔二二〕and sent his head to the capital.
In summer, the fourth month,
Tè’s (特) son Xióng (雄) again occupied Yìzhōu (益州).
In the fifth month,
the Yìyáng (義陽) barbarian Zhāng Chāng (張昌) raised an army in revolt,
making Qiū Shěn (丘沈) of Shāndū (山都) their leader,
who changed his surname to Liú (劉)
and falsely proclaimed the reign title Hàn (漢),
establishing the era name Shénfèng (神鳳).
They attacked and captured commanderies and counties.
Nányáng Tàishǒu Liú Bīn (南陽太守劉彬),
General Who Pacifies the South Yáng Yī (羊伊),
and General-in-Chief Who Guards the South, Xīnyě Wáng Xīn (新野王歆), were all killed.
In the sixth month,
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Hóng (荊州刺史劉弘) and others were dispatched to attack Zhāng Chāng (張昌) at Fāngchéng (方城),
but the imperial army was defeated.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Central Secretariat Director Biàn Cuì (卞粹), Court Attendant Féng Sūn (馮蓀), and Hénán Yǐn Lǐ Hán (河南尹李含) and others were disloyal to Chángshā Wáng (長沙王).
He suspected and killed them.
Zhāng Chāng (張昌) captured various commanderies south of the Yangtze.
Wǔlíng Tàishǒu Jiǎ Lóng (武陵太守賈隆), Línglíng Tàishǒu Kǒng Hóng (零陵太守孔紘), Yùzhāng Tàishǒu Yán Jì (豫章太守閻濟), and Wǔchāng Tàishǒu Liú Gēn (武昌太守劉根) were all killed.
Chāng’s (昌) separate commander Shí Bīng (石冰) plundered Yángzhōu (揚州).
Cìshǐ Chén Huī (刺史陳徽) fought him
and was greatly defeated,
and all the commanderies were lost.
Fēng Yún (封雲) from Línhuái (臨淮) raised an army in response,
plundering Xúzhōu (徐州) from Fùlíng (阜陵).
In the eighth month,
Héjiān Wáng Yóng (河間王顒) and Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎) raised armies to attack Chángshā Wáng (長沙王).
The Emperor made him Grand Commander,
to lead an army to resist them.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Liú Hóng and Zhāng Chāng fought at Qīngshuǐ,
and Zhāng Chāng was beheaded.
Yóng dispatched his general Zhāng Fāng,
and Yǐng dispatched his generals Lù Jī, Qiān Xiù, Shí Chāo, and others to press upon the capital.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor proceeded to Shísān Lǐ Qiáo
and sent General Huángfǔ Shāng to resist Fāng at Yíyáng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor moved his army to Xuānwǔ Cháng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
he stayed at Shílóu.
The sky split open,
and there was thunder without clouds.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor stopped at Héqiáo.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Huángfǔ Shāng was defeated by Zhāng Fāng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor's army was at Mángshān.
On the *dīnghài* day,
he proceeded to Yǎnshī.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
he stayed at Dòutián.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yáng Xuánzhī, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs and Marquis of Xìnjìn, died.
〔二三〕The Emperor returned to the east of the city.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the army advanced to Gōushì,
attacked Qiān Xiù,
and routed him.
A general amnesty was declared.
Zhāng Fāng entered the capital city,
burned the Qīngmíng and Kāiyáng gates,
and tens of thousands died.
Shí Chāo pressed the imperial carriage at Gōushì.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *rénkǎ* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
Shí Chāo burned Gōushì,
leaving no imperial furnishings or apparel.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Qiān Xiù and Fànyáng Wáng Xiāo were defeated outside Dōngyáng Mén.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Lù Jī was defeated at Jiànchūn Mén,
Shí Chāo fled,
and his sixteen chief generals, including Jiǎ Chóng, were beheaded.
〔二四〕Their heads were displayed at Tóngtuó Jiē.
Zhāng Fāng retreated and garrisoned at Shísān Lǐ Qiáo.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
a star fell in daylight,
with a sound like thunder.
The imperial army attacked Fāng's camp,
but was unsuccessful.
Fāng broke the Qiānjīn É sluice,
and all the water-powered mills dried up.
Thus, slaves of princes and dukes were enlisted to pound grain by hand to supply the army,
and all men aged thirteen and above, from the first rank downwards, who were not campaigning, were conscripted for service.
Slaves were also enlisted to assist the army,
known as the Four Divisions of Sīmǎ.
Both public and private sectors were in dire straits,
and a *shí* of rice cost ten thousand cash.
The imperial edicts only reached
a single city.
On the night of the *rén'yín* day,
〔二五〕a red *qì* filled the sky,
and there was a faint sound.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè seized Chángshā Wáng,
imprisoned him in Jīnyóng Chéng,
and he was subsequently harmed by Zhāng Fāng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
〔二六〕On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhōu Qǐ, a scholar from Yángzhōu, Wáng Jǔ, former Administrator of Nánpíng, and Gù Mì, former Administrator of Wúxīng, raised an army of righteousness to suppress Shí Bīng.
〔二七〕Bīng retreated,
and from Línhuái, he headed towards Shòuyáng.
General Zhēngdōng Liú Zhǔn dispatched Guǎnglíng Dùzhī Chén Mǐn to attack Bīng.
Lǐ Xióng attacked Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Luó Shàng from Píchéng,
〔二八〕Shàng abandoned the city and fled,
and Xióng took possession of the entire territory of Chéngdū.
Xiānbēi Duàn Wùchén was enfeoffed as Liáoxī Gōng.
In the first month of spring, on the *bǐngwǔ* day of Yǒngxīng元年,
Shàngshū Lìng Lè Guǎng died.
〔二九〕Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng, from Yè, hinted to the Emperor,
so a general amnesty was declared,
and the era name was changed to Yǒng'ān.
The Emperor, pressed by Héjiān Wáng Yóng,
secretly ordered Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Shěn and Qínzhōu Cìshǐ Huángfǔ Chóng to attack him.
Shěn raised an army and attacked Cháng'ān,
but was defeated by Yóng.
Zhāng Fāng extensively plundered Luòzhōng,
and returned to Cháng'ān.
At this time, there was a great famine in the army,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng was appointed Chancellor.
Yǐng dispatched Attendant Counselor Chéng Kuí and others with fifty thousand troops to garrison the twelve city gates.
Those in the palace whom Yǐng found objectionable
were all killed by him,
and he replaced the palace guard with three divisions of soldiers.
In the second month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Empress Yáng Shì was deposed
and imprisoned in Jīnyóng Chéng,
and Crown Prince Tán was demoted back to Qīnghé Wáng.
In the third month,
Chén Mǐn attacked Shí Bīng,
beheaded him,
and the two provinces of Yáng and Xú were pacified.
Héjiān Wáng Yóng submitted a memorial requesting to establish Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng as Imperial Younger Brother.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, being unworthy,
have succeeded to this grand enterprise,
for fifteen years now.
Calamity and rebellion have reached the heavens,
treason and disorder have repeatedly arisen,
even leading to the imprisonment and deposition of the inner palace,
and the ancestral temples being ruined and cut off.
Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng is gentle, benevolent, and harmonious,
and has been able to quell the violent rebellion.
Therefore, let Yǐng be appointed Imperial Younger Brother and Supreme Commander of All Military Affairs, inside and outside,
with his position as Chancellor remaining unchanged."
A general amnesty was declared,
widowers, widows, and the elderly were given three bolts of silk,
and there was a grand feast for five days.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
thieves stole ceremonial vessels from the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Grand Commandant Yóng was made Grand Preceptor,
and Grand Tutor Liú Shí was made Grand Commandant.
In the sixth month,
three new city gates were constructed.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *bǐngshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Right Guard General Chén Zhěn, by imperial edict, summoned all officials into the palace,
and then led troops to attack Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng.
On the *wùxū* day,
a general amnesty was declared,
and Empress Yáng Shì and Crown Prince Tán were reinstated.
On the *jǐhài* day,

Sītú Wáng Róng, Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè, Gāomì Wáng Jiǎn, 〔三０〕Píngchāng Gōng Mó, Wú Wáng Yàn, Yùzhāng Wáng Chì, Xiāngyáng Wáng Fàn, Right Director of the Department of State Affairs Xún Fān, and others escorted the Emperor on a northern campaign.
Upon reaching Ānyáng,
with a force of over one hundred thousand,
Yǐng sent his general Shí Chāo to resist and engage in battle.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the six armies were defeated at Dàngyīn,
arrows reached the imperial carriage,
officials scattered,
and Attendant Jī Shào died.
The Emperor's cheek was wounded,
he was hit by three arrows,
and lost six imperial seals.
The Emperor then proceeded to Chāo's camp,
feeling extremely hungry;
Chāo offered water,
and his attendants presented autumn peaches.
Chāo sent his younger brother Xī to escort the Emperor to Yè,
and Yǐng, leading all officials, greeted him on the roadside.
The Emperor dismounted from his carriage and wept,
and that evening he proceeded to Yǐng's camp.
Yǐng's mansion had the ceremonial attire of the Nine Imperial Bestowals.
The King of Chénliú sent貂蟬文衣鶡尾.
The next day,
the imperial carriage was prepared, and the Emperor proceeded to Yè,
accompanied only by Yùzhāng Wáng Chì, Sītú Wáng Róng, and Púyè Xún Fān.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
〔三一〕a general amnesty was declared,
and the era name was changed to Jiànwǔ.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùchén,
Yǐng killed Sīmǎ Yáo, the Prince of Dōng'ān.
Zhāng Fāng re-entered Luòyáng,
deposing Empress Yáng Shì and Crown Prince Tán.
Liú Yuánhǎi, the Left Worthy King of the Xiōngnú, rebelled in Líshí,
styling himself Great Chányú.
Wáng Jùn, the General Who Pacifies the North, sent Wūhuán cavalry to attack Sīmǎ Yǐng, the Prince of Chéngdū, at Yè,
and defeated him utterly.
Yǐng and the Emperor fled to Luòyáng in a single carriage;
the imperial equipage scattered,
and in their haste, they ascended and descended without provisions.
The imperial attendant and yellow gate officials carried three thousand private coins in their satchels,
which the Emperor decreed should be borrowed for use.
They bought food wherever they were to supply themselves,
and the palace women stopped to eat at roadside inns.
A palace woman brought more than a *shēng* of parched rice, dried garlic, and salted black beans to present to the Emperor.
The Emperor ate it,
and used a plain cloth quilt from a mid-ranking yellow gate official.
Next, they reached Huòjiā,
where they bought coarse rice,
served in clay bowls;
the Emperor ate two bowls.
An old man offered a steamed chicken,
which the Emperor accepted.
Upon reaching Wēn,
when about to visit the imperial mausoleum,
the Emperor lost his shoes,
and put on the shoes of a follower.
He prostrated himself, weeping,
and all those around him sobbed.
Upon crossing the Yellow River,
Zhāng Fāng led three thousand cavalry,
bearing a sun mirror and a blue-canopied carriage, to respectfully welcome them.
Fāng prostrated himself in homage,
but the Emperor personally stopped him.
On the day Xīnsì,
a great amnesty was proclaimed,
and those who followed were rewarded, each according to their merits.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Fāng requested the Emperor to visit the ancestral temple,
and then abducted the Emperor to Cháng'ān.
Fāng drove his carriage into the palace hall;
the Emperor quickly took refuge among the bamboo in the rear garden.
Fāng forced the Emperor into the carriage;
twelve attendants and yellow gate officials, playing drums and pipes, followed on foot.
Only Lú Zhì, the Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, attended by his side.
Fāng had the Emperor go to his camp.
The Emperor ordered Fāng to prepare carriages to carry the palace women and treasures.
The soldiers then took the palace women as wives and looted the imperial storerooms,
disputing over the contents of the treasuries.
The accumulated wealth since Wèi and Jìn
was swept clean, leaving nothing.
As they traveled, they reached Xīn'ān,
where it was bitterly cold.
The Emperor fell from his horse and injured his foot.
Gāo Guāng, a minister of the Imperial Secretariat, presented him with a face mask,
which the Emperor appreciated.
Sīmǎ Yóng, the Prince of Héjiān, led his officials, thirty thousand infantry and cavalry,
to welcome them at Bàshàng.
Yóng advanced and prostrated himself in homage,
but the Emperor dismounted to stop him.
The Western Expeditionary Headquarters was designated as the palace.

Only Xún Fān, the Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; Liú Tūn, the Sīlì (Regional Inspector); Zhèng Qiú, the Grand Master of Ceremonies; and Zhōu Fù, the Administrator of Hénán, with their remaining officials, stayed in Luòyáng,
forming a "Left-Behind Bureau" (Liútái),
acting on imperial authority.
It was known as the Eastern and Western Bureaus.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
and the reign era was changed back to Yǒng'ān.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Empress Yáng Shì was reinstated.
Lǐ Xióng usurped the title of Prince of Chéngdū,
and Liú Yuánhǎi usurped the title of King of Hàn.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīnghài,
an imperial edict stated:
"Heaven has afflicted the Jìn state,
and the heir apparent has failed to succeed.
Sīmǎ Yǐng, the Prince of Chéngdū, since becoming heir apparent,
has had deficient governance,
disappointing all within the four seas,
and cannot bear the heavy responsibility.
Let him return to his residence as a prince.
Sīmǎ Chì, the Prince of Yùzhāng, the beloved son of the former emperor,
whose good reputation grows daily,
and on whom the four seas focus their attention,
is now appointed Imperial Younger Brother,
to strengthen our Jìn state.
Sīmǎ Yuè, the Minister of Works, is appointed Grand Tutor,
and with Sīmǎ Yóng, the Grand Mentor, will assist Our person.
Wáng Róng, the Minister of the Masses, will participate in managing court affairs.
Wáng Yǎn, the Grand Master of Radiant Honor, is appointed Left Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
Sīmǎ Xiāo, the General Who Guards the South, Sīmǎ Jùn, the General Who Pacifies the North
Sīmǎ Jiǎn, the Prince of Gāomì, is appointed General Who Guards the South,
concurrently holding the title of Colonel Director of Retainers,
provisionally garrisoning Luòyáng.
Sīmǎ Mó, the Central Colonel of the East, is appointed General Who Establishes the North and Supervisor of Jìzhōu,
garrisoning Yè.
Liú Hóng, the Grand General Who Guards the South, will command Jīngzhōu,
to guard the southern lands.
Zhōu Fù and Miào Yìn will each return to their respective departments.
All officials will resume their posts.
Sīmǎ Qióng, the Prince of Qí, was previously ordered to return to his residence,
and Sīmǎ Ài, the Prince of Chángshā, unjustly suffered a severe penalty.
His son Shào is enfeoffed as Prince of Lèpíng County,
Since the recent frequent military campaigns,
manpower and resources have been greatly expended.
All imperial provisions are to be reduced by two-thirds,
and household taxes and land rents by one-third.
Burdensome policies are to be abolished,
and the people cherished, focusing on fundamentals.
After peace and clarity are restored,
We shall return to the Eastern Capital."
A great amnesty was proclaimed,
and the reign era changed.
Sīmǎ Yóng, the Prince of Héjiān, was made Supervisor of All Military Affairs, Internal and External.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎwǔ, which was the first day of the month,
the Emperor was in Cháng'ān.
In summer, fourth month,
an imperial edict enfeoffed Sīmǎ Shào, the Prince of Lèpíng, as Prince of Qí.
Zhāng Fāng deposed Empress Yáng Shì.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Wáng Róng, the Attendant, Minister of the Masses, and Marquis of Ānfēng, died.
Hán Zhì, the Administrator of Lǒngxī, attacked Zhāng Fǔ, the Inspector of Qínzhōu,
and killed him.
Lǐ Xióng usurped the imperial throne,
naming his state Shǔ.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
fire broke out in the Imperial Secretariat's various offices,
burning the Chónglǐ Tàl (gate).
Sīmǎ Yuè, the Prince of Dōnghǎi, amassed troops in Xúfāng,
intending to go west to welcome the imperial carriage.
Gōng Shīfān and others, generals under Sīmǎ Yǐng, the Prince of Chéngdū, gathered followers and attacked and captured commanderies and counties,
harming Lǐ Zhì, the Administrator of Yángpíng, and Zhāng Yán, the Administrator of Jíqùn, among others.
They then attacked Yè.
Sīmǎ Mó, the Duke of Píngchāng, dispatched General Zhào Xiāng to defeat them.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Sīmǎ Xiāo, the General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Fányáng, expelled Lǐ Yì, the Inspector of Jìzhōu.
Cáo Wǔ, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, killed Zhū Jiàn, the Administrator of Dānyáng.
Lǐ Xióng sent his general Lǐ Xiāng to raid Hàn'ān.
Liú Hóng, the General of Chariots and Cavalry, expelled Sīmǎ Shì, the General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Péngchéng, from Wǎn.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín, which was the first day of the month,
Gōng Shīfān again harmed Wáng Jǐng, the Administrator of Píngyuán, and Féng Xióng, the Administrator of Qīnghé.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Liú Qiáo, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, attacked Sīmǎ Xiāo, the Prince of Fányáng, at Xǔchāng,
and defeated him.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Sīmǎ Yǐng, the Prince of Chéngdū, was appointed Grand General Who Guards the Army and Supervisor of All Military Affairs North of the River,
garrisoning Yè.
Sīmǎ Yóng, the Prince of Héjiān, sent General Lǚ Láng to garrison Luòyáng.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"We have received a dispatch from Liú Qiáo, the Inspector of Yùzhōu,
stating that Liú Yú, the Administrator of Yǐngchuān, coerced Sīmǎ Xiāo, the General of Agile Cavalry,
to resist imperial edicts,
to concoct villainous rebellion,
to arbitrarily seize commanderies and counties,
to assemble troops,
to arbitrarily appoint Gǒu Xī as Inspector of Yǎnzhōu,
and to obstruct royal commands.
Liú Hóng, the Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jīngzhōu,
Sīmǎ Shì, the General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Péngchéng, and others
are each to lead their subordinates,
to gather directly at Xǔchāng,
and join forces with Qiáo.
Now We dispatch Zhāng Fāng, the General of the Right, as Grand Commander,
commanding one hundred thousand elite troops.
Lǚ Láng, the General Who Establishes Military Power, Qiān Chú, the General Who Expands Military Power, Diāo Mò, the General Who Establishes Authority, and others will serve as the army's vanguard,
all to gather at Xǔchāng,
to eliminate Yú and his brother."
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Shí Chāo, the former General of Chariots and Cavalry, was dispatched;
Wáng Chǎn, the Central Colonel of the North, was sent to suppress Yú and others.
Red vapor was seen in the north,
extending across the sky from east to west.
A comet appeared near the Big Dipper.
Sīmǎ Mó, the Duke of Píngchāng, sent General Sòng Zhòu and others to garrison Héquán.
In the eleventh month,
Zhōu Quán, the General Who Establishes Loyalty, falsely claimed to have received an imperial dispatch,
styled himself General Who Pacifies the West,
and reinstated the Empress.
Hé Qiáo, the Administrator of Luòyáng, attacked Quán,
killed him,
and again deposed the Empress.
In the twelfth month,
Lǚ Láng (呂朗) and others garrisoned Xíngyáng (滎陽) to the east.
Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎) advanced and occupied Luòyáng (洛陽).
Zhāng Fāng (張方), Liú Hóng (劉弘) and others all held back their troops and could not repel him.
Fànyáng Wáng Xiāo (范陽王虓) crossed from Guāndù (官渡),
captured Xíngyáng (滎陽),
and beheaded Shí Chāo (石超).
He attacked Xǔchāng (許昌),
and defeated Liú Qiáo (劉喬) at Xiāo (蕭).
Qiáo (喬) fled to Nányáng (南陽).
Right General Chén Mǐn (陳敏) raised an army in rebellion,
proclaiming himself Duke of Chǔ (楚公).
He falsely claimed to have received a secret imperial edict
to welcome the Emperor from Miǎnhàn (沔漢),
and drove away Yángzhōu (揚州) Inspector Liú Jī (劉機) and Dānyáng (丹楊) Administrator Wáng Kuàng (王曠).
[三七]He dispatched his younger brother, Huī (恢), south to seize Jiāngzhōu (江州).
The Inspector Yìng Miáo (應邈) fled to Yìyáng (弋陽).
In the first year of Guāngxī (光熙), in spring, on the first day of the first month, Wùzǐ (戊子),
there was a solar eclipse.
The Emperor was in Cháng'ān (長安).
Héjiān Wáng Yōng (河間王顒), hearing of Liú Qiáo's (劉喬) defeat,
was greatly alarmed.
He then killed Zhāng Fāng (張方),
and sought peace with Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越).
Yuè (越) did not agree.
Sòng Zhòu (宋冑) and others defeated Yǐng's (穎) general Lóu Póu (樓裒),
[三八]and advanced to threaten Luòyáng (洛陽).
Yǐng (穎) fled to Cháng'ān (長安).
On Jiǎzǐ (甲子),
[三九]Yuè (越) dispatched his generals Qí Hóng (祁弘), Sòng Zhòu (宋冑), Sīmǎ Zuǎn (司馬纂) and others to welcome the Emperor.
In the third month,
Dōnglái (東萊) Magistrate Liú Bó'gēn (劉柏根) rebelled,
proclaiming himself duke.
He attacked Línzī (臨淄).
Gāomì Wáng Jiǎn (高密王簡) fled to Liáochéng (聊城).
Wáng Jùn (王浚) dispatched generals to suppress Bó'gēn (柏根),
and beheaded him.
In summer, in the fourth month, on Jǐsì (己巳),
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越) garrisoned Wēn (溫).
Yōng (顒) dispatched Hóngnóng (弘農) Administrator Péng Suí (彭隨) and Běidì (北地) Administrator Diāo Mò (刁默) to resist Qí Hóng (祁弘) and others at Hú (湖).
In the fifth month,
the constellation Wǎngshǐ (枉矢) flowed southwest.
In Fànyáng Guó (范陽國), the ground burned,
and could be used for cooking.
On Rénchén (壬辰),
Qí Hóng (祁弘) and others battled Diāo Mò (刁默).
Mò (默) was utterly defeated.
Yōng (顒) and Yǐng (穎) fled to Nánshān (南山),
and then to Wǎn (宛).
[四０]Hóng's (弘) and others' Xiānbēi (鮮卑) troops greatly plundered Cháng'ān (長安),
killing over twenty thousand people.
On that day,
the sunlight scattered in all four directions,
red like blood.
On Jiǎwǔ (甲午), it was the same again.
On Jǐhài (己亥),
Hóng (弘) and others escorted the Emperor back to Luòyáng (洛陽).
The Emperor rode in an ox cart.
His imperial retinue walked on the grass.
The high officials and nobles trudged on foot.
On Wùshēn (戊申),
the General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Jiāngjūn), Fànyáng Wáng Xiāo (范陽王虓), killed Sīlì Xiàowèi (司隸校尉) Xíng Qiáo (邢喬).
On Jǐyǒu (己酉),
four each of the golden caskets and ceremonial texts were stolen from the Imperial Ancestral Temple (Tàimiào).
In the sixth month, on the first day, Bǐngchén (丙辰),
the Emperor arrived from Cháng'ān (長án),
ascended the old palace hall,
and was overcome with sorrow and wept.
He paid respects at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Empress Yáng (羊) was reinstated.
On Xīnwèi (辛未),
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the reign era was changed.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the first day, Yǐyǒu (乙酉),
there was a solar eclipse.
Jiǎ Bāo (賈苞), an official of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, stole the spirit robes and swords from the Imperial Ancestral Temple,
and was executed.
In the eighth month,
the Grand Tutor (Tàifù), Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越), was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Lù Shàngshū Shì),
and the General of Agile Cavalry, Fànyáng Wáng Xiāo (范陽王虓), was made Minister of Works (Sīkōng).
In the ninth month,
Dùnqīu (頓丘) Administrator Féng Sōng (馮嵩) seized Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎),
and sent him to Yè (鄴).
Dōngyíng Gōng Téng (東嬴公騰) was promoted in rank to Dōngyàn Wáng (東燕王).
Píngchāng Gōng Mó (平昌公模) was made Nányáng Wáng (南陽王).
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Minister of Works, Fànyáng Wáng Xiāo (范陽王虓), passed away.
Xiāo's (虓) Chief Clerk (Chángshǐ), Liú Yú (劉輿), murdered Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng (成都王穎).
In the eleventh month, on Gēngwǔ (庚午),
the Emperor passed away in Xiǎnyáng Diàn (顯陽殿),
aged forty-eight.
He was buried in Tàiyáng Líng (太陽陵).
When the Emperor was the Crown Prince,
the court all knew he was incapable of handling affairs of state,
and Emperor Wǔ (武帝) also had doubts.
He once summoned all the officials of the Eastern Palace (Dōnggōng),
and had them instruct the Crown Prince to decide on matters of the Imperial Secretariat.
The Emperor could not respond.
Empress Jiǎ (賈妃) sent her attendants to respond on his behalf,
often citing ancient principles.
The Palace Attendant (Gěishì) Zhāng Hóng (張泓) said:
"The Crown Prince is unlearned,
which Your Majesty knows.
Now, it is appropriate to decide based on the facts,
and not to cite books."
The Empress followed his advice.
Hóng (泓) then drafted the responses,
and had the Emperor write them out.
Emperor Wǔ (武帝) was greatly pleased upon seeing them,
and the Crown Prince thus remained secure.
When he ascended the great position,
governance came from below,
the social order was greatly corrupted,
bribery was rampant,
powerful families
oppressed others with their nobility.
Loyal and virtuous individuals found their paths blocked,
while slanderers and villains had their way,
promoting each other.
The world called this "mutual trade."
Gāopíng Wáng Shěn (高平王沈) wrote the 'Shìshí Lùn' (釋時論),
Nányáng Lǔ Bāo (南陽魯褒) wrote the 'Qiánshén Lùn' (錢神論),
Lújiāng Dù Sōng (廬江杜嵩) wrote the 'Rènzǐ Chūnqiū' (任子春秋),
[四一]all were works lamenting the times.
The Emperor once again, while in Huálín Yuán (華林園),
heard the sound of frogs,
and said to his attendants:
"Are these croaking for the public,
or for private purposes?"
Someone replied:
"If in public land, then public;
if in private land, then private."
And when the empire was in chaos,
and the common people were starving to death,
the Emperor said:
"Why don't they eat minced meat?"
His ignorance and obtuseness were all of this kind.
Later, he collapsed due to poisoning from eating porridge,
some say Sīmǎ Yuè (司馬越) poisoned him.
The historian comments: A talentless son,
claiming to be great by heavenly mandate.
Power did not originate from the emperor;
governance was near to ignoble people.
Bāo Sì (褒姒) and Shū Dài (叔帶) rose together;
Empress Xiāng (襄后) and the Quǎnróng (犬戎) acted in concert.
In ancient times,
Dān Zhū (丹朱) was unworthy,
King Nǎn (赧王) evaded blame.
Comparing their terrible virtues,
affairs were linked to fortune and misfortune.
Like a clay figure,
their true feelings were obscured.
The oppressive summer heat was about to wane,
the sounds of the wanton frogs rarely recorded,
thus revealing ridicule,
and symbolizing their downfall.
Could it be that talented and distinguished individuals still appeared in former generations,
but increasing wantonness and aiding tyranny were exclusively present in our current era?
Things called loyal and good,
had their roots severed here.
People called monstrous evils,
had their source estranged from this point.
Chánglè (長樂) brought no fortune,
Chénghuá (承華) was not destined to rule.
The populace was devastated,
the altars of soil and grain (state) became ruins.
In ancient times, those who ruined states and lost their lives,
shared the same path and chariot:
either they caused constant disorder,
or they were mostly incompetent and obscure.
Could it be that the sagely spirit lost its essence and vigor,
or that Emperor Wǔ (武皇) did not know his own son?
The eulogy says: Emperor Huì (惠皇) held the revered position,
attended court and heard words.
His body was dim,
his mind was clouded.
Looking down from a high terrace,
what grievances in the long night?
Jīnyǒng (金墉) destroyed the crown,
Dàngyīn (蕩陰) cast off the armor.
Both were destroyed,
a flood of calamity ensued.
Collation Notes
Annals of Emperor Xiàohuái (孝懷帝), Volume 5.
Emperor Xiàohuái, personal name Chì,
courtesy name Fēngdù,
was the twenty-fifth son of Emperor Wǔ.
In the first year of Tàixī [290 CE],
he was enfeoffed as the Prince of Yùzhāng Commandery.
During the reign of Emperor Huì,
when the imperial clan brought about disaster,
the Emperor, being young and modest, kept to himself.
His gate was closed to visitors,
and he did not involve himself in worldly affairs.
He devoted himself entirely to studying historical texts,
earning a good reputation at the time.
He was first appointed as a Sanqí Chángshì.
When Zhào Wáng Lún usurped the throne,
he was arrested.
After Lún's defeat,
he was made Shèshēng Xiàowèi.
He was successively promoted to Chēqí Dàjiāngjūn and Grand Administrator of all military affairs in Qīngzhōu,
but had not yet taken up his post.
In the first year of Yǒngxīng [304 CE],
he was reappointed as Zhènběi Dàjiāngjūn and Grand Administrator of all military affairs for the defense of Yèchéng.
On the ding-hai day of the twelfth month,
he was established as the Imperial Younger Brother (Heir Apparent).
The Emperor, knowing that Qīnghé Wáng Tán was originally the heir apparent,
was afraid and dared not accept.
The Diǎnshū Lìng, Lúlín Xiū Sù, said:
"The two prime ministers are managing the royal house,
aiming to bring peace to the state.
The important position of the heir apparent
should be given to someone of current high esteem.
As for the appointment of a respected and virtuous relative,
who else but Your Highness?
Qīnghé is young and weak,
and has not yet won the hearts of the people.
This is why he was elevated to the Eastern Palace,
but then again supported a feudal state.
Now the imperial carriage is displaced,
and the two palaces have been vacant for a long time.
We constantly fear that the Dī and Qiāng will water their horses in the Jīngchuān,
and the multitude like ants will draw their bows at the Bàshuǐ.
It is fitting to choose an auspicious day
to ascend to the position of heir apparent,
to assist the grand emperor above,
to quickly pacify the Eastern Capital,
and below to fulfill the eager expectations of the common people."
The Emperor said:
"You,
sir, are my Sòng Chāng."
He then assented.
On the geng-wu day of the eleventh month of the first year of Guāngxī [306 CE],
Emperor Xiàohuì passed away.
Empress Yáng, being the elder sister-in-law to the Imperial Younger Brother (Heir Apparent),
could not become the Empress Dowager.
She urged Qīnghé Wáng Tán to enter,
who had already reached the Shàngshū Pavilion.
S.hìzhōng Huá Hùn and others urgently summoned the Imperial Younger Brother.
On the gui-you day,
he ascended the imperial throne,
granted a general amnesty,
honored Empress Yáng as Empress Huì,
residing in the Hóngxùn Palace,
posthumously honored his birth mother, Grand Concubine Wáng, as Empress Dowager,
and established his consort, Liáng Shì, as Empress.
On the first day (ren-wu) of the twelfth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the ji-hai day,
Pēngchéng Wáng Zhí's son Róng was enfeoffed as the Prince of Lèchéng County.
Nányáng Wáng Mó killed Héjiān Wáng Yōng in Yōnggǔ.
On the xin-chou day,
Zhōngshū Jiān Wēn Xiàn was appointed Sītú,
and Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè Wáng Yǎn was appointed Sīkōng.
On the ji-you day,
Emperor Xiàohuì was buried in Tàiyánglíng.
Lǐ Xióng's separate commander, Lǐ Lí, raided Liángzhōu.
On the first day (gui-chou) of the first month of spring in the first year of Yǒngjiā [307 CE],
a general amnesty was granted,
the era name was changed,
and the punishment of exterminating the three kindreds was abolished.
Tàifù, Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè, was appointed to assist in government,
and Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Zhūgě Mín was killed.
On the xin-si day of the second month,
Wáng Mí of Dōnglái raised an army in rebellion,
raiding Qīng and Xú two prefectures.
Chángguǎng Tàishǒu Sòng Pí and Dōngmóu Tàishǒu Páng Kàng were both killed.
On the first day (ji-wei) of the third month,
Píngdōng Jiāngjūn Zhōu Fù beheaded and sent Chén Mǐn's head.
On the ding-mao day,
Empress Wǔdào Yáng was reburied.
On the geng-wu day,
Yùzhāng Wáng Quán was established as the Imperial Crown Prince.
On the xin-wei day,
a general amnesty was granted.
On the geng-chen day,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè moved his garrison to Xǔchāng.
Zhēngdōng Jiāngjūn, Gāomì Wáng Jiǎn, was appointed Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn and Grand Administrator of all military affairs in Jīngzhōu,
garrisoned at Xiāngyáng;
Ānběi Jiāngjūn, Dōngyàn Wáng Téng, was re-enfeoffed as Xīncài Wáng and Grand Administrator of all military affairs in Sī and Jì two prefectures,
garrisoned at Yè;
Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn, Nányáng Wáng Mó, was appointed Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn and Grand Administrator of all military affairs in Qín, Yōng, Liáng, and Yì four prefectures,
garrisoned at Cháng'ān.
All commanderies in Bìngzhōu were captured by Liú Yuánhǎi,
and Governor Liú Kūn alone held Jìnyáng.
In the fifth month of summer,
the Horse Pasture Commander Jí Sāng gathered a multitude in rebellion,
defeating Wèijùn Tàishǒu Féng Sōng,
and then capturing Yèchéng,
killing Xīncài Wáng Téng.
Yè Palace was burned,
and the fire did not go out for ten days.
He also killed former Yōuzhōu Cìshǐ Shí Xuān in Lèlíng,
then plundered Píngyuán,
and Shānyáng Gōng Liú Qiū was killed.
In Luòyáng, at Bùguǎnglǐ, the ground collapsed,
and two geese emerged.
The dark-colored one flew into the sky,
while the white one could not fly.
The Yi of Jiànníng Commandery attacked and captured Níngzhōu,
and more than three thousand people died.
On the first day (ji-you) of the seventh month of autumn,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè advanced and garrisoned at Guāndù,
to suppress Jí Sāng.
On the ji-wei day,
Píngdōng Jiāngjūn, Lángxié Wáng Ruì, was appointed Āndōng Jiāngjūn, Grand Administrator of all military affairs for the area south of the Yangtze in Yángzhōu, and given a temporary imperial staff,
garrisoned at Jiànyè.
On the first day (ji-mao) of the eighth month,
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn Gǒu Xī defeated Jí Sāng at Yè.
On the jia-chen day,
a partial amnesty was granted to the six prefectures of Yōu, Bìng, Sī, Jì, Yǎn, and Yù.
Eight commanderies from Jīngzhōu and Jiāngzhōu were separated to form Xiāngzhōu.
On the wu-shen day of the ninth month,
Gǒu Xī again defeated Jí Sāng,
capturing his nine strongholds.
On the xin-hai day,
there was a large star like the sun,
and smaller ones like dippers,
flowing from west to northeast,
the sky was entirely red,
and soon there was a sound like thunder.
Construction of the Qiānjīn Barrage began at Xǔchāng to facilitate transportation.
On the first day (wu-shen) of the eleventh month of winter,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the jia-yin day,
Shàngshū Yòupúyè Hé Yù was appointed Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn,
garrisoned at Yè.
On the wu-yin day of the twelfth month,
Tián Lán, Bó Shèng, and others from Bìngzhōu beheaded Jí Sāng at Lèlíng.
On the jia-wu day,
former Tàifù Liú Shí was appointed Táiwèi.
On the geng-zi day,
Guānglù Dàfū, Yánlíng Gōng Gāo Guāng, was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè, using a false edict, imprisoned Qīnghé Wáng Tán in Jīnyǒngchéng.
On the gui-mao day,
Yuè appointed himself Chéngxiàng.
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn Gǒu Xī was appointed Zhēngdōng Dàjiāngjūn.
On the first day (bing-wu) of the first month of spring in the second year [308 CE],
there was a solar eclipse.
On the ding-wei day,
a general amnesty was granted.
On the xin-mao day of the second month,
Qīnghé Wáng Tán was killed by Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè.
On the geng-zi day,
Shí Lè raided Chángshān,
and Ānběi Jiāngjūn Wáng Jùn suppressed and defeated him.
In the third month,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè garrisoned at Juànchéng.
Liú Yuánhǎi invaded Jí Commandery,
capturing Dùnqīu and Hénèi territories.
Wáng Mí raided Qīng, Xú, Yǎn, and Yù four prefectures.
On the ding-hai day of the fourth month of summer,
he entered Xǔchāng,
and all the commandery governors and generals fled.
On the jia-zi day of the fifth month,
Mí then raided Luòyáng,
Sītú Wáng Yǎn led his troops to resist him,
and Mí retreated.
On the jia-chen day of the seventh month of autumn,
Liú Yuánhǎi raided Píngyáng,
Tàishǒu Sòng Chōu fled to the capital,
Hédōng Tàishǒu Lù Shù fought valiantly,
and died.
On the ding-hai day of the eighth month,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè moved his garrison from Juànchéng to Púyáng.
In the ninth month,
Shí Lè raided Zhào Commandery,
and Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn Hé Yù fled from Yè to Wèiguó.
On the jia-xu day of the tenth month of winter,
Liú Yuánhǎi usurped the imperial title in Píngyáng,
still calling his state Hàn.
On the yi-si day of the eleventh month,
Shàngshū Lìng Gāo Guāng passed away;
on the ding-mao day,
Tàizǐ Shàofù Xún Pán was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
On the ji-you day,
Shí Lè raided Yè,
Wèijùn Tàishǒu Wáng Cuì was defeated in battle,
and died.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day of the twelfth month, the new moon,
there was a general amnesty.
Shuò (碩), Prince of Chángshā (長沙), was made King of Chángshā (長沙),
and Xiǎn (尟) was made Prince of Línhuái (臨淮).
In the spring of the third year, on the *jiǎwǔ* (甲午) day of the first month,
Shì (釋), Prince of Péngchéng (彭城), died.
On the *wùshēn* (戊申) day of the third month,
Jiǎn (簡), General-in-Chief of the Southern Expedition and Prince of Gāomì (高密), died.

Shān Jiǎn (山簡), Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed General of the Southern Expedition and Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Jīng (荊), Xiāng (湘), Jiāo (交), and Guǎng (廣).
Liú Tūn (劉暾), Colonel Director of Retainers, was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *dīngsì* (丁巳) day,
Yuè (越), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), returned to the capital.
On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
he led troops into the palace,
and by the Emperor's side, he arrested more than ten close officials, including Miù Bō (繆播), Director of the Central Secretariat, and Wáng Yán (王延), the Emperor's maternal uncle.
All were put to death.
On the *bǐngyín* (丙寅) day,
there was a partial amnesty in Hénán (河南) Commandery.
On the *dīngmǎo* (丁卯) day,
Liú Shí (劉寔), Grand Commandant, requested retirement,
and Wáng Yǎn (王衍), Minister of Works, was appointed Grand Commandant.
Yuè (越), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), concurrently held the post of Minister of Works.
Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海) plundered Líyáng (黎陽),
and Wáng Kān (王堪), General of Chariots and Cavalry, was sent to attack him.
The imperial army suffered a crushing defeat at Yánjīn (延津),
with over thirty thousand dead.
There was a great drought;
the Jiāng (江), Hàn (漢), Hé (河), and Luò (洛) rivers all dried up,
becoming fordable.
In the summer, fourth month,
Zhū Dàn (朱誕), General of the Left Stacked Crossbows, rebelled and defected to Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海).
Shí Lè (石勒) attacked and captured over a hundred fortified towns and counties in Jìzhōu (冀州).
In the autumn, on the *wùchén* (戊辰) day of the seventh month,
the ground in Dāngyáng (當陽) cracked in three places,
each three *zhàng* (丈) wide,
and over three hundred paces long.
On the *xīnwèi* (辛未) day,
Liú Mángdàng (劉芒蕩) from Píngyáng (平陽) claimed to be a descendant of the Hàn (漢) dynasty,
deceiving and enticing the Qiāng (羌) and Róng (戎),
and usurped the imperial title on Mǎlán Shān (馬蘭山).
Hǎo Suǒ (郝索), a Zhīhú (支胡) named Wǔdǒusǒu (五斗叟), gathered several thousand people and caused a disturbance,
stationing them at Xīnfēng (新豐),
and joining forces with Mángdàng (芒蕩).
Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海) sent his son, Cōng (聰), and Wáng Mí (王彌) to plunder Shàngdǎng (上黨),
and besiege Húguān (壺關).
Liú Kūn (劉琨), Inspector of Bìngzhōu (并州), sent troops to relieve it,
but they were defeated by Cōng (聰).
Wáng Kuàng (王曠), Administrator of Huáinán (淮南), and Generals Shī Róng (施融) and Cáo Chāo (曹超) fought against Cōng (聰),
and were again defeated;
Chāo (超) and Róng (融) died.
Páng Chún (龐淳), Administrator of Shàngdǎng (上黨), surrendered the commandery to the rebels.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngyín* (丙寅) day,
Liú Cōng (劉聰) besieged Jùnyí (浚儀),
and Cáo Wǔ (曹武), General Who Pacifies the North, was sent to suppress him.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
the imperial army was defeated.
Yuè (越), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), retreated to defend the capital.
Cōng (聰) reached Xīmíng Mén (西明門),
and Yuè (越) repelled him,
fighting outside Xuānyáng Mén (宣陽門),
and soundly defeating him.
Shí Lè (石勒) plundered Chángshān (常山),
and Wáng Jùn (王浚), General Who Pacifies the North, sent Xiānbēi (鮮卑) cavalry to relieve it,
dealing a great defeat to Lè (勒) at Fēilóng Shān (飛龍山).
Mó (模), General-in-Chief of the Western Expedition and Prince of Nányáng (南陽), sent his general Chúnyú Dìng (淳于定) to defeat Liú Mángdàng (劉芒蕩) and Wǔdǒusǒu (五斗叟),
and beheaded them both.
He sent Wáng Kān (王堪), General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Cáo Wǔ (曹武), General Who Pacifies the North, to attack Liú Cōng (劉聰).
The imperial army was defeated,
and Kān (堪) fled back to the capital.
Luó Xiàn (羅羨), a separate commander of Lǐ Xióng (李雄), surrendered Zǐtóng (梓潼).
Liú Cōng (劉聰) attacked Luòyáng's (洛陽) Xīmíng Mén (西明門),
but failed to take it.
A mountain in Yídū (宜都) collapsed,
and there were earthquakes in Jīng (荊) and Xiāng (湘) provinces.
In the winter, eleventh month,
Shí Lè (石勒) captured Chánglè (長樂),
and Wáng Bīn (王斌), General Who Pacifies the North, was killed.
Consequently, Líyáng (黎陽) was massacred.
Lǐ Yùn (李惲) and Bó Shèng (薄盛), leaders of the *Qǐhuó* (乞活), led their followers to relieve the capital,
and Cōng (聰) retreated.
Yùn (惲) and others also defeated Wáng Mí (王彌) at Xīnjí (新汲).
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐhài* (乙亥) day,
at night there was a white vapor like a belt,
rising from the ground to the sky,
each two *zhàng* (丈) in the north and south.
In the spring of the fourth year, on the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day of the first month, the new moon,
there was a general amnesty.
In the second month,
Shí Lè (石勒) attacked Juǎnchéng (鄄城),
and Yuán Fú (袁孚), Inspector of Yǎnzhōu (兗州), was defeated in battle
and killed by his subordinates.
Lè (勒) again attacked Báimǎ (白馬),
and Wáng Kān (王堪), General of Chariots and Cavalry, died there.
Wén Shuò (文碩), a general of Lǐ Xióng (李雄), killed Lǐ Guó (李國), Lǐ Xióng's (李雄) Grand General,
and surrendered Bāxī (巴西).
On the *wùwǔ* (戊午) day,
Qián Zèng (錢璯) from Wúxìng (吳興) rebelled,
claiming the title of General Who Pacifies the West.
In the third month,
Zhōu Qǐ (周玘), a clerk of the Prime Minister's Granary Bureau, led his fellow villagers to attack Zèng (璯),
and beheaded him.
In the summer, fourth month,
there was a great flood.
[一０] Qí Hóng (祁弘), a general, defeated Liú Língyáo (劉靈曜), a general of Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海), at Guǎngzōng (廣宗).
[一一] Lǐ Xióng (李雄) captured Zǐtóng (梓潼),
and there was an earthquake in Yǎnzhōu (兗州).
In the fifth month,
Shí Lè (石勒) plundered Jí (汲) Commandery,
capturing Hú Chǒng (胡寵), the Administrator.
Then he crossed the Yellow River to the south,
and Péi Chún (裴純), Administrator of Xíngyáng (滎陽), fled to Jiànyè (建鄴).
Strong winds broke trees.
There was an earthquake.
In the six provinces of Yōu (幽), Bìng (并), Sī (司), Jì (冀), Qín (秦), and Yōng (雍), there was a great locust plague,
devouring grass, trees, and the hair of cattle and horses,
all completely.
In the sixth month,
Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海) died,
and his son Hé (和) succeeded to the false throne.
Hé's (和) younger brother Cōng (聰) assassinated Hé (和) and enthroned himself.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Liú Cōng's (劉聰) cousin Yào (曜) and his general Shí Lè (石勒) besieged Huái (懷).
Sòng Chōu (宋抽), General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was ordered to relieve it,
but was defeated by Yào (曜),
and Chōu (抽) died.
In the ninth month,
Lè Yǎng (樂仰) from Hénèi (河內) arrested Péi Zhěng (裴整), the Administrator, and rebelled,
surrendering to Shí Lè (石勒).
Wáng Lóng (王隆), Supervisor of Military Affairs in Xúzhōu (徐州), abandoned his army at Xiàpī (下邳) and fled to Zhōu Fù (周馥).
Wáng Rú (王如) from Yōngzhōu (雍州) raised an army and rebelled at Wǎn (宛),
killing magistrates and chiefs,
and styling himself Grand General and Governor of the two provinces of Sī (司) and Yōng (雍).
He greatly plundered the Hàn (漢) and Miǎn (沔) areas.
Páng Shí (龐寔) from Xīnpíng (新平), Yán Yí (嚴嶷) from Fēngyì (馮翊), and Hóu Tuō (侯脫) from Jīngzhào (京兆) and others all raised armies in response.
Shān Jiǎn (山簡), General of the Southern Expedition, Wáng Chéng (王澄), Inspector of Jīngzhōu (荊州), and Dù Ruí (杜蕤), Central Protector of the South, all dispatched troops to aid the capital,
and fought against Rú (如) at Wǎn (宛).
All armies were greatly defeated;
Wáng Chéng (王澄) alone advanced with his forces to Yìkǒu (沶口),
but his forces dispersed and he returned.
In the winter, on the *xīnmǎo* (辛卯) day of the tenth month,
it was dim during the day,
until the *gēngzǐ* (庚子) day.
A large star fell in the southwest,
with a sound.
On the *rényín* (壬寅) day,
Shí Lè (石勒) besieged Cāngyuán (倉垣),
and Wáng Zàn (王讚), Administrator of Chénliú (陳留), defeated him in battle,
and Lè (勒) fled north of the river.
On the *rénzǐ* (壬子) day,
Wáng Jùn (王浚), General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Minister of Works,
and Liú Kūn (劉琨), General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed General-in-Chief Who Pacifies the North.
The capital suffered from famine.
Yuè (越), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), sent urgent military dispatches to summon troops from all over the realm.
The Emperor said to the envoy:
"Tell all the generals and regional commanders for me,
that if it is today,
it can still be saved;
later, it will be too late."
At that time, no one arrived.
Shí Lè (石勒) captured Xiāngchéng (襄城),
and Cuī Kuàng (崔曠), the Administrator, was killed.
Then he reached Wǎn (宛).
Wáng Jùn (王浚) sent Xiānbēi (鮮卑) commander Wén Yāng (文鴦) with cavalry to relieve it,
and Lè (勒) retreated.
Jùn (浚) again sent his separate general Wáng Shēnshǐ (王申始) to attack Lè (勒) at Wènshízīn (汶石津),
[一二] and greatly defeated him.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎxū* (甲戌) day,
Yuè (越), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), led his forces out to Xǔchāng (許昌),
taking his field headquarters with him.
The palace and imperial offices were left undefended,
desolation and famine worsened daily,
dead bodies lay across the palace halls,
and government offices and military camps all dug moats to defend themselves.
Robbers and bandits roamed openly,
and the sound of drums and gongs did not cease.
Yuè's (越) army reached Xiàng (項),
and he personally assumed the post of Inspector of Yùzhōu (豫州),
appointing Wáng Yǎn (王衍), Grand Commandant, as his Chief of Staff.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
the wandering Dī (氐) leader Wěi Bó (隗伯) and others attacked Yídū (宜都).
[一三] Jī Xī (嵇晞), the Administrator, fled to Jiànyè (建鄴).
Wáng Shēnshǐ (王申始) attacked Liú Yào (劉曜) and Wáng Mí (王彌) at Pínglěi (瓶壘),
and defeated them.
Zhōu Fù (周馥), General Who Guards the East, memorialized to welcome the imperial carriage to relocate the capital to Shòuyáng (壽陽).
Yuè (越) sent Péi Shuò (裴碩) to attack Fù (馥).
[一四] He was defeated by Fù (馥)
and fled to defend Dōngchéng (東城),
seeking aid from Ruì (睿), Prince of Lángxié (琅邪).
Xiāngyáng (襄陽) suffered a great plague,
with over three thousand dead.
Zhāng Guǐ (張軌), Inspector of Liángzhōu (涼州), was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
[一五]
In the twelfth month,
Gǒu Xī (苟晞), General-in-Chief of the Eastern Expedition, attacked Cáo Yí (曹嶷), a separate commander of Wáng Mí (王彌),
and defeated him.
On the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
[一六] Lǐ Hóng (李洪) from Píngyáng (平陽) led refugees into Dìnglíng (定陵) and caused unrest.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year,
the Emperor secretly ordered Gǒu Xī to attack Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè.
On the day Rénshēn,
Xī was defeated by Cáo Nì.
On the day Yǐwèi,
〔一七〕Yuè dispatched his Attendant-in-ordinary General Yáng Mào and Xúzhōu Inspector Péi Dùn to jointly attack Xī.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Lè entered Jiāngxià,
and its Administrator Yáng Mín fled to Wǔchāng.
〔一八〕On the day Yǐhài,
Lǐ Xióng attacked and captured Fúchéng,
and Zǐtóng Administrator Qiáo Dēng was killed.
Dù Tāo, a refugee from Xiāngzhōu, occupied Chángshā and rebelled.
〔一九〕On the day Wùyín,
the General of the East-Paciﬁed, Lángxié Wáng Ruì, sent General Gān Zhuó to attack the General of the East-Punishing Zhōu Fù at Shòuchūn,
and Fù's forces disintegrated.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Grand Tutor, Píngyuán Wáng Gàn, passed away.
In the second month,
Shí Lè raided Rǔnán,
and Rǔnán Wáng Yòu fled to Jiànyè.
On the day Wùwǔ of the third month,
an imperial edict detailing Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè's crimes was issued,
informing the regional commanders to attack him.
The General-in-chief of the East-Punishing Gǒu Xī was appointed Grand General.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè passed away.
On the day Wùzǐ of the fourth month,
Shí Lè pursued Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè's funeral procession,
catching up in Dōngjùn.
〔二０〕General Qián Duān died in battle,
the army disintegrated,
and Grand Commandant Wáng Yǎn, Minister of Personnel Liú Wàng, Court Justice Zhūgě Quán, Imperial Secretary Zhèng Yù, Wǔlíng Wáng Dàn, and others were all killed.
Over 100,000 people, from princes and dukes downward, died.
Dōnghǎi Crown Prince Pí and forty-eight other royal clan members were soon also captured by Shí Lè.
The bandits Wáng Sāng and Lěng Dào captured Xúzhōu,
its Inspector Péi Dùn was killed,
Sāng then crossed the Huái River,
reaching Lìyáng.
In the fifth month,
Rú Bān, a refugee from Yìzhōu, and Jiǎn Fǔ, a refugee from Liángzhōu, stirred up trouble in Xiāngzhōu,
capturing Inspector Gǒu Tiào.
〔二一〕They subsequently defeated the various commanderies of Líng and Guì in the south,
and plundered Wǔchāng in the east.
Ānchéng Administrator Guō Chá, 〔二二〕Shàolíng Administrator Zhèng Róng, and Héngyáng Grand Administrator Téng Yù were all killed.
Grand Minister of Works Wáng Jùn was promoted to Grand Marshal,
Grand General of the West-Punishing, Nányáng Wáng Mó, was made Grand Commandant,
Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Fù Zhī was made Minister of Education,
Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xún Pān was made Grand Minister of Works,
and General of the East-Paciﬁed, Lángxié Wáng Ruì, was made Grand General of the East-Punishing.
When Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè left,
he left Hénán Governor Pān Tāo in charge of the defense.
Grand General Gǒu Xī memorialized to move the capital to Cāngyuán,
and the Emperor was about to agree,
but the various high officials feared Tāo,
and dared not obey the edict.
Moreover, those in the palace and the imperial eunuchs were reluctant to leave their wealth
and did not wish to depart.
By this time, the famine was severe,
people were cannibalizing each other,
and eight or nine tenths of the officials had fled.
The Emperor summoned his ministers for a meeting.
He was about to leave, but his imperial guard was unprepared.
The Emperor slapped his hand and sighed,
"How can it be that there are no carriages!"
He then sent Minister of Education Fù Zhī out to Héyīn
to repair boats and rafts
in preparation for travel by water,
accompanied by several tens of court officials.
The Emperor walked out of the West Yè Gate,
reached Copper Street,
was plundered by bandits,
could not proceed, and returned.
On the day Guǐwèi of the sixth month,
〔二三〕Liú Yào, Wáng Mí, and Shí Lè jointly raided Luòchuān.
The imperial army was repeatedly defeated by the bandits,
and many died.
On the day Gēngyín,
Grand Minister of Works Xún Pān and Grand Master of Glorious Happiness Xún Zǔ fled to Huànyuán.
The Crown Prince's Left Commander Wēn Jī opened the Guǎngmò Gate at night and fled to Xiǎopíngjīn.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Liú Yào and Wáng Mí entered the capital.
The Emperor opened the Huálínyuán Gate,
left through the Héyīn Water Lily Pond,
intending to go to Cháng'ān,
but was pursued and overtaken by Yào and others.
Yào and others then burned down the palaces and ancestral temples,
and violated the imperial concubines and empresses.

Wú Wáng Yàn, Jìnglíng Wáng Máo, Left Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat Hé Yù, 〔二四〕Right Attendant Cáo Fù, Imperial Secretaries Lǘqiū Chōng, Yuán Càn, Wáng Gǔn, Hénán Governor Liú Mò, and others were all killed.
Over 30,000 officials, gentry, and commoners died.
The Emperor was taken in disgrace to Píngyáng,
and Liú Cōng appointed the Emperor as Duke of Kuàijī.
Xún Pān issued a proclamation to the provinces and garrisons,
appointing the King of Lángxié as the alliance leader.
Yùzhāng Wáng Duān fled east to Gǒu Xī,
who established him as Crown Prince,
personally took charge of the Imperial Secretariat,
fully appointed officials,
and held the county of Méng in Liángguó.
The people suffered from famine and scarcity,
and a *hú* of rice cost over ten thousand coins.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Grand Marshal Wáng Jùn, acting on imperial authority, provisionally established a Crown Prince,
appointed officials,
and assigned garrison commanders.
Shí Lè raided Gǔyáng,
and Pèi Wáng Zī was defeated and killed.
In the eighth month,
Liú Cōng sent his son Càn to attack and capture Cháng'ān.
Grand Commandant, General of the West-Punishing, Nányáng Wáng Mó, was killed,
and over four thousand surviving families from Cháng'ān fled to Hànzhōng.
On the day Guǐhài of the ninth month,
Shí Lè attacked Yángxià,
reaching Méng County.
Grand General Gǒu Xī and Yùzhāng Wáng Duān were both captured by the bandits.
In the tenth month of winter,
Lè raided the various commanderies of Yùzhōu,
and returned after reaching the Jiāng (Yangtze River).
In the eleventh month,
Yī Lú raided Tàiyuán.
General of the North-Paciﬁed Liú Kūn could not control him,
and moved the people of five counties to Xīnxīng,
giving their land to Yī Lú to inhabit.
In the first month of spring in the sixth year,
the Emperor was in Píngyáng.
Liú Cōng raided Tàiyuán.
Hú Kàng, a former Gate Guard General of the South-Punishing Protectorate, gathered a crowd and raided the Jīng region,
proclaiming himself Duke of Chǔ.
On the day Rénzǐ of the second month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Grand General of the East-Punishing, Lángxié Wáng Ruì, submitted a memorial to the Imperial Secretariat,
issuing a proclamation to the four directions to attack Shí Lè.
Grand Marshal Wáng Jùn issued a proclamation to the empire,
claiming to have received a secret imperial edict authorizing him to act on imperial authority,
and appointed Xún Pān as Grand Commandant.
Rǔyáng Wáng Xī was killed by Shí Lè.
〔二五〕
On the day Bǐngyín of the fourth month of summer,
General of the South-Punishing Shān Jiǎn died.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Jupiter, Mars, and Venus gathered in the constellations of Taurus and Sagittarius.
〔二六〕Shí Lè raided Jìzhōu.
Liú Càn raided Jìnyáng.
General of the North-Paciﬁed Liú Kūn sent his subordinate general Hǎo Shēn to lead forces to resist Càn.
Shēn was defeated
and died.
Tàiyuán Administrator Gāo Qiáo surrendered Jìnyáng to Càn.
On the day Gēngxū of the eighth month,
Liú Kūn fled to Chángshān.
On the day Jǐhài,
〔二七〕Yīnpíng Commandant Dǒng Chōng drove out Administrator Wáng Jiàn,
and with the commandery rebelled and surrendered to Lǐ Xióng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Liú Kūn sought troops from Yī Lú,
and memorialized to appoint Lú as Duke of Dài.
On the day Jǐmǎo of the ninth month,
Yī Lú sent his son Lìsūn to meet Kūn,
but he could not advance.
On the day Xīnsì,
former Yōngzhōu Inspector Jiǎ Pǐ attacked Liú Càn in the Sānfǔ region,
driving him away.
The Guānzhōng region was somewhat pacified.
He then, with Guard General Liáng Fēn and Jīngzhào Administrator Liáng Zōng, jointly enthroned Qín Wáng Yè as Crown Prince in Cháng'ān.
In the tenth month of winter,
Yī Lú personally led sixty thousand cavalry to encircle Méngchéng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ of the eleventh month,
Liú Càn fled,
and Liú Kūn gathered his remaining forces
and held Yangqǔ.
This year there was a great plague.
In the first month of spring in the seventh year,
Liú Cōng held a grand assembly,
and made the Emperor wear blue clothes and serve wine.
Attendant-in-ordinary Yǔ Mín cried out loud,
which Cōng disliked.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Emperor was assassinated,
〔二八〕and died in Píngyáng,
at the age of thirty.
When the Emperor was first born,
auspicious grain grew in Nánchāng, south of Yùzhāng.
Before this, a diviner of qi said,
"Yùzhāng has the qi of an emperor."
Afterward, the Prince of Yùzhāng was indeed made the Imperial Younger Brother.
When he was in the Eastern Palace,
he was humble and modest,
receiving court officials
and discussing books.
Upon his ascension to the throne,
he began to follow the old system,
presiding over the Tài jí Diàn,
and had the Shàngshū Láng read out the seasonal ordinances.
He also held court in the Eastern Hall.
During banquets,
he would discuss various affairs with all the officials
and consult the classics.
The Huángmén Shìláng Fù Xuān sighed, saying,
"Today we once again see the era of Emperor Wǔ!"
The Mìshū Jiān Xún Sōng also often said to people,
"Emperor Huái had a clear and brilliant natural disposition,
and early on showed heroic aspirations.
If he had encountered an era of peace,
he would have been a fine ruler who upheld tradition.
However, he succeeded after the turmoil caused by Emperor Huì,
and Dōnghǎi monopolized power.
There were no faults like those of Yōu and Lì,
yet there was the calamity of displacement."
Emperor Xiàomǐn
Emperor Xiàomǐn's personal name was Yè,
his courtesy name was Yànqí.
He was Emperor Wǔ's grandson
and the son of Wú Xiào Wáng Yàn.
He was adopted as the heir to his maternal uncle, Qín Xiàn Wáng Jiǎn,
and inherited the title of Prince of Qín.
In the second year of Yǒngjiā,
he was appointed Sànqí Chángshì and Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn.
When Luòyáng fell,
he sought refuge in Mì Xiàn, Xíngyáng,
where he met his maternal uncles, Xún Fān and Xún Zǔ.
From Mì, he headed south to Xǔyǐng.
Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Yán Dǐng, along with the former Fǔjūn Chángshǐ Wáng Pí, Sītú Chángshǐ Liú Chóu, Zhōngshū Láng Lǐ Xīn, and Fān, Zǔ, among others, conspired to escort the Emperor back to Cháng'ān.
Dǐng pursued and killed them;
Fān and Zǔ barely escaped.
Dǐng then, holding the Emperor, rode in an ox cart
from Wǎn to Wǔguān.
They frequently encountered mountain bandits,
and the soldiers scattered.
They then reached Lántián.
Dǐng informed Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Jiǎ Pǐ,
who immediately dispatched provincial troops to escort and protect them,
reaching Cháng'ān.
He also sent Fǔguó Jiāngjūn Liáng Zōng to assist in its defense.
At this time, a jade tortoise appeared in Bà Shuǐ,
and a divine horse neighed south of the city.
In the ninth month, xīn sì day, of the sixth year,
the Prince of Qín was enthroned as Crown Prince.
He ascended the altar to make an announcement to the spirits,
established ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain,
and declared a general amnesty.
Pǐ was promoted to Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn,
and Qínzhōu Cìshǐ, Nányáng Wáng Bǎo, was made Dàsīmǎ.
Jiǎ Pǐ attacked the bandit Zhāng Lián,
and was killed.
The multitude elected Shǐpíng Tàishǒu Qū Yǔn to lead as Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ,
and become the alliance leader,
selecting and appointing officials under imperial authority.
In the fourth month, bǐng wǔ day, of summer in the first year of Jiànxīng,
the news of Emperor Huái's demise was received.
Mourning rites were performed.
On the rén shēn day,
he ascended the imperial throne,
declared a general amnesty,
and changed the era name.
Wèi Jiāngjūn Liáng Fēn was made Sītú;
Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Qū Yǔn was made Shǐchíjié, Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, and Lù Shàngshū Shì;
Jīngzhào Tàishǒu Suǒ Lín was made Shàngshū Yòupúyè.
Shí Lè attacked Lóngxiáng Jiāngjūn Lǐ Yùn at Shàngbái.
Yùn was defeated
and died.
In the fifth month, rén chén day,
Zhèndōng Dàjiāngjūn, Lángyá Wáng Ruì, was made Shìzhōng, Zuǒchéngxiàng, and Dàdūdū Shǎnxī Zhūjūnshì.
Dàsīmǎ, Nányáng Wáng Bǎo, was made Yòuchéngxiàng and Dàdūdū Shǎnxī Zhūjūnshì.
He also issued an edict to the two princes, saying:
"The calamity of Yángjiǔ Bǎiliù,
even in prosperous times,
may still be encountered.
I, being young and immature,
have inherited this great enterprise.
Hoping to rely on the spirits of my ancestors
and the strength of all the dukes and righteous gentlemen,
to sweep away the fierce bandits,
and rescue the Imperial Palace,
I look forward but have not yet achieved it,
my heart and liver are torn apart.
In the past, Zhou and Shao divided Shǎn,
and the House of Jī prospered;
King Píng moved east,
and Jìn and Zhèng served as his輔.
Now, the Left and Right Chéngxiàng, with their eminent virtue and sagacity,
are close relatives of the state.
We must rely on these two dukes
to sweep away the wicked,
welcome the imperial coffin,
and restore the dynasty.
Order the thirty thousand troops from Yōu and Bìng provinces
to advance directly to Píngyáng.
The Right Chéngxiàng should lead thirty thousand warriors from Qín, Liáng, Liáng, and Yōng
directly to Cháng'ān.
The Left Chéngxiàng should lead his twenty thousand elite troops
directly to Luòyáng.
Dispatch vanguard forces
to serve as a rear guard for Yōu and Bìng.
Meet at the appointed time
to achieve this great功業."
He further issued an edict to the Prince of Lángyá, saying:
"I, being young and ignorant,
have inherited this great enterprise.
I have been unable to eliminate the wicked rebels
and welcome the imperial coffin.
I rest on my weapons, consumed by sorrow,
my heart and liver torn apart.
Previously, I received a memorial from Wèi Jùn,
knowing that you led the three armies
and have already occupied Shòuchūn.
You have sent proclamations to the feudal lords,
unifying your might and prestige.
I imagine that you are gradually advancing
and have already reached Luòyáng.
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Guǐ,
loyal to the imperial court,
has deployed flags for thousands of li
and has already reached Lǒng.
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Guāng
has also dispatched troops from Bā and Hàn
to garrison at Luò Gǔ. The brave warriors of Qín Chuān
are gathering like a forest.
Recently, an envoy returned,
fully informed of the situation in Píngyáng,
saying that Yōu and Bìng are flourishing,
and the remaining Hú are weak and broken.
However, they still rely on their strategic advantages,
so a large-scale expedition is necessary.
I do not know where you have reached now,
therefore I have rested the troops and horses
and have not yet advanced the army.
Where have you reached now?
I must await your instructions,
then I will personally go forth in the imperial carriage
to pacify the Central Plains.
You should reflect on and expand your strategies
and exert yourself to achieve distant plans,
so that the imperial tombs may be restored
and all within the four seas may benefit.
Therefore, I dispatched Diànzhōng Dōuwèi Liú Shǔ
You, with your eminent virtue and close relation,
shall greatly prosper the Eastern Xià
and expand the six directions.
If not you, then who!
However, the imperial temples in Luò Dū
cannot remain empty.
You should garrison and pacify them
to bring peace to the east of the mountains.
The Right Chéngxiàng should enter to assist
and follow in the footsteps of Zhōu and Shào
to bring about the restoration."
In the sixth month,
Shí Lè killed Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Tián Huī.
At this time,
the prefectures and counties east of the mountains successively fell to Lè.
In the eighth month, guǐ hài day, of autumn,
Liú Shǔ and others reached Yángzhōu.
Jiànyè was renamed Jiànkāng,
and Yè was renamed Línzhāng.
Dù Tāo attacked Wǔchāng,
burning cities and towns.
Dù Tāo's separate general Wáng Zhēn attacked Dùnyáng.
In the ninth month,
Sīkōng Xún Fān died in Xíngyáng.
Liú Cōng attacked Hénán,
and Hénán Yǐn Zhāng Máo died.
In the tenth month of winter,
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Táo Kǎn attacked Dù Tāo's confederate Dù Zēng at Shíchéng,
but was defeated by Zēng.
On the jǐ sì day,
there was a heavy hailstorm.
On the gēng wǔ day,
there was heavy snow.
In the eleventh month,
the refugee Yáng Wǔ captured Liángzhōu.
In the twelfth month,
there was an earthquake in Hédōng,
and it rained meat.
In the second year, in spring, the first month, on the *jǐsì* day of the new moon,
a black mist covered people like ink.
It lasted for several nights,
stopping only on the fifth day.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the sun fell to the ground at the *chén* hour.
Also, three suns appeared in succession,
emerging from the west and traveling eastward.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Yáng Wǔ greatly plundered Hànzhōng
and then fled to Lǐ Xióng.
In the second month, on the *rényín* day,
Sīkōng Wáng Jùn was appointed Dàsīmǎ;
Wèijiāngjūn Xún Zǔ was appointed Sīkōng;
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Guǐ was appointed Tàiwèi
and enfeoffed as Xīpíng Jùngōng;
Bìngzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Kūn was appointed Dàjiāngjūn.
In the third month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Shí Lè captured Yōuzhōu,
killed Shìzhōng, Dàsīmǎ, Yōuzhōu Mù, Bólíng Gōng Wáng Jùn,
burned down cities and towns,
and harmed over ten thousand people.
Dù Tāo's subordinate commander Wáng Zhēn attacked Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Táo Kǎn at Línzhàng.
Kǎn fled to Shèzhōng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
there was an earthquake.
In the fifth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Tàiwèi, concurrently Hùqiāng Xiàowèi, Liángzhōu Cìshǐ, Xīpíng Gōng Zhāng Guǐ died.
In the sixth month,
Liú Yào and Zhào Rǎn plundered Xīnfēng and other counties.
〔三二〕Āndōng Jiāngjūn Suǒ Zhēn attacked and defeated them.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Yào, Rǎn, and others again pressed towards the capital.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Qū Yǔn attacked and defeated them;
Rǎn was struck by a stray arrow and died.
In the ninth month,
Běizhōnglángjiāng Liú Yǎn captured Dùnqiū
〔三三〕 and beheaded Shí Lè's appointed Tàishǒu Shào Pān.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a qílín was seen in Xiāngpíng.
Chányú Dài Gōng Yīlú sent an envoy to offer horses.
In Púzi, a horse gave birth to a human.
In the third year, in spring, the first month,
bandits killed Jìnchāng Tàishǒu Zhào Pèi.
Xú Fù from Wúxìng harmed Tàishǒu Yuán Xiù.
Shìzhōng Sòng Zhé was appointed Píngdōng Jiāngjūn
and stationed at Huáyīn.
In the second month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zuǒchéngxiàng, Lángxié Wáng Ruì was promoted to Dàdūdū, Dū Zhōngwài Zhū Jūnshì;
〔三四〕 Yòuchéngxiàng, Nányáng Wáng Bǎo was appointed Xiàngguó;
Sīkōng Xún Zǔ was appointed Tàiwèi;
Dàjiāngjūn Liú Kūn was appointed Sīkōng.
Dài Gōng Yīlú was promoted and enfeoffed as Dài Wáng.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Táo Kǎn defeated Wáng Zhēn at Bālíng.
Dù Tāo's separate generals Dù Hóng and Zhāng Yàn fought Línchuān Nèishǐ Xiè Chī at Hǎihūn.
Chī was defeated
and died.
In the third month,
Yùzhāng Nèishǐ Zhōu Fǎng attacked Dù Hóng,
who fled.
Zhāng Yàn was beheaded in battle.
In summer, the fourth month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the fifth month,
Liú Cōng invaded Bìngzhōu.
In the sixth month,
bandits broke into the Hàn Bā and Dù mausoleums and the mausoleum of Empress Dowager Bó.
The empress dowager's face was lifelike.
An immeasurable amount of gold, jade, silk, and cloth was obtained.
At that time, as the imperial court was newly established
and lacking in many ceremonial garments,
an order was issued to collect the remaining items
to enrich the imperial treasury.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
there was an earthquake.
〔三五〕On the *xīnsì* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
An order was issued to Yōngzhōu to cover bones and bury corpses,
and to repair the mausoleums.
Those who violated this would be punished to the third degree of kinship.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Shí Lè captured Púyáng
and harmed Tàishǒu Hán Hóng.
Liú Cōng invaded Shàngdǎng.
Liú Kūn sent generals to rescue it.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the imperial army was defeated
in battle at Xiāngyuán.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Táo Kǎn attacked Dù Tāo.
Tāo was defeated and fled,
dying on the way.
Xiāngzhōu was pacified.
In the ninth month,
Liú Yào invaded Běidì.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Qū Yǔn was ordered to attack him.
In winter, the tenth month,
Yǔn advanced to attack Qīngbái Chéng.
〔三六〕Yùzhōu Mù, Zhēngdōng Jiāngjūn Suǒ Zhēn was appointed Shàngshū Púyè, Dūdū Gōngchéng Zhū Jūnshì.
Liú Cōng captured Fēngyì.
Tàishǒu Liáng Sù fled to Wànnián.
In the twelfth month,
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Shí sent one imperial seal.
Bandits killed Āndìng Tàishǒu Zhào Bān.
In the fourth year, in spring, the third month,
Dài Wáng Yīlú died.
His followers went over to Liú Kūn.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Liú Yào invaded Shàngjùn.
Tàishǒu Jiè Wéi led his followers and fled to Nánzhèng.
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Shí sent five thousand infantry and cavalry to assist the capital.
Shí Lè captured Lǐnqiu.
Běizhōnglángjiāng Liú Yǎn fled.
In the fifth month,
Píngyí Tàishǒu Léi Zhào harmed Nánguǎng Tàishǒu Mèng Huán.
He led over three thousand households from the two commanderies in rebellion
and surrendered to Lǐ Xióng.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngsì* day of the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
There was a great plague of locusts.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Liú Yào attacked Běidì.
Qū Yǔn led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve it.
The imperial army collapsed without a fight.
Běidì Tàishǒu Qū Chāng fled to the capital.
Yào advanced to Jīngyáng.
All the cities north of the Wèi River collapsed.
Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn Lǔ Chōng, Sànqí Chángshì Liáng Wěi, Shàofǔ Huángfǔ Yáng, and others all died.
In the eighth month,
Liú Yào pressed towards the capital.
Communication inside and outside was cut off.
Zhènxī Jiāngjūn Jiāo Sōng, Píngdōng Jiāngjūn Sòng Zhé, Shǐpíng Tàishǒu Zhú Huī, and others collectively responded to the national crisis.
〔三七〕Qū Yǔn and the high officials and administrators defended the small city of Cháng'ān to secure themselves.
Sànqí Chángshì Huá Jí supervised the troops of the four commanderies of Jīngzhào, Fēngyì, Hóngnóng, and Shàngluò, stationed them east of Bapà Shàng.
Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn Hú Sōng led the troops of the various commanderies west of the city and stationed them at Zhēmǎ Qiáo.
Neither dared to advance.
In winter, the tenth month,
the capital suffered severe famine.
A *dòu* of rice cost two *liǎng* of gold.
People ate each other.
More than half died.
The Grand Granary had dozens of *qū* (fermenting agents).
Qū Yǔn ground them into porridge to supply the emperor.
By this time, it was also exhausted.
The emperor wept and said to Yǔn:
"Now, being in such dire straits,
with no external relief,
to die for the altars of soil and grain [the nation]
is my duty.
However, I think of the officers and soldiers suffering such cruelty.
I now wish to hear of the city's fall as a shameful act of death,
hoping that the common people may be spared the suffering of slaughter and ruin.
Go and send the letter;
my decision is made."
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Shìzhōng Sòng Chǎng was sent to deliver a letter to Yào.
〔三八〕The emperor rode a sheep-drawn carriage,
bared his torso, and carried a jade disc in his mouth,
and, in a coffin-cart, went out to surrender.
The officials cried out and clung to the carriage,
grasping the emperor's hand.
The emperor himself was overcome with sadness.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Jí Láng committed suicide.
Yào burned the coffin-cart and accepted the jade disc,
then had Sòng Chǎng escort the emperor back to the palace.
Originally,
there was a children's rhyme that said:
"Where is the Son of Heaven? In the bean field."
〔三九〕At that time, Wáng Jùn was in Yōuzhōu.
Since beans have *huò* (leaves),
he killed the recluse Huò Yuán to fulfill it.
When the emperor went to Yào's camp,
the camp was indeed situated against a wall in the bean field east of the city.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the emperor was taken to Píngyáng,
accompanied by Qū Yǔn and all the officials.
Liú Cōng granted the emperor the title of Guānglù Dàfū, Huái'ān Hóu.
On the *rényín* day,
Cōng presided over the court.
The emperor prostrated himself before him.
Qū Yǔn fell to the ground, wept bitterly,
and then committed suicide.

Shàngshū Liáng Yǔn, 〔四０〕Shìzhōng Liáng Jùn, Sànqí Chángshì Yán Dūn, Zuǒchéng Zāng Zhèn, 〔四一〕Huángmén Shìláng Rèn Bō, Zhāng Wěi, Dù Màn, and the various commandery administrators were all harmed by Yào.
Huá Jí fled to Nánshān.
Shí Lè besieged Lèpíng.
Sīkōng Liú Kūn sent troops to relieve it,
but they were defeated by Lè.
Lèpíng Tàishǒu Hán Jù fled.
〔四二〕Sīkōng Chángshǐ Lǐ Hóng rebelled with Bìngzhōu
and surrendered to Lè.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day of the new moon,
〔四三〕there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Liú Kūn fled to Jì
and sought refuge with Duàn Pǐdī.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year,
the Emperor was in Píngyáng.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
a rainbow filled the sky,
and three suns shone together.
General Píngdōng, Sòng Zhé, fled to the area south of the Yangtze River.
Lǐ Xióng sent his generals Lǐ Gōng and Luó Yín to raid Bādōng.
In the second month,
Liú Cōng sent his general Liú Chàng to attack Xíngyáng,
but the Grand Administrator Lǐ Jǔ defeated him.
〔四四〕
In the third month,
Wáng Ruì, Prince of Lángyá, acting on imperial authority, changed the era name
and proclaimed himself King of Jìn in Jiànkāng.
In the fifth month of summer, on the day of Bǐngzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
〔四五〕
In the seventh month of autumn,
there was a great drought,
and locusts afflicted the four provinces of Sī, Jì, Qīng, and Yǒng.
Shí Lè also competed to seize the people's grain,
which at the time was called
"Húhuáng" (Barbarian Locusts).
In the eighth month,
Liú Cōng sent Zhào Gù to raid General Wèi, Huá Huì, in Dìngyǐng,
〔四六〕and subsequently killed him.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day of Bǐngzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
〔四七〕Liú Cōng went hunting,
and ordered the Emperor to act as General of Chariots and Cavalry,
dressed in military attire and holding a halberd as his guide.
The common people gathered to watch,
and some old people sighed and shed tears.
Liú Cōng heard of this and disliked it.
Later, during a grand assembly, Liú Cōng
ordered the Emperor to pour wine and wash cups.
After he returned and changed his clothes,
Liú Cōng again ordered the Emperor to hold an umbrella.
Many Jìn officials present lost their voices and wept.
Shàngshū Láng Xīn Bīn embraced the Emperor and cried bitterly,
and was subsequently killed by Liú Cōng.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Wùxū,
the Emperor was assassinated
and passed away in Píngyáng,
at the age of eighteen.
When the Emperor succeeded to the imperial throne,
it was during the chaos of Yǒngjiā,
the realm was collapsing,
and the households in Cháng'ān city numbered less than a hundred.
Walls and houses were dilapidated,
and thorny weeds grew into forests.
The court had no carriages, horses, ceremonial robes,
only wooden tablets for official titles.
The army consisted of merely one contingent,
there were only four official and private carriages in total,
weapons and equipment were largely lacking,
and supplies were not maintained.
Great villains were rampant,
the imperial capital was in grave danger,
but the feudal lords had no intention of relinquishing their positions,
and the generals stationed in critical areas failed to come to the aid of the emperor.
Thus, the ruler and his ministers were in distress,
leading to his murder and humiliation.
The court historian remarks: In ancient times, when the splendor of Yán was in decline,
many heroes feigned loyalty to the imperial clan;
when the virtue of Jīn was overshadowed,
the distressed together supported Huái and Mǐn.
Fányáng was desolate,
〔四八〕and military chariots did not gather.
Was it not that their strength was insufficient, but their sentiment was abundant?
The chattering remnants of the former regime,
merely sought to preserve their lord,
like those poets
who cherished their sweetgums.
Indeed, there were extraordinary events,
but no extraordinary achievements.
A detailed examination of his rise
reveals it was not divinely inspired,
thus, bearing a coffin and biting a sword
can be spoken of in this context.
At that time, the five sacred mountains and three dangerous passes
all fell to bandits.
Lóngzhōu and Niúshǒu
were thus established as sovereign states.
The trusted ministers were not in a time of challenging war,
and Liú and Shí had an overwhelming power.
Relief for hunger was cut off internally,
and military assistance was cut off externally.
The two capitals fell to the barbarians,
and the two emperors were taken captive by the barbarians.
King Zhōu fell at Líféng,
and Duke Wèi lost his heart by the Qí River.
To wish for even a single commandery,
how could it be obtained!
Gān Bǎo said: In ancient times, Emperor Gāozǔ Xuān, with his heroic talent and great capacity,
arose in response to the times.
At the beginning of Emperor Wèi Tàizǔ's foundation,
he strategized military and state affairs,
and his excellent plans frequently hit the mark.
Consequently, he commanded carriages and steered affairs,
serving three generations.
His nature was deep and formidable, like a city fortress,
yet he was broad-minded and accommodating;
he acted by using stratagems to manage affairs,
yet knew people well and was good at selecting
and promoting them.
Thus, both the wise and the foolish harbored respect,
and both great and small exerted their utmost effort.
Therefore, he captured Dèng Ài from the obscurity of farming,
and brought in Zhōu Tài from his travels.
He entrusted them with civil and military duties,
and each excelled in his
work.
Thus, he was able to capture Méng Dá in the west,
take Gōngsūn in the east,
eliminate Cáo Shuǎng internally,
and raid Wáng Líng externally.
His divine strategy was decisive,
and his campaigns were victorious in all four directions.
He controlled the many lords,
and great power was in his hands.
Consequently, the common people supported his abilities,
and the great foundation began to be constructed.
Emperor Shìzōng inherited the foundation,
and Emperor Tàizǔ continued the legacy.
Xuán Fēng caused internal disorder,
