clearing away the great calamity.
He re-assigned Jīng, Xiāng, and other four provinces,
to divide the power of the upstream regions,
restoring order from chaos,
strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.
Although he reigned for a short time,
his strategic vision was grand and far-reaching.
The historian says: The region of Wéiyáng acted rebelliously,
relying on the mighty currents.
The Jiāng of Chǔ was at war,
and Fāngchéng faced the enemy.
It was impossible not to trust the generals and ministers sincerely
to command the armies.
There were tens of thousands of battleships,
and the army was twice that of the imperial court.
He who held the advantage but had no ambition
was Duke Zhōu himself.
Authority was granted externally,
but suspicions arose internally.
They had armies coming down the river,
but he had no strong feudal lord to support him.
Shāng encountered nine rebellions,
Yáo ceased the eight musical notes.
The enlightened emperor, bearing the maps,
was in this very day.
He wielded the dragon stratagem in his grasp,
raised the heavenly banner by the river's edge,
burning their remaining embers,
like a field in autumn.
He removed his mourning clothes and stepped onto the battlefield,
slaughtered the rebels and bowed before the imperial palace.
He reduced the power of the garrisons,
and divided the provinces of Jiāng and Hàn.
He did not tread the path of the overturned carriage,
leaving plans for his descendants.
Seventy-plus years later,
he ultimately suffered the harm of Jìngdào.
Some say:
“Rise and fall depend on destiny,
not just on the upstream regions.”
Could it be that the initial policies were not different,
but those who continued them were?
A eulogy says: The sky-overturning calamity,
fierce beasts presented disaster.
The son of Lángyá,
benevolence and righteousness returned.
He respectfully conducted the affair of Zhào Bì,
and commanded the whip at Jīng Tái.
The clouds looked towards the obscure north,
the river gazed at the open south.
Jìnyáng repelled the enemy,
Hexī preserved its territory.
Though the Hú bandits were difficult,
his divine heart was unwavering.
Three regions galloped swiftly,
a hundred barbarian tribes echoed his call.
The precious Mandate was restored to prosperity,
its golden radiance shone brightly again.
The enlightened monarch was precocious,
military dispatches connected vital points.
Mǎng’s head was suspended in the morning,
Dǒng’s navel was burned at dusk.
His virtue did not falter,
his lingering influence is praiseworthy.
Collation Notes
Imperial Annals, Chapter 7, Emperor Chéng
Emperor Chéng, personal name Yǎn,
courtesy name Shìgēn,
was Emperor Míng's eldest son.
In the third year of Tàiníng, third month, on the day Wùchén,
he was established as crown prince.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Emperor Míng passed away.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the crown prince ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was declared,
and civil and military officials were promoted two grades.
Widows, widowers, orphans, and the elderly were bestowed silk,
two bolts per person.
Empress Yǔ was honored as Empress Dowager.
In autumn, ninth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the Empress Dowager began to preside over court affairs and issue edicts.
Sītú Wáng Dǎo recorded the affairs of the Shàngshū,
and together with Zhōngshū Lìng Yǔ Liàng, assisted in court administration.
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn, King Zōng of Nándùn, was made Piàojí Jiāngjūn.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, King Yòu of Rǔnán, was made Wèishàng Jiāngjūn.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Emperor Míng was buried at Wǔpíng Líng.
In winter, eleventh month, on the day Guǐsì, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Cáo Hún, the Xiàng of Guǎnglíng, committed a crime
and died in prison.
In the first year of Xiánhé, spring, second month, on the day Dīnghài,
a general amnesty was declared,
the reign title was changed,
and there was a grand feast for five days.
Widows, widowers, orphans, and the elderly were bestowed rice,
two hú per person.
Areas within one hundred *lǐ* of the capital were exempted from taxes for one year.
In summer, fourth month,
Shí Lè dispatched his general Shí Shēng to raid Rǔnán.
The people of Rǔnán seized Nèishǐ Zǔ Jì and rebelled.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Dèng Yōu passed away.
Fifth month,
there was a great flood.
Sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Shǐchíjié, Sànqí Chángshì, Jiān Huáiběi Zhūjūnshì, Běizhōngláng Jiāng, Xúzhōu Cìshǐ, Duke Liú Xiá of Quánlíng, passed away.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Xī Jiàn was made Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn Guō Mò was made Běizhōngláng Jiāng, acting *jié*, and Jiān Huáiběi Zhūjūn.
Liú Xiá's subcommanders Lǐ Lóng and Shǐ Dié supported Xiá's son Zhào to replace Xiá's position and resist Mò.
Liú Jiǎo, the Tàishǒu of Línhuái, attacked and defeated them,
beheading Lóng
and sending his head to the capital.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Shǐchíjié, Dūdū Jiāngzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ, Píngnán Jiāngjūn, Earl Yìng Zhān of Guānyáng, passed away.
Eighth month,
Gěishìzhōng, Qián Jiāngjūn, Dānyáng Yǐn Wēn Jiào was made Píngnán Jiāngjūn, acting *jié*, and Dūdū,
Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Ninth month,
there was a drought.
Lǐ Xióng's general Zhāng Lóng raided Fúlíng
and seized Tàishǒu Xiè Jùn.
In winter, tenth month,
Cáo Mài, the great-grandson of Emperor Wǔ of Wèi, was enfeoffed as King of Chénliú,
to continue the line of Wèi.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Wèijiāngjūn, King Yòu of Rǔnán, passed away.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor's younger brother Yuè was enfeoffed as King of Wú.
Chēqí Jiāngjūn, King Zōng of Nándùn, committed a crime
and was executed.
His clan was demoted to the surname Mǎ.
Tàizǎi, King Yáng of Xīyáng, was dismissed
and demoted to the King of Yìyáng County.
On the day Gēngchén,
an amnesty was declared for punishments of five years or less within one hundred *lǐ*.
That month,
Liú Yào's generals Huáng Xiù and Bó Chéng raided Cuán.
Píngběi Jiāngjūn Wèi Gāi led his forces to flee to Xiāngyáng.
Eleventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
a grand military review was held in the southern suburbs.
The stipends of kings and marquises were reformed,
with one-ninth of their income to be consumed.
Shí Lè's general Shí Cōng attacked Shòuyáng,
but failed.
He then invaded Qūnjí and Fùlíng.
Sītú Wáng Dǎo was given the additional title of Dàsīmǎ, acting Huángyuè, and Dūdū Zhōngwài Zhēngtǎo Zhūjūnshì, to repel them.
Sū Jùn, the Tàishǒu of Lìyáng, dispatched his general Hán Huǎng to attack Shí Cōng
and drove him away.
At that time, there was a severe drought;
it had not rained since the sixth month
until this month.
Twelfth month,
Liú Kǎi, the Tàishǒu of Jì, killed Xiàhóu Jiā, the Nèishǐ of Xiàpéi,
rebelled, and surrendered to Shí Lè.
King Qiáo of Liáng passed away.
In the second year, spring, first month,
Páng Yí, a Xiùcái from Níngzhōu, raised an army of righteousness
and attacked Lǐ Xióng's generals Rèn Huí
and Lǐ Qiān, etc.
Xióng dispatched his generals Luó Héng and Fèi Hēi to rescue them.
Yǐn Fèng, the Cìshǐ of Níngzhōu, dispatched his subordinate general Yáo Yuè and Yáng Shù, the Tàishǒu of Zhūtí, to aid Yí.
They fought at Táidēng;
Yuè and others were defeated,
and Shù died.
Third month,
there was an earthquake in Yìzhōu.
In summer, fourth month,
there was a drought.
On the day Jǐwèi,
there was an earthquake in Yùzhāng.
Fifth month, on the day Jiǎshēn, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Zǔ Yuē, the Cìshǐ of Yùzhōu, was given the additional title of Zhènxī Jiāngjūn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
there was a great flood in the capital.
In winter, tenth month,
Liú Yào dispatched his son Yìn to invade Báohǎn,
and then plundered the lands south of the Yellow River.
Eleventh month,
Zǔ Yuē, the Cìshǐ of Yùzhōu, and Sū Jùn, the Tàishǒu of Lìyáng, etc., rebelled.
Twelfth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Sū Jùn dispatched his general Hán Huǎng to enter Gūshú
and massacred Yúhú.
On the day Rénzǐ,
King Xióng of Péngchéng and King Xiū of Zhāngwǔ rebelled
and fled to Jùn.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the capital was placed on high alert.
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Yǔ Liàng was given acting *jié* as Zhēngtǎo Dūdū.
Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn Zhào Yìn was made Guànjūn Jiāngjūn and Lìyáng Tàishǒu.
He was ordered to lead an army with Zuǒ Jiāngjūn Sīmǎ Liú to resist Jùn.
They fought at Cíhú;
Liú was defeated
and died.
Xiāoqí Jiāngjūn Zhōng Yǎ was given acting *jié*,
and commanded a naval force
as the vanguard with Zhào Yìn
to resist Jùn.
On the day Bǐngyín,
King Yù of Lángyé was transferred and enfeoffed as King of Kuàijī.
King Yuè of Wú was enfeoffed as King of Lángyé.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Huán Yí, the Nèishǐ of Xuānchéng, fought Jùn at Wúhú.
Yí's army was defeated.
Chēqí Jiāngjūn Xī Jiàn dispatched Liú Jǔ, the Xiàng of Guǎnglíng, to lead an army to the capital.
In the third year, spring, first month,
Píngnán Jiāngjūn Wēn Jiào led an army to rescue the capital,
stationing at Xúnyáng.
He dispatched Dūhù Wáng Qiánqī, Dèng Yuè, the Tàishǒu of Xīyáng, and Jǐ Mù, the Tàishǒu of Póyáng, as the vanguard.
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn Táo Kǎn dispatched Dūhù Gōng Dēng to receive Jiào's orders.
Zhōng Yǎ and Zhào Yìn etc. stationed at Cíhú;
Wáng Qiánqī and Dèng Yuè etc. stationed at Zhídú.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Jùn crossed from Héngjiāng
and ascended Niúzhǔ.
Second month, on the day Gēngxū,
Jùn arrived at Jiǎngshān.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Biàn Kǔn was given acting *jié*
and commanded the Six Armies.
He fought Jùn at Xīlíng;
the imperial army was defeated.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Jùn attacked the Qīngxī stockade,
and taking advantage of the wind, set it on fire.
The imperial army was again heavily defeated.
Shàngshū Lìng, Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Biàn Kǔn,
Dānyáng Yǐn Yáng Màn,
Huángmén Shìláng Zhōu Dǎo,
and Lújiāng Tàishǒu Táo Zhān were all killed.
Thousands of people died.
Yǔ Liàng was again defeated inside Xuānyángmén,
and then fled with his younger brothers and Guō Mò and Zhào Yìn to Xúnyáng.
Thereupon, Sītú Wáng Dǎo, Yòuguānglù Dàfū Lù Yè, Xún Sōng, etc., guarded the Emperor at Tàijí Diàn.
Tàicháng Kǒng Yú guarded the ancestral temple.
The rebels, taking advantage of their victory, wielded their *gē* halberds, reaching the Emperor's seat,
and burst into the Empress Dowager's rear palace.
All the attendants on the left and right were plundered.
At this time, the Tàiguān only had a few *dàn* of burnt leftover rice
to supply the imperial meals.
The common people wailed and wept,
their cries shaking the capital.
On the day Dīngsì,
Jùn falsely issued an imperial edict for a general amnesty,
and also made Zǔ Yuē Shìzhōng, Tàiwèi, and Shàngshū Lìng,
while he himself became Piàojí Jiāngjūn and recorded the affairs of the Shàngshū.
Yǔ Bīng, the Tàishǒu of Wúqùn, fled to Kuàijī.
Third month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Empress Dowager Yǔ passed away.
In summer, fourth month,
Shí Lè attacked Wǎn.
Wáng Guó, the Tàishǒu of Nányáng, rebelled
and surrendered to Lè.
On the day Rénshēn,
Empress Míngmù was buried at Wǔpíng Líng.
In the fifth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Jùn (峻) forced the Emperor to move to Shítóu (石頭).
The Emperor ascended the carriage weeping bitterly,
and the palace was filled with cries of sorrow.
Jùn (峻) made Cāngwū (倉屋) the palace
and dispatched Guǎn Shāng (管商), Zhāng Jǐn (張瑾),
and Hóng Huī (弘徽) to raid Jìnling (晉陵),
and Hán Huǎng (韓晃) to raid Yìxīng (義興).
Yú Tán (虞潭), the Grand Administrator of Wúxīng (吳興), along with Yǔ Bīng (庾冰), Wáng Shū (王舒), and others, raised an army of righteousness in Sān Wú (三吳).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,

Táo Kǎn (陶侃), the Generalissimo Who Conquers the West; Wēn Qiáo (溫嶠), the General Who Pacifies the South; Yǔ Liàng (庾亮), the Protector-General; and Wèi Gāi (魏該), the General Who Pacifies the North, led a navy of forty thousand
and arrived at Càizhōu (蔡洲).
In the sixth month,
Hán Huǎng (韓晃) attacked Xuānchéng (宣城).
Huán Yí (桓彝), the Internal Administrator, fought bravely
and died.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wèi Gāi (魏該), the General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yōngzhōu (雍州), died in the army.
Máo Bǎo (毛寶), the Grand Administrator of Lújiāng (廬江), attacked the bandit garrison at Héféi (合肥)
and captured it.
In autumn, seventh month,
Zǔ Yuē (祖約) was attacked by Shí Cōng (石聰), a general of Shí Lè (石勒).
His forces scattered,
and he fled to Lìyáng (歷陽).
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍), a general of Shí Lè (石勒), attacked Liú Yào (劉曜) at Púbǎn (蒲坂).
In the eighth month,
Yào (曜) and Shí Jìlóng (石季龍) battled at Gāohóu (高候).
Jìlóng (季龍) was defeated,
and Yào (曜) then besieged Shí Shēng (石生) at Luòyáng (洛陽).
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Wáng Dǎo (王導), the Grand Minister of Works, fled to Báishí (白石).
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Táo Kǎn (陶侃) sent his Supervisor-General, Yáng Qiān (楊謙), to attack Jùn (峻) at Shítóu (石頭).
Wēn Qiáo (溫嶠) and Yǔ Liàng (庾亮) arrayed their forces at Báishí (白ishí).
Lǐ Yáng (李陽), the Grand Administrator of Jìnglíng (竟陵), resisted the bandits on the southern flank.
Jùn (峻) charged out with light cavalry,
fell from his horse,
and was beheaded.
His forces then completely collapsed.
The bandit faction then enthroned Jùn's (峻) younger brother Yì (逸) as their leader.
Zhāng Lián (張璉), the former Inspector of Jiāozhōu (交州), rebelled at Shǐxīng (始興)
and advanced to attack Guǎngzhōu (廣州).
Zēng Xié (曾勰), the Southern Military Governor, and others defeated him.
In winter, tenth month,
Zhāng Lóng (張龍), a general of Lǐ Xióng (李雄), raided Fúlíng (涪陵).
Zhào Bì (趙弼), the Grand Administrator, perished at the hands of the bandits.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Shí Lè (石勒) defeated Liú Yào (劉曜) at Luòyáng (洛陽)
and captured him.
In this year,
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍), a general of Shí Lè (石勒), attacked Pú Hóng (蒲洪), the Di (氐) chieftain, at Lǒngshān (隴山)
and compelled him to surrender.
In the fourth year, spring, first month,
the Emperor was at Shítóu (石頭).
Kuāng Shù (匡術), a bandit general, surrendered Yuànchéng (苑城),
and all officials went there.
Zhōng Yǎ (鍾雅), the Attendant Counselor, and Liú Chāo (劉超), the General of the Right Guard, planned to escort the Emperor out,
but were killed by the bandits.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zhào Yìn (趙胤), the General of the Champion Army, sent his general Gān Miáo (甘苗) to attack Zǔ Yuē (祖約) at Lìyáng (歷陽).
He defeated him,
and Yuē (約) fled to Shí Lè (石勒).
His general Qiān Téng (牽騰) led his troops to surrender.
Jùn's (峻) son, Shuò (碩), attacked Táichéng (臺城)
and also burned the East Hall of Tàijí (太極) and the Mìgé (祕閣),
all of which were destroyed.
There was a great famine in the city;
a *dǒu* (斗) of rice cost ten thousand cash.
In the second month,
there was a continuous heavy rain.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
all armies attacked Shítóu (石頭).
Lǐ Yáng (李陽) battled Sū Yì (蘇逸) at Zāpǔ (柤浦),
and Yáng's (陽) army was defeated.
Téng Hán (滕含), the Chief Clerk of Jiànwēi (建威), attacked them with elite troops,
and Yì (逸) and others were greatly defeated.
Hán (含) escorted the Emperor to Wēn Qiáo's (溫嶠) boat,
and all the officials prostrated themselves, weeping and begging for forgiveness.
Yìyáng Wáng Yáng (弋陽王羕) was guilty
and was executed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
At that time, after the ravages of war,
the palace complex was reduced to ashes,
so Jiànpíng Yuán (建平園) was made the palace.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Sū Yì (蘇逸), with over ten thousand men, was about to enter Wúxīng (吳興) from Yánlíng Hú (延陵湖).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wáng Yǔnzhī (王允之), a general, fought Yì (逸) at Lìyáng (溧陽)
and captured him.
On the *rén yín* day,
Xiāngzhōu (湘州) was merged with Jīngzhōu (荊州).
Liú Pí (劉毗), the Crown Prince of Liú Yào (劉曜), and his Grand Marshal Liú Yìn (劉胤) led all officials to flee to Shàngguī (上邽).
Guānzhōng (關中) fell into great chaos.
In the third month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Táo Kǎn (陶侃), the Generalissimo Who Conquers the West, was appointed Grand Commandant
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Chángshā Jùn (長沙郡).
Xī Jiàn (郗鑒), the General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Minister of Works
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Nánchāng Xiàn (南昌縣).
Wēn Qiáo (溫嶠), the General Who Pacifies the South, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and granted the authority of *kāifǔ yítóng sānsī* (開府儀同三司)
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Shǐ'ān Jùn (始安郡).
Other enfeoffments and appointments varied.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Lù Yè (陸曄), the Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, was appointed General of the Guards and granted the authority of *kāifǔ yítóng sānsī* (開府儀同三司).
Gāomì Wáng Hóng (高密王紘) was re-enfeoffed as Péngchéng Wáng (彭城王).

Yǔ Liàng (庾亮), the Protector-General, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Governor-General of military affairs in Xuānchéng (宣城) and west of the Jiāng (江) in Yángzhōu (揚州), and granted *jiǎjié* (假節).
He concurrently held the post of Inspector of Yùzhōu (豫州)
and was stationed at Wúhú (蕪湖).
In summer, fourth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Wēn Qiáo (溫嶠), the General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Shǐ'ān (始安), died.
In autumn, seventh month,
a comet appeared in the northwest.
There were great floods in Kuàijī (會稽), Wúxīng (吳興), Xuānchéng (宣城), and Dānyáng (丹楊).
An imperial edict granted a three-year exemption from rent and taxes to the prefectures and counties that suffered from bandits.
In the eighth month,
Liú Yìn (劉胤), a general of Liú Yào (劉曜), and others led their forces to invade Shí Shēng (石生)
and arrived at Yōng (雍).
In the ninth month,
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍), a general of Shí Lè (石勒), attacked Yìn (胤)
and beheaded him.
He then advanced and massacred Shàngguī (上邽),
completely annihilating the Liú (劉) clan
and burying over three thousand of their partisans alive.
In winter, tenth month,
Lúshān (廬山) collapsed.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Guō Mò (郭默), the General of the Right, killed Liú Yìn (劉胤), the General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu (江州).
Táo Kǎn (陶侃), the Grand Commandant, led his forces to suppress Mò (默).
In this year,
the sky split in the northwest.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the *jǐhài* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an imperial edict abolished the system of "hereditary appointments" for generals.
In the second month,
Lù Wán (陸玩), the Minister of Personnel, was appointed Left Palace Assistant to the Minister of Personnel,
and Kǒng Yú (孔愉) was appointed Right Palace Assistant.
In summer, fifth month,
there was a drought,
and also famine and pestilence.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Táo Kǎn (陶侃), the Grand Commandant, captured Guō Mò (郭默) at Xúnyáng (尋陽)
and beheaded him.
Liú Zhēng (劉徵), a general of Shí Lè (石勒), raided Nánshā (南沙).
Xǔ Rú (許儒), the Commandant, was killed,
and they advanced into Hǎiyú (海虞).
In the sixth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
a land tax was first levied:
three *shēng* (升) per *mǔ* (畝).
In autumn, eighth month,
Shí Lè (石勒) usurped the imperial throne,
and sent his general Guō Jìng (郭敬) to raid Xiāngyáng (襄陽).
Zhōu Fǔ (周撫), the Southern Central Protector-General, retreated to Wǔchāng (武昌),
and all the displaced people from the Central Plains surrendered to Lè (勒).
Guō Jìng (郭敬) then raided Xiāngyáng (襄陽)
and garrisoned Fánchéng (樊城).
In the ninth month,
the new palace was built,
and the repair of Yuànchéng (苑城) began.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Lèchéng Wáng Qīn (樂成王欽) was transferred to be Héjiān Wáng (河間王),
and Jùn (俊), son of Péngchéng Wáng Hóng (彭城王紘), was enfeoffed as Gāomì Wáng (高密王).
In winter, tenth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Emperor visited the residence of Wáng Dǎo (王導), the Grand Minister of Works,
and a grand banquet was held.
Lǐ Shòu (李壽), a general of Lǐ Xióng (李雄), raided Bādōng (巴東) and Jiànpíng (建平).
Wúqiū Ào (毋丘奧), the Supervisor of the Army, and Yáng Qiān (楊謙), the Grand Administrator, retreated to Yídū (宜都).
In the twelfth month,
Zhāng Jùn (張駿) declared himself a subject of Shí Lè (石勒).
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Liú Zhēng (劉徵) again raided Lóuxiàn (婁縣)
and then plundered Wǔjìn (武進).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Xī Jiàn (郗鑒), the Minister of Works, was advanced to Governor-General of military affairs in Wúguó (吳國).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
due to the lack of transport supplies,
over a thousand men, from dukes and princes downwards, were conscripted,
each to transport six *hú* (斛) of rice.
In the second month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
〔一一〕Duàn Liáo (段遼), the Inspector of Yōuzhōu (幽州) and Grand Chanyu, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
In the third month, on the first day, *rénxū*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict called for virtuous and outspoken men.
In summer, fourth month,
there was a drought.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
the rank of the former Héjiān Wáng Yǒng (河間王顒) was restored.
Róng (融), son of Péngchéng Wáng Zhí (彭城王植), was enfeoffed as Lèchéng Wáng (樂成王).
〔一二〕Zhēn (珍), son of Zhāngwǔ Wáng Hùn (章武王混), was enfeoffed as Zhāngwǔ Wáng (章武王).
In autumn, seventh month,
Lǐ Shòu (李壽), a general of Lǐ Xióng (李雄), invaded Yīnpíng (陰平).
Yáng Nándí (楊難敵), the Di (氐) chieftain of Wǔdū (武都), surrendered to him.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Lù Wán (陸玩), the Left Palace Assistant, was appointed Minister of Personnel.
In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
In the third month,
Zhào Yìn, General of the Western Central Army, and Kuāng Shù, Central Army Secretary, attacked Shí Lè's Mǎtóu Wù,
and conquered it.
Shí Lè's general Hán Yōng plundered Nánshā and Hǎiyú.
In summer, the fourth month,
Shí Lè's general Guō Jìng captured Xiāngyáng.
In the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Bǐngchén,
an edict was issued stating that all types of animal rearing,
which incurred high expenses,
should be entirely abolished.
Tàiwèi Táo Kǎn sent his son Bīn, who was a Staff Officer for the General of the Western Expedition, to join Huán Xuān, General of the Southern Central Army, in attacking Shí Lè's general Guō Jìng,
and defeated him,
conquering Fánchéng.
Jìnglíng Administrator Lǐ Yáng captured Xīnyě and Xiāngyáng,
and garrisoned them.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the first day Rénzǐ,
Tàiwèi Táo Kǎn was promoted to Dàjiāngjūn.
An edict was issued to recommend virtuous and capable individuals.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Emperor moved to the new palace.
In the eighth year, spring, the first month, on the first day Xīnhài,
an edict stated:
"Previously, the dog-like bandits ran rampant,
and the palaces and buildings were burned and destroyed.
Although the chief culprits have been eliminated,
there has been no time to construct new buildings.
Officials repeatedly reported that the court assemblies were cramped,
so this palace was built.
Through the diligent labor of the people,
it was completed in a short time.
Now that I can reside here,
I host a grand banquet for all the nobles,
with nine ranks of guests filling the court,
and all officials displaying their roles.
I know that gentlemen are diligent in performing rites,
and common people exert their utmost efforts.
I wish to abolish the strict laws,
so that all may share in this benevolence.
Therefore, a general pardon is granted for all crimes below a five-year sentence."
An order was issued for all commanderies to recommend strong men capable of lifting 1,500 *jīn* or more.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Lǐ Xióng's general Lǐ Shòu captured Níngzhōu.
The Inspector Yǐn Fèng and Jiànníng Administrator Huò Biāo both surrendered to him.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Zhāng Jùn was appointed Zhèn Xī Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Shí Lè sent envoys to offer bribes,
but an edict ordered them to be burned.
In summer, the fourth month,
an edict enfeoffed Miǎo, younger brother of the late Xīncài Prince Bì, as Xīncài Prince.
Silk and tribute were sent to summon the recluses Závu Qí Tāng of Xúnyáng and Yú Xǐ of Kuàijī.
In the fifth month,
a star fell in Féixiāng.
Qílín and Zōuyú were seen in Liáodōng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
〔一三〕Mùróng Kuì, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Liáodōng, died,
and his son Mùróng Huǎng succeeded him.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Wáng Shū, General of the Garrison Army, died.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
Shí Lè died,
and his son Shí Hóng succeeded to the spurious throne.
His general Shí Cōng surrendered with Qiáo.
In winter, the tenth month,
Shí Hóng's general Shí Shēng raised an army in Guānzhōng,
proclaimed himself Inspector of Qínzhōu,
and sent envoys to surrender.
Shí Hóng's general Shí Jìlóng attacked Shí Lǎng in Luòyáng,
then advanced to attack Shí Shēng,
destroying both of them.
In the twelfth month,
Guō Quán, a former subordinate general of Shí Shēng, sent envoys to request surrender.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month,
two meteorites fell in Liángzhōu.
Guō Quán was appointed Zhèn Xī Jiāngjūn and Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
〔一四〕
In the second month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhāng Jùn, Zhèn Xī Dàjiāngjūn, was promoted to Dàjiāngjūn.
In the third month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
there was an earthquake in Kuàijī.
In summer, the fourth month,
Shí Jìlóng, Shí Hóng's general, ordered Shí Bīn to attack Guō Quán in Méi,
and captured it.
In the sixth month,
Lǐ Xióng died,
and his nephew Bān succeeded to the spurious throne.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Tàiwèi and Chángshā Prince Táo Kǎn passed away.
There was a great drought,
and an edict ordered the Grand Provisioner to reduce meals,
relax punishments,
provide relief to orphans and widows,
and reduce expenses.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Yú Liàng, General of the Western Expedition, was additionally appointed Grand Supervisor of Military Affairs for the six provinces of Jiāng, Jīng, Yù, Yì, Liáng, and Yōng.
In autumn, the eighth month,
there was a grand prayer for rain.
It had not rained since the fifth month,
until this month.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
Lù Yè, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, and Duke of Jiānglíng, died.
In winter, the tenth month,
Lǐ Qī, son of Lǐ Xióng, murdered Lǐ Bān and enthroned himself.
Bān's brother Wǔ, along with his generals Jiāo Kuài and Luó Kǎi, all came to surrender.
In the eleventh month,
Shí Jìlóng murdered Shí Hóng,
and enthroned himself as Heavenly King.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Chōng, Prince of Dōnghǎi, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry,
and Yuè, Prince of Lángyá, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
Zhū Zòng of Lánlíng beheaded Shí Jìlóng's general Guō Xiáng,
and surrendered with Péngchéng.
In Xiánkāng first year, spring, the first month, on the first day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor underwent his capping ceremony,
granted a general amnesty,
changed the reign title,
increased the ranks of civil and military officials by one grade,
held a grand feast for three days,
and bestowed rice upon the sick, widows, orphans, and solitaries who could not support themselves,
five *hú* per person.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor personally performed the *Shìdiàn* ceremony.
The commanderies in Yángzhōu suffered from famine,
so envoys were sent to distribute relief.
In the third month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor visited the residence of the Sìtú.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Shí Jìlóng raided Lìyáng.
Sìtú Wáng Dǎo was promoted to Dà Sīmǎ, granted the Faux Yellow Axe, and appointed Grand Supervisor of All Punitive Expedition Forces,
to defend against him.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Emperor reviewed his troops at Guǎngmò Gate,
〔一五〕and separately ordered his generals,
sending General Liú Shì to relieve Lìyáng,
Zhào Yìn, General of the Western Expedition, to garrison Cíhú,
Lù Yǒng, General of Dragon's Might, to guard Niúzhǔ,
and Wáng Yǔnzhī, General of Martial Might, to guard Wúhú.
Sīkōng Xī Jiàn ordered Chén Guāng, Administrator of Guǎnglǐng, to lead troops to defend the capital.
The bandits retreated towards Xiāngyáng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the state of emergency was lifted.
Shí Yù, Shí Jìlóng's general, plundered Zhōnglú.
Wáng Guó, General of the Southern Central Army, retreated to secure Xiāngyáng.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Chángshā and Wǔlíng suffered from great floods.
Silk and tribute were sent to summon the recluses Zhái Tāng and Guō Fān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day Yǐwèi,
there was a solar eclipse.
In this year,
there was a great drought,
especially severe in Yúyáo of Kuàijī,
where a *dǒu* of rice cost five hundred,
〔一六〕and people sold each other.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnsì,
a comet appeared in Kuí.
Yú Tán, Administrator of Wú Commandery, was appointed General of the Guards.
In the second month,
the military tax on rice was calculated,
leaving a deficit of over five hundred thousand *dàn*.
Shàngshū Xiè Bāo and others were dismissed from office.
〔一七〕On the day Xīnhài,
Empress Dù was enthroned,
a general amnesty was granted,
and the ranks of civil and military officials were increased by one grade.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Gāogōulí sent envoys to offer local tribute.
In the third month,
there was a drought,
and an edict ordered the Grand Provisioner to reduce meals,
and exempt drought-affected commanderies and counties from corvée labor.
On the day Wùyín,
there was a grand prayer for rain.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Empress paid respects at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
There was hail.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Yángzhōu and Kuàijī suffered from famine,
and granaries were opened to distribute relief.
In winter, the tenth month,
Dèng Yuè, Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, sent Dūhù Wáng Suí to attack Yèláng,
and Xīnchāng Administrator Táo Xié to attack Xīnggǔ,
both conquering them.
An imperial edict stated:
"Looking back at past dynasties,
there has been none that did not praise and elevate their illustrious ancestral sacrifices
and treat the Three Guests with courtesy.
Thus, in ancient times, the state of Sòng
was established and flourished according to the rites of Zhōu;
and later, the princesses of the imperial house were enfeoffed as marquises in Wèi,
leaving a beautiful legacy in Hàn records.
Since the recent chaos and disorder,
the various states have been devastated and withered,
and the descendants of Zhōu and Hàn
have been cut off and left without successors.
Therefore, thoroughly seek out the close relatives of Duke Wèi and Duke Shānyáng,
who possess virtuous conduct and clear understanding,
and who can succeed to their ancestral sacrifices.
Let this be implemented according to the old statutes."
The Zhūquè Fúhéng was newly constructed.
In the eleventh month,
Jiànwēi Jiāngjūn Sīmǎ Xūn was dispatched to pacify Hánzhōng,
but he was defeated by Lǐ Shòu, a general of Lǐ Qī.
In the spring, the first month, on the day of Xīnmǎo, of the third year,
the Tàixué was established.
In the summer, the sixth month,
there was a drought.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the day of Dīngmǎo,
Mùróng Huǎng declared himself King of Yàn.
In the spring, the second month, of the fourth year,
Shí Jìlóng led an army of seventy thousand
to attack Duàn Liáo in Liáoxī.
Liáo fled to Pínggāng.
In the summer, the fourth month,
Lǐ Shòu assassinated Lǐ Qī
and usurped the spurious throne,
naming his state Hàn.
Shí Jìlóng was defeated by Mùróng Huǎng.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
Huǎng was promoted to Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn.
In the fifth month, on the day of Yǐwèi,
Sītú Wáng Dǎo was appointed Tàifù and Dūdū Zhōngwài Zhūjūnshì;
Sīkōng Xī Jiàn was appointed Tàiwèi;
and Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn Yǔ Liàng was appointed Sīkōng.
In the sixth month,
the title of Sītú was changed to Chéngxiàng,
and Tàifù Wáng Dǎo was appointed to it.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day of Bǐngwǔ,
Ānzhōu was established by dividing Níngzhōu.
In the spring, the first month, on the day of Xīnchǒu, of the fifth year,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the third month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ Dèng Yuè attacked Shǔ.
Mèng Yàn of Jiànníng captured Lǐ Shòu's general Huò Biāo and surrendered.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day of Xīnwèi,
Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn Yǔ Liàng dispatched his Cānjūn Zhào Sōng to attack Bājun and Jiāngyáng,
capturing Shí Jìlóng's generals Lǐ Hóng and Huáng Zhí, among others.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day of Gēngshēn,
Shǐchíjié, Shìzhōng, Chéngxiàng, Lǐng Yángzhōu Cìshǐ, Shǐxīng Gōng Wáng Dǎo passed away.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Hé Chōng was appointed Lù Shàngshū Shì.
In the eighth month, on the day of Rénwǔ,
the title of Chéngxiàng was again changed to Sītú.
On the day of Xīnyǒu,
Tàiwèi and Nánchāng Gōng Xī Jiàn passed away.
In the ninth month,
Shí Jìlóng's generals Kuí Ān and Lǐ Nóng captured Miǎnnán.
Zhāng Hè captured Zhūchéng,
and then raided Jiāngxià and Yìyáng.
Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn Máo Bǎo, Xīyáng Tàishǒu Fán Jùn,
and Yìyáng Tàishǒu Zhèng Jìn all died.
Kuí Ān and others advanced to besiege Shíchéng.
Jìnglíng Tàishǒu Lǐ Yáng resisted in battle
and defeated them,
beheading over five thousand enemy soldiers.
Ān then retreated,
and subsequently plundered Hándōng, relocating over seven thousand households to Yōu and Jì.
In the winter, the twelfth month, on the day of Bǐngxū,
Piàojì Jiāngjūn, Lángyá Wáng Yuè was appointed Sītú.
Lǐ Shòu's general Lǐ Yì raided Bādōng.
The defending general Láo Yáng was defeated in battle
and died.
In the spring, the first month, on the day of Gēngzǐ, of the sixth year,
Shǐchíjié, Dūdū Jiāng Yù Yì Liáng Yōng Jiāo Guǎng Qīzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Sīkōng, Dūtíng Hóu Yǔ Liàng passed away.
On the day of Xīnhài,
Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū Lù Wán was appointed Sīkōng.
In the second month,
Mùróng Huǎng fought against Shí Chéng, a general of Shí Jìlóng, in Liáoxī
and defeated him,
presenting the trophies of victory to the capital.
On the day of Gēngchén,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi.
In the third month, on the day of Dīngmǎo,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Chējì Jiāngjūn, Dōnghǎi Wáng Chōng was appointed Piàojì Jiāngjūn.
Lǐ Shòu captured Dānchuān.
The defending generals Mèng Yàn, Liú Qí, and Lǐ Qiū all died.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the day of Yǐmǎo,
following the precedent of the mid-restoration,
the emperor began to hold court in the Eastern Hall on the first and fifteenth days of the lunar month.
In the winter, the tenth month,
Línyì presented a trained elephant.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Guǐmǎo,
Lángyá was restored
to be comparable to Fēngpèi of Hàn.
In the spring, the second month, on the day of Jiǎzǐ, the first day of the month, of the seventh year,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Mùróng Huǎng sent an envoy to request the loan of the seal of the King of Yàn,
which was granted.
In the third month, on the day of Wùxū,
Empress Dù passed away.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the day of Dīngmǎo,
Empress Gōng was buried in Xīngpínglíng.
Households were officially registered,
and all officials from princes and dukes downwards were subject to the "land severance and white register" policy.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the day of Xīnyǒu,
Piàojì Jiāngjūn, Dōnghǎi Wáng Chōng passed away.
In the ninth month,
the office of Tàipú was abolished.
In the winter, the twelfth month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
Sīkōng, Xīngpíng Bó Lù Wán passed away.
Miscellaneous performances of the Yuèfǔ were abolished.
Ānzhōu was abolished.
In the spring, the first month, on the day of Jǐwèi, the first day of the month, of the eighth year,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the third month,
for the first time, Empress Wǔdào Yáng was accorded the honor of being enshrined with Emperor Wǔ in his ancestral temple.
In the summer, the sixth month, on the day of Gēngyín,
the emperor was unwell.
An imperial edict stated:
"I, with my meager years,
have been fortunate to inherit this grand lineage,
placed above kings and dukes,
for eighteen years now.
I have been unable to fully develop and expand the ways of governance,
or to eliminate lingering misfortunes.
Night and day I have been vigilant and anxious,
without a moment of peace.
Now, afflicted with an illness from which I may not recover,
my heart is filled with sorrow and fear.
Qiān Líng is but a youth,
not yet capable of facing such difficulties.
Sītú, Lángyá Wáng Yuè,
is my younger brother by the same mother,
and by nature, he is benevolent and senior.
His demeanor as a ruler
truly meets the expectations of the time.
Therefore, all you kings, dukes, ministers, and gentlemen,
assist him!
So that he may reverently maintain the illustrious ancestral sacrifices,
harmonize internal and external affairs,
and truly uphold the mean.
Alas,
be respectful!
Do not let fall the glorious mandate of our ancestors."
On the day of Rénchén,
Wǔlíng Wáng Xī, Kuàijī Wáng Yù, Zhōngshū Jiān Yǔ Bīng, Zhōngshū Lìng Hé Chōng, and Shàngshū Lìng Zhūgě Huī were summoned to receive the deathbed instructions.
On the day of Guǐsì,
the emperor passed away in the Western Hall,
at the age of twenty-two.
He was buried in Xīngpínglíng,
with the temple name Xiǎnzōng.
The Emperor was young and intelligent,
possessing the bearing of an adult.
When Nándùn Wáng Zōng was executed,
the Emperor was not aware of it.
After Sū Jùn was pacified,
he asked Yǔ Liàng:
“Where is the old white-headed man you always spoke of?”
Liàng replied that he had been executed for plotting rebellion.
The Emperor wept and said to Liàng:
“Uncle says someone is a bandit
and then kills him.
If someone says Uncle is a bandit,
what then?”
Liàng was frightened
and his color changed.
Yǔ Yì once sent wine to Wáng Yǔnzhī, the Governor of Jiāngzhōu.
Yǔnzhī gave it to a dog,
and the dog died.
He was scared and reported it to the throne.
The Emperor was angry and said:
“My elder uncle has already brought chaos to the realm;
does my younger uncle wish to do the same?”
When Yì heard this,
he drank poison and died.
However, while young, he was controlled by his maternal uncles,
and did not personally manage state affairs.
When he grew older,
he began to pay considerable attention to the myriad affairs of state,
aiming for simplicity and frugality.
He once wished to build an archery hall in the imperial garden,
which would cost forty *jīn*.
He stopped due to the labor and expense involved.
Though his martial bearing
might have fallen short of former kings,
his virtue of reverence and frugality
was enough to follow in the footsteps of past luminaries.
Emperor Kāng
Emperor Kāng's personal name was Yuè,
courtesy name Shìtóng.
He was Emperor Chéng's younger brother by the same mother.
In the first year of Xiánhé, he was enfeoffed as Wú Wáng.
In the second year, he was transferred and enfeoffed as Lángxié Wáng.
In the ninth year, he was appointed Sànqí Chángshì
and granted the title of Piàojì Jiāngjūn.
In the fifth year of Xiánkāng, he was promoted to Shìzhōng and Sītú.
On *gēngyín* in the sixth month of the eighth year,
Emperor Chéng was unwell
and issued an edict making Lángxié Wáng his heir.
On *guǐsì*,
Emperor Chéng passed away.
On *jiǎwǔ*,
he ascended the imperial throne
and granted a general amnesty.
All military and civil officials stationed in garrisons and officials holding the rank of two-thousand-*dàn*
were not permitted to leave their posts and rush to the capital.
On *jǐhài*,
Emperor Chéng's son Pī was enfeoffed as Lángxié Wáng,
and Yì as Dōnghǎi Wáng.
At this time, the Emperor was in mourning and did not speak,
entrusting governance to Yǔ Bīng and Hé Chōng.
In autumn, on *bǐngchén* in the seventh month,
Emperor Chéngdì was buried at Xīngpíng Líng.
The Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the western steps.
After the procession began,
he walked to Chānghé Mén,
ascended the plain carriage,
and proceeded to the mausoleum.
On *jǐwèi*,
Hé Chōng, the Zhōngshū Lìng, was appointed Piàojì Jiāngjūn.
In the eighth month, on *xīnchǒu*,
Péngchéng Wáng Hóng passed away.
Wáng Yǔnzhī, the Governor of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Wèi Jiāngjūn.
In the ninth month,
an edict ordered that officials of the Lángxié state and its administration be promoted according to their different ranks.
In winter, on *jiǎwǔ* in the tenth month,
Wèi Jiāngjūn Wáng Yǔnzhī died.
In the twelfth month,
the ranks of civil and military officials were increased by two grades.
On *rénzǐ*,
Empress Chǔ Shì was enthroned.
In spring, in the first month of the first year of Jiànyuán,
the reign title was changed.
Relief was provided for the widowed, lonely, and orphaned.
In the third month,
Yǔ Bīng, the Zhōngshū Jiān, was appointed Chēqí Jiāngjūn.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Zhōu Fǔ, the Governor of Yìzhōu, and Cáo Jù, the Administrator of Xīyáng, attacked Lǐ Shòu,
defeating his general Lǐ Héng at Jiāngyáng.
〔二四〕
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
On *rénwǔ* in the sixth month,
again, Xúnyáng Zhái Tāng and Kuàijī Yú Xǐ, recluses, were summoned with bolts of silk.
The responsible officials memorialized
that one year had passed since Emperor Chéng's death,
requesting a change from plain mourning attire
and a return to imperial meals as before.
On *rénwèi*,
an edict stated:
“The reduction and elevation of rites
rise and fall with the times,
indeed without constancy.
However, regarding the equivalence between sovereign and parent,
the importance of proper relationships and teachings
cannot be altered.
The creation of temporary regulations
originated in recent times.
Although said to suit the occasion,
it was truly the beginning of a decline into weakness.
The former kings upheld it,
but later generations still grew lax.
How much more so if we follow precedent
and further reduce the gravity?
It is morally impermissible.”
Shí Jìlóng led his troops to attack Mùróng Huàng,
and Huàng thoroughly defeated them.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Shí Jìlóng's general Dài Kāi led his troops to surrender.
On *dīngsì*,
an edict stated:
“Mùróng Huàng has destroyed the Jié bandits,
claiming over eighty thousand dead.
This must be the beginning of their heavenly downfall.
The affairs of the Central Plains
should be carefully considered.
Moreover, Dài Kāi has already led his partisans to submit,
and should be comforted and rewarded.
Envoys should be sent to the Ānxī and Piàojì generals
to consult on all military matters.”
Huán Wēn, the Fǔguó Jiāngjūn and Lángxié Nèishǐ, was appointed Qiánfēng Xiǎodū and given the *jié* staff,
leading troops into Línhuái. Yǔ Yì, the Ānxī Jiāngjūn, was appointed Zhēngtǎo Dàdūdū
and moved his garrison to Xiāngyáng.
On *gēngshēn*,
Jìnlíng and Wú Jùn suffered disasters.
In the eighth month,
Lǐ Shòu died,
and his son Shì succeeded to the false throne.
Shí Jìlóng sent his general Liú Níng to attack and capture Dí Dào.
In winter, on *xīnsì* in the tenth month,
Yǔ Bīng, the Chēqí Jiāngjūn, was appointed Dūdū Jīng, Jiāng, Sī, Yōng, Yì, Liáng, the military affairs of six prefectures, and Governor of Jiāngzhōu.
Hé Chōng, the Piàojì Jiāngjūn, was appointed Zhōngshū Jiān, Dūdū Yáng, Yù, the military affairs of two prefectures, Governor of Yángzhōu, and Lù Shàngshū Shì,
assisting in governance.
Huán Wēn, the Lángxié Nèishǐ, was appointed Dūdū Qīng, Xú, Yǎn, the military affairs of three prefectures, and Governor of Xúzhōu.
Chǔ Póu was appointed Wèi Jiāngjūn and concurrently Zhōngshū Lìng.
In the eleventh month, on *jǐsì*,
a general amnesty was granted.
In the twelfth month,
Shí Jìlóng invaded Zhāng Jùn.
Jùn sent his general Xiè Ài to resist him.
They fought a major battle at Héxī,
and Jìlóng was defeated.
In the twelfth month,
Gāogōulí sent envoys to pay tribute.
In spring, in the first month of the second year,
Zhāng Jùn sent his generals Hé Lín and Xiè Ài to attack the Southern Qiāng at Yútiánhé,
and thoroughly defeated them.
In the second month,
Mùróng Huàng and the Xiānbēi chieftain Yǔwén Guī fought at Chānglí.
Guī's forces were greatly defeated
and fled to Mòběi.
In the fourth month,
Zhāng Jùn's general Zhāng Guàn defeated Shí Jìlóng's general Wáng Zhuó at Sānjiāo Chéng.
In autumn, on *bǐngzǐ* in the eighth month,
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Yǔ Yì was promoted to Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn.
On *gēngchén*, Huán Xuān, who held the *jié* staff, was Dūdū Sī, Yōng, Liáng, the military affairs of three prefectures, Governor of Liángzhōu, Píngběi Jiāngjūn, and Jìnglíng Gōng, died.
On *dīngsì*,
Wèi Jiāngjūn Chǔ Póu was appointed Tèjìn, Dūdū Xú, Yǎn, the military affairs of two prefectures, and Governor of Yǎnzhōu,
stationed at Jīnchéng.
In the ninth month,
Yáng Qiān, the Administrator of Bādōng, attacked Lǐ Shì and Shì's general Shēn Yáng,
putting them to flight
and capturing their general Lè Gāo.
On *bǐngshēn*,
the imperial son Dān was established as Crown Prince.
On *wùxū*,
the Emperor passed away in the Shìgān Diàn
at the age of twenty-three
and was buried at Chóngpíng Líng.
Initially,
Emperor Chéng had an illness.
Zhōngshū Lìng Yú Bīng, considering himself the maternal uncle of the emperor and thus enjoying the position of a powerful minister,
whose authority rivaled that of the sovereign,
feared that after the passing of the current emperor,
the relationship with the imperial clan would become distant.
Therefore, he stated that the country faced strong enemies
and it was appropriate to establish an adult ruler.
Consequently, he had the (current) emperor established as the heir.
He established the system and era name,
re-establishing the inner court,
and then changed the era name to Jiànyuán.
Someone said to Yú Bīng:
"Guō Pú's prophecy states: 'At the time of establishing *shǐ*, hills and mountains collapse.'
*Lì* means
*jiàn* (establish);
*shǐ* means
*yuán* (origin/first);
'Hills and mountains'
is a taboo term (referring to the emperor)."
Yú Bīng was startled,
then sighed, saying:
"If there are good or ill omens,
how can altering things possibly avert them?"
By this time, it was indeed verified.
The court historian remarks: Such tyrannical behavior, reaching to the heavens,
did not happen overnight.
If severe punishments are meted out without resentment,
and the common people still look up to the ruler,
then one can also see the subtle workings of compliance and defiance.
Emperor Chéng, with his weakened resources,
held the lands of Jiānghuái.
Governance issued from Wèiyáng,
but his influence and authority were discordant.
With violent factions unleashed,
the sacred imperial regalia were in peril.
The capital lacked the resources of Áo and Yú,
and the palaces resembled the fires of Xiányáng.
Jié's dogs barked at Yáo;
the rebellious foxes continued the chaos.
Compared to Fāng Zhū and Hòu Yì,
how much more severe this was!
Our imperial carriage was overturned,
but there was no army like that of Jìn Wén.
Hanging by a fragile thread,
we still relied on the strength of Táo Gōng.
In ancient times, if the territories of feudal lords
unfortunately bordered imperial lands,
and the Son of Heaven made a tour,
they would vacate their palaces and face north in homage.
This was heard in the surviving strategies
and used as a constant standard.
Xiǎnzōng, at the gate of Wáng Dǎo,
gathered his robes and bowed forward.
How could this be as lowly as the Duke of Lǔ receiving jade?
The emperor was also frugal in his person,
which could perhaps inspire a rectification of prevailing弊.
Eulogy: The emperor manifested himself early,
while his maternal uncle served as his assistant.
Diligence in causing conflict,
clumsiness in leading troops.
Fire reached the lord's house,
and soldiers attacked the emperor's tent.
The carriage at Shítóu
filled the land with sorrow.
Empress Kāng, by nature,
observed mourning rituals meticulously.
When fallen norms were about to rise,
why was her lifespan so short?

Shàngshū Lìng, Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū, and Count Zhūgě Huī of Jiàn'ān died.
6th month, on the day of Guǐhài,

a general amnesty was declared.

In summer, 4th month, on the day of Jǐyǒu, the first day of the month,

12th month,

In summer, 4th month,
there was an earthquake.
Shǔ natives Dèng Dìng and Wěi Wén raised an army in rebellion.
Huán Wēn again attacked and defeated them,
and ordered Císhǐ Zhōu Fǔ of Yìzhōu to garrison Péngmó.
On the day of Dīngsì,
Dèng Dìng and Wěi Wén re-entered and occupied Chéngdū.
Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn Yáng Qiān abandoned Fúchéng
and retreated to defend Déyáng.
5th month, on the day of Wùshēn,
Mùróng Huǎng was promoted to Ān Běi Jiāngjūn.
Shí Jìlóng again sent his generals Shí Níng and Má Qiū to attack Liángzhōu,
reaching Qǔliǔ.
Zhāng Zhònghuá sent general Niú Xuán to resist them,
and retreated to defend Páohǎn.
6th month, on the day of Xīnyǒu,
a general amnesty was declared.
In autumn, 7th month,
Fàn Wén again captured Rìnán,
killing Dūhù Liú Xióng.
Wěi Wén established Fàn Bēn as emperor.
8th month, on the day of Wùwǔ,
Zhāng Zhònghuá's general Xiè Ài advanced and attacked Má Qiū,
and greatly defeated him.
9th month,
there was an earthquake.
In winter, 10th month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
Císhǐ Zhāng Zhònghuá of Liángzhōu was granted the titles of Dà Dūdū of military affairs in Lǒngyòu and Guānzhōng, Hù Qiāng Xiàowèi, and Dàjiāngjūn.
Dǐ King Yáng Chū of Wǔdū was granted the titles of Zhēng Nán Jiāngjūn, Císhǐ of Yōngzhōu, Píng Qiāng Xiàowèi, and Duke of Qiúchí.
Both were also granted the *Jiǎjié* (authority to execute without prior imperial approval).
In the twelfth month,
Zhènwēi Hùjūn Xiāo Jìngwén harmed Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn Yáng Qiān,
attacked Fúchéng,
and captured it.
Then he took Bāxī
In the fourth year, in summer, the fourth month,
Fàn Wén plundered Jiǔdé,
killing many.
In the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Huán Wēn was promoted to Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī,
and enfeoffed as Línhè Jùngōng;
Xī Zhōnglángjiāng Xiè Shàng was made Ānxī Jiāngjūn.
On the day Bing-shen in the ninth month,
Mùróng Huǎng died,
and his son Jùn succeeded to the spurious throne.
In winter, on the day Jǐ-wèi in the tenth month,
there was an earthquake.
Shí Jìlóng sent his general Fú Jiàn to raid Jìnglíng.
In the twelfth month,
Huáng Tāo of Yùzhāng declared himself Xiàoshén Huángdì,
gathered several thousand men,
and raided Línchuān.
The Grand Administrator Yǔ Tiáo attacked and suppressed him.
In the fifth year, in spring, on the xīn-sì day which was the first day of the first month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the day Gēng-yín,
there was an earthquake.
Shí Jìlóng usurped the imperial title at Yè.
In the second month,
Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn Chǔ Póu sent his subordinate general Wáng Kān on a northern expedition,
and captured Shí Jìlóng's general Zhī Chóng.
In summer, the fourth month,
Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Zhōu Fǔ and Lóngxiáng Jiāngjūn Zhū Táo attacked Fàn Bēn,
and Yìzhōu was pacified.
Zhōu Fǔ was enfeoffed as Jiànchéng Gōng.
Mùróng Jùn was granted the titles of Dàjiāngjūn, Yōupíng Èrzhōu Mù, Dàchányú, and Yān Wáng.
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn Huán Wēn sent Dūhù Téng Jùn to attack Fàn Wén,
but Téng Jùn was defeated by Wén.
Shí Jìlóng died,
and his son Shì succeeded to the spurious throne.
In the fifth month,
Shí Zūn deposed Shì and enthroned himself.
In the sixth month,
Huán Wēn encamped at Ānlù
and dispatched his generals to attack north of the Yellow River.
Shí Zūn's Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Xiá surrendered with Shòuyáng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Chǔ Póu advanced to Péngchéng and encamped,
sending his subordinate generals Wáng Kān and Lǐ Mài to fight against Shí Zūn's general Lǐ Nóng at Dàipí.
Wáng Kān was captured by Nóng,
and Lǐ Mài died.
In the eighth month,
Chǔ Póu retreated and encamped at Guǎnglíng,
while Xī Zhōnglángjiāng Chén Kuí burned Shòuchūn and fled.
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Sīmǎ Xūn attacked Shí Zūn's Chángchéng post,
and Chóuchí Gōng Yáng Chū attacked Xīchéng.
Both were defeated.
In winter, the tenth month,
Shí Zūn's general Shí Yù attacked Wǎn,
captured it,
and seized Nányáng Tàishǒu Guō Qǐ.
Sīmǎ Xūn advanced to Xuángōu,
but Shí Jìlóng's former general Má Qiū resisted him,
and Xūn retreated to Liángzhōu.
On the day Bǐng-chén in the eleventh month,
Shí Jiàn assassinated Shí Zūn and enthroned himself.
On the day Jǐ-yǒu in the twelfth month,
Shǐ Chíjié, Dūdū Xúyǎn Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Xúzhōu Cìshǐ, Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, Dūxiāng Hóu Chǔ Póu passed away.
Jiànwǔ Jiāngjūn, Wúguó Nèishǐ Xún Xiàn was appointed Shǐ Chíjié, Jiān Xúyǎn Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Běi Zhōnglángjiāng, Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the sixth year, in spring, the first month,
the Emperor held court,
but due to Chǔ Póu's funeral,
he suspended enjoyment of entertainment.
In the intercalary month,
Rǎn Mǐn assassinated Shí Jiàn,
usurped the title of Tiān Wáng,
and named his state Wèi.
Jiàn's younger brother Zhī usurped the imperial title at Xiāngguó.
On the day Dīng-chǒu,
a comet appeared in Kàng.
On the day Jǐ-chǒu,
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn Yīn Hào was given additional duties as Dūdū Yángyù Xúyǎn Qīng Wǔzhōu Zhūjūnshì and Jiǎjié.
The Dī chief Fú Hóng sent an envoy to surrender,
and was appointed Dī Wáng
and enfeoffed as Guǎngchuān Jùngōng.
Hóng's son, Jiàn, was granted Jié,
appointed Jiān Héběi Zhūjūnshì, Yòujiāngjūn,
and enfeoffed as Xiāngguó Xiàngōng.
In the third month,
Shí Jìlóng's former general Má Qiū poisoned Fú Hóng at Fāngtóu.
In summer, the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
Lújiāng Tàishǒu Yuán Zhēn attacked Héféi
and conquered it.
In the sixth month,
Shí Zhī sent his younger brother Kūn to attack Rǎn Mǐn's general Wáng Tài at Hándān,
and Kūn's army was defeated.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Fǔguó Jiāngjūn, Qiáo Wáng Wú Jì died.
Fú Jiàn led his forces into Guān.
In winter, the eleventh month,
Rǎn Mǐn besieged Xiāngguó.
In the twelfth month,
Sītú Cài Mó was dismissed to commoner status.
This year,
there was a great plague.
In the seventh year, in spring, on the dīng-yǒu day in the first month,
On the day Xīn-chǒu,
the Xiānbēi Duàn Kān surrendered with Qīngzhōu.
Fú Jiàn usurped the title of King
and named his state Qín.
On the day Wù-yín in the second month,
Duàn Kān was appointed Zhènběi Jiāngjūn
and enfeoffed as Qí Gōng.
Shí Zhī greatly defeated Rǎn Mǐn at Xiāngguó.
In summer, the fourth month,
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Sīmǎ Xūn led 30,000 infantry and cavalry,
entering Qínchuān from Hànzhōng,
and fought Fú Jiàn at Wǔzhàngyuán.
The imperial army was defeated.
Shàngshūlìng Gù Hé was granted Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
Liú Xiǎn assassinated Shí Zhī.
In the fifth month,
Zhī's Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Qǐ fled from Juānchéng to surrender.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Shàngshūlìng, Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Gù Hé passed away.
On the day Jiǎ-chén,
tidal waters entered Shítóu,
and several hundred people drowned.
In the eighth month,
Rǎn Mǐn's Yùzhōu Mù Zhāng Yù surrendered with Xǔchāng,
In the ninth month,
the two mausoleums of Jùnyáng and Tàiyáng collapsed.
On the day Jiǎ-chén,
the Emperor wore plain mourning clothes and presided over the Tàijí Diàn for three days,
sending Jiān Tàicháng Zhào Bá to repair the imperial tombs.
In winter, the tenth month,
there was thunder and rain,
with lightning.
In the eleventh month,
Shí Zhī's general Yáo Yìzhòng and Rǎn Mǐn's general Wèi Tuō each sent envoys to surrender.
and enfeoffed as Gāolíng Jùngōng;
Yìzhòng's son Xiāng was appointed Píngběi Jiāngjūn, Dūdū Bìngzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Bìngzhōu Cìshǐ, and Píngxiāng Xiàngōng;
On the day Xīn-wèi in the twelfth month,
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn Huán Wēn led his forces on a northern expedition,
reaching Wǔchāng and halting there.
At that time, Shí Jìlóng's former general Zhōu Chéng was garrisoned at Lǐnqīu,
Gāo Chāng at Yěwáng,
Lè Lì at Xǔchāng,
and Lǐ Lì at Wèiguó.
All successively surrendered.
In the eighth year, in spring, on the xīn-mǎo day in the first month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Liú Xiǎn usurped the imperial title at Xiāngguó,
but Rǎn Mǐn attacked and defeated him,
killing him.
Fú Jiàn usurped the imperial title at Cháng'ān.
In the second month,
the two mausoleums of Jùnpíng and Chóngyáng collapsed.
On the day Wù-chén,
the Emperor mourned for three days,
sending Diànzhōng Dūwèi Wáng Huì to Luòyáng
to guard the Five Mausoleums.
Zhènxī Jiāngjūn Zhāng Yù rebelled at Xǔchāng,
and had his partisan Shàngguān Ēn occupy Luòyáng.
Lè Hóng attacked Dūhù Dài Shī at Cāngyuán.
In the third month,
Běi Zhōnglángjiāng Xún Xiàn was stationed at Huáin.
Fú Jiàn's detached commander invaded Shùnyáng,
but Grand Administrator Xuē Zhēn attacked and defeated him.
In summer, the fourth month,
Rǎn Mǐn was destroyed by Mùróng Jùn.
Jùn usurped the imperial title at Zhōngshān
and called his state Yān.
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Xiè Shàng, along with Yáo Xiāng, fought Zhāng Yù at Jièqiáo in Xǔchāng.
The imperial army was defeated.
Fú Jiàn sent his younger brother Xióng to attack Yù
and captured him.
In autumn, the seventh month,
there was a great sacrifice for rain.
Shí Jìlóng's former general Wáng Zhuó sent an envoy to request surrender,
and was appointed Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn and Qínzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Dīng-yǒu,
Zhènjūn Dàjiāngjūn, Wǔlíng Wáng Xī was appointed Tàizǎi;
Fǔjūn Dàjiāngjūn, Kuàijī Wáng Yù was appointed Sītú;
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn Huán Wēn was appointed Tàiwèi.
In the eighth month,
the General Who Pacifies the West, Zhōu Fǔ, attacked Xiāo Jìngwén at Fúchéng
and beheaded him.
Rǎn Mǐn's son, Rǎn Zhì, surrendered Yè.
The Supervisor of the Army, Dài Shī, obtained the Imperial Seal of State Transmission
and sent it.
The inscription read:
"Received the Mandate of Heaven,
the Emperor's longevity is everlasting."
All the officials offered their congratulations.
In the ninth month,
Rǎn Zhì was captured by his general, Mǎ Yuàn,
and surrendered to Mùróng Kè.
The General of the Central Army, Yīn Hào, led his troops on a northern expedition.
He reached Sìkǒu,
and sent Dài Shī, the Administrator of Hénán, to hold Shímén,
and Liú [⿱丄卜?], the Administrator of Xíngyáng, to garrison Cāngyuán.
In winter, the tenth month,
Wáng Zhuó, the Inspector of Qínzhōu, was pressed by Fú Jiàn
and fled to Liángzhōu.
In the ninth year, spring, the first month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Zhāng Chónghuá sent Wáng Zhuó to fight Fú Jiàn's general, Fú Xióng,
and Wáng Zhuó's army suffered a crushing defeat.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Empress Dowager and the Emperor jointly paid respects at Jiànpínglíng.
In the third month,
there was a drought.
Ruǎn Fū, the Inspector of Jiāozhōu, attacked Fàn Fó of Línyì at Rìnán
and broke more than fifty of his stockades.
In summer, the fourth month,
Xiè Shàng, the General Who Guards the West, was appointed Minister of Personnel and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
In the fifth month,
there was a great plague.
Zhāng Chónghuá again sent Wáng Zhuó to attack Qínzhōu
and took it.
Yáng Chū, Duke of Qiúchí, was defeated by Fú Xióng.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
there was an earthquake,
〔一六〕with a sound like thunder.
In the eighth month,
Qīn, Prince of Héjiān and acting Grand Commandant, was sent to repair the Five Mausoleums.
In winter, the tenth month,
the General of the Central Army, Yīn Hào, advanced to Shānsāng,
and made Yáo Xiāng, the General Who Pacifies the North, his vanguard.
Yáo Xiāng rebelled
and counterattacked Yīn Hào.
Yīn Hào abandoned his baggage
and retreated to garrison Qiáochéng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Zhāng Chónghuá, the Governor of Liángzhōu, died.
His son Yàolíng succeeded him.
In this month,
Zhāng Zuò assassinated Yàolíng and proclaimed himself Governor of Liángzhōu.
In the eleventh month,
Yīn Hào sent his subordinates Liú Qǐ and Wáng Bīnzhī to attack Yáo Xiāng.
They were again defeated by Yáo Xiāng,
who then advanced to hold Sháopí.
In the twelfth month,
Xiè Shàng, the Minister of Personnel and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was additionally appointed General-in-Chief of the Armies of Yù, Yáng, and the western part of Jiāng,
and was made Inspector of Yùzhōu,
stationed at Lìyáng.
In the tenth year, spring, the first month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor held court.
Because the Five Mausoleums had not yet been restored,
he suspended music and was displeased.
Zhāng Zuò, the Governor of Liángzhōu, usurped the imperial title.
Zhōu Chéng, a surrendered general of Rǎn Mǐn, raised an army in rebellion
and attacked Luòyáng from Wǎnlíng.
〔一七〕On the day Xīnyǒu,
Dài Shī, the Administrator of Hénán, fled to Wěizhǔ.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
there was an earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Huán Wēn, the Grand Commandant and General Who Conquers the West, led his army to attack Guānzhōng.
Yīn Hào, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, was demoted to commoner.
Wáng Shù, formerly the Grand Administrator of Kuàijī, was appointed Inspector of Yángzhōu.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Huán Wēn fought Fú Jiàn's son, Fú Cháng, at Lántián
and utterly defeated him.
In the fifth month,
Guō Chǎng and others, *qǐhuó* (begging-for-life) refugees from Jiāngxī, seized Liú Shì, the Grand Administrator of Chénliú, and rebelled.
〔一八〕The capital was shaken with fright.
Zhōu Mǐn, the Minister of Personnel, was appointed General of the Central Army,
stationed at Zhōngtáng.
Xiè Shàng, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, returned from Lìyáng to guard the capital.
In the sixth month,
Fú Xióng, a general of Fú Jiàn, led all his troops and fought Huán Wēn at Báilùyuán,
and the imperial army suffered a crushing defeat.
In autumn, the ninth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Huán Wēn, running out of provisions,
withdrew.
In the eleventh year, spring, the first month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Tǒng, Prince of Rǔnán and Palace Attendant, died.
Yáng Chū, Duke of Qiúchí and Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiāng, was murdered by his subordinate Liáng Shì.
Chū's son, Guó, succeeded to the position,
and was then appointed General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Qínzhōu.
Duàn Kān, Duke of Qí, attacked Róng Guó, a general of Mùróng Jùn, at Lángshān
and defeated him.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Rénshēn,
there was a hoarfrost.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
there was an earthquake.
Yáo Xiāng led his troops to raid Wàihuáng,
and Gāo Jì, the General Who Commands the Army, utterly defeated him.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
there was another earthquake.
In the sixth month,
Fú Jiàn died.
His son, Fú Shēng, succeeded to the false throne.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Sòng Hùn and Zhāng Guàn assassinated Zhāng Zuò,
and enthroned Xuánjìng, Yàolíng's younger brother, as Grand General and Governor of Liángzhōu.
They sent envoys to surrender.
Zhōu Mǐn, the Minister of Personnel, was appointed Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat,
and Wáng Biāozhī, the General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed Right Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
In winter, the tenth month,
Xiè Shàng, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Armies of Bìng, Jì, and Yōu, and General Who Guards the West,
stationed at Mǎtóu.
In the twelfth month,
Mùróng Kè led his troops to raid Guǎnggù.
On the day Rénxū,
Féng Yāng of Shàngdǎng proclaimed himself Administrator,
betrayed Fú Shēng, and sent envoys to surrender.
In the twelfth year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
the Emperor held court.
Because of the mourning for the Empress Dowager's mother,
he suspended music and was displeased.
Duàn Kān, the General Who Guards the North, fought Mùróng Kè at Guǎnggù
and utterly defeated him.
Mùróng Kè retreated to hold Ānpíng.
In the second month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Emperor lectured on the *Classic of Filial Piety*.
In the third month,
Yáo Xiāng entered Xǔchāng.
Huán Wēn, the Grand Commandant, was appointed Grand Commander of the Punitive Expedition to attack him.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Huán Wēn fought Yáo Xiāng at Yīshuǐ
and utterly defeated him.
Yáo Xiāng fled to Píngyáng,
and moved his remaining troops, over three thousand households, between the Jiāng and Hàn rivers.
He captured Zhōu Chéng and returned.
He sent Má Mùzhī, the General Who Manifests Martial Might,
Chén Wǔ, the Supervisor of the Army,
and Dài Shī, the General Who Supports the State and Administrator of Hénán, to garrison Luòyáng.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Guǐsì,
there was a solar eclipse.
Mùróng Kè attacked Duàn Kān at Guǎnggù.
He sent Xún Xiàn, the General of the Northern Central Army, to lead an army to Lángyá to relieve Duàn Kān.
In the eleventh month,
Chē Guàn, acting Minister of Works and Palace Attendant,
Yuán Zhēn, the General Who Soars Like a Dragon, and others were sent with credentials to Luòyáng
to repair the Five Mausoleums.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngxū,
because of affairs concerning the Five Mausoleums,
an announcement was made at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
The Emperor and all the officials wore mourning clothes,
and mourned for three days at the Tàijí Hall.
In this year,
Yáng Guó, Duke of Qiúchí, was killed by his paternal cousin Jùn,
who then enthroned himself.
In the first year of Shēngpíng, spring, the first month, on the day Rénxū,
the Emperor came of age,
announced it at the Grand Ancestral Temple,
and began to personally handle all affairs of state.
A general amnesty was proclaimed,
the reign title was changed,
and the ranks of civil and military officials were raised by one grade.
The Empress Dowager resided in Chóngdé Palace.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
a meteor fell at Huáilǐ.
In this month,
Duàn Kān, the General Who Guards the North and Duke of Qí, was overthrown by Mùróng Kè
and perished.
Zhú Zhāntán of Fúnán presented a trained elephant.
〔一九〕The imperial edict stated:
"In the past, the late emperor, fearing that strange beasts from distant lands might cause harm to people,
forbade their entry.
Now, before it arrives,
it may be returned to its homeland."
In the third month,
the Emperor lectured on the *Classic of Filial Piety*.
On the day Rénshēn,
he personally offered sacrifices at the Zhōngtáng.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Xiè Shàng, the General Who Guards the West, died.
Fú Méi and
fought at Sānyuán,
and beheaded him.
In the sixth month,
Fú Jiān killed Fú Shēng and enthroned himself.
Xiè Yì, the Army Commander, was appointed Bearer of Credentials, General-in-Chief, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yùzhōu.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Zhāng Píng, a general of Fú Jiān, surrendered Bìngzhōu.
Consequently, he was appointed Inspector of Bìngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the *dìngwèi* day,
Empress Héshì was established.
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
Rice was bestowed upon the filial, the fraternal,
the widowed, and the solitary, five *hú* per person.
Unpaid rent and old debts were all to be waived.
There was a grand banquet for three days.
In winter, the tenth month,
the Empress paid respects at the Tàimiào.
In the eleventh month,
there was thunder.
In the twelfth month,
Wáng Biāozhī, the Tàicháng, was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè.
In the second year, in spring, the first month,
Sītú, King Yù of Kuàijī, bowed his head to return governance,
but the Emperor refused.
In the third month,
Mùróng Jùn captured various commanderies in Jìzhōu.
An edict commanded Ānxī Jiāngjūn Xiè Yì and Běizhōnglángjiāng Xún Xiàn to launch a northern expedition.
In the third month,
Cìfēi Dū Wáng Ráo presented a zhèn bird.
The Emperor was enraged,
whipped him two hundred times,
and ordered the Diànzhōng Yùshǐ to burn the bird at the Sìdá zhī Qú.
In summer, the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
A comet appeared in Tiānchuán.
In the sixth month,
Zhāng Píng, the Bìngzhōu Cìshǐ, being pressed by Fú Jiān,
led three thousand troops to Píngyáng.
Jiān pursued and defeated him.
Mùróng Kè advanced and occupied Shàngdǎng.
Guànjūn Jiāngjūn Féng Yāng with his troops rebelled and surrendered to Mùróng Jùn.
Jùn captured all the land north of the Yellow River.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Ānxī Jiāngjūn Xiè Yì died.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Xiè Wàn, the Wúxīng Tàishǒu, was appointed Xīzhōnglángjiāng, Chíjìe, Jiān Sī Yù Jì Bìng Sìzhōu Zhūjūnshì, and Yùzhōu Cìshǐ.
Xī Tán, the Sànqí Chángshì, was appointed Běizhōnglángjiāng, Chíjìe, Dūdū Xú Yǎn Qīng Jì Yōu Wǔzhōu Zhūjūnshì, and Xú Yǎn Èrzhōu Cìshǐ,
stationed at Xiàpī.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
King Cáo Mài of Chénliú died.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
there was thunder.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
there was an earthquake.
In the twelfth month,
Běizhōnglángjiāng Xún Xiàn and Mùróng Jùn fought at Shānchí,
and the imperial army was defeated.
In the third year, in spring, the third month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
an edict was issued stating that due to successive years of military campaigns,
food transport was insufficient.
From the imperial princes and dukes downward, thirteen households were to provide one person for one year to assist with transport.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Píngběi Jiāngjūn Gāo Chāng, being pressed by Mùróng Jùn,
fled from Báimǎ to Xíngyáng.
In winter, the tenth month, Mùróng Jùn raided Dōng'ā.
Xīzhōnglángjiāng Xiè Wàn was dispatched to Xiàcài,
and Běizhōnglángjiāng Xī Tán to Gāopíng to attack him,
but the imperial army was defeated.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Wáng Shù, the Yángzhōu Cìshǐ, was promoted to Wèijiāngjūn.
In the twelfth month,
Chūngjūn Jiāngjūn, King Pī of Lángyá, was again appointed Piàojì Jiāngjūn,
and King Yì of Dōnghǎi was appointed Chējì Jiāngjūn.
Xī, son of King Xī of Wǔlíng, was enfeoffed as King Liáng.
Wēn Fàngzhī, the Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ, led troops to attack Cānlí and Dānlǎo of Línyì,
and made them all surrender.
In the fourth year, in spring, the first month,
Gōng Yáng Jùn of Qiúchí died.
His son Shì succeeded him.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Mùróng Jùn died,
and his son Wěi succeeded to the bogus throne.
In the second month,
a phoenix with nine chicks was seen at Fēngchéng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
due to frequent military campaigns,
expenditures were reduced and meals curtailed.
In the eighth month, on the first day of *xīnchǒu*,
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
In winter, the tenth month,
a Tiāngǒu comet flowed in the southwest.
In the eleventh month,
Tàiwèi Huán Wēn was enfeoffed as Nánjùn Gōng.
Wēn's younger brother Chōng was enfeoffed as Fēngchéng Xiàn Gōng.
His son Jì was enfeoffed as Línhé Jùn Gōng.
A phoenix was again seen at Fēngchéng,
with many birds following it.
In the fifth year, in spring, the first month, on the *wùxū* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Rice, five *hú* per person, was bestowed upon the widowed, the solitary,
and those who could not support themselves.
Běizhōnglángjiāng, Dūdū Xú Yǎn Qīng Jì Yōu Wǔzhōu Zhūjūnshì, and Xú Yǎn Èrzhōu Cìshǐ Xī Tán died.
In the second month,
Zhènchūn Jiāngjūn Fàn Wāng was appointed Dūdū Xú Yǎn Qīng Jì Yōu Wǔzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Ānběi Jiāngjūn, and Xú Yǎn Èrzhōu Cìshǐ.
Píngnán Jiāngjūn, Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ, and Yángxià Hóu Téng Hán died.
In summer, the fourth month,
there was a great flood.
Tàiwèi Huán Wēn was stationed at Wǎn,
and sent his younger brother Huò to lead troops to capture Xǔchāng.
A phoenix was seen north of Miǎnrán.
In the fifth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
the Emperor died in the Xiǎnyáng Diàn,
aged nineteen at the time.
He was buried in Yǒngpíng Líng,
and given the temple name Xiàozōng.
Emperor Āi
Emperor Āi, personal name Pī,
courtesy name Qiānlíng,
was the eldest son of Emperor Chéng.
In the eighth year of Xiánkāng,
he was enfeoffed as King Lángyá.
In the first year of Yǒnghé, he was appointed Sànqí Chángshì.
In the twelfth year, he was promoted to Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn.
In the third year of Shēngpíng, he was appointed Piàojì Jiāngjūn.
In the fifth year, the fifth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
Emperor Mù died.
The Empress Dowager issued an edict:
"The Emperor suddenly succumbed to illness,
and no heir has been established.
King Pī of Lángyá is
of the legitimate line of the restoration,
and possesses brilliant virtue and great kinship.
Formerly in Xiánkāng,
he was slated to be the heir apparent.
However, being young and immature,
he was deemed not yet capable of handling national difficulties,
hence Xiǎnzōng humbly yielded.
Now, in terms of righteousness, prestige, and affection,
none can compare to him.
Let the King be installed in the grand succession."
Thereupon, all officials prepared the imperial carriage
and welcomed him at the Lángyá Residence.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
he ascended the imperial throne,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict stated:
"I have been fortunate to receive the clear mandate
and succeed to the grand succession.
Considering the ancestral temples of the former king,
without a master for offerings,
and the mourning court of the Grand Concubine,
utterly without reliance,
my grief and sorrow are profound,
tearing at my innermost being.
The dignity of the royal state
and the conjunction of emotion and ritual are paramount.
The importance of the heir
leaves no room for a second.
King Yì of Dōnghǎi is
a close relative.
He should inherit the main line.
Let Yì be King Lángyá."
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Emperor Mù was buried in Yǒngpíng Líng.
Mùróng Kè attacked and captured Yěwáng.
The defending general Lǚ Hù retreated and held Xíngyáng.
In the eighth month, on the night of *jǐmǎo*,
the sky split,
several *zhàng* wide,
with a sound like thunder.
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Empress Wángshì was established.
Empress Héshì of Emperor Mù was styled Yǒng'ān Gōng.
Lǚ Hù rebelled and fled to Mùróng Wěi.
In winter, the tenth month,
Ānběi Jiāngjūn Fàn Wāng was found guilty
and demoted to a commoner.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict stated:
"Xiǎnzōng, Emperor Chéng, in his dying testament,
considering the many difficulties of the time,
wished to promote the practices of the lofty ancient times,
and establish virtue broadly and heavily,
to ensure the prosperity of the state.
Yet, national misfortunes continued,
Kāng Mù died young,
and the imperial succession was not smooth.
I, with meager virtue,
have again inherited the ancestral legacy.
Reflecting on this eternal longing,
my grief and sorrow are overwhelming.
Indeed, the principle of generational order
should be rooted in natural family ties.
To inherit the body and succeed to the foundation
is an ancient and modern constant.
It is fitting to succeed Xiǎnzōng above,
to rectify the original line."
In the twelfth month,
Zhāng Xuánjìng, the Liángzhōu Cìshǐ, was promoted to Dàdūdū Lǒngyòu Zhūjūnshì, Hùqiāng Xiàowèi, and Xīpíng Gōng.
In the spring, the first month, on the *rénzǐ* day of the first year of Lónghé
a general amnesty was declared,
and the reign era was changed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the land tax was reduced;
each *mǔ* was to yield two *shēng*.
In this month,
Lǚ Hù and Fù Mòbō, generals of Mùróng Wěi, attacked and captured minor fortresses,
〔二三〕 thereby threatening Luòyáng.
In the second month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Yǔ Xī, Auxiliary General of the State and Administrator of Wú County, was appointed Northern Central Proctor and Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces,
stationed at Xiàpī;
Yuán Zhēn, Front Vanguard Supervisor and Dragon Gallop General, was appointed Western Central Proctor, Supervisor of Military Affairs of Yù, Sī, Bìng, and Jì provinces, and Inspector of Yù Province,
stationed at Rǔnán.
Both were granted *jié*.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the birth mother, Lady Zhōu, was honored as Empress Dowager.
In the third month, on the *jiǎyín* *shuò* day,
〔二四〕there was a solar eclipse.
In summer, the fourth month,
there was a drought.
An edict was issued to release minor offenders
and relieve the distressed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
there was an earthquake in Liáng Province,
〔二五〕and Hào Wěi Mountain collapsed.
Lǚ Hù again raided Luòyáng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Dài Shī, Auxiliary General of the State and Administrator of Hénán, fled to Wǎn.
In the fifth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Yǔ Xī, Northern Central Proctor, and Dèng Xiá, Administrator of Jìnglíng, were dispatched with a naval force to relieve Luòyáng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Lǚ Hù and others retreated to defend Xiǎopíngjīn.
Wáng Yì, Prince of Lángyé, was promoted to Grandee Remonstrant, General of Agile Cavalry, and was granted the right to establish a staff.
Dèng Xiá advanced and garrisoned Xīnchéng.
Hé Qiān, a subordinate general of Yǔ Xī, and Liú Zé, a general of Mùróng Wěi, engaged in battle at Tánqiū
and were defeated.
In the eighth month,
Yuán Zhēn, Western Central Proctor, advanced to Rǔnán
and transported fifty thousand *hú* of rice to supply Luòyáng.
In winter, the tenth month,
the poor were given rice,
five *hú* per person.
Zhāngwǔ Wáng Zhēn passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùwǔ* *shuò* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
An edict stated:
“Military campaigns are underway,
and we have not been able to lighten taxes and labor.
The celestial phenomena are out of order,
and severe drought is causing harm.
Is it that governance is not harmonious,
or that there are unacknowledged talents like those of Bǎizhú and Wèibīn?
Let hidden talents be sought out and promoted,
harsh and trivial regulations be abolished,
and laws and ordinances be thoroughly discussed,
with all things tending towards reduction and essentiality.”
Yǔ Xī retreated from Xiàpī to garrison Shānyáng.
Yuán Zhēn retreated from Rǔnán to garrison Shòuyáng.
In the spring, the second month, on the *jǐhài* day of the first year of Xīngníng,
〔二六〕a general amnesty was declared,
and the reign era was changed.
In the third month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Empress Dowager passed away at her residence in Lángyé.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor rushed to mourn.
An edict commanded Sītú and Kuàijī Wáng Yù to oversee all internal and external affairs.
In summer, the fourth month,
Mùróng Wěi raided Xíngyáng.
The Administrator Liú Yuǎn fled to Lǔyáng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
there was an earthquake in Yáng Province,
and lakes and waterways overflowed.
In the fifth month,

Huán Wēn, General Who Conquers the West, was additionally granted the titles of Grandee Remonstrant, Grand Marshal, Superintendent of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside the Capital, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and was granted the Yellow Ax.
Yuán Zhēn, Western Central Proctor, was again appointed Supervisor of Military Affairs of Sī, Jì, and Bìng provinces.
Yǔ Xī, Northern Central Proctor, was appointed Supervisor of Military Affairs of Qīng Province.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Mùróng Wěi captured Mìchéng.
Liú Yuǎn, Administrator of Xíngyáng, fled to Jiānglíng.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Zhāng Tiānxī assassinated Zhāng Xuánjìng, Inspector of Liáng Province and Duke of Xīpíng,
and declared himself Grand General, Protector of the Qiāng, Shepherd of Liáng Province, and Duke of Xīpíng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Empress Dowager Zhāng was interred.
In the eighth month,
a comet appeared in the asterisms of Jiǎo and Kàng,
entering Tiānshì.
In the ninth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Grand Marshal Huán Wēn led his army in a northern expedition.
On the *guǐhài* day,
due to the birth of an imperial prince,
a general amnesty was declared.
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Huī, heir apparent of Chénliú Wáng, was established as king.
In the eleventh month,
Zhāng Jùn, a former general of Yáo Xiāng, killed Zhào Pí, Supervisor of Jiāng Province,
burned Wǔchāng,
plundered the imperial treasury, and rebelled.
Huán Chōng, Inspector of Jiāng Province, attacked and beheaded him.
In this year,
Mùróng Chén, a general of Mùróng Wěi, attacked Yuán Pī, Administrator of Chénliú, at Chángpíng.
Zhū Bīn, Administrator of Rǔnán, took advantage of the void to raid Xǔchāng
and captured it.
In the spring, the second month, on the *gēngyín* day of the second year,
there was an earthquake in Jiānglíng.
Mùróng Píng, a general of Mùróng Wěi, raided Xǔchāng.
Lǐ Fú, Administrator of Yǐngchuān, died there.
Píng then invaded Rǔnán.
Zhū Bīn, Administrator, fled to Shòuyáng.
He further advanced to besiege Chén County.
Zhū Fǔ, Administrator, fortified the city and held out.
Huán Wēn dispatched Liú Hù, Chancellor of Jiāngxià, to attack and repel them.
The title of General of the Left Army was changed to General of Agile Cavalry.
The offices of General of the Right Army, General of the Front Army, General of the Rear Army, and the three general ranks of the Five Schools were abolished.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor personally ploughed the ceremonial field.
In the third month, on the *gēngxū* *shuò* day,
a large review of households was conducted,
and strict laws and prohibitions were enforced,
known as the *Gēngxū* Regulations.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor was unwell.
The Emperor had a deep fondness for Huáng-Lǎo Daoism,
practiced *duàngǔ* (abstention from grains),
and consumed elixirs of immortality.
Excessive intake
led to poisoning,
rendering him unable to attend to affairs of state.
Empress Dowager Chóngdé once again took charge of court affairs as regent.
