In summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Mùróng Wěi dispatched his general Lǐ Hóng to invade Xǔchāng.
The imperial army suffered a defeat at Xuánhù.
Zhū Bīn fled to Huáinán.
Zhū Fǔ retreated to secure Péngchéng.
Huán Wēn dispatched Yuán Zhēn, Western Central Proctor, and Liú Hù, Chancellor of Jiāngxià, among others, to dig the Yángyí canal to facilitate transport.
Wēn led his naval forces to Héfèi.
Mùróng Chén again garrisoned Xǔchāng.
In the fifth month,
the people of Chén were moved to dry land to avoid them.
〔二七〕On the *wùchén* day,
Wáng Shù, Inspector of Yáng Province, was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Guards.
Huán Wēn was appointed Administrator of Yáng Province and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an envoy was sent to summon Wēn to serve as Chancellor,
but Wēn refused.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wēn was again summoned to court.
In the eighth month,
Wēn arrived at Zhěqí,
then built a city there and resided in it.
Fú Jiān's separate commanders invaded Hénán.
Mùróng Wěi raided Luòyáng.
In the ninth month,
Chén Yòu, General of the Champions, left Shěn Jìn, Chief Clerk, to defend Luòyáng
and led his troops to flee to Xīnchéng.
In the spring, the first month, on the *gēngshēn* day of the third year,
Empress Wáng passed away.
In the second month,
on the *yǐwèi* day,

Huán Huò, General of the Right, was appointed Supervisor of Military Affairs of Jīng Province, Yáng Province's Yìchéng, Yōng Province's Jīngzhào, and concurrently Southern Barbarian Commandant and Inspector of Jīng Province;

Huán Chōng was appointed Supervisor of Military Affairs of Jiāng Province, Jīng Province's Jiāngxià and Suí County, Yù Province's Rǔnán, Xīyáng, Xīncài, and Yǐngchuān (six counties), Southern Central Proctor, and Inspector of Jiāng Province,
concurrently Southern Barbarian Commandant.
Both were granted *jié*.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor passed away in the Western Hall
at the age of twenty-five.
He was interred in Ānpínglíng.
The deposed Emperor, Hǎixī Gōng
was named Yì,
courtesy name Yánlíng,
and was the younger brother of Emperor Āi by the same mother.
In the eighth year of Xiánkāng, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dōnghǎi.
In the eighth year of Yǒnghé, he was appointed Palace Attendant,
soon after promoted to General Who Stabilizes the Army;
in the fourth year of Shēngpíng, he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
In the fifth year,
he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lángyé.
At the beginning of Lónghé,
he was transferred to Grandee Remonstrant, General of Agile Cavalry, and was granted the right to establish a staff with powers equal to the Three Revered Ministers.
In the second month, *bǐngshēn* day, of the third year of Xīngníng,
Emperor Āi passed away,
without an heir.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict saying:
"The Emperor's illness could not be cured after all;
difficulties and calamities repeatedly befell us,
and his lineage has become extinct.
My grief is unbearable.
Wáng Yì, the Prince of Lángxié,
possesses brilliant virtue and is a close relative,
fitting to be the successor.
He should revere the ancestors
and succeed to the great lineage.
He should quickly rectify the grand ceremony
to bring peace to both people and spirits."
Thereupon, all officials welcomed him at the Lángxié residence.
On that same day,
he ascended the imperial throne
and declared a general amnesty.
In the third month, *rénshēn* day,
Emperor Āi was buried at Ānpíng Líng.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
Sànqí Chángshì and Prince Qīn of Héjiān passed away.
On *bǐngzǐ* day,
〔二八〕Mùróng Wěi's general, Mùróng Kè, captured Luòyáng.
Níngshuò General Zhú Yáo fled to Xiāngyáng,
while Guānjūn Chángshǐ and Yángwǔ General Shěn Jìng died there.
In the sixth month, *wùzǐ* day, of summer,
Shǐchíjié, Dūdū Yì Níng Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Zhènxī Jiāngjūn, Yìzhōu Cìshǐ, and Jiànchéng Gōng Zhōu Fǔ passed away.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Xiongnú Zuǒxiánwáng Wèi Chén and Yòuxiánwáng Cáo Gǔ led a force of twenty thousand to invade Fú Jiān's Xìngchéng.
〔二九〕On *jǐyǒu* day,
Wáng Yù, the Prince of Kuàijī, was re-enfeoffed as the Prince of Lángxié.
On *rénzǐ* day,
Empress Yǔ was established.
Chāngmíng, son of Wáng Yù, the Prince of Lángxié, was enfeoffed as the Prince of Kuàijī.
In the tenth month of winter,
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Sīmǎ Xūn rebelled,
proclaiming himself Prince of Chéngdū.
In the eleventh month,
he led his troops to Jiàngé,
attacking Fú.
Xīyí Xiàowèi Wúqiū Wěi abandoned the city and fled.
On *yǐmǎo* day,
he besieged Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Zhōu Chǔ in Chéngdū.
Huán Wēn dispatched Jiāngxià Xiàng Zhū Xù to rescue him.
In the twelfth month, *wùxū* day,
Kuàijī Nèishǐ Wáng Biāozhī was appointed Shàngshū Púyè.
In the second month, *jǐchǒu* day, of spring of the first year of Tàihé,
Liángzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Tiānxī was appointed Dàjiāngjūn, Dūdū Lǒngyòu Guānzhōng Zhūjūnshì, and Xīpíng Jùngōng.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
Xuānchéng Nèishǐ Huán Mì was appointed Chíjié, Jiān Liáng Yì Èrzhōu Zhēngtǎo Zhūjūnshì.
In the third month, *xīnhài* day,
Xīncài Wáng Miǎo passed away.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Huán Huò sent Dūhù Huán Pí to attack Nánzhèng.
Bì Qīn of Wèixīng raised an army in response to Pí.
In the fourth month of summer,
there was a drought.
In the fifth month, *wùyín* day,
Empress Yǔ passed away.
Zhū Xù attacked Sīmǎ Xūn in Chéngdū.
His army collapsed;
Xūn was captured
and beheaded.
In the seventh month, *guǐyǒu* day, of autumn,
Empress Xiào was buried at Jìngpíng Líng.
In the ninth month, *jiǎwǔ* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Liáng and Yì prefectures.
In the tenth month, *xīnchǒu* day, of winter,
Fú Jiān's generals Wáng Měng and Yáng Ān attacked Nánxiāng.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Huán Huò went to rescue it.
His army reached Xīnyě, and Měng and Ān retreated.
Wáng Yù, the Prince of Kuàijī, was appointed Chéngxiàng.
In the twelfth month,
Zhào Hóng, Zhào Yì, and others from Nányáng rebelled, occupying Wǎnchéng.
Tàishǒu Huán Dàn fled to secure Xīnyě.
〔三０〕Mùróng Wěi's general Mùróng Lì captured Lǔ Jùn and Gāopíng.
In the first month of spring of the second year,
Běizhōnglángjiāng Yǔ Xī committed a crime
and fled into the sea.
In the fourth month of summer,
Mùróng Wěi's general Mùróng Chén plundered Jìnglín.
Tàishǒu Luó Chóng attacked and defeated him.
Fú Jiān's general Wáng Měng plundered Liángzhōu.
Zhāng Tiānxī resisted him,
and Měng's army was defeated.
In the fifth month,
Yòujiāngjūn Huán Huò attacked Zhào Yì,
causing him to flee.
He advanced and captured Mùróng Wěi's general Zhào Pán,
sending him to the capital.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Kuàijī Nèishǐ Xī Yīn was appointed Dūdū Xú Yǎn Qīng Yōu Sìzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Píngběi Jiāngjūn, and Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the tenth month, *yǐsì* day, of winter,
Péngchéng Wáng Xuán passed away.
On *dīngsì* day, the first day of the third month of spring of the third year,
there was a solar eclipse.
On *guǐhài* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
In the fourth month, *guǐsì* day, of summer,
there was a hailstorm
and strong winds that broke trees.
In the eighth month, *rènyín* day, of autumn,
Shàngshū Lìng, Wèijiāngjūn, and Lántián Hóu Wáng Shù passed away.
In the fourth month, *gēngxū* day, of summer of the fourth year,
Dàsīmǎ Huán Wēn led his troops to campaign against Mùróng Wěi.
In the seventh month, *xīnmǎo* day, of autumn,
Wěi's general Mùróng Chuí led his troops to resist Wēn.
Wēn attacked and defeated him.
〔三一〕
In the ninth month, *wùyín* day,
Huán Wēn's subordinate generals Dèng Xiá and Zhū Xù encountered Wěi's general Fù Mòbō at Línzhǔ,
and again heavily defeated him.
On *wùzǐ* day,
Wēn arrived at Fāngtóu.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
due to an interrupted grain supply,
he burned his boats and returned.
On *xīnchǒu* day,
Mùróng Chuí pursued and defeated Wēn's rear guard at Xiāngyì.
In the tenth month of winter,
a large star streaked westward,
with a sound like thunder.
On *jǐsì* day,
Wēn gathered his scattered soldiers
and encamped at Shānyáng.
Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Yuán Zhēn rebelled at Shòuyáng.
In the eleventh month, *xīnchǒu* day,
Huán Wēn met Wáng Yù, the Prince of Kuàijī, at Túzhōng from Shānyáng,
planning a future campaign.
In the twelfth month,
he then captured Guǎnglíng and resided there.
In the first month, *jǐhài* day, of spring of the fifth year,
Yuán Zhēn's sons, Shuāngzhī and Àizhī, murdered Liángguó Nèishǐ Zhū Xiàn and Rǔnán Nèishǐ Zhū Bīn.
In the second month, *guǐyǒu* day,
Yuán Zhēn died.
Chénjùn Tàishǒu Zhū Fǔ established Zhēn's son Jǐn as his successor
and sought aid from Mùróng Wěi.
In the fourth month, *xīnwèi* day, of summer,
Huán Wēn's subordinate general Zhú Yáo defeated Jǐn at Wǔqiū.
On *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the seventh month of autumn,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eighth month, *guǐchǒu* day,
Huán Wēn attacked Yuán Jǐn at Shòuyáng
and defeated him.
In the ninth month,
Fú Jiān's general Wáng Měng attacked Mùróng Wěi
and captured his Shàngdǎng.
Li Hóng, a demon rebel from Guǎnghàn, and Lǐ Jīngēn, a demon rebel from Yìzhōu, gathered a crowd and rebelled.
〔三二〕Hóng proclaimed himself Sage King,
with over ten thousand followers.
Zītóng Tàishǒu Zhōu Xiāo suppressed and pacified them.
In the tenth month of winter,
Wáng Měng heavily defeated Mùróng Wěi's general Mùróng Píng at Lùchuān.
In the eleventh month,
Měng captured Yè,
seized Mùróng Wěi,
and took full control of his territory.
In the first month of spring of the sixth year,
Fú Jiān dispatched his general Wáng Jiàn to aid Yuán Jǐn.
General Huán Yī intercepted and attacked him,
heavily defeating him.
On *dīnghài* day,
Huán Wēn captured Shòuyáng
and beheaded Yuán Jǐn.
In the third month, *rénchén* day,
Jiān Yì Níng Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì, Guānjūn Jiāngjūn, Yìzhōu Cìshǐ, and Jiànchéng Gōng Zhōu Chǔ passed away.
In the fourth month, *wùwǔ* day, of summer,
a general amnesty was declared,
and rice was bestowed upon the poor and solitary,
five *hú* per person.
Fú Jiān's general Fú Yǎ attacked Qiúchí.
Yáng Zuǎn, the Duke of Qiúchí, surrendered to him.
In the sixth month,
the capital, along with Dānyáng, Jìnlíng, Wú Jùn, Wúxìng, and Línhǎi, all experienced great floods.
In the eighth month of autumn,
former Níngzhōu Cìshǐ Zhōu Zhòngsūn was appointed Jiǎjié, Jiān Yì Liáng Èrzhōu Zhūjūnshì, and Yìzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the tenth month, *rénzǐ* day, of winter,
Gāomì Wáng Jùn passed away.
In the eleventh month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Huán Wēn moved from Guǎnglíng and encamped at Báishí.
On the day *dīngwèi*,
he went to the court,
and then plotted the emperor's deposition.
He falsely accused the emperor of having suffered from an old debilitating illness since his time as a prince,
and that his favorites Xiàng Lóng, Jì Hǎo, Zhū Língbǎo, and others attended him in his inner chambers.
Moreover, two beautiful women, Lady Tián and Lady Mèng, had given birth to three sons.
He intended to enfeoff the eldest.
People at the time were bewildered by this.
Huán Wēn then covertly urged the Empress Dowager to undertake the actions of Yī and Huò.
On the day *jǐyǒu*,
the hundred officials were assembled in the court hall,
and an edict from Empress Dowager Chóngdé was proclaimed, stating:
"The imperial house faces difficulties.
Mù-dì and Āi-dì had short reigns,
the national succession was not nurtured,
and no heir apparent was established.
Lángyé Wáng Yì, being a close younger brother,
was therefore brought in to assume the great position.
Unexpectedly, his virtue was not established,
leading to this state of affairs.
He is muddled and disorderly,
constantly violating ritual norms.
He has these three abominable sons,
and it is unknown whose children they are.
Human morality is lost,
and scandalous rumors spread far and wide.
Since he cannot uphold the altars of soil and grain,
nor reverently continue the ancestral temples,
and moreover, these illegitimate sons are growing up,
he intends to establish one as heir apparent.
To deceive and betray the ancestors,
and to shake the imperial foundation—
if this can be tolerated,
what cannot be borne?
Now, Yì is deposed as Dōnghǎi Wáng,
and the king is to return to his residence,
with guard and attendance ceremonies
all according to the precedent of Chāngyì in the Hàn dynasty.
But this unfortunate widow [referring to herself]
suffers from these myriad worries.
Recalling the living and the deceased,
my heart is as if cut.
For the grand plan of the altars of soil and grain,
I am compelled by righteousness.
As I write this, my grief is overwhelming;
how can I speak of it?"
Thereupon, the hundred officials entered the Tàijí Qiándiàn.
On that very day, Huán Wēn ordered the Palace Attendant Liú Xiǎng to seize the emperor's seals and ribbons.
The emperor, wearing a white turban and plain clothes,
walked down the Xītáng,
and rode out of the Shénshòumén in a ox-cart.
The assembled officials bowed in farewell,
all weeping sorrowfully.
The Imperial Censor and Palace Administrator, leading a hundred soldiers, escorted him to the residence of Dōnghǎi.
Initially,
Huán Wēn harbored disloyal ambitions,
wishing first to achieve merit north of the Yellow River [Héshuò]
to gain popular support.
But after the defeat at Fāngtóu,
his prestige and reputation suffered a setback,
so he secretly plotted to depose and enthrone [an emperor]
to strengthen his authority.
However, he was wary of the emperor's adherence to principle,
fearing public criticism.
Since the imperial inner chambers were heavily guarded and private,
and slander regarding the bedchamber was easy,
he therefore declared the emperor to be an eunuch,
and thus carried out his deposition and humiliation.
Initially,
the emperor had always been concerned about this throughout his life,
and once summoned the diviner Hù Qiān to consult the oracle.
After the divination was completed,
Hù Qiān replied:
"The Jìn house has the solidity of a bedrock,
but Your Majesty has the omen of leaving the palace."
It indeed turned out as he said.
In the first month of the second year of Xián'ān,
the emperor was demoted and enfeoffed as Hǎixī Xiàn Gōng.
In the fourth month,
he was moved to Wúxiàn,
and the Magistrate of Wú Commandery, Diāo Yí, was ordered to guard him.
Additionally, the Imperial Censor Gù Yǔn was dispatched to supervise him.
In the eleventh month,
the rebel leader Lú Sǒng sent his disciple, the Palace Administrator Xǔ Lóng, to his gate in the morning,
claiming to have a secret edict from the Empress Dowager
to welcome and restore him.
The emperor initially intended to follow him,
but accepted his wet nurse's advice and stopped.
Xǔ Lóng said:
"The great matter is about to succeed,
why listen to the words of women and children?"
The emperor said:
"I have sinned here,
and fortunately received leniency.
How dare I act rashly!
Moreover, if there were an edict from the Empress Dowager,
then officials should come.
Why send only you?
You must be causing trouble."
He then shouted to his attendants to bind him,
and Xǔ Lóng, fearful, fled.
The emperor knew that the mandate of heaven could not be regained,
and deeply worried about unexpected calamity.
So he stopped listening and thinking,
without thought or worry,
indulging in pleasures all day,
addicted to his inner concubines,
and not raising his sons,
hoping to preserve his natural lifespan.
People at the time pitied him
and wrote songs for him.
The court, seeing that the emperor was content with humiliation,
no longer worried about him.
In the tenth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*, of the eleventh year of Tàiyuán,
he passed away in Wú,
at the age of forty-five.
The historian says: Xiàozōng, from the state of being an infant in swaddling clothes,
used the transforming influence of his mother.
For over ten years, there was peace within and without.
With the talent of Wǔ'ān,
he opened up the borders;
with the style of Wén Wáng,
it spread over the Jiāng and Hàn regions.
Then, what Confucius called, 'I have no objection to him!'
Āi Huáng was magnanimous and benevolent,
fit to be a ruler,
but grand sacrifices to avert heaven's wrath
tainted his virtue.
Dōnghǎi [referring to the deposed emperor] refused Xǔ Lóng's carriage,
and humbled himself before the defiant minister.
This is what is called 'the soft overcoming the hard and strong,'
allowing him to live out his natural years.
The eulogy says:
He cast aside his robes,
declaring transformation,
great filial piety was his principle.
He followed those saints and good men,
achieving genuine reverence.
The western banner reached Yùlěi,
the northern banner reached Jīnyōng.
The relocated Yīn and old Bó [tribes],
all came to follow.
Āi Hòu was magnanimous and benevolent,
his spirit gathered.
Hǎixī faced many troubles,
the disaster of the time reached him.
He was different from Āhéng,
I am not Chāngyì.
Collation Notes
Annals of Emperors, No. 9: Emperor Jiǎnwén
Emperor Jiǎnwén, given name Yù,
courtesy name Dàowàn,
was the youngest son of Yuán-dì.
He was intelligent and precocious in childhood,
and beloved by Yuán-dì.
Guō Pú saw him and said to others:
"The one who will revive the Jìn dynasty [Jìnzuò]
will surely be this man."
As he grew up, he was pure, serene, and had few desires,
especially skilled in玄言 [xuányán] discourse.
In the first year of Yǒngchāng,
Yuán-dì issued an edict stating:
"My late father Wǔ Wáng and late grandfather Gōng Wáng ruled Lángyé,
with succession passed down through generations.
The national heir had not been established,
and the ancestral sacrifices lacked a master.
I often feel grief in my heart.
My son Yù is benevolent, intelligent, and possesses great wisdom;
he can reverently attend to the ancestral temple [Zōngmiào]
to comfort the boundless kindness.
Therefore, Yù is enfeoffed as Lángyé Wáng,
and will draw revenue from Kuàijī and Xuānchéng as before."
In the first year of Xiánhé,
his birth mother, Lady Zhèng, passed away.
The emperor was seven years old at the time,
and wept bitterly in mourning,
insisting on wearing heavy mourning clothes.
Chéng-dì pitied him and allowed it,
so he was moved and enfeoffed as Kuàijī Wáng,
and appointed Palace Attendant [Sànqí Chángshì].
In the ninth year,
he was promoted to General of the Right [Yòu Jiāngjūn],
and additionally appointed Attendant-in-ordinary [Shìzhōng].
In the sixth year of Xiánkāng, he was promoted to General of the Guards [Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn],
and concurrently held the position of Director of the Imperial Library [Mìshū Jiān].
In the first year of Jiànyuán, in the fifth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Emperor Kāng decreed:
“The Grand Master of Ceremonies (Tàicháng) is responsible for serving Heaven and Earth,
and also manages the ancestral temples.
The duties involved
can be said to be weighty.
Therefore, throughout history, those selected for this position
have invariably been chosen with keen discernment from among the eminent men of the time,
and were also refined scholars.
Winding-Stair King Shū Lǚ (Huìjī Wáng Shū Lǚ) embraces purity and emptiness,
and is unwavering in his devotion to the Dao.
He leisurely occupies the highest ranks,
offering advice and opinions in the imperial court.
He shall continue to hold his original post as Grand Master of Ceremonies (Tàicháng) as before.”
In the first year of Yǒnghé,
Empress Dowager Chóngdé presided over the court,
and he was promoted to General-in-chief Who Soothes the Army (Fǔjūn Dàjiàngjūn) and Supervisor of the Six Departments of the Imperial Secretariat (Lù Shàngshū Liù Tiáoshì).
In the second year,
Piaojī Hécōng died.
Empress Dowager Chóngdé decreed that the Emperor should personally oversee all affairs of state.
In the eighth year,
he was promoted to Minister of Works (Sītú),
but he firmly declined the appointment.
When Emperor Mù was first capped,
the Emperor kowtowed and offered to return governance,
but was not permitted.
When the deposed Emperor ascended the throne,
since the King of Lángxié had no heir,
he was again transferred and enfeoffed as King of Lángxié.
His son Chāngmíng was enfeoffed as King of Huìjī.
The Emperor firmly declined,
and thus, although enfeoffed as Lángxié, he did not abandon the title of Huìjī.
In the first year of Tàihé,
he was promoted to Chancellor (Chéngxiàng) and Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat (Lù Shàngshūshì),
and was permitted to enter the court without hurrying,
to be announced without being named,
to wear his sword and shoes into the palace,
and was granted a feather banner, drum and wind instruments, and sixty sword-wielding guards.
He again firmly declined.
When the deposed Emperor was deposed,
the Empress Dowager decreed:
“The Chancellor (Chéngxiàng), Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat (Lù Shàngshū), and King of Huìjī (Huìjī Wáng) is a direct descendant of Zhōngzōng.
He possesses brilliant virtue and excellent qualities,
and is outstanding, profound, and detached.
His spirit resides outside worldly affairs.
Because he is fully trusted and competent,
he has served as the chief minister for three generations.
His moral influence has spread far and wide,
and the people's hopes have long converged on him.
This has been the case for a long time.
It is fitting to follow the will of Heaven and man,
and to govern the imperial realm.
The authorities should clearly adhere to the old precedents
and implement this in due course.”
Thereupon, Grand Marshal Huán Wēn (Dàsīmǎ Huán Wēn) led the officials into the Taijián Front Hall,
prepared the imperial carriage and ceremonial procession,
and respectfully welcomed the Emperor from his Huìjī residence.
In the court hall, the Emperor changed his attire,
donning a plain kerchief and single robe,
and facing east, bowed to receive the imperial seal and ribbon.
In the first year of Xián'ān, in the eleventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
he ascended the imperial throne.
Huán Wēn moved his quarters to the central hall
and ordered troops to guard it.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Wēn memorialized to depose Grand Tutor (Tàizǎi) and King Wǔlíng Xī (Wǔlíng Wáng Xī) and his son Zǒng.
A decree ordered the Administrator of Wèijùn, Máo Ānzhī, to lead his assigned palace guards within the palace.
The era name was changed to Xián'ān.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhou Yí (Zhōu Yí), acting as Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), was sent to announce the news at the ancestral temple.
On the day Xīnhài,
Huán Wēn sent his younger brother Mì to compel King Xīncài Huǎng (Xīncài Wáng Huǎng) to go to the Western Hall
and confess his conspiracy to rebel with Grand Tutor (Tàizǎi) and King Wǔlíng Xī (Wǔlíng Wáng Xī) and others.
The Emperor wept when confronted,
and Wēn had them all arrested and handed over to the Court of Judicial Review (Tíngwèi).
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the two sons of the King of Dōnghǎi and their mother were killed.
Originally,
the Emperor, being pure, detached, and noble,
had governed for three generations,
and Wēn had always respected and feared him.
When the Emperor first ascended the throne,
Wēn had prepared a statement to present himself,
but when the Emperor granted him an audience
and wept before him,
Wēn was intimidated and unable to speak.
At this point,
the relevant authorities, acting on Wēn's implicit instruction,
memorialized for the execution of King Wǔlíng Xī (Wǔlíng Wáng Xī).
The Emperor did not permit it.
Wēn insisted repeatedly,
and the Emperor replied with an imperial handwritten decree:
“If the Jin dynasty's destiny is long-lasting,
then you should obediently carry out the previous decree.
If, however, the great fortune has departed,
then please yield the path to the worthy.”
Wēn read it,
sweated and changed color,
and dared not speak again.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xī and his three sons were deposed
and exiled to Xīn'ān.
On the day Bǐngchén,
King Xīncài Huǎng (Xīncài Wáng Huǎng) was banished to Héngyáng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
a decree stated:
“The royal house has suffered many misfortunes;
Emperors Mù and Āi died young,
the imperial lineage was removed prematurely,
and the divine artifacts (throne) lacked a master.
The King of Dōnghǎi, as a younger brother of the same mother and a close relative,
entered to inherit the great succession.
After ruling for a year,
he was dim-witted and disrupted norms,
losing human ethics.
Great calamity was approaching,
and the spirits of our ancestors would have no one to rely on.
The Empress Dowager deeply feared for the imperial foundation
and made a major decision at the time.
The Grand Marshal (Dàsīmǎ), following the will of Heaven and man,
and collaborating with divine strategy,
personally led the nobles
to respectfully receive the bright mandate.
With the clouds and mist dispersed,
the imperial realm became clear.
Then, looking to my humble self,
I respectfully received this grand inheritance.
Even Yī Yǐn's stabilization of the Yin court
or Bólù's pacification of the Hàn house
could not surpass this.
I, with meager virtue,
have presumptuously taken the supreme position.
I am truly fearful and insignificant,
unable to bear this heavy responsibility.
Trembling with apprehension,
I know not how to succeed.
Wishing to renew with all the people,
there shall be a great amnesty throughout the realm,
a great five-day feast,
and all civil and military officials shall have their ranks increased by two grades.
Filial, loyal, chaste widows, orphans, and the solitary shall each receive five hú of rice.”
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wēn's army of thirty thousand men was granted
one bolt of cloth per person
and one hú of rice.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Grand Marshal Huán Wēn (Dàsīmǎ Huán Wēn) was promoted to Chancellor (Chéngxiàng),
but he refused.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Wēn returned from Báishí
and then garrisoned Gūshú.
Champion General Máo Wǔshēng (Guànjūn Jiàngjūn Máo Wǔshēng) was appointed Military Commissioner of the forces in Miǎnzhōng of Jīngzhōu and Yìchéng of Yángzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
a decree stated that since the capital had a year's worth of provisions,
the transport of grain for one year would be temporarily suspended.
On the day Gēngyín,
the deposed King of Dōnghǎi Yì (Dōnghǎi Wáng Yì) was made Duke of Hǎixī (Hǎixī Gōng),
with an estate of four thousand households.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Énglù wine was first offered at the ancestral temple.
In the second year, in the first month of spring, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the kings of Báijì and Línyì each sent envoys to present local products.
In the second month,
Fú Jiān attacked Mùróng Huán in Liáodōng
and destroyed him.
In the third month, on the *dìngyǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“I, Zhèn, residing as *Āhéng* for three generations,
was unable to bring about the *shíyōng* of that time,
which led to *Hǎixī*'s loss of virtue,
almost overturning the imperial succession.
It is thanks to the virtue of the ancestral spirits and deities,
the *Huángtàihòu*'s virtuous nature that responded to the opportune moment,
the loyal and worthy *fānbǔ*,
and the united efforts of all officials,
that we were able to sweep away the mists and clouds in the vast heavens,
and radiate the morning brilliance throughout the universe.
Thus, with my humble self,
I was entrusted with the position above the *wánggōng*.
I rely on the multitude of worthy individuals
to assist me in my shortcomings.
Indeed, to strengthen the fundamental and curb the trivial,
to suppress extravagance and competition,
to make the clear and the turbid flow separately,
and the capable and the incapable distinguished,
so that offices have no corrupt policies,
and scholars no slanderous criticisms—
if there are no rewards or punishments,
then how can virtue and propriety be applied?
Moreover, the powerful enemies have not been eliminated,
and the labors and toils have not ceased.
Apart from the essentials of military affairs, state ceremonies, and sacrifices,
all extravagant and wasteful expenditures shall be reduced.
As for the worthy who live in seclusion in remote valleys,
and the gentlemen who either stay aloof or engage in worldly affairs—
though their aspirations may reach the dark skies,
and they may conceal themselves in secluded caves,
would they not be willing to humble their noble principles
to further the beauty of harmonious assistance?
How does that compare to those who are content with mountains and waters,
dwelling leisurely in hills and valleys,
pursuing the purity of a common man,
but forgetting the great cause of benefiting all?
The ancients did not borrow worthy men from previous generations;
I, Zhèn, therefore ponder on them today.
All officials, both inside and outside the court,
should diligently perform their duties,
so that good deeds are not unreported,
and evil deeds are not unheard of,
so that poets have no criticism of those who eat without working,
and I can achieve my sincere desire.”
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict stated:
“I have inherited the grand foundation of my ancestors,
but am ignorant of the way of governance,
fearing I cannot rightly manage the celestial work,
and splendidly continue the former achievements.
From dawn to dusk, I worry,
as if wading through deep waters.
Thanks to the loyal virtue of the prime ministers,
whose sagacity reaches that of *Yī* and *Wàng*,
the sincerity of the multitude of lords,
who unite in agreement,
the internal and external officials who fully offer their guidance and support,
and the civil and military officers who pledge their selfless devotion,
I hope that through this path,
we can ultimately achieve great success.
I constantly think of how the wars have not ceased,
and both public and private sectors are exhausted.
The *fānzhèn* have duties of governing and managing their territories,
and the soldiers on expedition and garrison duty harbor the toil of *Dōngshān*.
Some have reached old age on the battlefield,
their loyal efforts unfulfilled;
others have been on campaign for a long time,
with no provisions saved.
How could I not rise at dawn,
and forget sleep past midnight?
Though I cannot personally soothe and inspect them,
I wish to convey my heart to them.
Ambassadors shall be dispatched to the *Dàsīmǎ*,
and also to inquire of the *fāngbó*,
reaching as far as the border garrisons,
to proclaim the imperial edict and hold great feasts,
and to seek their well-being.
Furthermore, provisions and grants shall be planned,
making sure they are thorough and widespread.”
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
“After the past incidents,
all systems were not yet fully restored.
The regular salaries of all officials
were meager and restricted,
which was a matter of adapting to the times.
However, to retire from court but not have one's salary replace farming income,
is not a long-standing system.
Now that resources are gradually abundant,
plans can be made to increase salaries.”
*Zōuyú* was seen in *Yùzhāng*.
In summer, the fourth month,
*Hǎixī Gōng* was relocated to *Xīcháilǐ* in *Wúxiàn*.
Empress Yǔ was posthumously demoted to lady (*fūrén*).
In the sixth month,
envoys were sent to enfeoff *Bǎijì Wáng Yúgōu* as *Zhèndōng Jiāngjūn*,
and Governor of *Lèlàng*.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
former *Hùjūn Jiāngjūn* Yǔ Xī raised an army in rebellion,
entering *Jīngkǒu* from *Hǎilíng*. *Jìnling Tàishǒu* Biàn Dān fled to *Qǔ'ē*.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *rénchén* day,
Huán Wēn dispatched *Dōnghǎi Nèishǐ* Zhōu Shàosūn to suppress Xī.
He was captured
and executed in the market of *Jiànkāng*.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
*Kuàijī Wáng Chāngmíng* was established as the Crown Prince,
and Imperial Son Dàozǐ was enfeoffed as *Lángxié Wáng*,
also holding the title of *Kuàijī Nèishǐ*.
On this day,
the Emperor passed away in the Eastern Hall,
at the age of fifty-three.
He was buried in *Gāopínglíng*,
with the temple name *Tàizōng*.
His dying edict appointed Huán Wēn as regent,
following the precedents of Zhūgě Liàng and Wáng Dǎo.
The Emperor was graceful and dignified in his youth,
skilled in demeanor and deportment.
He devoted himself to classical texts,
and did not concern himself with his living quarters.
Dust settled thickly on his mat,
but he remained serene.
Once, he rode with Huán Wēn and *Wǔlíng Wáng Xī* on a carriage to *Bǎnbriáo*.
Wēn suddenly ordered drums to be beaten and horns blown,
the carriage sped up and soldiers ran,
to observe his reaction.
Xī was greatly frightened
and asked to alight,
but the Emperor remained calm and showed no fear.
Wēn was thereafter awed by him.
Wēn, relying on his civil and military authority,
repeatedly achieved great merits,
and furthermore, engaged in deposing and establishing emperors,
his prestige shaking both inside and outside the court.
Although the Emperor held a revered position,
he merely remained silent and adhered to the Dao,
often fearing deposition.
Before this,
the planet Mars (*Yínghuò*) entered *Tàiwēi*,
and soon after, *Hǎixī* was deposed.
When the Emperor ascended the throne,
Mars again entered *Tàiwēi*,
and the Emperor greatly disliked this omen.
At that time, *Zhōngshū Láng* Xī Chāo was on duty,
and the Emperor invited him in,
saying:
“The length of one's life,
I originally do not count it.
So, there must not be a repeat of the former incident, surely?”
Chāo replied:
“*Dàsīmǎ* Chén Wēn is currently strengthening the state internally
and expanding his strategies externally.
As for extraordinary events,
I guarantee against them with a hundred lives.”
When Chāo later requested leave to visit his father,
the Emperor said to him:
“Convey my regards to your honored father.
The affairs of the family and state
have come to this!
It is because I was unable to protect and assist with the Dao.
My shame and regret are so profound,
words cannot express them.”
He then recited Yǔ Chǎn's poem, saying:
“A man of ambition grieves the perilous court,
a loyal minister mourns the master's disgrace,”
and tears flowed down, drenching his lapel.
Although the Emperor possessed a serene and open mind,
he lacked great strategies for saving the world.
Therefore, Xiè Ān referred to him as a type like Emperor Huì,
only his *qīngtán* was somewhat better.
The Buddhist monk Zhī Dàolín once said,
“Kuàijī has a distant physique but no distant spirit.”
Xiè Língyùn, tracing his actions,
also considered him to be of the same ilk as Nǎn and Xiàn.
Emperor Xiaowu
Emperor Xiàowǔ, personal name Yào,
courtesy name Chāngmíng,
was the third son of Emperor Jiǎnwén.
In the seventh month of the third year of Xīngníng, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
he was first enfeoffed as *Kuàijī Wáng*.
In the second year of Xián'ān, in autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
he was made Crown Prince.
On this day,
Emperor Jiǎnwén passed away,
and the Crown Prince immediately ascended the imperial throne.
An imperial edict stated:
"We, being unworthy,
suddenly suffer from this great misfortune;
crying to Heaven and knocking the earth,
we know not where to plead.
We are but a tender youth,
as precarious as a dangling banner tassel.
Deeply considering the gravity of the altars of soil and grain,
we greatly fear being unable to bear the burden.
We rely on the spirits of our ancestors,
and the accumulated virtue of their sacrifices.
The pure customs and profound transformations of the late emperor
remain chanted by the people.
The prime ministers and ministers are eminent and virtuous,
with abundant merits and virtues.
The trust of the dying command
truly relies on their assistance and instruction.
May the various lords perform their duties,
and all officials diligently govern.
We hope that our frail and solitary person has support,
and that the foundation of the imperial pole does not fall.
The former emperor's grace and kindness
spread throughout the four seas.
We wish to extend this remaining benevolence
to bring peace to the common people.
Let there be a great amnesty throughout the realm,
and let the people make a fresh start."
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
his deceased imperial mother, the Princess of Kuàijī, was posthumously honored as Empress Shùn.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Emperor Jiǎnwén was buried at Gāopíng Líng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the rebel Lú Sǒng entered the palace courtyard early in the morning.
Commander of Agile Cavalry Máo Ānzhī and others pursued and captured him.
In this year,
the Three Wú region suffered a great drought,
and many people died of starvation.
An edict commanded that relief be distributed in all affected areas.
Fú Jiān captured Qiúchí
and seized the Inspector of Qínzhōu, Yáng Shì.
In the first year of Níngkāng, in spring, first month, on the day Jǐchǒu, the first day of the month,
the reign era was changed.
In the second month,
Grand Marshal Huán Wēn came to court.
In the third month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
an edict abolished the tax on the four types of bamboo gratings in Dānyáng and other items.
In summer, fifth month,
there was a drought.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐhài,

Huán Wēn, bearer of imperial credentials, court attendant, Grand Commandant of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside, Chancellor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Marshal, Governor of Yángzhōu, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces, and Duke of Nánjùn, passed away.
On the day Gēngxū,
Right General Huán Huò was promoted to General Who Conquers the West.
Jiāngzhōu Inspector Huán Chōng was appointed General of the Central Army, Grand Commandant of Military Affairs of Yáng, Yù, and Jiāng provinces, and Inspector of Yángzhōu,
stationed at Gūshú.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Empress Dowager Chóngdé presided over the court and acted as regent.
In the ninth month,
Fú Jiān's general Yáng Ān raided Chéngdū.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wáng Biāozhī was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs,
Minister of Personnel Xiè Ān was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs,
and Commander of Wúgúo Diāo Yí was appointed General of the Northern Central Army and Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces,
stationed at Guǎnglíng.
The offices of Grand Master of Ceremonies, Grand Minister of Agriculture, and Privy Treasurer were reinstated.
In winter, tenth month,
the Duke of Xīpíng, Zhāng Tiānxī, offered local tribute.
In the eleventh month,
Fú Jiān's general Yáng Ān captured Zǐtóng and Liáng and Yì provinces.
Inspector Zhōu Zhòngsūn led five thousand cavalry and fled south.
In the second year, in spring, first month, on the day Guǐwèi, the first day of the month,
there was a great amnesty.
Yù, the deceased heir apparent of Kuàijī, was posthumously enfeoffed and given the posthumous title of Prince Xiàn of Línchuān.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
General of the Northern Central Army and Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces, Diāo Yí, passed away.
In the second month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Dānyáng Administrator Wáng Tǎnzhī was appointed General of the Northern Central Army and Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces.
On the day Dīngsì,
a comet appeared in the constellations Nǚ and Xū.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngxū,
a comet appeared in the constellation Dī.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Rénxū,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict stating:
"Recently, celestial phenomena have been irregular,
and Heaven has shown abnormalities.
Observing these changes,
we are filled with trembling and fear.
To transform misfortune into good fortune is
the way of antiquity.
How dare We not strive to reform our heart
to ponder the middle path?
Moreover, the Three Wú region is a vital territory,
a crucial and hoped-for commandery,
yet it has suffered from both floods and droughts,
and the people have lost their livelihoods.
Day and night we are worried,
unable to forget this in our hearts.
It is appropriate to provide timely relief and assistance
to save them from their distress.
In the counties of Yìxīng, Jìnlíng, and Kuàijī in the Three Wú region that have suffered particularly severe flooding,
one year's rent and cloth taxes shall be entirely exempted.
For those less severely affected, half a year's exemption shall be granted.
Those who have received relief loans shall have them converted into grants."
In the fifth month,
Zhāng Yù of Shǔ proclaimed himself King of Shǔ,
led his forces to besiege Chéngdū,
and sent envoys to declare submission.
In autumn, seventh month,
there was an earthquake in Liángzhōu,
and mountains collapsed.
Fú Jiān's general Dèng Qiāng attacked Zhāng Yù
and annihilated him.
In the eighth month,
because the Grand Autumn (a specific official ritual or imperial marriage) was about to be established,
marriages were temporarily suspended.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
a comet appeared in the Tiānshì constellation.
In winter, eleventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Dàn bandits of Tiānmén attacked the commandery.
Administrator Wáng Fěi died in the conflict.
General Who Conquers the West Huán Huò dispatched troops to suppress them.
Qián Bùshè and Qián Hóng of Chángchéng raised a rebellion.
Wúxīng Administrator Zhū Xù suppressed them.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
General Who Stabilizes the Distant Huán Shíqián defeated Fú Jiān's general Yáo Cháng at Diànjiāng.
In the third year, in spring, first month, on the day Xīnhài,
there was a great amnesty.
In summer, fifth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
General of the Northern Central Army, Inspector of Xú and Yǎn provinces, and Marquis of Lántián, Wáng Tǎnzhī, passed away.
On the day Jiǎyín,
General of the Central Army and Inspector of Yángzhōu, Huán Chōng, was appointed General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Xúzhōu,
stationed at Dāntú.
Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiè Ān concurrently held the post of Inspector of Yángzhōu.
In autumn, eighth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Empress Wáng was established.
There was a great amnesty,
and all civil and military ranks were advanced by one grade.
In the ninth month,
the Emperor lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
〔一０〕the Shénshòu Gate suffered a fire.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict stating:
"Recently, the solar eclipse gave warning of change,
and the floods and droughts were inappropriate.
Although we have disciplined ourselves to seek remedies,
we have not exhausted all means.
Therefore, let rice be granted to the poor among the common people,
five *hú* per person."
On the day Guǐsì,
the Emperor performed the ancestral rites in the Central Hall,
offering sacrifices to Confucius,
with Yán Huí as his co-sacrificant.
In the first year of Tàiyuán, in spring, first month, on the day Rén'yín, the first day of the month,
the Emperor came of age,
and appeared at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
The Empress Dowager returned political authority.
On the day Jiǎchén,
there was a great amnesty,
and the reign era was changed.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor began to preside over court.
General Who Conquers the West Huán Huò was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the West.
General of the Army Xī Yīn was appointed Grand General Who Guards the Army.
General of the Central Army Huán Chōng was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry.
Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Xiè Ān was concurrently appointed Supervising Secretary of the Central Secretariat and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
he paid respects at the Jiànpíng and other four imperial tombs.
In summer, fifth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
there was an earthquake.
On the day Jiǎyín,
an edict stated:
"Recently, Heaven has observed us,
and warnings have frequently manifested.
We are fearful of this,
and tremble in our heart.
We ponder how to review prisoners' cases and delay executions,
and pardon faults and forgive crimes,
hoping to use these great changes
to make a fresh start with the people."
Thereupon, a great amnesty was issued,
and all civil and military ranks were advanced by one grade.
In the sixth month,
Fànzhī, son of Qīn, Prince of Héjiān, was enfeoffed as Prince Wǔ of Zhāng.
In autumn, seventh month,
Fú Jiān's general Gǒu Cháng captured Liángzhōu,
took Inspector Zhāng Tiānxī captive,
and took possession of all his territory.
On the day Yǐsì,
the system of land measurement for tax collection was abolished.
For those below ducal and princely rank, the household tax was three *hú* of rice,
and those in service were exempted from conscription.
In winter, in the tenth month,
people from Huáinán were relocated to the north of the Huái River.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénshēn, the first day of the month (jǐsì),
〔一一〕there was a solar eclipse.
An imperial edict ordered the Grand Steward to reduce the imperial meals.
In the twelfth month,
Fú Jiān sent his general Fú Luò to attack Dài,
and captured the King of Dài, Tuòbá Yìjiàn.
In the second year, in spring, in the first month,
he continued extinct lineages
and honored meritorious officials.
In the third month,
Zhū Xù, the Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, was appointed as General of the Southern Central Army, Inspector of Liángzhōu, and Overseer of all armies in Miǎnzhōng,
stationed at Xiāngyáng.
In the intercalary month, on the day Rénwǔ,
there was an earthquake.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
a violent storm
broke trees and unroofed houses.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
it rained hail.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
there was an earthquake.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐsì,
〔一二〕a violent storm
stirred up sand and stones.
Línyì offered tribute of local products.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
〔一三〕the Old Man Star (Canopus) appeared.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénchén,
Huán Chōng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, came to court.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xiè Ān, Palace Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Minister of Works.
On the day Bǐngchén,

Huán Huò, Imperial Commissioner, Grand Administrator of all military affairs in the six provinces of Jīng, Liáng, Níng, Yì, Jiāo, and Guǎng, Inspector of Jīngzhōu, and General-in-chief of the West, passed away.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,

Huán Chōng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Grand Administrator of all military affairs in the seven provinces of Jīng, Jiāng, Liáng, Yì, Níng, Jiāo, and Guǎng, concurrently holding the title of Protector-Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and Inspector of Jīngzhōu;
Wáng Yùn, Palace Assistant, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu and Overseer of all armies south of the Jiāng River and in Jìnlíng;
Xiè Xuán, Cavalry Commander of the West, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, Administrator of Guǎnglíng, and Overseer of all armies north of the Jiāng River.
On the day Rénýn,
Wáng Biāozhī, Regular Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Wáng Shào, Palace Assistant, was appointed Palace Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the third year, in spring, in the second month, on the day Yǐsì,
the new palace was built,
and the Emperor moved to the residence of the King of Kuàijī.
In the third month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
there was thunder and rain,
a violent storm,
unroofing houses and breaking trees.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Cáo Huī, King of Chénliú, passed away.
In the sixth month,
there was a great flood.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor entered the new palace.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) appeared in the south.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and for commanderies and counties that suffered from floods and droughts, their rent and taxes were reduced.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
he visited Jiànpíng and seven other imperial tombs.
In the second month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Fú Jiān sent his son Pī to capture Xiāngyáng,
and captured Zhū Xù, General of the Southern Central Army.
He also captured Shùnyáng.
In the third month,
there was a great epidemic.
On the day Rénxū,
an imperial edict stated:
"The treacherous enemy runs rampant,
our border defenses have fallen,
and the dangers at our frontiers
are greater than in peacetime.
All officials, both internal and external,
should exert their utmost effort and cooperate
to restore order to all affairs.
Furthermore, the annual harvest has been poor,
and many common people are destitute.
Therefore, the imperial provisions
should be made economical;
the provisions for the imperial relatives,
and the stipends for all officials,
may temporarily be halved.
All expenses for labor,
unless they are crucial for military or state affairs,
should all be suspended or reduced,
to cope with the current difficulties."
On the day Guǐwèi,
General of the Right Máo Wǔshēng was ordered to lead an army to attack Shǔ.
In summer, in the fourth month,
Wéi Zhōng, a general of Fú Jiān, captured Wèixīng,
and Jí Yì, the Grand Administrator, died there.
In the fifth month,
Jù Nán and [一四]Péng Chāo, generals of Fú Jiān, captured Xūyí,
and Máo Zǎozhī, the Inner Historian of Gāomì, was captured by the bandits.
In the sixth month,
there was a great drought.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Xiè Xuán, General Who Campaigns Against Barbarians, and Péng Chāo and Jù Nán fought at Jūnchuān,
and Xiè Xuán utterly defeated them.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Dīnghài,
Wáng Yùn, General of the Left, was appointed Palace Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
On the day Yǐwèi,
a violent storm
stirred up sand and stones.
In the ninth month,
bandits killed Fù Zhàn, the Grand Administrator of Jiàn'ān.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day Jǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
〔一五〕
In the fifth year, in spring, in the first month, on the day Yǐsì,
he visited the Chóngpíng Tomb.
In summer, in the fourth month,
there was a great drought.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed for crimes punishable by five years of imprisonment or less.
〔一六〕
In the fifth month,
there was a great flood.
Xiè Ān, Minister of Works, was appointed General of the Guards and accorded the honors of the Three Ducal Ministers.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
an earthquake shook the four pillars of the Hánzhāng Hall,
and also killed two palace attendants.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
due to the successive years of famine,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and all outstanding rents and old debts from before the third year of Tàiyuán were remitted;
as for the widowed, lonely, poor, and elderly who could not support themselves,
each person was granted five hú of rice.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Liángyá Wáng Dàozǐ, General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Minister of Works.
In autumn, in the ninth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Empress Wáng passed away.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Lǐ Xùn, Grand Administrator of Jiǔzhēn, rebelled in Jiāozhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Empress Dìng was buried at Lóngpíng Mausoleum.
In the sixth year, in spring, in the first month,
the Emperor first adopted Buddhism,
establishing a monastery within the palace
and inviting various śramaṇas to reside there.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Xiè Shí, Palace Assistant, was appointed Palace Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
The office of Overseer of Transport Commissioners was first established.
In summer, in the sixth month, on the day Gēngzǐ, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
There were great floods in the three provinces of Yáng, Jīng, and Jiāng.
On the day Jǐsì,
institutions were reformed,
unnecessary expenses were reduced,
and the number of officials and soldiers was reduced by seven hundred.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
an amnesty was proclaimed for crimes punishable by five years of imprisonment or less.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Dù Yuàn, Grand Administrator of Jiāozhǐ, beheaded Lǐ Xùn,
and Jiāozhōu was pacified.
There was a great famine.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
〔一七〕Xī Yīn, General-in-chief of the Pacified Army, was appointed Minister of Works.
Tán Yuánzhī from Kuàijī rebelled,
proclaiming himself General Who Pacifies the East;
Xiè Àizhī, Army Adviser of the Pacified Army, suppressed and pacified him.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Fú Jiān sent his Grand Administrator of Xiāngyáng, Yán Zhèn, to raid Jìnglíng,
〔一八〕but Huán Shíqián, Grand Administrator of Xiāngyáng, attacked and captured him.
〔一九〕
In the seventh year, in spring, in the third month,
Fàn Xióng of Línyì sent an envoy to present local products.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the ninth month,
five states of the Eastern Yi sent envoys to present local tribute.
Dōu Guì, a general of Fú Jiān, burned the fields and grain north of the Miǎn River,
and abducted the people of Xiāngyáng before departing.
〔二一〕
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
there was thunder.
In the eighth year, in spring, in the second month, on the day Guǐwèi,
yellow fog filled all four directions.
In the third month,
there were great floods in Shǐxīng, Nánkāng, and Lúlíng,
with the flat ground submerged five zhàng deep.
On the day Dīngsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In summer, in the fifth month,
Yáng Liàng, General Who Upholds the State, attacked Shǔ,
captured five cities,
and seized Wèi Guāng, a general of Fú Jiān.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Guō Qià, General Who Spreads Martial Might, and Zhāng Chóng, a general of Fú Jiān, fought at Wǔdāng,
〔二二〕and Guō Qià inflicted a great defeat upon them.
In the eighth month,
Fú Jiān led his forces across the Huái River,

and dispatched Xiè Shí, Commander-in-chief of the Expeditionary Forces, Xiè Xuán, General of Champion Merit, Xiè Yǎn, General Who Upholds the State, and Huán Yī, Western Central Army General, among others, to resist him.
In the ninth month,
an imperial edict ordered the Minister of Works, Liángyá Wáng Dàozǐ, to record the six categories of matters of the Department of State Affairs.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Fú Jiān's younger brother Róng captured Shòuchūn.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the various generals and Fú Jiān fought at the Féi River,
and we utterly defeated them.
[二三]Tens of thousands were captured or beheaded.
We seized Fú Jiān's imperial carriage and a mica chariot.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
[二四]an imperial edict was issued for General of the衛 Shè Hái to reward the returning army at Jīnchéng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Língdàn, the heir apparent of the King of Chénliú, was established as the King of Chénliú.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
as the banditry and difficulties had just been pacified,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Shè Shí, General of the Central Army, was appointed Grand Secretary.
The prohibition on alcohol was lifted.
For the first time, the tax on rice for the common people was increased,
to five *shí* per household.
The former King of Jùdīng, Zhái Liáo, rebelled against Fú Jiān.
[二五]He raised an army in Hénán.
Mùróng Chuí, from Yè, joined forces with Liáo,
and then attacked Fú Jiān's son Huī in Luòyáng.
Gōng Yáng Shì of Qiúchí fled back to Lǒngyòu,
[二六]and sent envoys to declare himself a vassal.
In the ninth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Sūn Bǎo, the grandson of the King of Wǔlíng, was enfeoffed as the King of Línchuān.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zūn, the son of King Xīnníng Xī, was established as the King of Xīnníng.
[二七]On the *xīnhài* day,
visitations were made to the four imperial mausoleums, including Jiànpíng.
Liú Láozhī, General of the Dragon Stratagem, captured Qiáochéng.
Guō Bǎo, a general under Huán Chōng, General of Chariots and Cavalry, attacked the three commanderies of Xīnchéng, Wèixīng, and Shàngyōng,
and they surrendered.
In the second month, on the *xīnsì* day,

Huán Chōng, Bearer of a Credential, Grand Administrator of Military Affairs of seven provinces (Jīng, Jiāng, Liáng, Níng, Yì, Jiāo, Guǎng), General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Inspector of Jīng Province, passed away.
Mùróng Chuí, from Luòyáng, and Zhái Liáo attacked Fú Jiān's son Pī in Yè.
In the third month,
Shè Ān, General of the衛, was appointed Grand Tutor.
Mùróng Hóng, Administrator of the Northern Prefecture under Fú Jiān, and Mùróng Chōng, Administrator of Píngyáng, both raised armies and rebelled against Fú Jiān.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
one hundred additional students were admitted to the Imperial Academy.
Zhāng Tiānxī was enfeoffed as the Duke of Xīpíng.
Zhào Tǒng, Administrator of Jìnglíng, was sent to attack Xiāngyáng,
and he captured it.
Yáo Cháng, a general under Fú Jiān, rebelled against Fú Jiān,
raised an army in Běidì,
proclaimed himself king,
and named his state Qín.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day (the first day of the month),
Empress Dowager Chǔ of Chóngdé passed away.
Mùróng Hóng was killed by his uncle Chōng,
who then proclaimed himself Imperial Younger Brother and Heir Apparent.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Chúnzhī, Acting Minister of Works and King of Gāomì, was dispatched to repair and visit the five imperial mausoleums in Luòyáng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Empress Kāngxiàn was interred at Chóngpíng Mausoleum.
Baìjì sent envoys to offer tribute of local products.
Fú Jiān and Mùróng Chōng fought west of Zhèng,
and Fú Jiān's army suffered a great defeat.
In the eighth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Xī Yīn, Minister of Works, passed away.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Shè Xuán, Commander of the Vanguard, attacked Zhāng Chóng, Fú Jiān's general and Inspector of Yǎn Province, at Juànchéng,
and captured it.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Grand Tutor Shè Ān was additionally appointed Grand Administrator of Military Affairs of fifteen provinces: Yáng, Jiāng, Jīng, Sī, Yù, Xú, Yǎn, Qīng, Jì, Yōu, Bìng, Liáng, Yì, Yōng, and Liáng.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Tánzhī, King of Héjiān, passed away.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
due to the celestial phenomena being out of order,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Chóng, the younger brother of the former King of Xīncài Huǎng, was established as the King of Xīncài.
Fú Lǎng, Fú Jiān's Inspector of Qīng Province, led his troops and surrendered.
In the twelfth month,
Lǚ Guāng, Fú Jiān's general, assumed imperial authority west of the Yellow River,
and styled himself the Duke of Jiǔquán.
Mùróng Chōng usurped the imperial throne at Āfáng.
In the tenth year, in spring, in the first month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
visitations were made to the various imperial mausoleums.
In the second month,

the Emperor passed away in the Qīngshǔ Diàn,
at the age of thirty-five.
He was buried in Lóngpíng Líng.
The Emperor was known for his intelligence and perceptiveness in his youth.
When Jiǎnwén passed away,
he was ten years old.
He did not attend the mourning until dusk.
When his attendants remonstrated with him,
he replied,
"When sorrow comes, one weeps.
What constancy is there?"
Xiè Ān once praised this, believing his profound understanding was no less than that of the previous emperor.
After he gained real power,
he naturally possessed the demeanor of a ruler.
However, he later indulged in wine and women,
almost to the point of a "long night" of drinking.
In his later years, a long star was seen.
The Emperor was greatly displeased by it,
and raising his cup in Huálín Yuán, he toasted it, saying,
"Long star,
I offer you a cup of wine.
Since ancient times, has there ever been an emperor of ten thousand years?"
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight for consecutive years,
and earthquakes, floods, and droughts occurred one after another as calamities.
As his sober days were few,
and there were no upright persons by his side,
he ultimately could not change.
At that time, Consort Zhāng was favored.
She was almost thirty years old.
The Emperor joked to her, saying,
"You should be deposed because of your age."
The Consort secretly grew angry.
Towards evening,
the Emperor, being drunk,
suddenly died.
At that time, Dàozǐ was confused and muddled,
and Yuánxiǎn monopolized power,
so the culprits were never investigated.
Initially,
Emperor Jiǎnwén saw a prophecy which said:
"The Jìn dynasty's fate will end with Chāngmíng."
When the Emperor was in his mother's womb,
Empress Dowager Lǐ dreamt of a divine person who said to her,
"You will give birth to a son.
Name him 'Chāngmíng'."
When he was born,
the east was just dawning,
so he was named after it.
Emperor Jiǎnwén later understood,
and then wept.
When the Qīngshǔ Diàn was built,
those who knew thought
"Qīngshǔ"
sounded like "Chǔ"
in reverse,
a sign of sorrow.
Soon after, the Emperor died,
and the Jìn dynasty began to decline from then on.
The court historian remarks: Previous historians said,
"Without decline,
how can a ruler rise?"
Indeed, if Heaven bestows a divine sage,
who gloriously accepts the succession,
soaring like a dragon through the clouds,
and leaping across deep rivers;
if Shàokāng, with a single army,
could establish the imperial design,
and Chéng Tāng, with a base of seventy *lǐ*,
could revive the royal enterprise;
calming the rivers and seas when they overflowed,
and mending the broken firmament;
if matters are different from these,
then it should not be followed.
Emperor Jiǎnwén, with his pure and serene disposition,
was in a difficult situation.
Governance was in the hands of the Huán clan,
and "I" merely presided over sacrifices.
After Tàizōng died,
Níngkāng succeeded to the throne,
Heaven guided his heart,
and treacherous officials perished by themselves.
At that time, (Jìn's influence) stretched west beyond Jiànxiù and across Língshān,
north beyond the mighty Chánghé and reaching Qīngluò.
The armies of Jīng and Wú
roared like clouds.
Renowned worthies emerged,
and old virtues remained: Xiè Ān could stabilize society,
Biaōzhī was sufficient to rectify the administration,
Huán Chōng conscientiously served the royal house day and night,
and Xiè Xuán was skilled in military affairs.
At that time, Heaven showed favor,
and the powerful Dǐ clan collapsed on its own.
A five-foot tall child,
waving his sleeves by the river,
thought of planting flags on Tiānshān
and sealing Hángǔ Pass;
yet administrative principles were not upheld,
and prestige and grace were rarely established.
Dàozǐ was muddled in court affairs,
Guóbǎo gathered petty individuals,
the honors of appointment
were never by imperial decree,
and the bribes for pardoning crimes
flowed directly to powerful gates.
Poisons of taxation increased yearly,
and the distressed populace grew annually.
Therefore, Wénrén and Xǔ Róng wrote letters to the palace gate.
Lièzōng knew of their uprightness,
but disliked hearing unpleasant truths.
He indulged in drunkenness from morning to evening,
and drank countless cups throughout the night.
Even if
"Chāngmíng"
was revealed in a dream,
how could he listen to divine words?
And the decline of the Metal element (Jìn dynasty)
was also due to human affairs.
The saying goes,
"When the politics of a great nation have not yet declined,
the chaos of small states is already overthrown."
When Fú Jiān was in his period of great tribulation,
abandoning his forces at Féishuǐ,
the Emperor was called "Wǔ"
—was this not excellent?
A eulogy says: The ruler, like a string of pearls,
whose path is not of harmonious peace.
Emperor Jiǎn, serene and quiet,
brought no harm.
Xiàowǔ ascended the throne,
and treacherous heroes perished on their own.
Yān attacked the road,
Zhèng Shū divided the reins.
Singers attended the imperial feast,
wine was offered to the celestial demon.
The Metal element lacked strength,
and human affairs withered first.
