Mùróng Xiáng, a general of Mùróng Bǎo, usurped the imperial throne at Zhōngshān.
Mùróng Bǎo fled to Huánglóng.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
Lǚ Guāng was attacked by his Attendant Counselor Yáng Guǐ and Palace Attendant Guō Nún.
Lǚ Guāng's son, Lǚ Zuǎn, attacked and routed them.
In the ninth month,
Mùróng Lín, a general of Mùróng Bǎo, beheaded Mùróng Xiáng at Zhōngshān,
and then usurped the imperial throne.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Mùróng Lín was defeated by the Wèi army.
In the second year, in spring, in the third month,
two dragon boats were damaged.
In summer, in the fifth month,
Lán Hàn assassinated Mùróng Bǎo and proclaimed himself Grand General and King of Chānglí.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Mùróng Bǎo's son, Mùróng Shèng, beheaded Lán Hàn,
and usurped the title of King of Chánglè,
acting as Son of Heaven.

Wáng Gōng, the Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, Yú Kǎi, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, Yīn Zhòngkān, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Huán Xuán, the Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, Yáng Quánqī, the Colonel of the Southern Man, and others raised an army and rebelled.
In the eighth month,
Wáng Yú, the Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, fled to Línchuān.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
Dèng Qǐfāng, the General Who Pacifies the North, and Mùróng Fǎ, a general of Mùróng Dé, fought at Guǎnchéng;
the imperial army was defeated.
On the bǐngxū day,
Mùróng Shèng usurped the imperial throne at Huánglóng.
Huán Xuán heavily defeated the imperial army at Báishí.
In the ninth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
Dàozǐ, the Grand Tutor and Prince of Kuàijī, was granted the yellow battle-ax.

Yuánxiǎn, the heir apparent of the Prince of Kuàijī and General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Wáng Xún, the General of the Van, and Xiè Yǎn, the General of the Right, were dispatched to attack Huán Xuán and others.
On the jǐhài day,
Yú Kǎi was defeated at Niúzhǔ.
On the bǐngwǔ day,
Dàozǐ, the Prince of Kuàijī, encamped at Zhōngtáng,
and Yuánxiǎn defended Shítou.
On the jǐyǒu day,
Wáng Xún, the General of the Van, defended the northern suburbs,
and Xiè Yǎn, the General of the Right, prepared the Xuānyáng Gate.
Liú Láozhī, the General Who Guards the State, positioned himself at Xīntíng,
and sent his son, Jìngxūan, to defeat Wáng Gōng.
Wáng Gōng fled to Qǔ'ā Chángtáng Hú;
the lake warden apprehended and sent him to the capital,
where he was executed.
Thereupon, Yīn Mào, the Grand Master of Ceremonies, was sent to convey terms to Yīn Zhòngkān and Huán Xuán.
Huán Xuán and others fled to Xúnyáng.
In winter, in the tenth month,
a zōuyú was reported seen in Xīnyě.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the rénwǔ day,
Yīn Zhòngkān and others formed an alliance at Xúnyáng,
and nominated Huán Xuán as the alliance leader.
In the eleventh month,
Dèwén, the Prince of Lángyá, was appointed General of the Guards and accorded the privileges of the Three Ducal Ministers,
and Wáng Yǎ, the General of the Palace Army, was appointed Left Grandee Secretary.
In the twelfth month, on the jǐchǒu day,
Wèi Wáng Guī ascended the throne,
with the reign title Tiānxīng.
Wéi Huá, a man from Jīngzhào, led refugee commoners from Xiāngyáng in rebellion,
and surrendered to Yáo Xīng.
On the jǐyǒu day,
Dù Jiǒng, the former Prefect of Xīn'ān, rebelled at Jīngkǒu.
Yuánxiǎn, the heir apparent of the Prince of Kuàijī, attacked and beheaded him.
Tūfà Wūgū declared himself King of Wǔwēi.
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the xīnyǒu day,
Yùn, a member of the imperial clan, was enfeoffed as Prince of Huáilíng.
In the second month, on the jiǎchén day,
Guózhèn, the Prince of Héjiān, died.
Fàn Húdá of Línyì captured Rìnán
and Jiǔzhēn,
and then raided Jiāozhǐ.
Dù Yuàn, the Prefect, attacked and defeated him.
Duàn Yè declared himself King of Liáng.
Yáng Shèng, the Duke of Qiúchí, sent envoys to pledge allegiance
and present local products.
In the third month, on the jǐmǎo day,
Lady Chén, his birth mother, was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager Dé.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the yǐwèi day,
Wáng Xún, the Grand Secretary, was promoted to General of the Guards,
and Yuánxiǎn, the heir apparent of the Prince of Kuàijī, was appointed Inspector of Yángzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the wùzǐ day,
Dèwén, the Prince of Lángyá, was appointed Minister over the Masses.
Mùróng Dé captured Qīngzhōu,
killed Pìlǘ Hún, the General Who Soars Like a Dragon,
and then usurped the imperial throne at Guǎnggù.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
Tūfà Wūgū died.
His younger brother, Lìlùgū, succeeded to the spurious throne.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Yáo Xīng captured Luòyáng,
and seized Xīn Gōngjìng, the Prefect of Hénán.
In the eleventh month, on the jiǎyín day,
Sūn Ēn, a demonic rebel, captured Kuàijī.
Wáng Níngzhī, the Grand Administrator, died there.
Huán Qiān, the Grand Administrator of Wú Jùn, Xīn Càiwáng Chóng, the Prefect of Línhǎi, and Wèi Yǐn, the Prefect of Yìxīng, all abandoned their posts and fled.
Xiè Miǎo, the Prefect of Wúxīng, and Sīmǎ Yì, the Prefect of Yǒngjiā, were both killed.
〔一０〕Xiè Yǎn, the General of the Guards, and Liú Láozhī, the General Who Guards the State, were sent to intercept and attack
and repel them.
In the twelfth month,
Huán Xuán attacked Jiānglíng.
Yīn Zhòngkān, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, and Yáng Quánqī, the Colonel of the Southern Man, were both killed.
Lǚ Guāng established his heir apparent, Lǚ Shào, as King of Heaven,
and called himself Supreme Emperor.
On that day,
Lǚ Guāng died,
and Lǚ Zuǎn assassinated Lǚ Shào and enthroned himself.
In this year,
Jīngzhōu suffered a great flood,
with the water reaching three zhàng on flat ground.
In the fourth year, in spring, in the first month, on the yǐhài day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the second month, on the jǐchǒu day,
a comet appeared in Kuí and Lóu,
and advanced to Zǐwēi.
In the third month,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi.
In summer, in the fourth month,
there was an earthquake.
Sūn Ēn raided Jiá Kǒu.
In the fifth month, on the bǐngyín day,
Wáng Xún, the Palace Attendant, General of the Guards, and Marquis of Dōngtíng, died.
On the jǐmǎo day,
Xiè Yǎn, the Grand Administrator of Kuàijī, was defeated by Sūn Ēn
and died.
Sūn Ēn then raided Línhǎi.
In the sixth month, on the gēngchén new moon day,
there was a solar eclipse.
There was a drought.
Liú Yù, the Army Supervisor Who Guards the State, defeated Sūn Ēn at Nánshān.
Lú Xún, a general of Sūn Ēn, captured Guǎnglīng.
〔一一〕More than three thousand people died.
Hé Chéng, the Master of the Prince of Lángyá, was appointed Left Grandee Secretary.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the rénzǐ day,
Empress Dowager Lǐ, the Grand Empress Dowager, passed away.
On the dīngmǎo day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In this month,
Yáo Xīng attacked Qífú Gān_Guī
and made him surrender.
In the eighth month, on the dīnghài day,
Wáng Yǎ, the Right Grandee Secretary, died.
On the rényín day,
Empress Dowager Wén was buried at Xiūpíng Líng.
In the ninth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
there was an earthquake.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
Gāo Yǎzhī, the General Who Pacifies the North, fought Sūn Ēn at Yúyáo;
the imperial army was defeated.

Yuánxiǎn, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed General of the Rear, accorded the privileges of the Three Ducal Ministers, and Grand Supervising Military Governor of the Sixteen Provinces of Yáng, Yù, Xú, Yǎn, Qīng, Yōu, Jì, Bìng, Jīng, Jiāng, Sī, Yōng, Liáng, Yì, Jiāo, and Guǎng.
Liú Láozhī, the General of the Van, was appointed General Who Guards the North.
Yànzhāng, Yuánxiǎn's son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dōnghǎi.
In the twelfth month, on the wùyín day,
a comet appeared in Tiānshì.
In this year,
the various commanderies west of the Yellow River proclaimed Lǐ Xuánshèng, the King Wǔzhāo of Liáng, as Governor of Qín and Liáng Provinces and Duke of Liáng,
with the reign title Gēngzǐ.
In the fifth year, in spring, in the second month, on the bǐngzǐ day,
Sūn Ēn again raided Jiá Kǒu.
Lǚ Chāo assassinated Lǚ Zuǎn,
and his elder brother, Lǚ Lóng, usurped the spurious throne.
In the third month, on the jiǎyín day,
all the stars flowed westward,
passing through Tàiwēi.
In summer, in the fifth month,
Sūn Ēn raided Hùdú.
Yuán Shānsōng, the Grand Administrator of Wú Jùn, died there.
〔一二〕Júqú Méngxùn killed Duàn Yè,
and proclaimed himself Grand Commander and Governor of Běiliángzhōu.
〔一三〕
In the sixth month, on the jiǎxū day,
Sūn Ēn reached Dāntú.
On the yǐhài day,
martial law was declared both inside and outside the capital,
and all officials moved into the palace chambers.
Gāo Sù, the General Who Displays Prowess, and Zhāng Chóngzhī, the General of the Right Guards, defended Shítou.
Liú Xí, the General Who Guards the State, blocked the mouth of the Huái River with a barrier.
Sīmǎ Huīzhī, the Governor of Dānyáng, garrisoned the southern bank.
Huán Qiān, the General Who Displays Prowess, Sīmǎ Yǔnzhī, the General Who Guards the State, and Máw Suì, the Roving General, prepared Báishí.
Wáng Gǔ, the General of the Left Guards, and Kǒng Ānguó, the General of the Palace Army, encamped at Zhōnghuángtáng.
Shàngzhī, the Inspector of Yùzhōu and Prince of Qiáo, was summoned to guard the capital.
Gāo Yǎzhī, the General Who Pacifies the North, attacked Sūn Ēn at Yùzhōu in Guǎnglīng,
and was captured by the rebels.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Duàn Jī assassinated Mùróng Shèng.
〔一四〕Shèng's uncle Xī exterminated the Duàn clan,
and consequently usurped the imperial title.
In the ninth month,
Lǚ Lóng surrendered to Yáo Xīng.
In winter, the tenth month,
Yáo Xīng led his army to invade Wèi,
but was greatly defeated and returned.
In this year,
there was a famine,
and alcohol was prohibited.
In the first year of Yuánxīng, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngwǔ* day (the first day of the month),
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the era name was changed.
Yuán Xiǎn, the General of the Rear, was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Controller of Campaigns,
Liú Láozhī, the General Guarding the North, was appointed Yuán Xiǎn's vanguard,
Wáng Shàngzhī, the General of the Vanguard and Prince of Qiáo, was appointed commander of the rear detachment,
to suppress Huán Xuán.
In the second month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor, in military attire, bade farewell to Yuán Xiǎn at Xīchí.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Jiān Shìzhōng Qíwáng Róuzhī was dispatched with a *zōuyú* banner to issue a proclamation to the two prefectures of Jīng and Jiāng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Huán Xuán defeated the imperial army at Gūshú.
Prince of Qiáo Shàngzhī and Prince of Qí Róuzhī both died in the battle.
Wú Yǐnzhī, the General of the Right, was appointed Area Commander-in-chief of the two prefectures of Jiāo and Guǎng, and Administrator of Guǎngzhōu.
In the third month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Liú Láozhī rebelled and surrendered to Huán Xuán.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the imperial army was defeated at Xīntíng.
Yuán Xiǎn, the General of Agile Cavalry and Heir Apparent of the Prince of Kuàijī,
Yànzhāng, the Prince of Dōnghǎi,
Máo Tài, the General of Champion Might,
and Máo Suì, the General of Roaming Cavalry, were all killed.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Huán Xuán appointed himself Shìzhōng, Chancellor, and Director of the Secretariat,
and appointed Huán Qiān as Shàngshū Púyè.
〔一五〕Tàifù, the Prince of Kuàijī Dàozǐ, was moved to Ānchéng.
Xuán soon after also styled himself Tàiwèi and Governor of Yángzhōu,
controlling all governmental affairs,
and appointed Lángyá Wáng Déwén as Tàizǎi.
Xīn Jǐng, the Administrator of Línhǎi, attacked Sūn Ēn,
〔一六〕and beheaded him.
In this month,
Tūfà Lìlùgū died,
and his younger brother Tán succeeded to the usurped throne.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Chóng, the Prince of Xīncài, was murdered by his slave.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Shàngshū Xiàshè caught fire.
In winter, the tenth month,
Liú Guǐ, the Administrator of Jìzhōu, rebelled and fled to Mùróng Dé.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Dàozǐ, the Prince of Kuàijī, was murdered by Huán Xuán.
A partial amnesty was granted for crimes of grand rebellion or less in Guǎnglín and Péngchéng.
In the second year, in spring, the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Liú Yù, the General Establishing Might, defeated Xú Dàofù at Dōngyáng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Huán Xuán styled himself Grand General.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Sūn Wúzōng, the Administrator of Jìzhōu, was murdered by Huán Xuán.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐsì* day (the first day of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Xuán again styled himself Chancellor and King of Chǔ.
In the ninth month,
Yǔ Zè, the Administrator of Nányáng, raised an army of righteousness,
but was defeated by Xuán.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Xuán moved the Emperor to Yǒng'ān Gōng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple were moved to the state of Lángyá.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
and demoted the Emperor to King of Pínggù.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor was forced to flee to Xúnyáng.
In the third year, in spring, the second month,
the Emperor was in Xúnyáng.
On the night of the *gēngyín* day,
a tidal wave entered Shítóu,
drowning people and homes.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Liú Yù, the General Establishing Martial Might, along with Liú Yì of Pèiguó and Hé Wújì of Dōnghǎi, raised an army of righteousness.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Huán Xiū, the Administrator of Xúzhōu appointed by Huán Xuán, was beheaded at Jīngkǒu,
and Huán Hóng, the Administrator of Qīngzhōu, at Guǎnglín.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the righteous army crossed the Jiāng.
In the third month, on the *wǔwǔ* day,
Liú Yù beheaded Wú Fǔzhī, Huán Xuán's general, at Jiāngchéng,
and Huángfǔ Fū at Luóluò.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Xuán's forces scattered and fled.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Liú Yù established a provisional government,
and appointed all officials.
On the *rénxū* day,

Wáng Mì, Huán Xuán's Situ, recommended Liú Yù to act as General Guarding the Army, Administrator of Xúzhōu, Area Commander-in-chief of the eight prefectures of Yáng, Xú, Yǎn, Yù, Qīng, Jì, Yōu, and Bìng, and to be granted the *jiǎjié* authority.
Liú Yù appointed Mì to lead as Administrator of Yángzhōu and Director of the Secretariat.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Liú Yù executed Wáng Yú, the Left Shàngshū Púyè, his son Wáng Suí, the Administrator of Jīngzhōu,〔一七〕 and Wēn Xiáng, the Administrator of Sīzhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Huán Xuán forced the Emperor to move west.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a secret edict stated that due to being held captive by Xuán,
all state affairs were suspended,
and ordered Zūn, the Prince of Wǔlíng, to, in accordance with old precedents,
act as regent and manage all governmental affairs,
with the addition of Shìzhōng,
all other titles remaining as before.
A general amnesty was also granted for crimes of plotting rebellion and grand rebellion or less,
except for those descended from Huán Xuán's direct line, who were not to be pardoned.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zūn, the Grand General and Prince of Wǔlíng, assumed regency,
and managed all state affairs.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor arrived at Jiānglíng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Hé Wújì, the General Assisting the State, and Liú Dàoguī, the General Arousing Martial Might, fought against Yǔ Zhì and〔一八〕 Hé Dànzhī, Huán Xuán's generals, at Pénkǒu,
and greatly defeated them.
Xuán again forced the Emperor to move east.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Liú Yì, the General of Champion Might, fought against Huán Xuán at Zhēngróng Zhōu,
and again defeated him.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor again went to Jiānglíng.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Wáng Kāngchǎn, the Administrator of Jīngzhōu, and Wáng Téngzhī, the Administrator of Nánjùn, escorted the Emperor to reside in Nánjùn.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Féng Qiān, the Supervisor, beheaded Huán Xuán at Mòpán Zhōu.
〔一九〕The imperial carriage returned to Jiānglíng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Treacherous villains and usurpers have existed since ancient times.
We were unable to curb and suppress them in their infancy,
leading to this displacement.
Fortunately, General Guarding the Army Yù, with his brilliant strategy and resolute action,
and his unmatched loyalty and courage,
and General of Champion Might Yì and others, whose sincere loyalty has long been evident,
collaborated in this excellent plan.
As the righteous voice resonated,
scholars and commoners alike pledged their allegiance,
the state was restored to peace,
and the four seas celebrated.
A general amnesty is hereby proclaimed.
All those who, under duress, were forced to comply with the rebellion,
shall not be questioned."
On the *wùyín* day,
〔二０〕the spirit tablets were enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the intercalary month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Huán Zhèn, Huán Xuán's former general and General Establishing Martial Might, captured Jiānglíng.
Liú Yì and Hé Wújì retreated to Xúnyáng,
and the Emperor again became a refugee in the rebel camp.
In the sixth month,
Máo Qú, the Administrator of Yìzhōu, attacked Huán Xī, the usurping Administrator of Liángzhōu,
and beheaded him.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Empress Yǒng'ān Hé Shì passed away.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Empress Zhāng of Emperor Mù was interred with her at Yǒngpíng Líng.
In the ninth month,
Diāo Chěng, former Assistant to the Imperial Secretariat, and Wáng Màizhī, Secretary of the Imperial Secretariat, plotted rebellion,
and were executed.
In winter, the tenth month,
Lú Xún invaded Guǎngzhōu,
and Wú Yǐnzhī, the Administrator, was defeated by Xún.
They captured Ruǎn Tiǎnzhī, the Chancellor of Shǐxīng, and returned.
〔二一〕Mùróng Dé died,
and his nephew Chāo succeeded to the usurped throne.
In the first year of Yìxī, in the spring, first month,
the Emperor was in Jiānglíng.
Lǔ Zōngzhī, the Administrator of Nányáng, raised an army of righteousness,
and attacked and captured Xiāngyáng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Liú Yì was stationed at Mǎtóu.
Huán Zhèn had the Emperor encamped at Jiāngjīn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zōngzhī defeated Huán Zhèn's general, Wēn Kǎi, at Zuòxī,
then advanced to Jìnán,
where he was defeated by Zhèn.
Liú Dàoguī, General of Martial Might, attacked Huán Qiān,
who fled.
The imperial carriage returned to the capital,
and the Emperor and the Prince of Lángyá went to Dàoguī's boat.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict stated:
"I, with my meager virtue,
have early on inherited the great enterprise.
Unable to bring peace to all, near and far,
or to suppress the wicked and traitorous.
The rebellious minister Huán Xuán took advantage of the opportunity to commit atrocities,
deceiving heaven and man,
and usurping the supreme position.
I personally was forced to wander,
drifting to remote regions,
and the foundation of Emperor Xuān
was on the verge of collapsing.
Fortunately, Liú Yù, General of the Garrison Army, with his loyalty, martial spirit, and decisive judgment,
truly surpassed all in ancient times.
When he conceived the plan,
loyal and virtuous men agreed with his covenant,
and wiping away tears, he rallied the troops,
and righteous warriors were moved in their hearts.
Thus, with a single sweep of the frost-edged spear,
the great villain fled,
and with the awe-inspiring might of the Three Commanders,
the great evildoers were beheaded.
However, the remnant villain Zhèn raged wildly,
continuing the evil in Jīngyǐng.
Fortunately, Heaven blessed the altars of earth and grain,
and the banners of righteousness were victorious again.
The cunning rogues were disheartened and collapsed,
and I was able to return to the rightful throne.
This is truly due to the spiritual power of the ancestral temple
and the meritorious service of those who protected the throne.
How can I alone
enjoy this blessing?
I wish to share it with the myriad people,
and fortunately, this new beginning.
Therefore, there shall be a great amnesty,
and the reign year shall be changed,
except for Huán Xuán, Huán Zhèn, their immediate ancestors, and their accomplices, who are not included in this pardon.
All officials are granted two ranks of nobility,
〔二二〕and widows, widowers, orphans, and the solitary are given five *hú* of grain per person.
There shall be a great feast for five days."
On the day Dīngsì of the second month,
the Provisional Court prepared the imperial carriage and ceremonial equipage
to welcome the Emperor from Jiānglíng.
Dài Níngzhī, Administrator of Hóngnóng, Xú Huìzǐ, Principal Secretary of Jiànwēi, and others plotted rebellion
and were executed.
Qiáo Zòng, a staff officer of the Pacification of the West, murdered Máo Qú, the General of the Pacification of the West and Inspector of Yìzhōu,
and revolted with Shǔ.
In the third month,
Huán Zhèn again attacked Jiānglíng,
and Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, Inspector of Jīngzhōu, fled to Xiāngyáng.
Liú Huáisu, General of Jianwei, campaigned against Zhèn
and beheaded him.
The Emperor returned from Jiānglíng.
On the day Yǐwèi,
all officials went to the palace gate to request punishment for their faults.
An edict stated:
"This is not your fault, my lords.
Return and perform your duties."
On the day Wùxū,
a three-day mourning period was held for Empress Zhāng,
and he attended at the West Hall.
Liú Yù and Hé Wúyì and others submitted memorials requesting to resign their positions,
which was not allowed.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Sīmǎ Déwén, the Prince of Lángyá, was appointed Grand Marshal.
Sīmǎ Zūn, the Prince of Wǔlíng, was appointed Grand Tutor.
Liú Yù, General of the Garrison Army, was additionally appointed Attendant-in-ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of All Military Affairs, Internal and External.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an edict stated:
"Since the recent national calamity,
people have been devastated.
The usual offerings
have not been changed from the old,
how can this be seen as treating people as if wounded,
or following the admonitions of Yǔ and Tāng to take blame upon themselves?
Measures should be taken to reduce and economize."
In the summer, fourth month,
Liú Yù returned to garrison Jīngkǒu.
On the day Wùchén,
a farewell feast was held at the East Hall.
On the day Guǐwèi of the fifth month,
silk fans and *chūpú* were prohibited.
Sīmǎ Xiù, General of Roaming Cavalry and Prince of Zhāngwǔ,
and Sīmǎ Guǐzhī, Inspector of Yìzhōu, plotted rebellion
and were executed.
Huán Liàng, Fú Hóng, and Diāo Yù, former generals of Huán Xuán, raided Xiāngzhōu.
The defending general repelled them.
In the autumn, on the day Jiǎzǐ of the eighth month,
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, Prince of Línchuān, was enfeoffed as Prince of Kuàijī.
In the winter, eleventh month,
Qífú Gān’guī attacked Qiúchí.
Yáng Shèng, the Duke of Qiúchí, decisively defeated him.
In this year,
Xuán Shèng, King Wǔzhāo of Liáng, sent an envoy to present a memorial acknowledging vassalage.
In the second year, spring, first month,
Sīmǎ Róngqī, Inspector of Yìzhōu, attacked Qiáo Zǐmíng, a general of Qiáo Zòng, at Báidì
and defeated him.
In the summer, fifth month,
Sīmǎ Fǎlián, Prince of Gāomì, was enfeoffed as Prince of Gāoyáng.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Yáng Zījìng, Inspector of Liángzhōu, committed a crime
and was executed.
In the winter, tenth month,
in recognition of the restoration efforts,
Liú Yù, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yùzhāng Commandery.
Liú Yì, General of the Protecting Army, was enfeoffed as Duke of Nánpíng Commandery.
Hé Wúyì, General of the Right, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ānchéng Commandery.
Other enfeoffments and rewards varied according to their merits.
On the day Yǐhài,
Kǒng Ānguó, General of the Left, was appointed Left Senior Secretary of the Department of State Affairs.
In the twelfth month,
the Administrator of Línglíng, Ruǎn Yě, was murdered by bandits.
In the third year, spring, on the day Jǐyǒu of the second month,
Liú Yù, General of Chariots and Cavalry, came to court.
Yīn Zhòngwén, Administrator of Dōngyáng, Yīn Shúwén, Commandant of the Southern Barbarians, Yīn Dàoshū, Administrator of Jìnlíng, and Luò Qiú, Administrator of Yǒngjiā, were executed.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
〔二三〕a great amnesty was declared,
and the prohibition on alcohol was lifted.
In the summer, fifth month,
there was a great flood.
In the sixth month,
Hèlián Bóbó, a general of Yáo Xīng, presumptuously proclaimed himself Heavenly King at Shuòfāng,
and his state was named Xià.
In the autumn, on the first day (Wùxū) of the seventh month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Sīmǎ Zūnzhī, the Prince of Rǔnán, committed a crime
and was executed.
In the eighth month,
Liú Jìngxuān, General of Champion Army, was sent with a staff of authority to oversee all military affairs for the expedition against Shǔ.
In the winter, eleventh month,
Hèlián Bóbó greatly defeated Tūfà Tán,
who fled to Nánshān.
In this year,
Gāo Yún and Féng Bá killed Mùróng Xī.
Yún presumptuously ascended the imperial throne.
In the fourth year, spring, on the day Jiǎchén of the first month,
Sīmǎ Déwén, the Prince of Lángyá, was appointed Minister of Works,
and Liú Yù, General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Yángzhōu and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Sīmǎ Zūn, Attendant-in-ordinary, Grand Tutor, and Prince of Wǔlíng, passed away.
In the summer, fourth month,
Kǒng Ānguó, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and Left Senior Secretary of the Department of State Affairs, died.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Mèng Chǎng, Minister of Personnel, was additionally appointed Left Senior Secretary of the Department of State Affairs.
In the winter, on the day Guǐchǒu of the eleventh month,
〔二四〕there was thunder.
Yáng Sīpíng, Inspector of Liángzhōu, committed a crime
and was executed in the marketplace.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
a great wind uprooted trees.
In this month,
Tūfà Tán presumptuously ascended the throne as King of Liáng.
In the twelfth month,
Cáo Língdàn, the Prince of Chénliú, passed away.
In the fifth year, spring, on the day Xīnmǎo of the first month,
a great amnesty was declared.
On the day Gēngxū,
Liú Yì, General of the Protecting Army, was appointed General of the Guards and given the ceremonial privilege of establishing an administration and having three dukes.
Hé Wúyì, General of Aiding the State, was additionally appointed General Pacifying the South.
On the day Wùxū,
there was an earthquake in Xúnyáng.
In the second month,
Mùróng Xīngzōng, a general of Mùróng Chāo, raided Sùyù.
Liú Qiānzǎi, Administrator of Yángpíng, and Zhào Yuán, Administrator of Nányáng, were both captured by the bandits.
〔二五〕
On the day Jǐhài of the third month,
there was heavy snow,
〔二六〕several feet deep on level ground.
Liú Yù, General of Chariots and Cavalry, led his army to attack Mùróng Chāo.
In the summer, on the day Bǐngyín of the sixth month,
there was thunder at the Grand Ancestral Temple.
Liú Yù decisively defeated Mùróng Chāo at Línqú.
In the autumn, seventh month,
Qífú Gān’guī, a general of Yáo Xīng, presumptuously proclaimed himself King of Western Qín at Yuànchuān.
On the day Wùchén of the ninth month,
Líbān assassinated Gāo Yún.
Féng Bá, a general of Gāo Yún, attacked Líbān
and killed him.
〔二七〕Bá presumptuously ascended the throne as King,
and continued to use the title Yàn.
In the winter, tenth month,
Sūn Shào, Prince of Qīnghé of Wèi, assassinated his lord, Guī.
In the sixth year, in spring, the second month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Liú Yù attacked Mùróng Chāo,
and conquered him.
All of Qí territory was pacified.
In this month,
Lú Xún, the Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, rebelled
and invaded Jiāngzhōu.
In the third month,
Tūfǎ Tán and Jǔqú Méngxùn battled at Qióngquán;
Tán was defeated.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Hé Wú-jì, the General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, fought Xún at Yùzhāng;
the royal army was defeated,
and Wú-jì died.
In summer, the fourth month,
Zhūgě Chángmín, the Inspector of Qīngzhōu, Liú Fān, the Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, [二八]and Liú Dàolián, the Inspector of Bìngzhōu, entered the capital to defend it.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
there was a great wind
that uprooted trees.
[二九]On the *wùzǐ* day,
Liú Yì, the General of the Guards, fought Lú Xún at Sāngluò Zhōu;
[三０]the royal army was defeated.
Mèng Chǎng, the Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was afraid
and committed suicide.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Xún reached Huáikǒu,
and internal and external alert was declared.
Sīmǎ Déwén, the Grand Marshal and Prince of Lángyá, oversaw all military affairs of the palace city
and was stationed at Zhōnghuángtáng.
Liú Yù, the Grand Commandant, was stationed at Shítou.
Liáng Zhēnzhī, the Prince of Liáng, was stationed at Nányèmén.
Liú Jìngxuan, the General of the Champions, was stationed in the northern suburbs.
Mèng Huáiyù, the General Who Assists the State, was stationed on the southern bank.
Wáng Zhòngdé, the General Who Establishes Might, was stationed at Yuèchéng.
Liú Huáimò, the General Who Expands Might, was stationed at Jiànyángmén.
At Huáikǒu, three fortresses—Zāpǔ, Yàoyuán, and Tíngwèi—were built to resist them.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the *chīwěi* ornament of the Grand Ancestral Temple was struck by lightning.
[三一]
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
Lú Xún fled.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wáng Zhòngdé, the General Who Assists the State, Liú Zhōng, the Administrator of Guǎngchuān, Kuǎi Ēn, the Administrator of Héjiān, and others were ordered to lead troops to pursue him.
In this month,
Lú Xún invaded Jīngzhōu.
Liú Dàoguī, the Inspector, Lǔ Zōngzhī, the Inspector of Yōngzhōu, and others defeated him.
They also defeated Xú Dàofù at Huáróng,
and the bandits fled again to Xúnyáng.
In the eighth month,
Yáo Xīng’s general Huán Qiān invaded Jiānglíng.
[三二]Liú Dàoguī defeated him.
In winter, the eleventh month,
the Shǔ bandits under Qiáo Zòng captured Bādōng,
and the defending generals Wēn Zuò and Shí Yánzǔ died.
In the twelfth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Liú Yù defeated Lú Xún at Yùzhāng.
In the seventh year, in spring, the second month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Liú Fān, the General of the Right, beheaded Xú Dàofù at Shǐxīng
and sent his head to the capital.
In summer, the fourth month,
Lú Xún fled to Jiāozhōu,
and Dù Huìdù, the Inspector, beheaded him.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,

Liú Dàoguī, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was appointed Grand General of the Expedition to the West, and was granted the privilege of establishing an administration and having the same status as the Three Dukes.
In winter, the tenth month,
Jǔqú Méngxùn attacked Liáng.
Xuánshèng, King Wǔzhāo of Liáng, fought him
and was defeated.
In the eighth year, in spring, the second month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Kǒng Jìng, the Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the third month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
the ground in Shānyīn sank four feet
with a sound like thunder.
In summer, the fifth month,
Qǐfú Gōngfǔ assassinated Qǐfú Gān-guī.
Qǐfú Chìpán, Gān-guī’s son, executed Gōngfǔ
[三三]and usurped the spurious throne.
In the sixth month,
Lǔ Zōngzhī, the General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed General Who Guards the North.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Jìdù, Prince of Wǔlíng, died.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
[三四]Liú Dàoguī, the Grand General of the Expedition to the West, died.
In the eighth month,
Empress Wáng died.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Chúnzhī, Prince of Gāomì, died.
In the ninth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Empress Xī was buried at Xiūpínglíng.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Liú Yù, the Grand Commandant, murdered Liú Fān, the General of the Right and Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, and Xiè Hùn, the Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Yù falsely issued an edict saying:
“Liú Yì harbored malicious intent
and plotted rebellion in the southern summer.
Fān and Hùn assisted in the chaos,
freely indulging in wickedness.
Thanks to Níngfǔ’s profound discernment,
who grasped the opportune moment and thwarted their sharpness,
the wicked party was executed,
and the altars of soil and grain are secure.
The virtue of cherishing life
is rooted in its origin;
extending clemency and compassion
truly relies on profound grace.
Moreover, the matter involved great evildoers,
and the calamity originated from the chief culprit.
Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm,
except for Liú Yì.
All civil and military officials shall be promoted one rank.
Filial, obedient, loyal, and righteous individuals,
as well as those hidden or neglected,
shall surely be brought to prominence.”
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Liú Yù led an army to attack Yì.
Wáng Zhèn’è, Yù’s military advisor, captured Jiānglíng city,
and Yì committed suicide.
In winter, the eleventh month,
Jǔqú Méngxùn usurped the title of King of Héxī.
In the twelfth month,
Zhū Língshí, the Administrator of Xīlíng, was appointed General Who Establishes Might
[三五]and Inspector of Yìzhōu, and was ordered to lead an army to attack Shǔ.
Ten commanderies of Jīngzhōu were separated to establish Xiāngzhōu.
In this year,
Lúlíng and Nánkāng experienced four earthquakes.
In the ninth year, in spring, the third month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Liú Yù murdered Zhūgě Chángmín, the Former General, and his brother Zhūgě Límín, the Grand General Who Assists the State, and his cousin Zhūgě Xiùzhī, the General Who Pacifies the North.
On the *wùyín* day,
[三六]Liú Yù was given the additional title of General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yùzhōu.
Fàn Húdá of Línyì attacked Jiǔzhēn.
[三七]Dù Huìdù, the Inspector of Jiāozhōu, beheaded him.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *rénxū* day,
forty *qǐng* of Empress’s cosmetics fields at Línyí and Húshú were abolished
and given to the poor,
and the restrictions on the lake ponds were lifted.
Lǔ Zōngzhī, the General Who Guards the North, was enfeoffed as Duke of Nányáng Commandery.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Zhū Língshí conquered Chéngdū
and beheaded Qiáo Zòng,
and Yìzhōu was pacified.
In the ninth month,
Liú Yù’s second son, Liú Yìzhēn, was enfeoffed as Duke of Guìyáng.
In winter, the twelfth month,
Qiúzhī, Prince of Ānpíng, died.
[三八]
In this year,
Gāogōulí, Wōguó, and the Copper Head Master of the Southwestern Yí all presented local products.
In the tenth year, in spring, the third month, on the *wùyín* day,
there was an earthquake.
In summer, the sixth month,
Qǐfú Chìpán led an army to attack Tūfǎ Tán
and destroyed him.
In autumn, the seventh month,
there was a great wind north of the Huái River
that destroyed houses.
In the ninth month, on the first day, *dīngsì*,
there was a solar eclipse.
Línyì sent envoys to present local products.
In this year,
the eastern palace was built.
In the eleventh year, in spring, the first month,
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, and Lǔ Zōngzhī, the Inspector of Yōngzhōu, both raised armies to revolt against Liú Yù.
Yù led an army to attack them.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Xiè Yù, the Minister of Personnel, was appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the second month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Yáo Xīng died,
and his son Yáo Hóng succeeded to the spurious throne.
[三九]
In the third month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Yùn, Prince of Huáilíng, died.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Liú Yù and Xiūzhī battled at Jiāngjīn.
Xiūzhī was defeated
and fled to Xiāngyáng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Liú Jìngxuan, the Inspector of Qīng and Jì Prefectures, was murdered by his military advisor Sīmǎ Dàocì.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
two comets were seen.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Xiūzhī and Zōngzhī fled to Yáo Hóng.
[四０]For the merit of pacifying Shǔ,
Liú Yù’s son Liú Yìlóng was enfeoffed as Duke of Péngchéng,
and Zhū Língshí as Duke of Fēngchéng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Huòshān collapsed,
and six bronze bells emerged.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
there was a great flood in the capital
that damaged the Grand Ancestral Temple.
On the last day of the month, *xīnhài*,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
[四一]Xiè Yù, the Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, died.
Liú Mùzhī, the Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
a great amnesty was proclaimed.
In the twelfth year, in the first month of spring,
Yáo Hóng sent his general Lǔ Guǐ to raid Xiāngyáng.
Zhào Lúnzhī, the Inspector of Yōngzhōu, attacked and repelled him.
In the second month,
Liú Yù was given the additional title of Grand Commander of Internal and External Armies.
In the sixth month of summer,
Hèlián Bóbó attacked Yáo Hóng's Qínzhōu,
and captured it.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Liú Liǔ, newly appointed as Minister of Personnel and Marquis of Dūxiāngtíng, died.
In the eighth month of autumn,
Liú Yù and Wáng Déwén, the Prince of Lángyé, led a host to attack Yáo Hóng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a great amnesty was proclaimed.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Yáo Guāng, a general of Yáo Hóng, surrendered Luòyáng.
〔四二〕On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Huīzhī, the acting Minister of Works and Prince of Gāomì, was sent to pay respects at the Five Mausoleums.
In the thirteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the *jiǎxū* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the second month,
Lǐ Xuánshèng, King Wǔzhāo of Liáng, died.
Shìyè, the heir apparent, succeeded to the throne as Shepherd of Liángzhōu and Duke of Liáng.
In the third month,
Wáng Zhèn'è, the General Who Soars Like a Dragon, decisively defeated Yáo Shào, a general of Yáo Hóng, at Tóngguān.
In summer,
Liú Yù defeated É Qīng, a general of Wèi, at Héqu.
〔四三〕He beheaded É Qīng's subordinate general Ā Bógān.
In this month,
Lǐ Shìyè, the Duke of Liáng, decisively defeated Jǔqú Méngxùn at Xiānzhījiàn.
〔四四〕
In the fifth month,
〔四五〕Liú Yù captured Tóngguān.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Xiūzhī, the Prince of Kuàijī, died.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Línyì offered trained elephants and white parrots as tribute.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Liú Yù captured Cháng'ān,
seized Yáo Hóng,
collected his ritual vessels,
and returned them to the capital.
Xú Dàoqī, a pirate from Nánhǎi, captured Guǎngzhōu.
Liú Qiānzhī, the Administrator of Shǐxīng, pacified him.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Liú Mùzhī, the Left Minister and Former General, died.
In the fourteenth year, in the first month of spring, on the *xīnsì* day,
〔四六〕a great amnesty was proclaimed.
Shěn Tiánzǐ, the Inspector of Qīngzhōu, killed Wáng Zhèn'è, the General Who Soars Like a Dragon, in Cháng'ān.
In the sixth month of summer,
Liú Yù was made Chancellor,
and advanced to be enfeoffed as Duke of Sòng.
In the tenth month of winter,
Shìyè, the Duke of Liáng, was made General Who Guards the West,
and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiǔquán.
In the eleventh month,
Hèlián Bóbó decisively defeated the imperial army north of Qīngní.
Zhū Língshí, the Inspector of Yōngzhōu, burned the palace of Cháng'ān,
and fled to Tóngguān.
Soon after, he suffered another crushing defeat,
and Zhū Língshí died.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor passed away in the Eastern Hall,
at the age of thirty-seven.
He was buried at Xiūpínglíng.
The Emperor was not intelligent;
from childhood to adulthood,
he could not speak,
and even with changes in temperature,
he could not distinguish them.
All his actions,
were not his own initiative.
Therefore, when Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
he survived because of this.
An early prophecy said,
"After Chāngmíng, there will be two emperors."
Liú Yù was about to usurp the throne,
so he secretly ordered Wáng Sháozhī to strangle the Emperor and install Emperor Gōng,
to fulfill the prophecy of "two emperors."
Emperor Gōng
Emperor Gōng's personal name was Déwén,
his courtesy name was Déwén.
He was the younger brother of Emperor Ān by the same mother.
Initially enfeoffed as Prince of Lángyé,
he successively held the posts of General of the Central Army, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, and Kaǐfǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
He was given the additional title of Attendant-in-Ordinary,
and concurrently held the posts of Minister of Education and Director of the Six Sections of the Imperial Secretariat.
In the early Yuánxīng era,
he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
When Huán Xuán held power,
he advanced to the position of Grand Tutor,
was granted the ceremonial cap and robes,
and a green ribbon.
When Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
he made the Emperor the Duke of Shíyáng County,
and he resided with Emperor Ān in Xúnyáng.
When Huán Xuán was defeated,
he followed to Jiānglíng.
After Huán Xuán's death,
Huán Zhèn suddenly arrived,
leaped on horseback, brandished a halberd,
and went straight to the steps,
staring with wide eyes, he said to Emperor Ān:
"What wrong did my family commit against the state,
to be slaughtered and exterminated like this?"
The Emperor then got off the bed and said to Zhèn:
"How could this be my brothers' intention!"
Zhèn then dismounted and bowed.
After Zhèn was pacified,
he was reinstated as Prince of Lángyé.
He also concurrently held the post of Inspector of Xúzhōu,
and soon after was appointed Grand Marshal,
concurrently Minister of Education,
and accorded special ceremonial honors.
In the fifth year of Yìxī,
he was provided with Left and Right Chiefs of Staff, a Grand Administrator, and four Attendant-in-Ordinary with the title of Zhonglang.
He was granted feather banners and drum and pipe music.
In the twelfth year,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Grand Marshal, with his brilliant virtue and close kinship,
and the Grand Commandant, with his glorious achievements,
both uphold the eternal principles,
harmonize the two *qì*,
and inspire outstanding talents,
who long to assist in governance.
Yet, they are elegantly modest and reserved,
not opening their doors to all,
which truly aligns with the humble way of the great sages,
but deviates from the urgent need to attract worthy men to aid the world.
In ancient times, when carts with rush-covered wheels were used to summon,
extraordinary men emerged together.
When Dōngpíng established its administration,
talented scholars flocked to it.
Such a flourishing multitude
is something I admire.
Let an imperial order be given to the two offices [Grand Marshal and Grand Commandant]
to recruit as before,
and they will certainly elevate the worthy and outstanding,
following the path of former sages."
Thus, he began to recruit subordinates.
At that time, Grand Commandant Yù supervised all internal and external armies.
An imperial edict stated:
"The Grand Marshal holds a high position and heavy responsibility;
among his close and worthy relatives, none are his equal.
Although his office receives orders,
he himself need not pay respects."
When Liú Yù embarked on his northern campaign,
the Emperor submitted a memorial,
requesting to lead his appointed contingent,
to set out on the military road,
and to pay respects at the imperial mausoleums.
The court granted his request,
so he departed with Yù.
When the officials concerned stated that he could not bid farewell at the imperial mausoleums while on a military campaign,
the Emperor again submitted a memorial, saying:
"Your servant is pushing the chariot into the field,
about to face the rigors of campaign.
Unable to express my feelings at the tomb,
my private heart is boundlessly distressed.
I humbly wish for Your Heavenly Mercy,
to especially grant my request,
so that my humble sincerity may be roughly expressed,
and I will have no regrets when I set out on the road."
This was granted.
When Yáo Hóng was destroyed, he returned to the capital.
In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year, on the day Wùyín,
Emperor Ān崩died.
Liú Yù矯falsely claimed an imperial edict, saying:
“Only my Jìn dynasty
has received the bright mandate,
its enterprise flourishing throughout the nine regions,
its light dwelling across the four seas.
I, being without virtue,
happened upon a time of great difficulty.
Fortunately, relying on my chief ministers,
its downfall was averted.
Then, trusting in divine protection,
I was able to suppress calamities and chaos,
and thus wore the imperial crown, ruling the
unified realm.
Just as I was about to rely on my premier
to renew this grand enterprise,
I encountered a severe illness
that will prevent my recovery.
Looking up, I reflect on the spiritual mandate of my ancestors,
who entrusted their burdens to worthy kin.
Now, you, Grand Marshal and Prince of Lángxié,
whose body is descended from the former emperor,
whose bright virtue shines gloriously,
you are the designated heir apparent,
the one upon whom the hopes of the populace converge.
Therefore, you shall rule over the Jìn state,
uphold the ancestral sacrifices,
truly grasp the mean,

Even the slightest gains or losses

Celestial Body
Anciently, there were three schools of thought concerning heaven:
one was the Gàitiān [Canopy Heaven] theory,
the second was the Xuānyè [Infinite Night] theory,
and the third was the Húntiān [Armillary Heaven] theory.
During the reign of Hàn Língdì,
Cài Yōng submitted a memorial from Shuòfāng,
stating: "
The Xuānyè school of thought
has no masters or methods whatsoever.
The methods and calculations of the Zhōubì [Gnomon of Zhou] are fully preserved,
but in examining the form of heaven,
they contain many discrepancies.
Only the Húntiān theory closely apprehends its true nature.
The bronze instrument used by the imperial astronomical observatory today is based on its method.
It erects an eight-foot spherical body, embodying the form of heaven and earth,
to rectify the ecliptic,
to observe and analyze convergence and divergence,
to track the movements of the sun and moon,
and to calculate the five planets.
It is subtle, profound, and exquisite,
a method that remains unchanged through a hundred generations.
The officials have the instrument but not the original text,
and previous records are also incomplete."
What Cài Yōng called the Zhōubì
is precisely the Gàitiān theory.
Its origin is attributed to Páoqīshì, who established the celestial calendar and degrees.
Its transmission is said to have come from the Dùkǒng [Duke of Zhou] who received it from Yīn Gāo,
and the people of Zhōu recorded it,
hence it is called Zhōubì.
Bì
means 'thigh' or 'gnomon';
a gǔ [thigh]
is a biǎo [gnomon].
It states that heaven resembles an inverted canopy,
and earth resembles a covering plate,
with heaven and earth both high in the middle and low at the periphery.
The area directly under the North Pole is the center of heaven and earth;
this land is the highest,
and slopes downwards on all four sides.
The three luminaries are hidden and revealed,
thus causing day and night.
The center of heaven is sixty thousand lǐ higher than the outer rim where the winter solstice sun is located.
The land under the North Pole is also sixty thousand lǐ higher than the land at the outer rim,
and the outer rim is twenty thousand lǐ higher than the land under the North Pole.
Heaven and earth rise together in a continuous incline,
and the sun is always eighty thousand lǐ from the earth.
The sun is attached to heaven and rotates horizontally,
dividing the path it travels between winter and summer into seven transverse lines and six intervals.
The circumference of each line
is calculated according to arithmetic,
using the Gōugǔ double difference method to determine sundial shadows and polar excursions,
thereby obtaining distances.
All of these are derived from the gnomon's gǔ [thigh/hypotenuse].
Hence it is called Zhōubì.
Moreover, the Zhōubì school says:
"Heaven is round like an open canopy,
and earth is square like a chessboard.
Heaven rotates sideways like a grinding mill, moving left,
while the sun and moon move right.
As they follow heaven's leftward rotation,
the sun and moon actually move eastward,
but heaven pulls them to set in the west.
This is comparable to an ant walking on a millstone:
the millstone rotates left, and the ant moves right,
but the millstone is faster and the ant is slower,
so it cannot but follow the millstone in its leftward turn.
The shape of heaven is higher in the south and lower in the north.
When the sun rises, it is high,
hence it is seen;
when the sun sets, it is low,
hence it is not seen.
Heaven's position is like a leaning canopy,
thus the pole is to the north of man,
which is its proof.
The pole is in the center of heaven,
yet now it is to the north of man,
which is why we know heaven's shape is like a leaning canopy.
The sun rises in the yang region in the morning,
and enters the yin region in the evening.
The yin qi is dark and obscure,
thus it sets and is not seen.
In summer, there is much yang qi and little yin qi.
The yang qi is bright,
shining together with the sun,
so when the sun rises it is immediately seen,
with nothing to obstruct it,
hence summer days are long.
In winter, there is much yin qi and little yang qi.
The yin qi is dark and obscure,
concealing the light of the sun,
so even when it rises it remains hidden and unseen,
hence winter days are short."
The writings of the Xuānyè school are lost.
Only Xī Méng, a secretary in the Hàn Imperial Library, recorded a tradition passed down from his former teacher, saying:
"Heaven has no substantial body at all.
Looking up at it,
it is immensely high and distant, without limit.
The eyes become blurry and vision fails,
hence it appears azure.
This is like looking across a great distance at the Huángshān mountains and seeing them all green,
or looking down into a thousand-fathom deep valley and seeing it profoundly black.
Azure is not its true color,
and black has no substance.
The sun, moon, and all the stars
naturally float and arise within empty space.
Their movements and rest all require qì.
Therefore, the Qīyào [seven luminaries] sometimes move and sometimes stop,
sometimes go with and sometimes against the flow,
appearing and disappearing without regularity,
advancing and retreating differently,
because they are not rooted or tied to anything.
Hence, they are all distinct.
Therefore, the celestial pole always remains in its place,
and the Northern Dipper does not set in the west with the other stars.
Shètí and Tiánxīng both move eastward,
the sun moves one degree a day,
the moon moves thirteen degrees a day.
Their speeds vary as they please,
which shows that they are not bound to anything.
If they were attached to a celestial body,
it would not be so."
During the Xiánkāng reign of Emperor Chéng,

Earth is deep, unfathomable in its unfathomableness.
Heaven is firmly above,
having a shape of constant stability;

When they cover and encompass each other,

There is no principle of them being different in shape, one square and one round.
Their radiant lights are spread out and arranged,

Yáo Xìn, Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Wú, created the Xīntiānlùn, saying:

Now, a person's chin extends forward over the chest,

Moreover, at the winter solstice, the pole is extremely low,

so the sun is far from humans,
but the Dǒu pole is close to humans,
and northern qi arrives,
hence the ice and cold.
At the summer solstice, the pole rises,
and Heaven moves closer to the north,
so the Dǒu pole is far from humans,
and the sun is close to humans,
and southern qi arrives,
hence the steaming heat.
When the pole is high,

When the pole is low,
the sun travels deeply within the earth,

Heaven is low to the earth,

From Yú Xǐ, Yú Sǒng, and Yáo Xìn, all put forward theories of seeking novelty and peculiarity;

As for the profound principles of the Húntiān theory,

Wáng Zhòngrèn of Hàn, based on the Gàitiān theory,

This is very incorrect.

A person's eyes can only see
