On the first day of the first month, *jǐmǎo* day, of the first year of Tàiníng of Emperor Míng's [reign],
the sun had a halo but no light.
On *guǐsì* day,
yellow fog filled all four directions.
The divination says:
"The imperial way has lost its clarity,
*yīn* and *yáng* are muddled,
and ministers have secret plots."
Jīng Fáng said:
"When inferiors monopolize punishment,
this is called dividing imperial authority,
and by covering the subtle, the sun loses its brightness."
Before this,
Wáng Dūn killed the Grand Minister of the Secretariat Diāo Xié, the Minister of Personnel Zhōu Yǐ, and General of Agile Cavalry Dài Ruòsī, among others.
This was the manifestation of monopolizing punishment.
After Dūn usurped authority,
he eventually suffered his punishment.
In the eleventh month, *bǐngzǐ* day,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
The imperial historians did not witness it,
but the Administrator of Guìyáng, Huà Bāo, reported it.
In the seventh month of the ninth year of Xiánhé of Emperor Chéng's [reign],
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
In the seventh month of the first year of Xiánkāng,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
In the seventh month of the second year,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
After this, the Yǔ clan monopolized power,
becoming noble through the empress's family.
This also implies women monopolizing state power,
hence the frequent appearances of white rainbows piercing the sun year after year.
In the first month, *rénshēn* day, of the eighth year,
there was a black spot in the sun,
which disappeared on *bǐngzǐ* day.
In summer,
the emperor passed away.
In the eighth year of Yǒnghé of Emperor Mù's [reign],
Zhāng Chónghuá was in Liángzhōu,
when the sun suddenly turned red like fire,
with a three-legged crow within it,
its form clearly visible,
and it stopped after five days.
In the tenth month, *gēngchén* day, of the tenth year,
there was a black spot in the sun,
as large as a chicken egg.
In the third month, *wùshēn* day, of the eleventh year,
there were two black spots in the sun,
as large as peaches.
At that time, the Son of Heaven was young and weak,
and had not personally handled state affairs for a long time.
In the tenth month, *bǐngwǔ* day, of the third year of Shēngpíng,
there was a black spot in the sun,
as large as a chicken egg.
Soon after, the emperor passed away.
On the night of the ninth month, *wùchén* day, of the third year of Tàihé of Hǎixī Gōng's [reign],
two rainbows appeared in the east.
In the fourth month, *wùchén* day, of the fourth year,
the sun had a halo,
thick and dense,
and a white rainbow pierced the center of the sun.
In the tenth month, *yǐwèi* day,
there was a black spot in the sun.
In the second month, *xīnyǒu* day, of the fifth year,
there was a black spot in the sun,
as large as a plum.
In the third month, *xīnwèi* day, of the sixth year,
a white rainbow pierced the sun,
and the sun had a halo,
fivefold.
In the eleventh month,
Huán Wēn deposed the emperor,
which was the first year of Xián'ān of Jiǎnwén's [reign].
In the eleventh month, *dīngchǒu* day, of the second year of Xián'ān of Jiǎnwén's [reign],
there was a black spot in the sun.
In the eleventh month, *jǐyǒu* day, of the first year of Níngkāng of Emperor Xiàowǔ's [reign],
there was a black spot in the sun,
as large as a plum.
In the third month, *gēngyín* day, of the second year,
there were two black spots in the sun,
as large as duck eggs.
In the eleventh month, *jǐsì* day,
there was a black spot in the sun,
as large as a chicken egg.
At that time, the emperor was already grown,
but Empress Kāngxiàn, as his paternal aunt-in-law, presided over the court,
which indeed damaged the imperial way,
hence the blemishes on the sun.
In the second month, *gēngzǐ* day, of the thirteenth year of Tàiyuán,
there were two black spots in the sun,
as large as plums.
In the sixth month, *xīnmǎo* day, of the fourteenth year,
there was again a black spot in the sun,
as large as a plum.
In the eleventh month, *xīnmǎo* day, of the twentieth year,
there was again a black spot in the sun.
At this time, the Prince of Kuàijī interfered in government affairs as the emperor's younger maternal brother.
In the twelfth month, *rénchén* day, of the first year of Lóng'ān of Emperor Ān's [reign],
the sun had a halo,
with a "back *qióng*."
After this, he did not personally attend to all state affairs,
and Yuánxiǎn, the heir apparent of the Prince of Kuàijī, monopolized the exercise of authority and punishment.
In the eleventh month, *xīnhài* day, of the fourth year,
there was a black spot in the sun.
In the second month, *jiǎzǐ* day, of the first year of Yuánxīng,
the sun had a halo,
and a white rainbow pierced the center of the sun.
In the third month, *gēngzǐ* day,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
Soon after,
Huán Xuán conquered the capital,
and the imperial army was defeated.
The next year,
Xuán usurped the throne.
In the first year of Yìxī, on the *gēngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
the sun had a multicolored halo.
In the sixth year, on the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fifth month,
there was a solar halo,
with a pearl-like appearance.
At that time, Lú Xún was pressing upon the capital,
and there was a state of emergency inside and outside the city.
In the seventh month,
Lú Xún fled.
In the seventh year, in the seventh month,
five rainbows appeared in the east.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will be deposed."
After this, Liú Yù usurped the Jìn.
In the tenth year,
the sun was in Dōngjǐng,
and there was a white rainbow more than ten *zhàng* long obstructing the sun from the south.
Calamity was in the Qín region,
an omen of Qín's demise.
In the second year of Yuánxī of Emperor Gōng, on the *rénchén* day of the first month,
a white vapor penetrated the sun,
and to the east and west were straight auroral extensions, each one *zhàng* long,
with white vapor interwoven through them.
Lunar anomalies
In the fourth year of Huángchū of Emperor Wén of Wèi, in the eleventh month,
the moon formed a halo around the Běidǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a great mourning,
and a general amnesty for the empire."
In the seventh year, in the fifth month,
the emperor passed away,
Emperor Míng ascended the throne,
and a general amnesty was granted to the empire.
In the fifth year of Yǒngjiā of Emperor Xiàohuái, on the *rénshēn* day of the third month, during the *bǐng* night,
there was a lunar eclipse,
which was total.
On the *dīng* night, there was another eclipse,
which was total.
The prognostication said:
"When the moon is totally eclipsed,
a great person will suffer distress."
It also said:
"A noble person of that state will die."
In the fourth year of Tàihé of Hǎixī Gōng, in the intercalary month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the moon formed a halo around Zhěn,
and again there was a white halo penetrating the northern part of the moon,
haloing the three stars of the Dǒubǐng.
The prognostication said:
"This is ominous for the king."
In the sixth year,
Huán Wēn deposed the emperor.
In the fifth year of Lóng'ān of Emperor Ān, on the *jiǎzǐ* day of the third month,
the moon grew "teeth."
The prognostication said:
"When the moon grows 'teeth,'
the Son of Heaven will have treacherous ministers,
and his subordinates will slaughter each other."
This was an omen of Huán Xuán's usurpation and rebellion.
In the ninth year of Yìxī, on the first day of the twelfth month, *xīnmǎo*,
the moon was still seen in the east.
This is called *zènì*,
and then the princes and kings will be in awe.
At this time, Liú Yù assisted in governance,
and his prestige and punishments were self-imposed,
which was the response to *zènì*.
In the eleventh year, in the eleventh month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the moon entered and haloed Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler is worried,
and treasures will be released."
Another account says:
"A lunar halo
indicates an amnesty."
Moon obscuring and transgressing the Five Planets
Whenever the moon eclipses the five planets,
that state will perish.
When the five planets enter the moon,
there will be a chase among the ministers in its domain.
In the fifth year of Tàihé of Emperor Míng of Wèi, on the *jiǎchén* day of the twelfth month,
the moon transgressed Zhēnxīng.
In the second year of Qīnglóng, on the *yǐchǒu* day of the tenth month,
the moon again transgressed Zhēnxīng.
The prognostication was the same as above.
On the *wùyín* day,
the moon transgressed Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will die,
and there will be war."
In the seventh month of the first year of Jǐngchū,
Gōngsūn Wényì rebelled.
In the first month of the second year,
Emperor Xuān was sent to suppress him.
In the first month of the third year,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
In the third month of the fourth year, on the *jǐsì* day,
Tàibái and the moon appeared together in broad daylight,
and the moon transgressed Tàibái.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the tenth month of the first year of Jǐngchū, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the moon transgressed Yínghuò.
The prognostication said:
"A noble person will die."
In the fourth month of the second year,
Sītú Hán Jì passed away.
In the first year of Jiāpíng of Qí Wáng, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the first month,
Tàibái attacked the moon.
Emperor Xuān memorialized to depose Empress Dowager Yǒngníng and Cáo Shuǎng and others.
In the second year of Tàiyān of Emperor Huì, in the eleventh month, on the *gēngchén* day,
The prognostication said:
"There will be a chase among the ministers in the state."
In the twelfth month, on the *rénnyín* day,
Tàibái transgressed the moon.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in the empire."
In the first month of the third year, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the prognostication was the same as in the first year of Qīnglóng.
Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Chén Zhěn and others led troops to support the emperor in attacking Chéngdū Wáng,
the six armies were defeated,
and war pressed upon the imperial carriage.
Two years later,
the emperor passed away.
In the second year of Tàixīng of Emperor Yuán, in the eleventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
the moon transgressed Yínghuò.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a rebellious minister."
In the twelfth month of the third year, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Tàibái entered the moon,
in Dǒu.
Guō Pú said:
"The moon belongs to Kǎn,
a symbol of the realm of Yin law.
Tàibái, representing the element Metal, came to transgress it,
Heaven's intention seems to be that
the administration of justice is out of balance,
and its own laws are being destroyed."
In the twelfth month of the fourth year, on the *dīnghài* day,
the moon transgressed Suìxīng,
in Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"That state will suffer war and famine,
and people will flee."
In the third month of the first year of Yǒngchāng,
Wáng Dūn rebelled,
leading troops from Jiāng and Jīng to attack,
defeating the capital,
and killing generals and ministers.
Furthermore,
Zhènběi Jiāngjūn Liú Wěi fled,
the common people all abandoned their fields,
and suffered from warfare.
In the fourth month,
Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ and Qiáo Wáng Sīmǎ Chéng were also killed,
as was Zhènnán Jiāngjūn Gān Zhuó.
In the second month of the first year of Xiánkāng of Emperor Chéng, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Tàibái entered the moon.
In the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the moon transgressed Tàibái.
In the fourth year, on the *jǐsì* day of the fourth month,
and on the *yǐsì* day of the seventh month,
the moon both obscured Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will die.
And there will be war,
which the ruler dislikes."
The following year,
Shí Jìlóng's forces greatly ravaged Miǎnnán,
and thus there was a state of emergency inside and outside the city.
In the fifth year, in the fourth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the moon transgressed Suìxīng,
in Wèi.
The prognostication said:
"The state will suffer famine,
and people will flee."
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the moon transgressed Suìxīng,
in Máo.
By winter,
there was the defeat at Miǎnnán and Zhūchéng,
and more than ten thousand households of common people fled.
In the sixth year, in the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Tàibái entered the moon.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will die."
In the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the moon transgressed Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler dislikes it."
In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Yǒnghé of Emperor Mùdì,
the Moon was in Dōngjǐng,
and encroached upon Suìxīng.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will suffer famine,
and its people will flee."
At this time, military conflicts frequently erupted.
In the eleventh month of the tenth year,
the Moon covered Tiánxīng,
in Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will have military conflicts."
At this time, Huán Wēn attacked Fú Jiàn.
Jiàn fortified Cháng'ān,
and Wēn retreated.
In the eighth month of the twelfth year,
Huán Wēn defeated Yáo Xiāng.
On the day Rénwǔ in the eleventh month of the first year of Shēngpíng,
the Moon covered Suìxīng,
in Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine."
Another prognostication said:
"Yùzhōu will suffer disaster."
On the day Yǐhài in the intercalary third month of the second year,
the Moon encroached upon Suìxīng,
in Fáng.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the third year,
Xiè Wàn, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, was defeated.
On the day Yǐyǒu in the third month of the third year,
the Moon encroached upon Tàibái,
in Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will die."
Another prognostication said:
"There will be military conflicts in Zhàodì,
and the Hú will be uneasy."
In the first month of the fourth year,
Mùróng Jùn died.
At Chénshí on the day Yǐchǒu in the first month of the fifth year,
the Moon was in Wēixù,
and covered Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The empire will scatter and disperse."
On the day Dīngwèi in the third month,
the Moon encroached upon Tiánxīng,
in Zhěn.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a great mourning."
In the fifth month,
Emperor Mùdì passed away.
In the seventh month,
Mùróng Kè attacked Lǚ Hù, the Inspector of Jìzhōu, at Yěwáng,
and captured it,
and Hù fled.
At this time, Huán Wēn, with a large army, was at Wǎn.
Hearing of Hù's defeat,
he retreated.
On the day Bǐngxū in the tenth month of the first year of Xīngníng of Emperor Āidì,
the Moon covered Tàibái,
in Xūnǚ.
The prognostication said:
"The empire will scatter and disperse."
Another prognostication said:
"The disaster will be in Yángzhōu."
In the third year,
Luòyáng fell.
Afterwards, Huán Wēn expended Yángzhōu's resources and provisions for a northern expedition,
suffered a crushing defeat,
and more than half of his men died.
When he campaigned against Yuán Zhēn,
Huáinán was devastated and broken.
Later, Mùróng Wěi and Fú Jiān alternately invaded the borders.
On the day Yǐmǎo in the first month of the third year,
the Moon covered Suìxīng,
in Cān.
The prognostication said:
"Cān,
signifies the division of Yìzhōu."
In the sixth month,
Zhōu Fǔ, General Guarding the West and Inspector of Yìzhōu, died.
In the tenth month,
Sīmǎ Xūn, Inspector of Liángzhōu, entered Yìzhōu and rebelled.
Zhū Xù led his forces to assist Inspector Zhōu Chǔ in suppressing him.
On the day Bǐngzǐ in the second month of the first year of Tàihé of Hǎixī,
the Moon covered Yínghuò,
in Cān.
The prognostication said:
"There will be internal strife,
a sign that the Emperor will not finish his reign."
Another prognostication said:
"Cān,
is Wèidì."
In the fifth year,
Mùróng Wěi was destroyed by Fú Jiān.
On the day Wùyín in the second month of the twelfth year of Tàiyuán of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
Yínghuò entered the Moon.
The prognostication said:
"A rebellious minister will die,
or there will be those who kill each other."
Another prognostication said:
"Female relatives will govern,
and the empire will be in chaos."
At this time, the Prince of Lángxié assisted in governance.
Wáng Guóbǎo, the queen's cousin, gained favor through their familial closeness.
Furthermore, Yuán Yuèmèi from Chénjùn deceitfully and unscrupulously advanced,
colluded with the Emperor and prime minister,
and fanned the flames of factionalism.
In the thirteenth year,
[三一]the Emperor executed Yuè in the marketplace.
Thus, a rift formed between the Emperor and prime minister,
and the seeds of chaos were sown.
On the day Wùzǐ in the twelfth month of the thirteenth year,
[三二]Chénxīng entered the Moon,
in Wēi.
The prognostication said:
"A treacherous minister desires to kill the ruler,
within three years,
there will certainly be internal evil."
After this, Mùróng Chuí, Zhái Liáo, Yáo Cháng, Fú Dēng, and Mùróng Yǒng all raised armies and contended for power.
On the day Yǐwèi in the twelfth month of the fourteenth year,
the Moon encroached upon Suìxīng.
The prognostication was the same as above.
[三三]In the fifteenth year,
Zhái Liáo occupied Sī and Yǎn,
and the various armies repeatedly attacked but could not overcome him.
The Mùróng clan also expanded across Bìng and Jì.
In the seventh month,
there was a drought.
In the eighth month,
there were great floods in various commanderies,
[三四]and Yǎnzhōu also suffered from locusts.
On the day Yǐyǒu in the first month of the eighteenth year,
Yínghuò entered the Moon.
The prognostication said:
"Trouble is within the palace,
it is not from rebels but from thieves."
Another prognostication said:
"There is a rebellious minister,
or there will be those who are executed."
In the ninth month of the twenty-first year,
the Emperor suddenly died in the inner palace.
The common people declared
that Lady Zhāng had secretly committed a great act of treason.
Furthermore,
Wáng Guóbǎo, being cunning and deceitful,
eventually met his just punishment.
On the day Jǐsì in the fourth month of the nineteenth year,
the Moon covered Suìxīng,
in Wěi.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine,
and the state of Yān will perish."
In the twentieth year,
Mùróng Chuí sent his son Bǎo to attack Wèi,
but was instead defeated by them,
with tens of thousands dead.
In the twenty-first year,
Chuí died,
and the state subsequently declined and perished.
In the first year of Ān Dì’s Lóng’ān reign, in the sixth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Moon occulted Venus
outside the Duānmén gate of Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"The nation will suffer from warfare."
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Moon occulted Jupiter
in Dōngbì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine,
and warfare in Wèi territory."
In the sixth month of the second year,
Xī Huī dispatched Dèng Qǐfāng and others with ten thousand men to attack Mùróng Bǎo at Huátái,
and Qǐfāng was defeated.
In the ninth month of the third year,
Huán Xuán and others all raised troops;
thus, a state of emergency was declared internally and externally.
In the first month of the fourth year, on the day Yǐhài,
the Moon violated Saturn
in Qiānniú.
The prognostication said:
"There will be warfare and death in Wú and Yuè,
and the empress will be in distress."
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Moon again violated Saturn
in Qiānniú.
In the tenth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Moon occulted Jupiter
in Běihé.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine,
and the Hú will have warfare."
In the fifth month of that fourth year,
Sūn Ēn broke into Kuàijī,
killing the Internal Scribe Xiè Yǎn.
Later, he again defeated Gāo Yǎzhī at Yúyáo,
where seventeen or eighteen out of ten people died.
In the seventh month,
Grand Empress Dowager Lǐ Shì passed away.
In the first year of Yuánxīng,
Sūn Ēn raided Línhǎi,
and the populace starved to death,
almost entirely dispersed and perished.
In the fourth month of the first year of Yuánxīng, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the Moon occulted Mercury.
In the seventh month,
there was a great famine,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
In the eleventh month of the second year, on the day Xīnsì,
the Moon violated Mars.
The prognostication was entirely the same as above.
In the twelfth month of the second year,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
exiling the Emperor and Empress to Xúnyáng,
and making Empress Hén of Yǒng'ān the Lord of Línglíng.
〔三五〕In the second month of the third year,
Liú Yù completely exterminated the Huán clan.
In the second month of the third year, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Moon occulted Jupiter in Zuǒjiǎo.
The prognostication said:
"Warfare will erupt throughout the land."
In the second month of this year, on the day Bǐngchén,
〔三六〕Liú Yù raised righteous troops,
killing Huán Xiū and others.
In the first month of the following year,
the combined armies attacked Huán Zhèn,
and eventually extinguished all of the Huán.
In the fourth month of the first year of Yìxī, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Moon violated Saturn
in Dōngbì.
The prognostication said:
"That territory will lose its state."
Another interpretation said:
"A nobleman will die."
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Moon occulted Saturn
in Dōngbì.
〔三七〕The prognostication said:
"That state will perish through conquest."
Another interpretation said:
"People will be displaced."
In the tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Moon occulted Saturn
in Yíngshì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the eleventh month,
Wèi Yǒngzhī, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, passed away.
In the second month of the second year,
Sīmǎ Guóyáng and others attacked and captured Yìyáng.
In the third year,
Wáng Mì, the Grand Chancellor and Inspector of Yángzhōu, passed away.
In the first month of the fourth year,
Tàibǎo Wǔlíng Wáng Zūn passed away.
In the third month,
Kǒng Ānguó, the Left Assistant, passed away.
In the twelfth month of the second year, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Moon occulted Venus
in Wēi.
The prognostication said:
"Qí will lose its state."
Another interpretation said:
"The ruler of a powerful state will die."
In the fourth month of the fifth year,
Liú Yù's great army campaigned north against Mùróng Chāo,
and eventually exterminated him.
In the sixth month of the seventh year, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Moon violated Jupiter
in Bì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be border warfare,
and also famine."
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
the Moon violated Jupiter
in Cān.
The prognostication said:
"Yìzhōu will have warfare and famine."
In the seventh month,
Zhū Língshí conquered Shǔ;
the Shǔ people soon rebelled,
and were again suppressed.
In the first month of the eighth year, on the day Gēngxū,
the Moon violated Jupiter
in Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the seventh month of the ninth year,
Zhū Língshí destroyed Shǔ.
In the fifth month of the twelfth year, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Moon violated Jupiter
in Zuǒjiǎo.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine."
In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, on the day Rénshēn,
the Moon violated Saturn
in Zhāng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a great mourning throughout the land."
In the following year,
the Emperor passed away.
〔三八〕
In the seventh month of Gōng Dì’s Yuánxī first year,
the Moon violated Jupiter.
The prognostication was entirely the same as above.
〔三九〕In the twelfth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Moon violated Venus in Yǔlín.
In the sixth month of the second year,
the Emperor abdicated his position,
ceding it to Sòng.
The Gathering of the Five Planets
In the seventh month of Wèi Míng Dì’s Tàihé fourth year, on the day Rénxū,
〔四０〕Venus violated Jupiter.
The prognostication said:
"If Venus violates the five planets,
there will be great warfare."
In the third month of the fifth year,
Zhūgě Liàng, with a large army, raided Tiānshuǐ.
At that time, Xuān Dì was the Grand General
and repelled him.
In the second month of Qīnglóng second year, on the day Jǐwèi,
Venus violated Mars.
The prognostication said:
"Great warfare will arise,
and there will be a great battle."
In the fourth month of this year,
Zhūgě Liàng occupied Wèinán,
and Wú also raised troops to support him,
causing Wèi to rush to its defense in the east and west.
In the third year of Huì Dì’s Yuánkāng reign,
Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus, three planets, gathered in Bì and Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies warfare and death.
Bì and Mǎo
are the territory of Zhào."
Later, Empress Jiǎ trapped and killed the Crown Prince;
the King of Zhào deposed the Empress
and then killed her,
executing Zhāng Huá and Péi Wěi,
and then usurped the throne,
deposing the Emperor as the Retired Emperor.
From this point, the realm plunged into continuous chaos and calamity.
In the eleventh month of Yǒngníng (永寧) 2nd year (301 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) and Tàibái (太白) fought in Xūwēi (虛危).
The prognostication stated:
“Great armies will arise,
breaking armies and killing generals.
Xūwēi (虛危)
is also the division of Qí (齊).”
In the twelfth month,
Yínghuò (熒惑) attacked Tàibái (太白) in Yíngshì (營室).
The prognostication stated:
“Armies will arise throughout the land,
a warning of the loss of the ruler.”
One account says:
“The prime minister will be changed.”
Initially,
Qí Wáng Jǐong (齊王冏) went to the capital,
and was allowed to remain to assist in governance.
He then became arrogant and defied the ruler.
In this month,
Chéngdū (成都) and Héjiān (河間) issued a proclamation to Chángshā Wáng (長沙王) to attack him.
Jǐong (冏) engaged in battle,
and the palaces were attacked and burned.
Jǐong’s (冏) army was defeated,
and he was wiped out.
His elder brother, Shàngjūn Jiāngjūn Shí (上軍將軍寔), and over two thousand others were also killed.
In Tàiyán (太安) 2nd year (303 CE),
Chéngdū (成都) again attacked Chángshā (長沙).
At this time, both public and private sectors suffered from famine and hardship,
and the common people were exhausted.
In the first month of Tàiyán (太安) 3rd year (304 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be war.”
In the seventh month,
Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Chén Zhěn (左衞將軍陳眕) accompanied the emperor to attack Chéngdū (成都),
and the six armies suffered a crushing defeat.
In the ninth month of Guāngxī (光熙) 1st year (306 CE),
Zhēnxīng (填星) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星).
The prognostication stated:
“When Zhēn (填) and Suì (歲) conjoin,
it signifies internal turmoil.”
At this time, Sīmǎ Yuè (司馬越) monopolized power,
and ultimately met with destruction due to his lack of decorum,
which was the manifestation of internal turmoil.
On the Guǐwèi (癸未) day of the twelfth month,
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星).
The prognostication stated:
“It signifies internal military conflict,
with a great battle.”
After this, Héjiān Wáng (河間王) was killed by Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越).
In the first month of the following year,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越) killed Zhūgě Méi (諸葛玫) and others.
In the fifth month,
Jí Sāng (汲桑) defeated Féng Sōng (馮嵩),
and killed Dōngyàn Wáng (東燕王).
In the eighth month,
Gǒu Xī (苟晞) greatly defeated Jí Sāng (汲桑).
In the seventh month of Huái Dì Yǒngjiā (懷帝永嘉) 6th year (312 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑), Suìxīng (歲星), and Tàibái (太白) gathered between Niú (牛) and Nǚ (女),
lingering and moving back and forth.
Examining the prognostication, it stated
“Niú (牛) and Nǚ (女)
are the division of Yángzhōu (揚州).”
After this, the two capitals fell,
and Yuán Dì (元帝) revived the dynasty in Yáng (揚) territory.
On the Guǐwèi (癸未) day of the fifth month of Jiànwǔ (建武) 1st year (317 CE),
Tàibái (太白) and Yínghuò (熒惑) conjoined in Dōngjǐng (東井).
The prognostication stated:
“When metal and fire conjoin, it is called 'shining brightly,'
signifying a death.”
At this time, Mǐn Dì (愍帝) was captured in Píngyáng (平陽),
and died in the enemy court in the seventh month.
On the Jiǎwǔ (甲午) day of the seventh month of Yuán Dì Tàixīng (元帝太興) 2nd year (319 CE),
Suìxīng (歲星) and Yínghuò (熒惑) met in Dōngjǐng (東井).
On the Yǐwèi (乙未) day of the eighth month,
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星),
conjoining in Yì (翼).
The prognostication stated:
“It signifies war and famine.”
On the Bǐngchén (丙辰) day of the sixth month of the 3rd year (320 CE),
Tàibái (太白) and Suìxīng (歲星) conjoined in Fáng (房).
The prognostication was the same as above.
In Yǒngchāng (永昌) 1st year (322 CE), Wáng Dūn (王敦) attacked the capital,
and the six armies suffered a crushing defeat.
Wáng Dūn (王敦) died shortly after.
On the Yǐchǒu (乙丑) day of the eleventh month of Chéng Dì Xiánkāng (成帝咸康) 3rd year (337 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星) in Yíngshì (營室).
The prognostication stated:
“It signifies war and famine.”
In the second month of the 4th year (338 CE),
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍) conquered Yōuzhōu (幽州),
and moved over ten thousand households southward.
In the 5th year (339 CE),
Jìlóng's (季龍) army of fifty thousand raided Miǎnnán (沔南),
and plundered over seven thousand households before leaving.
His twenty thousand cavalry also besieged and captured Zhūchéng (邾城),
killing and plundering over five thousand people.
On the Guǐchǒu (癸丑) day of the twelfth month of the 4th year (338 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星),
in Jī (箕).
The prognostication stated:
“The king will lose territory.”
In the 7th year (341 CE),
Mùróng Huàng (慕容皝) declared himself King of Yān (燕).
In the third month of the 7th year (341 CE),
Tàibái (太白) and Yínghuò (熒惑) conjoined within Tàiwēi (太微),
encroaching upon Zuǒ Zhífǎ (左執法).
In the following year,
Xiǎnzōng (顯宗) died.
On the Jǐyǒu (己酉) day of the twelfth month of the 8th year (342 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Yínghuò (熒惑) in Wèi (胃).
The prognostication stated:
“Great armies will arise.”
Thereafter, Yú Yì (庾翼) raised a large army,
planning to attack Shí Jìlóng (石季龍),
and exclusively controlled the upper reaches of the river.
On the Dīngwèi (丁未) day of the eighth month of Kāng Dì Jiàn Yuán (康帝建元) 1st year (343 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星),
in Zhěn (軫).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be great armies.”
In this year, Shí Jìlóng's (石季龍) general Liú Níng (劉寧) invaded and occupied Dí Dào (狄道).
In the fifth month of Mù Dì Yǒnghé (穆帝永和) 4th year (348 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) entered Lóu (婁),
encroaching upon Zhēnxīng (填星).
The prognostication stated:
“Great armies will arise,
there will be deaths,
the disaster will be in Zhào (趙).”
In that year, Shí Jìlóng (石季龍) died.
The following year, Rǎn Mǐn (冉閔) killed Shí Zūn (石遵) and over one hundred thousand of the various Hú (胡) peoples.
Thereafter, Chǔ Póu (褚裒) led a northern expedition,
lost his army, and died.
On the Wùxū (戊戌) day of the third month of the 6th year (350 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星).
The prognostication stated:
“It signifies war.”
On the Wùzǐ (戊子) day of the third month of the 7th year (351 CE),
Suìxīng (歲星) and Yínghuò (熒惑) conjoined in Kuí (奎).
In that year, Liú Xiǎn (劉顯) killed Shí Zhī (石祗) and the various Hú (胡) chieftains,
and the central plains fell into great chaos.
On the Dīngmǎo (丁卯) day of the seventh month of the 12th year (356 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星),
in Liǔ (柳).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be great armies in the Zhōu (周) territory.”
In the eighth month of that year,
Huán Wēn (桓溫) attacked Fú Jiàn (苻健),
then retreated.
He subsequently defeated Yáo Xiāng (姚襄) at Yīshuǐ (伊水),
and pacified the Zhōu (周) territory.
On the Wùwǔ (戊午) day of the eighth month of Shēngpíng (升平) 2nd year (358 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星),
in Zhāng (張).
The prognostication stated:
“Great armies will arise.”
On the Gēngwǔ (庚午) day of the eighth month of the 3rd year (359 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星),
within Tàiwēi (太微).
The prognostication stated:
“The king will be displeased by this.”
On the Dīngmǎo (丁卯) day of the tenth month of the 5th year (361 CE),
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星),
in Yíngshì (營室).
The prognostication stated:
“A high official has a hidden conspiracy.”
One account says:
“There will be military conflict in Wèi (衞) territory.”
At this time, Huán Wēn (桓溫) wielded autocratic power,
and conspired to transfer the Jìn (晉) dynasty.
On the Wùwǔ (戊午) day of the eighth month of Hǎixī Gōng Tàihé (海西公太和) 1st year (366 CE),
Tàibái (太白) encroached upon Suìxīng (歲星),
within Tàiwēi (太微).
On the Jiǎyín (甲寅) day of the sixth month of the 3rd year (368 CE),
Tàibái (太白) obscured Yínghuò (熒惑),
within Tàiwēi Duānmén (太微端門).
In the 6th year (371 CE),
Hǎixī Gōng (海西公) was deposed.
[四一]
On the Jǐyǒu (己酉) day of the first month of Jiǎnwén Xián'ān (簡文咸安) 2nd year (372 CE),
Suìxīng (歲星) encroached upon Zhēnxīng (填星),
in Xūnǚ (須女).
The prognostication stated:
“It signifies internal turmoil.”
In the seventh month,
the emperor died.
Huán Wēn (桓溫) wielded autocratic power,
and conspired to kill Shìzhōng Wáng Tǎnlán (侍中王坦之) and others,
which was the manifestation of internal turmoil.
On the Guǐyǒu (癸酉) day of the eleventh month of Xiàowǔ Níngkāng (孝武寧康) 2nd year (374 CE),
Tàibái (太白) obscured Yínghuò (熒惑),
in Yíngshì (營室).
The prognostication stated:
“When metal and fire conjoin, it is called 'shining brightly,'
signifying military conflict and death.”
In the seventh month of Tàiyuán (太元) 1st year (376 CE),
Fú Jiān (苻堅) attacked Liángzhōu (涼州),
defeated it,
and captured Zhāng Tiānxī (張天錫).
In the eleventh year of Tàiyuán, on the jǐchǒu day of the twelfth month,
Tàibái transgressed Suìxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies warfare and famine."
At this time, Hèshuò was not yet pacified,
and troops were continuously engaged in external conflicts,
leading to a great famine in winter.
In the seventeenth year, on the dīngchǒu day of the ninth month,
Suìxīng, Yínghuò, and Tiánxīng were all in Kàng and Dī.
In the twelfth month, on the guǐyǒu day,
Tiánxīng departed,
but Yínghuò and Suìxīng were still conjoined.
The prognostication stated:
"When the three stars conjoin,
this is called 'startling establishment and abrupt severance of conduct,'
with internal and external warfare, death, and famine,
and the replacement of kings and dukes."
In the nineteenth year, in the tenth month,
Tàibái, Tiánxīng, Yínghuò, and Chénxīng conjoined in Dī.
In the twelfth month, on the guǐchǒu day,
Tàibái transgressed Suìxīng,
in Dǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies disorder and famine,
and internal warfare.
Dǒu
is the division of Wúyuè."
By the first year of Lóng'ān,
Wáng Gōng and others raised troops,
exposing Wáng Guóbǎo's crimes,
and the court executed him.
Thereafter, there were continuous years of floods, droughts, and famine.
In the first year of Lóng'ān of Emperor Ān, in the second month,
Suìxīng and Yínghuò both entered Yǔlín.
The prognostication stated:
"The central army will rise in revolt."
In the fourth month,
Wáng Gōng and others raised troops,
and internal and external martial law was declared.
In the first year of Yuánxīng, on the gēngzǐ day of the eighth month,
Tàibái transgressed Suìxīng,
to the southeast of Shàngjiāng.
The prognostication stated:
"Chǔ will suffer warfare and famine."
Another interpretation stated:
"Calamity will befall Shàngjiāng."
In the second year,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne.
In the third year,
Liú Yù completely annihilated the Huán clan.
In the second year, on the dīngchǒu day of the tenth month,
Tàibái transgressed Tiánxīng,
in Lóu.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the third year, on the rénchén day of the second month,
Tàibái and Yínghuò conjoined in Yǔlín.
In the twelfth month of the second year,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
exiling the Emperor and Empress.
In the second month of the third year,
Liú Yù raised a righteous army,
and Huán Xuán forced the Emperor to move east.
In the second year of Yìxī, on the dīngwèi day of the twelfth month,
Yínghuò and Tàibái both entered Yǔlín,
and also conjoined in Bì.
In the first month of the third year,
Mùróng Chāo raided north of the Huái River and Xúzhōu,
reaching Xiàpī.
In the eighth month,
Liú Jìngxuān was dispatched to attack Shǔ.
In the third year, on the guǐhài day of the second month,
Yínghuò, Tiánxīng, Tàibái, and Chénxīng gathered in Kuí and Lóu,
following Tiánxīng,
the division of Xúzhōu.
At this time,
Mùróng Chāo proclaimed himself emperor in Qí,
with continuous warfare in Xú and Yǎn,
and continuous years of raids and looting,
reaching the Huái and Sì Rivers.
Yáo Xīng and Qiáo Zòng proclaimed themselves emperors in Qín and Shǔ,
and Lú Xún and Wèi invaded both north and south.
In its fifth year,
Liú Yù subjugated Mùróng Chāo in the north.
In its sixth month, on the xīnmǎo day,
Yínghuò transgressed Chénxīng,
in Yì.
The prognostication stated:
"Warfare will erupt throughout the realm."
In the eighth month, on the jǐmǎo day,
Tàibái obscured Yínghuò.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be great warfare."
In its fourth year,
Yáo Lüè dispatched troops to attack Hèlián Bóbó,
and was largely defeated by him.
In the fifth year, on the jiǎxū day of the fourth month,
Yínghuò transgressed Chénxīng,
in Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"All signify warfare."
In the twelfth month, on the xīnchǒu day,
Tàibái transgressed Suìxīng,
in Kuí.
The prognostication stated:
"Great warfare will erupt,
and Lǔ will experience warfare."
In the fourth month of this year,
Liú Yù campaigned against Mùróng Chāo.
In the second month of the sixth year,
Mùróng Chāo was eliminated in the land of Lǔ.
In the seventh year, on the dīngmǎo day of the seventh month,
Suìxīng transgressed Tiánxīng,
in Cān.
The prognostication stated:
"The conjunction of Suì and Tián
signifies internal disorder."
Another interpretation stated:
"Yìzhōu will fight,
not prevail,
and lose territory."
At this time, Zhū Língshí attacked Shǔ,
and eventually annihilated it.
The next year,
Xiè Hùn and Liú Yì were executed.
In the eighth year, on the jiǎshēn day of the seventh month,
Tàibái transgressed Tiánxīng,
in Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"Qín will experience great warfare."
In the ninth year, on the bǐngwǔ day of the second month,
Yínghuò and Tiánxīng both transgressed Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"Qín will experience warfare."
In the third month, on the rénchén day,
Suìxīng, Yínghuò, Tiánxīng, and Tàibái gathered in Dōngjǐng,
following Suìxīng.
Dōngjǐng
is the division of Qín.
In the thirteenth year,
Liú Yù pacified Guānzhōng,
and thereafter transferred the Jìn dynasty's mandate.
In the fourteenth year, on the guǐsì day of the tenth month,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi,
transgressing Xīfān Shàngjiāng,
then proceeded directly to the inside of Zuǒyèmén,
staying for twenty days before retrograding.
Until the fifth day of the third month of the first year of Yuánxī of Emperor Gōng,
it emerged about three chǐ west of Xīfān Shàngjiāng,
and then returned to Tàiwēi in direct motion.
At this time, Tiánxīng was in Tàiwēi,
and Yínghuò circled Tiánxīng forming a hook,
and in the fourth month of that year, on the bǐngxū day,
it exited from Duānmén.
The prognostication stated:
"When Yínghuò and Tiánxīng form a hook in the celestial court,
the world's reign will change."
In the twelfth month,
the King of Lángyá, brother of Emperor Ān's mother, ascended the throne,
who was Emperor Gōng.
The following year,
the throne was abdicated to Sòng.
Collation Notes

Treatise Three: Astronomy, Part Two (Lunar and Five-Planet Transgressions of Constellations, Abnormalities of Fixed Stars and Attached Phenomena, Unlucky Stars and Guest Stars, Meteor Showers and Falls, Clouds and Vapors) Lunar and Five-Planet Transgressions of Constellations (Abnormalities of Fixed Stars and Attached Phenomena)
In the fourth year of Huángchū of Emperor Wèi Wén, in the third month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the moon encroached upon Xīn Dàxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"Xīn is the position of the Son of Heaven;
it bodes ill for the king."
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
According to Liú Xiàng's Wǔjì Lùn, it says:
"Tàibái is lesser yin,
weak,
and ought not to move independently.
Therefore, Jiwèi is set as its boundary,
and it should not traverse the sky.
If it traverses the sky, then it is seen in daylight,
and its prognostication signifies warfare and mourning,
disobedience to authority,
and a change of kings;
strong states weaken,
and small states strengthen."
At this time, Sūn Quán received a noble title from Wèi,
but raised troops and maintained his defenses.
In the twelfth month of that year, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
the moon encroached upon Xīn Dàxīng.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the fifth year, in the tenth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
The prognostication was the same as above.
Moreover, Suìxīng entered Tàiwēi and retrograded,
remaining there for 149 days before exiting.
The prognostication stated:
"If the Five Planets enter Tàiwēi,
entering from the right for thirty days or more,
the human sovereign will have great sorrow."
Another saying states:
"There will be an amnesty."
In the seventh year, in the fifth month,
the Emperor died.
Emperor Míng ascended the throne
and issued a great amnesty to the world.
In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the day Rénxū,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi.
Until the day Rénshēn,
it met with Suìxīng,
and together they encroached upon the right Zhífǎ.
It did not exit until the day Guǐyǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"If it enters from the right for thirty days or more,
the human sovereign will have great sorrow."
It also stated:
"If the moon or the Five Planets encroach upon the left or right Zhífǎ,
high-ranking ministers will have sorrow."
Another saying states:
"The Zhífǎ will be executed;
Jīn and Huǒ are especially severe."
In the eleventh month,
the imperial prince Dōngwǔyáng Wáng Jiàn died.
In the seventh year, in the first month,
Piaojì Jiāngjūn Cái Hóng was dismissed and became a commoner.
In the fourth month,
Zhēngnán Dàjiāngjūn Xiàhóu Shàng died.
In the fifth month,
the Emperor died.
The Shǔ Jì states that Emperor Míng asked Huáng Quán, saying:
"With the world divided into three,
which land is truly righteous?"
He replied:
"One should verify it with astronomy.
Previously, Yínghuò guarded Xīn and Emperor Wén died;
Wú and Shǔ had no incidents.
This is the omen."
However, the histories of the Three Kingdoms do not contain the phrase "Yínghuò guarding Xīn";
it is suspected that it refers to entering Tàiwēi.
In the eighth month,
Wú then besieged Jiāngxià,
and raided Xiāngyáng.
Dàjiāngjūn Xuāndì rescued Xiāngyáng,
beheading Wú generals Zhāng Bà and others.
This was the fulfillment of the omen of "warfare, mourning, and a change of kings."
In the fifth year of Tàihé of Emperor Míng, in the fifth month,
Yínghuò encroached upon Fáng.
The prognostication stated:
"The four stars of Fáng
represent the positions of high-ranking ministers and generals.
If the moon or the Five Planets encroach upon or guard them,
the generals and ministers will have sorrow."
In the seventh month of that year,
Chējì Jiāngjūn Zhāng Hé pursued Zhūgě Liàng
and was killed by Liàng.
In the twelfth month,
Tàiwèi Huá Xīn died.
In the eleventh month of that year, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the moon encroached upon Xuānyuán Dàxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"The empress will have sorrow."
In the sixth year, in the third month, on the day Yǐhài,
the moon again encroached upon Xuānyuán Dàxīng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Tàibái was seen in daylight in Nándǒu,
and remained visible for over eighty days.
It was seen.
The prognostication stated:
"Wú will have troops."
The next year,
Sūn Quán dispatched Zhāng Mí and others, leading ten thousand soldiers,
to bestow upon Gōngsūn Wényì the title of King of Yān.
Wényì beheaded Mí and others,
and captured their troops.
In the third year of Qīnglóng, in the first month,
Empress Dowager Guō Shì died.
In the second year of Qīnglóng, in the third month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the moon encroached upon Yúguǐ.
Yúguǐ governs executions and killings.
The prognostication stated:
"Many people will fall ill,
and the state will have sorrow."
It also stated:
"High-ranking ministers will have sorrow."
In the summer and winter of that year,
there was a great plague.
In the fourth year, in the fifth month,
Sītú Dǒng Zhāo died.
In the fifth month of that year, on the day Dīnghài,
Tàibái was seen in daylight,
lasting for over thirty days.
Judging by its celestial longitude,
it indicated either Qín and Wèi,
or Chǔ.
At this time,
Zhūgě Liàng was stationed south of the Wèi River, and
Xuāndì was engaged in a standoff with him;
Sūn Quán raided Héféi,
and also sent Lù Yì and Sūn Sháo and others into the Huái and Miǎn regions.
The Son of Heaven personally led an eastern expedition.
Shǔ was originally Qín territory,
so this meant that the armies of Qín, Wèi, and Chǔ had all risen up.
In the seventh month of that year, on the day Jǐsì,
the moon encroached upon Jiànbì.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be a fire disaster."
In the third year, in the seventh month,
Chónghuá Diàn suffered a fire.
In the third year, in the sixth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Tiánxīng encroached upon Jǐngyuè.
On the day Wùxū,
Tàibái again encroached upon it.
The prognostication stated:
"In general, if the moon or the Five Planets encroach upon Jǐngyuè,
it always signifies military disaster."
Another saying states:
"Axes and battle-axes will be used,
and high-ranking ministers will be executed."
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Tiánxīng encroached upon Dōngjǐng Jùxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"If Tiánxīng enters Jǐng,
important people will have sorrow."
Its proximity to Jù indicates a period of yin.
Its prognostication stated:
"Great floods
and poor harvests."
In the summer of the first year of Jǐngchū,
there were great floods,
damaging the five grains.
In the tenth month of that year, on the day Rénshēn,
Tàibái was seen in daylight,
in Wěi,
remaining visible for over two hundred days.
It was seen.
The prognostication stated:
"Wěi represents Yān;
there will be military action."
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
the moon encroached upon Gōujíng.
The prognostication stated:
"The king will have sorrow."
In the intercalary first month of the fourth year, on the day Jǐsì,
Tiánxīng encroached upon Jǐngyuè.
In the third month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Tiánxīng encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Tàibái and the moon appeared together in daylight in Jǐng.
In the fifth month, on the day Rén yín,
Tàibái encroached upon Bì Zuǒgǔ Dìyīxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"Bì represents border troops,
and also governs criminal punishment."
In the ninth month,
Hú Ābìshī from beyond the northern frontier of Liángzhōu invaded various states.
Xīyù Xiàowèi Zhāng Jiù attacked them,
beheading and capturing tens of thousands.
In the seventh month of that year, on the day Jiǎyín,
Tàibái encroached upon Xuānyuán Dàxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"The empress will have sorrow."
In the first year of Jǐngchū,
Empress Máo Shì died.
In the second month, *yǐyǒu* day, of the first year of Jǐngchū,
the moon encroached upon the second star of Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"A general will suffer misfortune."
In the seventh month of that year,
Sītú Chén Jiǎo passed away.
In the fourth month of the second year,
Sītú Hán Jì passed away.
In the seventh month, *xīnmǎo* day, of that year,
Tài Bái (Venus) was visible during the day,
for over two hundred eighty days.
At that time, Gōngsūn Wényì proclaimed himself King of Yān,
appointed various officials,
and dispatched troops to resist and defend.
Xuāndì campaigned against and annihilated him.
In the second month, *jǐchǒu* day, of the second year,
the moon encroached upon the *jù* star of Xīn,
and also encroached upon the central great star.
In the fifth month, *yǐhài* day,
the moon again encroached upon the *jù* star of Xīn and the central great star.
According to the prognostication, it said:
"It is ill omened for the king.
If it encroaches upon the front star,
the crown prince will suffer misfortune."
In the first month of the third year,
the Emperor passed away.
The crown prince ascended the throne,
but was eventually deposed.
In the tenth month, *jiǎwǔ* day, of that year,
the moon encroached upon Jī.
The prognostication said:
"A general will die."
In the fourth month of the first year of Zhèngshǐ,
Chējì Jiāngjūn Huáng Quán passed away.
In the intercalary eleventh month, *guǐchǒu* day, of that year,
the moon encroached upon the central great star of Xīn.
In the fourth month, *wùwǔ* day, of the first year of the Young Emperor's Zhèngshǐ reign,
the moon encroached upon the first star at the eastern end of Mǎo.
In the tenth month, *gēngyín* day,
the moon again encroached upon the four northern Dipper stars of Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"When the moon encroaches upon Mǎo,
the Hú will be unrestful."
In the sixth month of the second year,
the Xiānbēi Āmiàor and others raided the western region.
Dūnhuáng Tàishǒu Wáng Yán defeated them,
beheading over twenty thousand.
In the third year,
he again beheaded the great chief of the Xiānbēi and over one thousand others.
In the ninth month, *guǐyǒu* day, of the second year,
the moon encroached upon the northwest star of Yúguǐ.
In the second month, *dīngwèi* day, of the third year,
it again encroached upon the southwest star.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a monetary decree."
Another interpretation said:
"Ministers will suffer misfortune."
In the third month of the third year,
Tàiwèi Mǎn Chǒng passed away.
In the first month of the fourth year,
the Emperor came of age (underwent the capping ceremony),
and bestowed money upon his officials, each according to their rank.
In the tenth and eleventh months of the fourth year,
the moon twice encroached upon Jǐngyuè.
In that month,
Xuāndì attacked Zhūgě Kè,
and Kè abandoned the city and fled.
In the second month of the fifth year,
Cáo Shuǎng campaigned against Shǔ.
In the eleventh month, *guǐsì* day, of the fifth year,
Tián Xīng (Saturn) encroached upon the *jù* star of Kàng.
The prognostication said:
"Among the feudal lords, there will be some who lose their states."
In the seventh month, *dīngchǒu* day, of the seventh year,
the moon encroached upon the left horn.
The prognostication said:
"There will be warfare in the realm,
and the left general will die."
In the seventh month, *yǐhài* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) encroached upon the *jù* star of Bì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be border troops."
Another interpretation said:
"Punishments will be applied."
In the first month, *xīnhài* day, of the ninth year,
the moon encroached upon the southern star of Kàng.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out."
Another interpretation said:
"A general will die."
In the seventh month, *guǐchǒu* day,
Tián Xīng encroached upon Jiàn Bì.
The prognostication said:
"It is not advisable for the king to leave the palace or descend from the hall."
In the first year of Jiāpíng,
the Son of Heaven visited the imperial tombs,
and Xuāndì presented a memorial to execute Cáo Shuǎng and others.
The Son of Heaven lodged in the wilderness,
and thereby lost his power.
In the sixth month, *rénxū* day, of the first year of Jiāpíng,
Tài Bái encroached upon the *jù* star of Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"The state will lose governance,
and ministers will cause rebellion."
In the fourth month, *xīnsì* day,
Tài Bái encroached upon Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will be executed."
Another interpretation said:
"War will break out."
In the third month, *jǐwèi* day, of the second year,
Tài Bái again encroached upon the *jù* star of Jǐng.
In the seventh month of the third year,
Wáng Líng conspired with Chǔ Wáng Biāo,
and both were executed,
and the ruler's authority subsequently diminished.
In the fifth month, summer, of the thirteenth year of Chìwū of Wú Sūn Quán,
when the sun reached its northernmost point,
Yínghuò retrograded
and entered Nándǒu.
In the seventh month, autumn,
it encroached upon the third star of Kuí and moved eastward.
The *Hàn Jìn Chūnqiū* says
"retrograded."
According to the prognostication:
"When Yínghuò enters Nándǒu,
the King of Wú will die within three months."
Another interpretation said:
"When Yínghuò retrogrades,
there will be a dead ruler in that region."
In the second year of Tàiyuán,
Quán passed away,
which was the fulfillment of this omen.
Therefore, the *Guó Zhì* recorded it under Wú.
At this time,
Wáng Líng plotted to enthrone Chǔ Wáng Biāo,
saying,
"There are stars in the Dipper,
so there should be someone who becomes suddenly noble."
He asked Hào Xiáng, a star observer.
Xiáng suspected something was amiss,
and wishing to please him,
did not mention that Wú would suffer death and loss,
but instead said,
"Huáinán and Chǔ are divided,
and Wú and Chǔ share the same omen;
a king will surely rise."
Thus, Líng's plan was settled.
In the twelfth month, on the day *bǐngshēn* of the second year of Jiāpíng,
the Moon encroached upon Yúguǐ.
In the fourth month, on the day *wùyín* of the third year,
the Moon encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
In the fifth month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
the Moon encroached upon the constellation Kàngjù.
The prognostication said:
"A general will die."
Another interpretation said:
"There will be warfare."
In this month,
Wáng Líng and the Prince of Chǔ, Piāo, were executed.
In the seventh month,
Empress Zhēn perished.
In the third month of the fourth year,
Wu generals raided,
and Zhèn Dōng Jiāngjūn Zhūgě Dàn defeated and repelled them.
In the seventh month, on the day *jǐsì*, of that year,
the Moon encroached upon Yúguǐ.
In the ninth month, on the day *yǐsì*,
it encroached again.
In the tenth month, on the day *guǐwèi*,
Yínghuò encroached upon the southern star of Kàng.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will cause rebellion."
In the eleventh month, on the day *dīngwèi*, of the fourth year,
the Moon again encroached upon Guǐjīshī.
In the sixth month, on the day *wùwǔ*, of the fifth year,
Tàibái encroached upon Jiǎo.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will conspire,
but not succeed."
On the day *gēngchén*,
the Moon encroached upon the Jī constellation.
The prognostication said:
"A general will die."
In the seventh month,
the Moon encroached upon Jǐngyuè.
On the day *bǐngwǔ*,
the Moon again encroached upon the northwest star of Guǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The state will have worries."
In the eleventh month, on the day *guǐyǒu*,
the Moon encroached upon the Jù star of Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"A general will die."
In the first month of the first year of Zhèngyuán,
Zhèn Dōng Jiāngjūn Wúqiū Jiǎn and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Wén Qīn rebelled,
their armies were both defeated,
and they were executed.
In the second month,
Lǐ Fēng, his younger brother Yì, and the Empress's father Zhāng Jī, conspired to rebel,
but the plot was exposed,
all were executed,
and Empress Zhāng was deposed.
In the ninth month,
the Emperor was deposed and made Prince of Qí.
The Shǔ general Jiāng Wéi attacked Lǒngxī,
and Chē Qí Jiāngjūn Guō Huái attacked and defeated him.
In the second month, on the day *wùwǔ*, of the second year of Gāoguì Xiānggōng Zhèngyuán,
Yínghuò encroached upon the first star of the western end of the northern shaft of Dōngjǐng.
In the seventh month, on the day *yǐmǎo*, of the first year of Gānlù,
Yínghuò encroached upon the Yuè star of Dōngjǐng.
On the day *rénxū*,
the Moon again encroached upon the Yuè star.
In the eighth month, on the day *xīnhài*,
the Moon encroached upon Jī.
In the ninth month, on the day *rénchén*, of the first year of Tàipíng when Wú deposed Sūn Liàng,
Tàibái encroached upon the Southern Dǒu,
as recorded in the *Wú Zhì*.
The prognostication said:
"When Tàibái encroaches upon Dǒu,
the state will have soldiers,
and a great minister will rebel."
The next year,
Zhūgě Dàn rebelled.
The year after that,
Sūn Chēn deposed Liàng.
Both Wú and Wèi had military affairs.
In the ninth month, on the day *dīngsì*, of the first year of Gānlù,
the Moon encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
In the sixth month, on the day *jǐyǒu*, of the second year,
the Moon encroached upon the great central star of Xīn.
In the eighth month, on the day *rénzǐ*,
Suìxīng encroached upon Jǐngyuè.
In the ninth month, on the day *gēngyín*,
Suìxīng retrograded,
riding upon Jǐngyuè.
In the tenth month, on the day *bǐngyín*,
Tàibái encroached upon the Kàngjù star.
The prognostication said:
"Rebellious ministers will cause disorder,
and the ruler will worry."
In the fifth month of the first year of Jǐngyuán,
there was the incident of Chéng Jì and the execution of Zhūgě Dàn,
all of which were its manifestations.
In the third month, on the day *gēngzǐ*, of the second year,
Tàibái encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"The state will lose governance,
and great ministers will cause disorder."
That night,
Suìxīng again encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out."
By the first year of Jǐngyuán,
the Gāoguì Xiānggōng was defeated.
In the eighth month, on the day *rénchén*, of the third year,
Suìxīng encroached upon the Zhì star of Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Axes and execution blocks will be used,
and great ministers will be executed."
In the fourth month, on the day *jiǎshēn*, of the fourth year,
Suìxīng again encroached upon the southeast star of Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The southeast star of Guǐ presides over military affairs;
when Wood enters Guǐ,
great ministers will be executed."
In the first year of Jǐngyuán,
Shàngshū Wáng Jīng was killed.
In the second month of the first year of Yuándì Jǐngyuán,
the Moon encroached upon the Jiàn constellation.
According to prognostication:
"When the Moon or the Five Planets encroach upon the Jiàn constellation,
great ministers will slander each other."
After this, Zhōng Huì and Dèng Ài defeated Shǔ,
and Huì slandered Ài.
In the fourth month of the second year,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi,
encroaching upon the Right Zhífǎ.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will have great worries."
Another said:
"Great ministers will worry."
In the tenth month of the fourth year,
Suìxīng guarded Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"Generals and chancellors will worry."
Another said:
"There will be a great amnesty."
The next year,
Dèng Ài and Zhōng Huì were both exterminated,
and the land of Shǔ was granted amnesty.
In the fifth year,
the Emperor abdicated.
In the ninth month of the fourth year of Wǔdì Xiánníng,
Tàibái was due to appear but did not.
The prognostication said:
"This is called 'losing its lodging';
if there is no army defeated,
then there must be a state destroyed."
At this time, Yáng Hù presented a memorial requesting to attack Wú,
and the Emperor granted it.
In the eleventh month of the fifth year,
the troops set out,
and Tàibái first appeared in the west in the evening.
In the third month of the first year of Tàikāng,
the Wú army was greatly defeated,
Sūn Hào presented himself bound to beg for forgiveness,
and the state of Wú consequently perished.
In the third month of the eighth year of Tàikāng,
Yínghuò guarded Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"Kings dislike this."
In the fourth month, on the day *yǐyǒu*, of the first year of Tàixī,
the Emperor perished.
In the fourth month of the third year of Huìdì Yuánkāng,
Yínghuò guarded Tàiwēi for sixty days.
The prognostication said:
"Feudal lords and the Three Dukes will conspire against their superiors,
and there will certainly be executed ministers."
Another said:
"The Son of Heaven's state will perish."
This spring, Tàibái guarded Bì,
up to this point for over a hundred days.
The prognostication said:
"There will be the worry of urgent decrees."
Another said:
"The chancellor will die."
Also, the borders will be unstable.
Later, Jiǎ Hòu entrapped and killed the Crown Prince.
In the tenth month, on the day *yǐwèi*, of the sixth year,
Tàibái was seen in daylight.
In the sixth month of the ninth year,
Yínghuò guarded Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"Kings dislike this."
In the eighth month,
Yínghuò entered Yǔlín.
The prognostication said:
"Imperial troops will rise up in great numbers."
After this,
the Emperor was deposed and made Tàishàng Huáng,
and soon after, the Three Princes raised armies to attack Zhào Wáng Lún,
and Lún sent all his central army troops to confront them for several months.
In the third month of the first year of Yǒngkāng,
the central star of Táitái Cè split apart,
and Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
The divination said:
"If the Táitái Cè star is abnormal,
the Sāngōng are in distress.
If Tàibái is seen in daylight,
it signifies a disloyal minister."
In this month,
Empress Jiǎ killed the crown prince.
Soon after, Zhào Wáng Lún deposed and killed the Empress,
and executed Sīkōng Zhāng Huá.
In the fifth month of that year,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Nándǒu.
The divination said:
"The prime minister will die,
and a great war will erupt.
Dǒu
is also the division of Wú."
At this time,
Zhào Wáng Lún was the prime minister.
The following year,
he usurped the throne,
and the Sān Wáng raised armies to punish him.
In the second year of Tàian,
Shí Bīng conquered Yángzhōu.
In the eighth month of that year,
Yínghuò entered Jī.
The divination said:
"The sovereign will lose his position,
and war will break out."
The following year,
Zhào Wáng Lún usurped the throne
and changed the reign era.
In the second month of the second year,
Tàibái appeared in the west,
retrograding into Dōngjǐng.
The divination said:
"The state will lose its governance,
and great ministers will cause chaos."
At this time,
Qí Wáng Jiǒng raised troops to attack Zhào Wáng Lún.
Lún was destroyed,
and Jiǒng, wielding military power, did not attend court,
monopolizing power and indulging in extravagance.
The following year,
he was executed.
In the first year of Yǒngníng,
from the first month to the intercalary month,
the five planets traversed the sky,
moving erratically horizontally and vertically.
The Star Treatise says:
"The sun is Yang,
the way of the ruler;
the stars are Yin,
the way of the ministers.
When the sun appears, the stars vanish;
ministers may not act independently.
If stars are seen in the sky at noon, it is called traversing the sky;
the divination for this is 'disloyal ministers,
or a change of ruler'."
Now, all five planets traversed the sky,
a celestial anomaly never before seen.
Shí Shì said:
"If Chénxīng (Mercury) is seen in daylight,
the state will either perish or be in great chaos."
After this,
the Táidǐng and Fāngbó
alternately wielded great power,
the two emperors went into exile,
and it eventually led to the six Barbarians successively becoming kings,
alternately occupying Huáxià,
which is also unprecedented in records.
In the fourth month of that year,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) was seen in daylight.
In the fifth month,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
The divination was the same as before.
In the seventh month,
Suìxīng guarded Xū and Wēi.
The divination said:
"If Wood (Jupiter) guards Xū and Wēi,
there will be military worries.
Xū and Wēi
are the division of Qí."
Another saying:
"Guarding Xū
means famine;
guarding Wēi
means excessive corvée labor,
and the common people will be exhausted."
Chénxīng entered Tàiwēi.
The divination said:
"It signifies internal chaos,"
another saying:
"Ministers will kill each other."
Tàibái guarded Yòu Yèmén.
The divination said:
"It signifies war,
chaos,
and bandits."
On the Wùwǔ day of the eighth month,
Tiánxīng (Saturn) offended Zuǒ Zhífǎ,
and also offended Shàng Xiàng.
The divination said:
"Shàng Xiàng is in distress."
Yínghuò guarded Mǎo.
The divination said:
"Zhào and Wèi will suffer disaster."
Chénxīng guarded Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"Qín will suffer disaster."
On the Dīngwèi day of the ninth month,
the moon offended Zuǒ Jiǎo.
The divination said:
"The sovereign is in distress."
Another saying:
"The Zuǒ Wèi Jiāngjūn will die,
and there will be war under Heaven."
On the Guǐyǒu day of the fourth month of the second year,
Suìxīng was seen in daylight.
The divination said:
"The ministers will be powerful."
Initially,
Qí Wáng Jiǒng pacified the capital,
and then remained to assist in governance,
subsequently monopolizing power without respect for the ruler.
In this month,
Chéngdū and Héjiān issued a declaration to Chángshā Wáng to attack him.
Jiǒng and them engaged in battle,
attacking and burning the palace.
Jiǒng's army was defeated,
and he was annihilated.
His elder brother, Shàng Jūn Jiāngjūn Shí, and over twenty others were also killed.
In the second year of Tàian,
Chéngdū attacked Chángshā,
whereupon both public and private sectors were ravaged by famine,
and the common people were exhausted.
In the second month of the second year of Tàian,
Tàibái entered Mǎo.
The divination said:
"The empire will be disturbed,
and a great war will erupt."
In the seventh month,
Yínghuò entered Dōngjǐng.
The divination said:
"War will break out,
and the state will be in chaos."
In this autumn,
Tàibái guarded Tàiwēi Shàng Jiàng.
The divination said:
"Shàng Jiàng will perish by war."
In the winter of this year,
Chéngdū and Héjiān attacked Luòyáng.
In the eighth month,
Chángshā Wáng escorted the Emperor out to resist the two kings.
In the first month of the third year,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè arrested Chángshā Wáng,
and Zhāng Fāng then killed him.
In the first month of the third year,
Yínghuò entered Nándǒu;
the divination was the same as in Yǒngkāng.
In the seventh month,
Zuǒ Wèi Jiāngjūn Chén Zhěn led his troops to escort the Emperor to attack Chéngdū.
The six armies were defeated,
and soldiers pressed upon the imperial carriage.
At this time,
bandits and thieves rose up throughout the empire,
with Zhāng Chāng being particularly strong.
In the seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day, of the first year of Yǒngxīng,
Tàibái invaded Jiǎo and Kàng,
passed through Fáng and Xīn,
and traversed Wěi and Jī.
In the ninth month,
it entered Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"Invading Jiǎo,
there will be great wars throughout the realm;
invading Kàng,
there will be great military conflicts,
and the ruler will be worried;
entering Fáng and Xīn,
signifies military disasters and deaths;
invading Wěi and Jī,
the empress will be worried."
Another prognostication said:
"The realm will be in great chaos.
Entering Nándǒu,
there will be military disasters and deaths."
Another prognostication said:
"Generals will cause rebellion.
The regions it invades and guards
are the astrological divisions of Yǎnzhōu, Yùzhōu, Yōuzhōu, Jìzhōu, and Yángzhōu."
In the seventh month of that year,
there was the Battle of Dàngyīn.
In the ninth month,
Wáng Jùn killed the Inspector of Yōuzhōu, Hé Yǎn,
and attacked Yè.
Yè collapsed,
whereupon Yǎn and Yù became the focus of the realm's military conflicts.
Chén Mǐn also caused chaos in the lands of Yángzhōu.
Liú Yuánhǎi, Shí Lè, Lǐ Xióng, and others rose from humble origins
to occupy provinces and commanderies.
Empress Yángshì was repeatedly deposed and imprisoned.
These were all corresponding events.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day, of the second year,
Tàibái invaded the Láng star.
The prognostication stated:
"Great military conflicts will arise."
In the ninth month,
Suìxīng guarded Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be military conflicts,
and Jǐng is also the astrological division of Qín."
In that year,
Gǒu Xī defeated Gōng Shīfān;
Zhāng Fāng defeated Wáng Xiāo, the Prince of Fànyáng;
the various generals west of the pass attacked Wáng Yǒng, the Prince of Héjiān.
Wáng Yǒng fled,
and the Prince of Dōnghǎi intercepted and killed him.
In the fourth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
Tàibái deviated from its course,
moving from Yì into Wěi and Jī.
The prognostication stated:
"Tàibái deviates from its course and moves north,
this is called 'rebirth against the norm.'
If there is no shattered army,
there will certainly be a massacred city."
In the fifth month,
Jí Sāng attacked Yè.
FÉng Sōng, the Administrator of Wèijùn, sallied out to fight,
but was utterly defeated.
Jí Sāng then harmed Wáng Téng, the Prince of Dōngyàn,
killed over ten thousand people,
and burned all the palaces from the Wèi period.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Yínghuò guarded Xīn.
The prognostication stated:
"The ruler will suffer ill."
On the *jǐhài* day,
Tiánxīng guarded Fáng and Xīn.
The prognostication stated:
"Tiánxīng guarding Fáng
brings many misfortunes and deaths;
guarding Xīn,
the country will be in chaos,
and there will be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
At this time,
Sīmǎ Yuè wielded exclusive power,
ultimately leading to his destruction through impropriety,
which was the fulfillment of the domestic chaos prognostication.
In the eleventh month,
the Emperor died,
and Emperor Huái ascended the throne,
issuing a great amnesty throughout the realm.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīnghài* day, of the first year of Yǒngjiā of Emperor Huái,
stars streamed and scattered.
According to Liú Xiàng's explanation,
the listed constellations of the celestial officials
are symbols of those in high positions;
the multitude of small, unnamed stars
represent the common people.
This was an omen of the scattering and dispersal of all officials and common people.
Thereafter, the realm fell into great chaos,
and officials and common people,
numbering in the tens of thousands, migrated and died.
In the first month, on the *gēngwǔ* day, of the second year,
Tàibái was hidden and not seen.
In the second month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
it first appeared in the morning in the east.
This is called "due to be seen but not seen,"
and the prognostication is the same as the previous entry.
Thereafter, countless armies were destroyed and generals killed,
the Emperor died in the enemy court,
and the central plains were overrun and subjugated.
In the first month, on the *gēngzǐ* day, of the third year,
Yínghuò invaded Zǐwēi.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be a king who dies in the wilderness,
and also palaces will be burned by fire."
At this time, Gāo Tángchōng, the Grand Astrologer, memorialized
that the imperial carriage should move to another location,
otherwise Luòyáng would certainly be lost.
In the sixth month of the fifth year,
Liú Yào and Wáng Mí entered the capital,
burned palaces and temples,
captured the Emperor and took him to Píngyáng.
In the third year,
Tiánxīng long guarded Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"When Tiánxīng remains in a certain position for a long time,
that state will have good fortune."
At this time,
the General of Pacifying the East, Wáng Shǐ, the Prince of Lángxié, began to possess the lands of Yángzhōu.
In the eleventh month of that year,
there was an earthquake.
Chén Zhuó considered this to be the corresponding event to the earthquake.
In the tenth month of the fifth year,
Yínghuò guarded Xīn.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day, of the sixth year,
Tàibái invaded Tàiwēi.
The prognostication stated:
"Soldiers will enter the Son of Heaven's court,
and the ruler will suffer ill."
In the seventh month,
the Emperor died in the enemy court,
and the realm observed mourning and a great lamentation.
In the seventh month of the first year of Tàixīng of Emperor Yuán,
Tàibái invaded Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"Wú and Yuè will have military conflicts,
and great men will be worried."
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day, of the second year,
Yínghuò invaded Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"Military conflicts will arise,
and noble officials will kill each other."
In the eighth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Tàibái invaded the main star of Xuānyuán.
The prognostication stated:
"The empress's court will be worried."
In the fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day, of the third year,
Tàibái entered Tàiwēi,
and also invaded the star of the Senior General.
The prognostication stated:
"The Son of Heaven will lead the army personally,
and the Senior General will be executed."
In the ninth month,
Tàibái invaded Nándǒu.
In the tenth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Yínghuò was in Dōngjǐng,
south of Wǔ Zhūhóu,
and lingered there for thirty days.
The prognostication stated:
"If Yínghuò guards Jǐng for more than twenty days,
great men will be worried.
If it guards Wǔ Zhūhóu,
there will be princes who are executed."
In the third month of the first year of Yǒngchāng,
Wáng Dūn led the forces of Jiāng and Jīng to attack the capital.
The Six Armies resisted and fought,
but were defeated.
The ruler merely offered apologies.
Thereupon, Zhōu Yǐ, the General of the Household Guard, Diāo Xié, the Minister of the Secretariat, and Dài Ruòsī, the General of Agile Cavalry, were killed.
Furthermore,
Liú Wèi, the General Pacifying the North, fled.
In the fourth month,
Sīmǎ Chéng, the Prince of Qiáo, Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, and Gān Zhuó, the General Pacifying the South, were also killed.
In the intercalary twelfth month,
the Emperor died.
In the first month of the third year of Tàiníng of Emperor Míng,
Yínghuò retrograded
and entered Tàiwēi.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be military disasters and deaths,
and the ruler will suffer ill."
In the intercalary eighth month,
the Emperor died.
Two years later,
Sū Jùn rebelled,
attacked and burned the palaces,
and the Empress Dowager died of distress.
The Son of Heaven was imprisoned and abducted to Shítouchéng,
and military chaos spread far and wide,
not ceasing until the fourth year.
In the sixth year of Xiánhé of Emperor Chéng, in the first month, on the day bǐngchén,
the moon entered Nán Dǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be soldiers."
In this month,
Shí Lè killed people from Luèlóu and Wǔjìn two counties.
The following year,
Shí Lè's forces again plundered Nánshā and Hǎiyú.
In the eleventh month of that year,
Yínghuò guarded Wèi and Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"Zhào and Wèi will have soldiers."
In the seventh month of the eighth year,
Shí Lè died,
and Shí Jìlóng established himself.
At this time,
although the two Shís usurped imperial titles,
their strength and weakness were always prognosticated by Mǎo,
and did not concern Tàiwēi or Zǐgōng.
In the eighth year, in the third month, on the day jǐsì,
the moon entered Nán Dǒu.
This was the same prognostication as in the sixth year.
In the seventh month of that year,
Shí Lè died.
Péng Biāo with Qiáo,
Shí Shēng with Cháng'ān,
and Guō Quán with Qínzhōu all submitted.
Thereupon, the Dūhù Qiáo Qiú was dispatched to lead troops to rescue Biāo.
Biāo was defeated,
and Qiú retreated.
Furthermore,
Shí Jìlóng and Shí Bīn attacked and destroyed Shēng and Quán.
In the seventh month of that year,
Yínghuò entered Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Hú king will die."
Another said:
"Zhào territory will have soldiers."
In this month,
Shí Lè died,
and Shí Jìlóng attacked and captured many places.
In the eighth month,
the moon again transgressed Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Hú will be uneasy."
In the ninth year, in the third month, on the day jǐhài,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ,
transgressing Jīshī.
The prognostication said:
"Soldiers are in the northwest;
there will be armies destroyed and generals killed."
In the sixth and eighth months,
the moon again transgressed Mǎo.
At this time,
although Shí Hóng succeeded to Lè's position,
Shí Jìlóng wielded power arbitrarily and was tyrannical.
In the eleventh month, he deposed Hóng and established himself,
then imprisoned and killed him.
In the second month, on the day Jǐhài, of the first year of Xiánkāng,
Táibái (Venus) encroached upon Mǎo (the Pleiades).
The prognostication stated:
"Troops will rise,
and there will be a drought in the middle of the year."
In the fourth month,
Shí Jìlóng led his cavalry to Lìyáng.
Sītú Wáng Dǎo was promoted to Dàsīmǎ,
and troops were trained and garrisoned in strategic locations.
At this time,
Shí Jìlóng also besieged Xiāngyáng.
In the sixth month,
there was a drought.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngxū, of that year,
the moon entered Mǎo.
The prognostication stated:
"The Hú king will die."
In the eighth month, on the day Wùxū,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Dōngjǐng (Castor and Pollux).
The prognostication stated:
"If there are no troops,
troops will rise;
if there are troops,
troops will cease."
In the eleventh month,
the moon encroached upon Mǎo.
In the first month, on the day Xīnhài, of the second year,
the moon encroached upon the second star south of Fáng (Scorpio).
In the eighth month,
the moon again encroached upon Mǎo.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Táibái encroached upon Nándǒu (Sagittarius),
and was visible during the day.
The prognostication stated:
"Dǒu represents the prime minister,
and also the division of Yángzhōu.
If Jīn (Venus) encroaches upon it,
it is an omen of death and mourning.
Its visibility during the day
signifies disloyalty to the sovereign,
and also war and mourning."
Subsequently,
Shí Jìlóng usurped the title of Heavenly King.
He raised an army of seventy thousand,
and in the second month of the fourth year, he attacked Duàn Liáo at Jì from Lǒngxī.
He also attacked Mùróng Huàng at Jíchéng,
but failed to overcome him.
Huàng defeated Shí Jìlóng's general Má Qiū,
and captured and killed Duàn Liáo.
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu, of the third year,
the moon encroached upon the upper star of Fáng.
In the eighth month,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ (Cancer),
and encroached upon Jīshī (Praesepe).
On the day Jiǎxū,
the moon encroached upon the distance star of Dōngjǐng.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the moon encroached upon Jiànxīng (Alpha Sagittarii).
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐsì, of the fourth year,
Táibái was visible during the day,
in Liǔ (Hydra).
The prognostication stated:
"It signifies war
and disloyalty to the sovereign."
The following year,
Shí Jìlóng launched a major raid on Miǎnnán.
Thereupon, internal and external security was heightened.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùxū,
Yínghuò encroached upon Yòuzhífǎ (Epsilon Leonis).
The prognostication stated:
"A high official will die,
and those in power will worry."
In the ninth month,
Táibái again encroached upon Yòuzhífǎ.
According to the prognostication:
"If the five planets cause disaster simultaneously,
Jīn (Venus) and Huǒ (Mars) are particularly severe."
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Táibái encroached upon the upper star of Fáng.
The prognostication stated:
"The prime minister will worry."
In the fourth month, on the day Yǐwèi, of the fifth year,
the moon encroached upon the distance star of Bì (Hyades).
The prognostication stated:
"Troops will rise."
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the moon encroached upon the upper star of Fáng.
The prognostication stated:
"Generals and prime ministers will worry."
In that month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Chancellor Wáng Dǎo passed away,
and Yǔ Bīng took over as regent.
In the eighth month,
Tàiwèi Xī Jiàn passed away.
There was also the defeat at Zhūchéng in Miǎnnán,
and over ten thousand households of common people fled.
In the first month of the sixth year,
Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn Yǔ Liàng passed away.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎchén, of the sixth year,
Yínghuò encroached upon Tàiwēi Shàngjiāngxīng (Beta Leonis).
The prognostication stated:
"The supreme general will worry."
In the fourth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Yínghuò encroached upon Yòuzhífǎ.
The prognostication stated:
"Those in power will worry."
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the moon encroached upon the central star of Qiānniú (Aquila).
The prognostication stated:
"A great general will worry."
At this time,
Shàngshūlìng Hé Chōng, who held the position of Zhífǎ,
was reprimanded.
Wishing to avoid further blame,
he sought to become Zhōngshūlìng the following year.
In the fourth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Táibái encroached upon the distance star of Bì.
The prognostication stated:
"War will break out."
Another prognostication stated:
"The empress will worry."
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Táibái encroached upon the great star of Xuānyuán (Regulus).
The prognostication stated:
"The empress will worry."
In the third month of the seventh year,
Empress Dùshì passed away.
In the third month, on the day Rénwǔ, of the seventh year,
the moon encroached upon Fáng.
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Táibái entered Yúguǐ.
In the fifth month,
Táibái was visible during the day.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the moon encroached upon Yúguǐ.
In the sixth month of the eighth year,
Yínghuò encroached upon the second upper star of Fáng.
The prognostication stated:
"The second prime minister will worry."
In the eighth month, on the day Rén'yín,
the moon encroached upon Bì.
The prognostication stated:
"Inferiors will offend superiors,
and war will break out."
In the tenth month,
the moon again obscured the great star of Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the second year of Jiànyuán,
Chējì Jiāngjūn Yǔ Bīng passed away.
