Zhū Língshí annihilated Shǔ.
In the second month of the ninth year,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"There will be military losses."
Tàibái infringed upon Nánhé.
The divination said:
"Troops will rise."
On the *rénchén* day of the fifth month,
Tàibái infringed upon Yòuzhífǎ,
and was seen in daylight.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the seventh month,
the Moon occulted Gōuqín.
The divination said:
"Ministers of speech will have worries."
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the ninth month,
Suìxīng infringed upon the great star of Xuānyuán.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Moon infringed upon Zuǒjiǎo.
At this time, Liú Yù usurped authority,
and warfare did not cease.
In the tenth month,
Yù attacked Sīmǎ Xiūzhī,
[二三]the imperial army was at a disadvantage,
and Xiūzhī and others fled to Cháng'ān.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the first month of the tenth year,
the Moon infringed upon Bì.
The divination said:
"A general or minister will be punished with his entire family."
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the second month,
the Moon infringed upon the northern star of Fáng.
On the *rénfēng* day of the fifth month,
the Moon infringed upon the southern star of Qiānniú.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Suìxīng infringed upon the great star of Xuānyuán.
All divinations were the same as above.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the sixth month,
the Moon occulted Dī.
The divination said:
"A general will die,
and there will be executions in the state."
On the *gēngchén* day of the seventh month,
the Moon infringed upon Tiānguān.
The divination said:
"Troops will rise."
Yínghuò infringed upon Jǐngyuè.
Tiánxīng infringed upon Yúguǐ,
and then remained there.
The divination said:
"Great men will have worries,
and ancestral temples will be altered."
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the eighth month,
the Moon occulted the southern star of Qiānniú.
The divination was the same as above.
In the ninth month,
Tiánxīng infringed upon Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"The ruler will have worries."
On the *dīngsì* day,
Tàibái entered Yǔlín.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the Moon infringed upon Xīxián.
The divination said:
"There is a secret plot."
In the eleventh year,
Línyì raided Jiāozhōu,
but was repelled and defeated.
On the *dīngsì* day of the third month of the eleventh year,
the Moon entered Bì.
The divination said:
"Troops will rise throughout the land."
Another interpretation said:
"There will be frontier troops."
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the intercalary month,
Tiánxīng again entered Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"There will be drought,
a great plague,
and rebellious ministers."
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the fifth month,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
it trespassed against the Right Law Enforcer.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Tàibái trespassed against Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will have troops."
On the *wùyín* day,
it trespassed against Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The state will have worries."
In the seventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Moon trespassed against Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the eighth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Moon trespassed against Dī.
The prognostication was the same as above.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Tàibái moved directly,
entering Tàiwēi from the Right Yèmén.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
it observed the Left Law Enforcer.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the Moon entered Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Moon entered Yúguǐ and had a halo.
In the twelfth year, fifth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Suìxīng remained between Fáng and Xīn,
in the celestial division of Sòng.
Liú Yù was first enfeoffed as Sònggōng.
In the sixth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Tàibái moved directly into the Right Yèmén of Tàiwēi.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Moon trespassed against Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the seventh month,
the Moon trespassed against Niúxiù.
In the tenth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Moon entered Bì.
In the thirteenth year, fifth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Moon trespassed against Xuānyuán.
On the *dīnghài* day,
it trespassed against Qiānniú.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yínghuò trespassed against the Right Law Enforcer.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Moon trespassed against Qiānniú.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Moon trespassed against Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler worries."
In the ninth month, on the *rénchén* day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Xuānyuán.
In the tenth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Moon trespassed against Bì.
All prognostications were the same as above.
The Moon trespassed against Jī.
The prognostication said:
"The state will have worries."
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Moon trespassed against Bì.
The prognostication was the same as above.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Tiánxīng trespassed against Tàiwēi,
remaining accumulated for over seventy days.
The prognostication said:
"An omen of the demise of the ruler."
On the *rénxū* day,
the Moon trespassed against Tàiwēi.
In the fourteenth year, third month, on the *guǐsì* day,
〔二四〕Tàibái trespassed against Wǔzhūhóu.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Moon trespassed against Tàiwēi.
In the seventh month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will have troops,
and there will be drought,
and military losses."
It also said:
"Great men worry,
ancestral temples are changed,
and there are rebellious ministers."
At this time, Liú Yù usurped authority,
military campaigns frequently arose,
and famine and drought followed one another.
Afterwards, the Jìn dynasty was ultimately overthrown.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Moon trespassed against Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"A military commander will die."
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Tàibái trespassed against Xuānyuán.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tiánxīng entered Tàiwēi,
trespassing against the Right Law Enforcer,
and then remained within Tàiwēi,
accumulating for over two hundred days before departing.
The prognostication said:
"Tiánxīng guarding Tàiwēi
is an omen of the demise of the ruler,
and there will be a change of king."
In the ninth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
Tàibái entered Tàiwēi,
trespassing against the Left Law Enforcer.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Moon entered Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"Great men worry."
In the tenth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Moon entered Tàiwēi.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi,
trespassing against the Xiīfān Shàngjiàng,
then moved directly,
to inside the Left Yèmén,
remained for twenty days,
then moved retrogradely.
In the seventh month of Yìxī twelve,
Liú Yù attacked Yáo Hóng.
In the eighth month of the thirteenth year,
Yáo Hóng was captured,
and Sī, Yǎn, Qín, and Yōng were all pacified.
In the fourteenth year,
Liú Yù returned to Péngchéng,
and received the title of Sònggōng.
In the eleventh month,
the Left Púyè, former General Liú Mùzhī, died.
The following year,
the Western barbarians invaded Cháng'ān,
the Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Zhū Língshí and his various armies were defeated and annihilated,
and the government troops abandoned it and moved east.
In the twelfth month,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first month of Gōngdì Yuánxī first year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
in the third month, on the *rén'yín* day,
in the fifth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Moon all trespassed against Tàiwēi,
all prognostications were the same as above.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Chénxīng trespassed against Xuānyuán.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Tàibái trespassed against Tàiwēi.
In the seventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Moon trespassed against Tàiwēi,
and Tàibái appeared in daytime.
From Yìxī first year until now,
Tàibái crossed the sky nine times,
and there were four solar eclipses,
all originating from the above,
omens of a change of dynasty and new rulers,
and subjects losing their lord.
That night,
Tàibái trespassed against Kūxīng.
In the twelfth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the Moon and Tàibái both entered Yǔlín.
In the second year, second month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
〔二五〕Tiánxīng trespassed against Tàiwēi.
All prognostications were the same as above.
In the seventh month of the first year,
Liú Yù received the title of Sòngwáng.
In the sixth month of this year,
the Emperor abdicated in favor of Sòng.
〔二六〕Yāoxīng, Kèxīng
In the ninth month of Wèi Wéndì Huángchū third year, on the *jiǎchén* day,
a guest star appeared within the Left Yèmén of Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said;
"When a guest star appears from Tàiwēi,
the state will have military losses."
In the tenth month,
the Emperor marched south against Sūn Quán.
After this,
there were numerous campaigns.
In the sixth year, tenth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
a broom star appeared in Shǎowēi,
passing through Xuānyuán.
The prognostication
"foretells military losses,
and the pattern of abolishing the old and establishing the new."
At this time, the Emperor's army was in Guǎnglíng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
he personally donned armor and observed the troops.
In the fifth month of the following year,
the Emperor passed away.
In the sixth year of Tàihé of Emperor Míng, in the eleventh month, on the day bǐngyín,
a comet appeared in Yì (Wings),
nearing the General's Star in Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure).
The divination said:
"This signifies war and mourning."
Master Gān (Gān Shì) said:
"The country over which a comet or broom-star appears
will suffer its calamity.
Yì is also the astrological division of Chǔ,
which is the territory enfeoffed to Sūn Quán."
The next year,
Sūn Quán suffered a defeat in Liáodōng.
The year after that,
Zhūgě Liàng entered Qínchuān.
Sūn Quán dispatched troops,
stationing them along the Jiānghuái (Yangtze and Huai Rivers) at strategic points.
Sūn Quán himself besieged Xīnchéng to support Zhūgě Liàng,
and the Son of Heaven personally led an expedition eastward against Sūn Quán.
In the fourth year of Qīnglóng, in the tenth month, on the day jiǎshēn,
a comet appeared in Dàchén (Great Star),
three chǐ long.
On the day yǐyǒu,
it appeared again in the East.
In the eleventh month, on the day jǐhài,
a comet was seen,
violating the eunuch's star Tiānjì (Heavenly Net).
The divination said:
"Dàchén represents the Heavenly King;
there will be mourning in the world."
Liú Xiàng's (Liú Xiàng) Wǔjìlùn (Discourse on the Five Records) states:
"In the Chūnqiū (Spring and Autumn Annals),
when a comet appears in the East
and no constellation is mentioned,
it means it did not enter a constellation.
The eunuchs are in Tiānshì (Heavenly Market Enclosure),
which signifies war both within and without the court.
Tiānjì signifies earthquakes,
and comets and broom-stars primarily signify war and mourning."
In the sixth month of Jǐngchū first year,
there was an earthquake.
In the ninth month,
the Wú (Wu) general Zhū Rán besieged Jiāngxià.
Empress Máo (Máo Shì) passed away.
In the first month of the second year,
Gōngsūn Wényì was attacked.
In the first month of the third year,
Emperor Míng passed away.
In the eighth month of Jǐngchū second year,
a comet was seen in Zhāng (Extended Net),
three chǐ long,
moving westward against the usual direction,
and disappeared after forty-one days.
The divination was the same as above.
Zhāng
is the astrological division of Zhōu.
In the tenth month, on the day guǐsì,
a guest star was seen in Wēi (Rooftop),
moving retrogradely,
north of Lígōng (Detached Palace) and south of Téngshé (Flying Serpent).
On the day jiǎchén,
it violated Zōngxīng (Ancestral Stars).
On the day jǐyǒu,
it disappeared.
The divination said:
"Where a guest star appears, there will be war and mourning.
Xū (Emptiness) and Wēi represent the ancestral temple,
and also graves.
If a guest star approaches Lígōng,
then there will be great mourning within the palace,
symbolizing the deceased sovereign being brought to the ancestral temple."
In the first month of the third year,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Zhèngshǐ of the Young Emperor (Shǎo Dì), in the tenth month, on the day yǐyǒu,
a comet was seen in the West,
in Wěi (Tail),
thirty chǐ long,
brushing against Qiānniú (Cowherd),
and violating Tàibái (Venus).
In the eleventh month, on the day jiǎzǐ,
it further violated Yǔlín (Feathered Forest).
The divination said:
"Wěi is Yàn,
and also Wú;
Niú is also the division of Wú and Yuè.
Tàibái is the commander-in-chief,
and Yǔlín is the central army.
This signifies mourning in Wú and Yuè,
and movement of the central army."
In the fifth month of the second year,
Wú sent three generals to raid the border.
The Wú crown prince Dēng (Dēng) died.
In the sixth month,
Emperor Xuān (Xuān Dì) attacked Zhūgě Kè (Zhūgě Kè) at Wǎn.
Grand Commandant Mǎn Chǒng (Mǎn Chǒng) passed away.
In the eighth month of the sixth year, on the day wùwǔ,
a comet was seen in Qīxīng (Seven Stars),
two chǐ long,
white in color,
advancing to Zhāng,
and disappeared after twenty-three days.
In the eleventh month of the seventh year, on the day guǐhài,
it was seen again in Zhěn (Chariot),
one chǐ long,
and disappeared after one hundred fifty-six days.
In the third month of the ninth year,
it was seen again in Mǎo (Pleiades),
six chǐ long,
bluish-white in color,
with its rays pointing southwest.
In the seventh month,
it was seen again in Yì,
two chǐ long,
advancing to Zhěn,
and disappeared after forty-two days.
According to the divination:
"Qīxīng and Zhāng are the astrological divisions of Zhōu;
Yì and Zhěn are Chǔ;
Mǎo is Zhào and Wèi.
Comets signify removing the old and establishing the new,
and are associated with war and mourning."
In the first year of Jiāpíng,
Emperor Xuān executed Cáo Shuǎng (Cáo Shuǎng) and his brothers and their associates,
all of whom had their three kindreds exterminated,
and the capital was put under strict military control.
In the third year,
King Biāo (Biāo) of Chǔ was executed,
and Wáng Líng (Wáng Líng) was ambushed in Huáinán.
Huáinán is
Eastern Chǔ.
The various kings of Wèi (Wei) were confined in Yè.
In the eleventh month of Jiāpíng third year, on the day guǐhài,
a comet appeared in Yíngshì (Encampment),
moving westward,
and disappeared after ninety days.
The divination said:
"There will be war and mourning.
Shì represents the imperial harem,
and there will soon be disorder in the harem."
In the second month of the fourth year, on the day dīngyǒu,
a comet was seen in the West,
in Wèi (Stomach),
five or six zhàng long,
white in color,
with its rays pointing south,
passing through Cān (Orion),
and disappeared after twenty days.
In the eleventh month of the fifth year,
a comet was again seen in Zhěn,
five zhàng long,
west of the Left Enforcer in Tàiwēi,
pointing southeast,
and disappeared after one hundred ninety days.
According to the divination:
"Wèi
is the astrological division of Yǎnzhōu.
Cān
is associated with military affairs.
Tàiwēi is
the Emperor's court.
The Zhífǎ (Enforcer)
represents the executive officials.
Comets and broom-stars signify war and mourning,
and the removal of the old and establishment of the new."
In the second month of Zhèngyuán first year,
Lǐ Fēng (Lǐ Fēng), his younger brother Lǐ Yì (Lǐ Yì), and the Empress's father Zhāng Jī (Zhāng Jī), among others, plotted rebellion,
and were all executed;
the Empress was also deposed.
In the ninth month,
the Emperor was deposed as King of Qí.
In the eleventh month of the first year of Zhèngyuán of Gāoguì Xiānggōng,
a white vapor emerged from the side of the Southern Dipper,
several zhàng wide,
its length reaching the sky.
Wáng Sù said,
"This is Chī Yóu's banner.
There will be chaos in the southeast!"
In the first month of the second year,
a comet was seen at the border of Wú and Chǔ,
reaching the sky in the northwest.
Zhèndōng Dàjiāngjūn Guànqiū Jiǎn and others rebelled in Huáinán,
and Jǐngdì suppressed and pacified them.
According to divination,
"When Chī Yóu's banner appears,
the king will conquer the four quarters."
Afterward, Huáinán was again conquered,
and Bāshǔ in the west was pacified.
That year was
the first year of Wǔfèng for Sūn Liàng, the ruler of Wú.
The constellations Dǒu and Niú
are the divisions of Wú and Yuè.
According to divination,
"There will be war and mourning in Wú,
an omen of discarding the old and establishing the new."
In the third year of Tàipíng,
Sūn Lín, with a large army, besieged the palace,
deposing Liàng as the King of Kuàijī.
Thus, the Guózhì also records this in Wú.
Huáinán and Jiāngdōng are both in Yángzhōu territory,
thus the omens at that time appeared in Wú and Chǔ.
The Chǔ division is Wèi's Huáinán,
which often shares the same disasters as Wú.
Therefore, Guànqiū Jiǎn took the comet as an omen for himself,
then raised an army and was defeated.
Three years later,
which was the second year of Gānlù of Wèi,
Zhūgě Dàn also rebelled in Huáinán,
and Wú dispatched generals to aid him.
When the city fell,
tens of thousands of Dàn's troops and Wú soldiers perished,
which was an omen of the previous long comet.
In the eleventh month of the second year of Gānlù,
a comet was seen in Jiǎo,
white in color.
The divination said,
"When a comet appears between the two horns and is white,
an army will rise without fighting,
and there will be a great mourning in the state."
In the first year of Jǐngyuán,
Gāoguì Xiānggōng was harmed by Chéng Jì.
In the tenth month, Dīngchǒu day, of the fourth year,
a guest star was seen in Tàiwēi,
moving southeast,
passing through Zhěn constellation,
and disappearing after seven days.
The divination said,
"When a guest star appears in Tàiwēi,
there will be war and mourning."
In the first year of Jǐngyuán,
Gāoguì Xiānggōng was harmed.
In the eleventh month, Rén Yín day, of the third year of Jǐngyuán of Yuándì,
a comet was seen in Kàng,
white in color,
five cùn long,
〔二七〕moving northward,
and disappearing after forty-five days.
The divination said,
"It signifies war and mourning."
Another said,
"When a comet appears in Kàng,
the Son of Heaven loses his virtue."
In the fourth year,
Zhōng Huì and Dèng Ài attacked Shǔ
and conquered it.
The two generals rebelled
and were both executed.
In the fifth month of the second year of Xiánxī,
a comet was seen in Wángliáng,
more than a zhàng long,
white in color,
pointing southeast,
and disappearing after twelve days.
The divination said,
"Wángliáng
is the Son of Heaven's imperial chariot.
A comet sweeping it signifies
an omen of abdication and succession,
an image of discarding the old and establishing the new.
White color signifies mourning.
Wángliáng is in the Dōngbì constellation,
and also the division of Bìngzhōu."
In the eighth month,
Wéndì passed away.
In the twelfth month,
Wǔdì received the abdication of Wèi.
In the first month, Bǐng Xū day, of the fourth year of Tàishǐ of Wǔdì,
a comet was seen in Zhěn,
bluish-white in color,
moving northwest,
then turning east.
The divination said,
"It signifies war and mourning.
Zhěn is also the division of Chǔ."
In the third month,
Empress Dowager Wáng passed away.
In the tenth month,
Wú bandits attacked Jiāngxià and Xiāngyáng.
In the ninth month of the fifth year,
a comet appeared in Zǐgōng.
The divination is as above.
Zǐgōng
is the emperor's inner palace.
In the tenth year,
Wǔyuán Yáng Empress passed away.
In the twelfth month of the tenth year,
a comet appeared in Zhěn.
The divination said,
"Wars will break out across the land.
Zhěn is also the division of Chǔ."
In the sixth month, Jiǎ Xū day, of the second year of Xiánníng,
a comet appeared in Dī.
The divination said,
"The Son of Heaven loses his virtue and changes policies.
Dī
is also the division of Yǎnzhōu."
In the seventh month,
a comet appeared in Dàjiǎo.
Dàjiǎo is the emperor's seat.
In the eighth month,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi,
reaching Yì, Běidǒu, and Sāntái.
The divination said,
"Tàiwēi
is the emperor's court;
great men will suffer misfortune."
Another said,
"There will be a change of ruler.
Yì
is also the division of Chǔ.
Běidǒu governs killing and punishment,
Sāntái are the Three Dukes."
In the first month of the third year,
a comet appeared in the west.
In the third month,
a comet appeared in Wèi.
Wèi
is the division of Xúzhōu.
In the fourth month,
a comet appeared in Nǚyù.
Nǚyù is the inner palace.
In the fifth month,
it again appeared in the east.
In the seventh month,
a comet appeared in Zǐgōng.
The divination said,
"The ruler of the land will change."
In the fourth month of the fourth year,
Chī Yóu's banner appeared in Dōngjǐng.
Two years later,
the forces of three directions attacked Wú,
which was its fulfillment.
In the third month of the fifth year,
a comet appeared in Liǔ.
In the fourth month,
it again appeared in Nǚyù.
In the seventh month,
it appeared in Zǐgōng.
The divination said,
"External officials will encroach upon the sovereign.
Liǔ
is also the division of Sānhé.
Dàjiǎo, Tàiwēi, Zǐgōng, and Nǚyù all represent the ruler."
The following year Wú perished,
which was its fulfillment.
Comets signify war and mourning.
In the campaign against Wú,
troops from Sānhé, Xú, and Yǎn all marched out,
engaging in battle in the lands of Wú and Chǔ.
The Wú chancellor and grand commanders, and those below them, were executed in the tens;
the common officers and soldiers were decapitated in the tens of thousands.
All these were its omens.
In the eighth month of the second year of Tàikāng,
a comet appeared in Zhāng.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military disaster and death.”
In the eleventh month,
a comet appeared in Xuānyuán.
The prognostication stated:
“The imperial harem will be affected by this.”
In the third month, on the day Wùshēn, of the fourth year,
a comet appeared in the southwest.
In this year,
Qí Wáng Yōu (齊王攸), Rènéng Wáng Líng (任城王陵), Lángxié Wáng Zhòu (琅邪王伷), and Xīndū Wáng Gāi (新都王該) died.
In the ninth month of the eighth year,
a comet appeared in the Southern Dipper,
tens of *zhàng* long,
and disappeared after more than ten days.
The prognostication stated:
“The Dipper governs noble titles and salaries;
the state will experience great sorrow.”
Another interpretation stated:
“A comet in the Dipper [signifies]
the illness of a ruler,
a change of government in the realm,
great chaos, and the outbreak of war.”
In the fourth month of the first year of Tàixī,
a guest star was in Zǐgōng.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military disaster and death.”
Towards the end of Tàikāng,
Wǔdì indulged in feasts and excursions,
and suffered many illnesses.
In this month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Yǒngpíng,
Empress Jiǎ executed Yáng Jùn (楊駿) and his partisans,
exterminating their three clans,
and Grand Empress Dowager Yáng (楊太后) was also assassinated.
Furthermore, Rǔnán Wáng Liàng (汝南王亮), Tàibǎo Wèi Guàn (太保衞瓘), and Chǔ Wáng Wěi (楚王瑋) were executed.
These were the corresponding omens for military disaster and death within the imperial family.
In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuánkāng of Huìdì,
a comet appeared in Kuí,
reaching Xuānyuán and Tàiwēi,
passing through Sāntái and Tàilíng.
The prognostication stated:
“Kuí corresponds to Lǔ,
and also to military arsenals;
Xuānyuán corresponds to the imperial harem;
Tàiwēi is the court of the Son of Heaven;
Sāntái represents the Three Ministers;
Tàilíng signifies the accumulation of corpses and death.”
Thereafter, the Imperial Armory caught fire,
and the Western Qiāng rebelled.
Five years later,
Sīkōng Zhāng Huà (司空張華) met with disaster,
Empress Jiǎ was deposed and died,
and Lǔgōng Jiǎ Mì (魯公賈謐) was executed.
In the following year,
Zhào Wáng Lún (趙王倫) usurped the throne.
Thereupon, the Three Princes raised armies to suppress Lún,
and over one hundred thousand soldiers died in battle.
In the third month of the first year of Yǒngkāng,
an ominous star appeared in the south.
The prognostication stated:
“When an ominous star appears,
great military conflicts will soon arise in the realm.”
In this month, Empress Jiǎ murdered the Crown Prince.
Zhào Wáng Lún soon deposed and killed the Empress,
executed Sīkōng Zhāng Huà,
and then deposed the Emperor and enthroned himself.
Thereupon, the Three Princes rose simultaneously,
alternately seizing control of the realm.
In the twelfth month of that year,
a comet appeared west of Qiānniú,
pointing towards Tiānshì.
The prognostication stated:
“Niú is the beginning of the Seven Regulators;
the appearance of a comet there
is an omen for changing the reign title and imperial designation.
Tiānshì is also called Tiānfǔ,
and also the Emperor’s banner,
with the Emperor seated within it.”
In the following year,
Zhào Wáng Lún usurped the throne,
changed the reign title,
and was soon destroyed by a great army.
In the fourth month of the second year,
a comet appeared in the Qí astrological division.
The prognostication stated:
“Qí will suffer military disaster and death.”
At this time,
Qí Wáng Jiǒng (齊王冏) raised an army to suppress Zhào Wáng Lún.
After Lún was destroyed,
Jiǒng hoarded military power and did not attend court,
monopolizing authority and indulging in extravagance.
In the following year,
he was executed.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tài'ān,
a comet was visible in daylight.
In the third month of the second year,
a comet appeared in the east,
pointing to Sāntái.
The prognostication stated:
“An omen of military disaster and death.
Sāntái represents the Three Dukes.”
In the first month of the third year,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè (東海王越) seized the Grand Commandant and Chángshā Wáng (長沙王),
and Zhāng Fāng (張方) then killed them.
In the fifth month of the first year of Yǒngxīng,
a guest star guarded Bì.
The prognostication stated:
“The Son of Heaven will have no heir.”
Another interpretation stated:
“High ministers will be executed.”
At this time, the various princes held military power.
Thereafter, Huìdì lost control,
ultimately having no successor.
In the eighth month of the second year,
a comet appeared in Mǎo and Bì.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military disaster and death.
Mǎo and Bì are also the astrological divisions of Zhào and Wèi.”
In the tenth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
a comet appeared in the Northern Dipper.
The prognostication stated:
“The celestial authority will change hands,
and the Son of Heaven will flee.”
It also stated:
“Powerful states will raise armies,
and feudal lords will contend for power.”
Thereafter,
the various princes engaged in battle,
all corresponding to the omens.
In the following year,
Huìdì passed away.
In the seventh month of the fourth year of Xiánhé of Chéngdì,
a comet appeared in the northwest,
violating the Dipper,
and disappeared after twenty-three days.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military chaos.”
In the twelfth month,
Guō Mò (郭默) killed the Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, Liú Yìn (劉胤).
The Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Táo Kǎn (陶侃), suppressed Mò,
and executed him.
At this time, Shí Lè (石勒) also began to assume an imperial title.
In the first month, on the day Xīnsì, of the second year of Xiánkāng,
a comet appeared in the west in the evening,
in Kuí.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military disaster and death.
Kuí
also represents border troops.”
In the first month of the third year,
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍) usurped the title of Heavenly King.
In the fourth year,
Shí Jìlóng attacked Mùróng Huàng (慕容皝),
but failed.
After retreating,
Huàng pursued and attacked him,
and also defeated Má Qiū (麻秋).
At this time, Huàng declared himself a vassal,
which was the corresponding omen for border troops.
In the second month, on the day Gēngchén, of the sixth year,
a comet appeared in Tàiwēi.
In the third month of the seventh year,
Empress Dù (杜皇后) passed away.
On the sixth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jiànyuán of Kāngdì,
a comet appeared in Kàng,
seven *chǐ* long,
and white in color.
The prognostication stated:
“Kàng represents the imperial court,
and governs military disaster and death.”
In the second year,
Kāngdì passed away.
On the day Yǐmǎo, in the eleventh month of the fifth year of Yǒnghé of Mùdì,
a comet appeared in Kàng.
Its tail pointed west,
was white in color,
and one *zhàng* long.
In the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu, of the sixth year,
a comet appeared again in Kàng.
The prognostication stated:
“This portends military disaster, death, and pestilence.”
In the eighth month of that fifth year,
Chǔ Póu (褚裒) launched a northern expedition,
and his army was defeated.
In the eleventh month,
Rǎn Mǐn (冉閔) killed Shí Zūn (石遵),
and also slaughtered over one hundred thousand Hú,
whereupon the central plains fell into great chaos.
In the twelfth month,
Chǔ Póu passed away.
In this year,
there was a great plague.
In the second year of Shēngpíng, fifth month, on the day Dīnghài,
a comet appeared in Tiānchuán,
located in Wèi.
The divination said:
"This foretells military conflict and mourning,
discarding the old and establishing the new.
Appearing in Tiānchuán
means foreign invasion."
Another account states:
"It portends a great flood."
In the fourth year, fifth month,
there was a great flood throughout the land.
In the fifth year,
Emperor Mù (Mùdì) passed away.
In the first year of Āidì's Xīngníng era, eighth month,
a broom star appeared in Jiǎo Kàng,
entering Tiānshì.
According to the divination, it said:
"This foretells military conflict and mourning."
In the third year, first month,
Empress Wáng (Wáng Shì) passed away.
In the second month,
the Emperor passed away.
In the third month,
Mùróng Kè attacked and captured Luòyáng,
and Shěn Jìn and others died in battle.
In the fourth year of Hǎixī's Tàihé era, second month,
a guest star appeared in the western wall of Zǐgōng,
and did not vanish until the seventh month.
The divination said:
"A guest star guarding Zǐgōng
means a minister will assassinate his lord."
In the sixth year,
Huán Wēn deposed the Emperor, making him the Duke of Hǎixī.
In the second year of Xiàowǔ's Níngkāng era, first month, on the day Dīngsì,
a broom star appeared in Nǚxū,
passing through Dī Kàng, Jiǎo, Zhěn, Yì, and Zhāng.
By the third month, on the day Bǐngxū,
a comet was seen in Dī.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
a broom star appeared in Tiānshì.
The divination said:
"This foretells military conflict and mourning."
In the first year of Tàiyuán, seventh month,
Fú Jiān conquered Liángzhōu,
and captured Zhāng Tiānxī.
In the eleventh year of Tàiyuán, third month,
a guest star was in Nándǒu,
and did not vanish until the sixth month.
The divination said:
"There will be war,
and an amnesty."
Thereafter, Sī, Yōng, Yǎn, and Jì provinces constantly had military service.
In the twelfth year, first month, there was a great amnesty,
and in the eighth month, another great amnesty.
In the fifteenth year, seventh month, on the day Rénshēn,
a broom star appeared in Běihéshù,
passing through Tàiwēi, Sāntái, and Wénchāng,
entering Běidǒu.
Its color was white,
and it was over ten zhàng long.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùxū,
it entered Zǐgōng and then vanished.
The divination said:
"Běihéshù is also called Húmén,
meaning the Hú will have military conflict and mourning.
Sweeping Tàiwēi
and entering Zǐwēi
means the king will be affected.
Sāntái represents the Three Dukes,
and Wénchāng represents the generals and prime ministers;
the generals, prime ministers, and Three Dukes will suffer disaster.
Entering Běidǒu
means the feudal lords will be executed."
Another account states:
"Sweeping Běidǒu
means powerful states will mobilize troops,
feudal lords will contend for power,
and great men will worry."
In the twenty-first year,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Lóng'ān,
Wáng Gōng, Yīn Zhòngkān, Huán Xuán, and others all raised armies,
claiming their purpose was to execute Wáng Guóbǎo.
The court assented and killed him,
and also beheaded his younger cousin Xù.
Sīmǎ Dàozǐ thereby lost power,
and chaos ensued.
In the eighteenth year, second month,
a guest star was in Wěizhōng,
and did not vanish until the ninth month.
The divination said:
"Yān will have military conflict and mourning."
In the twentieth year,
Mùróng Chuí's son Bǎo attacked Wèi,
but was defeated by them,
and tens of thousands died.
In the twenty-first year,
Chuí died,
and the state subsequently declined and perished.
In the twentieth year, ninth month,
a hairy star, like scattered cotton, appeared,
moving southeast,
passing through Nǚxū,
to Kūxīng.
The divination said:
"When a hairy star appears,
within three years,
a rebellious minister will surely be executed in the marketplace."
At this time,
Wáng Guóbǎo was stirring up trouble in the court.
In the twenty-first year, ninth month,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Lóng'ān,
Wáng Gōng and others raised troops,
and the court killed Wáng Guóbǎo and Wáng Xù.
In the fourth year of Āidì's Lóng'ān era, second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
a broom star appeared in Kuí,
three zhàng long,
reaching up to Gédào and the western boundary of Zǐgōng,
entering the head of Běidǒu,
and reaching Sāntái.
In the third month,
it then passed through Tàiwēi Dìzuò Duānmén.
The divination said:
"A comet sweeping the Emperor's court Gédào
is a sign of changing lords."
It passed through Sāntái and entered Běidǒu.
The divination is the same as the above entry.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùyín,
a broom star appeared in Guànsǔo, Tiānshì, and Tiānjīn.
The divination said:
"Noble ministers will die in prison,
and there will be military conflict and mourning both inside and outside the capital.
Tiānjīn being cut off by bandits
means the king's path throughout the realm will be blocked."
According to the divination:
"The disaster is in Wú Yuè."
In the fifth year, second month,
Sūn Ēn's army rebelled,
attacking and invading commanderies and states.
Thereupon, both internal and external defenses were heightened,
military camps and garrisons were established,
and the entrance to the Huái River was barricaded.
In the ninth month,
Huán Xuán's memorial arrived,
defying the imperial edict and insulting the sovereign.
Thereafter, Xuán usurped the throne,
plunging the capital into chaos,
with a great famine,
people resorting to cannibalism,
and the common people fleeing and scattering.
All these were its manifestations.
In the first year of Yuánxīng, tenth month,
a guest star, white as scattered cotton, appeared
west of Tàiwēi,
and entered Tàiwēi by the twelfth month.
The divination said:
"Troops will enter the Emperor's court."
In the second year, twelfth month,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
exiling the Emperor and Empress to Xúnyáng,
and making Empress Hé (Hé Hòuhòu) of Yǒng'ān the Lady of Línglíng.
In the third year, second month,
Liú Yù executed all of the Huán (Huán Shì) clan.
In the eleventh year of Yìxī, fifth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
two comets appeared in Tiānshì,
sweeping Dìzuò,
north of Fáng Xīn.
Fáng Xīn is the region of Sòng.
According to the divination:
"He who obtains the comet's tail will rise,
discarding the old and establishing the new;
this is a sign of Sòng's rise."
In the fourteenth year, fifth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
a broom star appeared in the midst of Běidǒu Kuí.
In the seventh month, on the day Guǐhài,
a comet appeared west of Tàiwēi,
its handle rising from below Shàngxiāngxīng,
its tail gradually lengthening to over ten zhàng,
advancing to sweep Běidǒu, Zǐwēi, and Zhōngtái.
The divination said:
"A comet appearing in Tàiwēi
means the altars of soil and grain will perish,
and the world will change kings;
entering Běidǒu and Zǐwēi
means the imperial palace will be empty."
In the fourteenth year,
Liú Yù returned to Péngchéng
and accepted the title of Duke of Sòng.
In the twelfth month,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Gōngdì, first month, on the day Wùxū,
a broom star appeared in the western boundary of Tàiwēi.
The divination said:
"A sign of revolution."
In that year,
Sòng took control of the world.
Stars fell and
In the thirteenth year of Jiànxīng, during the reign of the Latter Lord of Shǔ,
Zhūgě Liàng led a large army to attack Wèi.
They encamped south of the Wèi River.
A long star, red and with radiating points,
flowed from the northeast to the southwest,
landing in Liàng's camp.
It landed three times and returned twice,
starting large and returning small.
The divination said:
"When two armies are confronting each other,
if a large meteor runs above the army or falls into it,
it is a sign of utter defeat."
In the ninth month,
Liàng died in the army.
The camp was burned, and the army retreated.
The various commanders harbored mutual resentment,
and many annihilated each other.
In the second year of Jǐngchū, during the reign of Emperor Míng of Wèi,
Xuāndì besieged Gōngsūn Wényì at Xiāngpíng.
On the night of Rénzǐ in the eighth month,
a large meteor, several tens of zhàng long,
white with a radiant mane,
flowed from the northeast of Shǒushān,
falling southeast of Xiāngpíng city.
The divination said:
"When a city is under siege, and a meteor runs above it or falls within it, the city will fall."
It also said:
"Where a star falls,
there will be a battlefield beneath it."
It also said:
"Wherever a star falls,
the state will change its surname."
In the ninth month,
Wényì broke through the encirclement and fled,
but was beheaded at the place where the star fell.
The city was massacred,
and its inhabitants were buried alive.
In the sixth month of the fourth year of Jǐngyuán, during the reign of Emperor Yuán,
two large meteors, both as big as dipper-shaped constellations,
appeared in the west,
then flowed separately to the north and south.
Their light illuminated the ground,
and there was a rumbling sound.
According to divination:
"Meteors represent noble envoys;
large stars represent important envoys."
In this year,
Zhōng and Dèng conquered Shǔ.
The two stars were likely the symbols of the two commanders.
The two commanders turning against each other was the omen of their separate flows to the north and south.
After Zhōng Huì rebelled,
the three armies were enraged;
the rumbling sound
was a sign of the soldiers' and generals' anger.
In the seventh month of the fourth year of Tàishǐ, during the reign of Emperor Wǔ,
stars fell like rain,
all flowing westward.
The divination said:
"Falling stars signify the rebellion of the common people.
The westward flow
is a symbol of the people of Wú returning to Jìn."
Two years later,
Sūn Xiù, the Commander of Xiàkǒu in Wú, led more than two thousand troops and followers to surrender.
On Rénzǐ in the eighth month of the ninth year of Tàikāng,
stars fell like rain.
Liú Xiàng's commentary says:
"It is an omen of the lower displacing the upper."
Three years later,
the Emperor passed away, and Emperor Huì ascended the throne.
From this point, the world fell into chaos.
On Jiǎwǔ in the ninth month of the fourth year of Yuánkāng, during the reign of Emperor Huì,
a stray arrow moved northeast,
spanning the entire sky.
On the night of Bǐngwǔ in the sixth month of the sixth year,
a stray arrow emerged from the Dǒu Kuí (Northern Dipper's ladle) and moved southeast.
According to divination:
"Chaos is used to suppress chaos.
The Northern Dipper governs execution.
Emanating from the Dǒu Kuí,
the one who executes from the center
is a sign of injustice."
After this,
King Zhào killed Zhāng and Péi,
and deposed Empress Jiǎ,
to rectify the injustice of the Crown Prince.
Consequently, he usurped the throne himself,
leading to mass slaughter and annihilation.
This was the omen of using chaos to suppress chaos.
Another interpretation says
it was an omen of the Dī chieftain Qí Wànnián's rebellion.
On Xīnsì in the eleventh month of the second year of Tài'ān,
a star fell in broad daylight, descending from the north in the middle of the sky.
Its light turned white,
and there was a sound like thunder.
According to divination:
"It is called Yíngshǒu.
Wherever Yíngshǒu appears,
there will be great warfare
and bloodshed below."
The following year,
Liú Yuánhǎi and Shí Lè attacked and plundered Bìngzhōu,
causing much destruction and slaughter.
Wáng Jùn raised an army in Yān and Dài,
and brought Xiānbēi forces to attack and plunder Yèzhōng,
leaving the people devastated.
The sound like thunder
was a sign of anger.
On Yǐchǒu in the seventh month of the first year of Yǒngxīng,
a star fell with a sound.
In the tenth month of the second year,
a star again fell with a sound.
The divination is the same as above.
After this,
Zhōngxià was consequently lost.
In the fifth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
a stray arrow flowed southwest.
At this time,
Sīmǎ Yuè defeated the Héjiān army in the west,
and escorted the Emperor.
Soon after, he arrested Miào Yìn, Hé Suí, and others,
showing a disloyal heart.
The world detested him.
When he died, Shí Lè burned his coffin and corpse;
this was the fulfillment of the omen.
On Xīnmǎo in the ninth month of the first year of Yǒngjiā, during the reign of Emperor Huái,
a large star, like the sun,
flowed from the southwest to the northeast.
Smaller ones, like dippers,
followed it.
The sky was entirely red,
and there was a sound like thunder.
The divination said:
"Meteors represent noble envoys;
large stars represent important envoys."
In the fifth month of this year,
Jí Sāng killed Wáng Téng, the King of Dōngyàn,
and then occupied Héběi.
In the eleventh month,
Hé Yù was first dispatched as General who Conquers the North,
to garrison west of Yè.
Tián Zhēn and others greatly defeated Jí Sāng, beheading him at Lèlíng.
Consequently, Zhēn was made Administrator of Jí Jùn,
and his brother Lán, Administrator of Jùlù.
The smaller stars following were
an omen of minor generals and separate commanders.
Sīmǎ Yuè resented that the areas east of Wèijùn and south of Píngyuán all sided with Sāng,
and so he rewarded Zhēn and others.
Thus, there was widespread looting and devastation.
The sound like thunder
was an omen of anger.
On Gēngzǐ in the tenth month of the fourth year,
a large star fell to the northwest,
with a sound.
Soon after, the Emperor was forced to flee to Píngyáng.
On Rénchén in the fourth month of the third year of Tàixīng, during the reign of Emperor Yuán,
a stray arrow emerged from Xū and Wēi,
and disappeared into Yì and Zhěn.
The divination said:
"Wherever a stray arrow strikes,
it is where the world will attack.
Yì and Zhěn
are the divisions of Jīngzhōu."
In the second year of Tàiníng,
Wáng Dūn killed Qíao Wáng Chéng and Gān Zhuó.
Then Dūn himself was annihilated.
This was the fulfillment of the stray arrow striking Yì.
On Jiǎwǔ in the seventh month of the first year of Yǒngchāng,
a meteor as large as an urn,
over a hundred zhàng long,
blue-red in color,
came from the west.
Its tail split into over a hundred branches,
some scattering.
At that time, Wáng Dūn's rebellion
was the omen for the displacement of the common people.
On Xīnwèi in the sixth month of the third year of Xiánkāng, during the reign of Emperor Chéng,
a meteor, as large as two Dǒu Kuí,
blue-red in color,
its light illuminating the ground,
emerged from Kuí
and disappeared north of Lóu.
According to divination:
"It signifies famine,
and that the five grains will not be stored."
In this month,
there was a great drought
and famine.
On Gēngwǔ Shuò in the second month of the sixth year,
a meteor, as large as a dipper,
its light illuminating the ground,
emerged from Tiānshì,
traveled west, and entered Tàiwēi.
The divination said:
"A great man will bear this."
In the sixth month of the eighth year,
Emperor Chéng passed away.
In the sixth month, on the day of Xīnsì, in the eighth year of Yǒnghé of Emperor Mùdì,
before sunset,
there was a shooting star as large as a three-dòu ladle (kúi),
issuing from the directions of Chén and Sì,
traveling southeast.
By calculating its altitude and path,
it was between the constellations Jī and Dòu,
which is the portion of Yān.
The prognostication states:
"It represents the head of the camp.
Beneath the head of the camp,
blood will flow profusely."
At this time,
Mùróng Jùn usurped the title of Great Yān,
and his campaigns of conquest were endless.
In the fourth month, on the day of Guǐwèi, in the tenth year,
a shooting star as large as a dǒu appeared,
reddish-yellow in color,
issuing from Zhīnǚ,
and disappearing in Zàofù,
with a sound like thunder.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in Yān and Qí,
and the common people will become refugees."
In the twelfth month of that year,
Mùróng Jùn then occupied Línzhāng,
and completely possessed the lands of Yōu, Bìng, Qīng, and Jì.
The various generals along the Hé (Yellow River) scattered and fled,
and the river crossings were cut off.
Mùróng Kè attacked Qí.
In the eleventh month of the second year of Shēngpíng,
a crooked arrow flew from the southeast to the northwest,
its length half the sky.
In the tenth month, on the day of Gēngxū, in the fourth year,
Tiāngǒu appeared in the southwest.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a great war,
and blood will flow."
In the tenth month, on the day of Rénshēn, in the fourth year of Tàihé of Hǎixī,
a large shooting star descended to the west,
with a sound like thunder.
The following year,
an envoy was sent to strip Yuán Zhēn of his official status, making him a commoner.
Huán Wēn attacked Shòuchūn.
Zhēn died of illness,
and his son Jǐn took his place,
seeking aid from Fú Jiān.
Wēn defeated Fú Jiān's army.
In the sixth year,
Shòuchūn city fell.
In the tenth month, on the day of Yǐmǎo, in the sixth year of Tàiyuán of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
a streaking star traveled southeast through Yì and Zhěn,
with a sound like thunder.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in the land of Chǔ,
armies will be defeated,
and the common people will become refugees."
In the twelfth month,
Fú Jiān's Governor of Jīngzhōu, Liáng Chéng, and the Administrator of Xiāngyáng, Yán Zhèn, led their troops to attack Jìnglíng.
Huán Shíqián attacked and thoroughly defeated them,
capturing Zhèn alive,
beheading seven thousand,
and capturing ten thousand civilians.
The sound like thunder
is an omen of angry generals and commanders.
In the intercalary month, on the day of Wùchén, in the thirteenth year,
Tiāngǒu descended in the northeast,
with a sound.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a great battle,
and blood will flow."
After this,
Mùróng Chuí, Zhái Liáo, Yáo Cháng, Fú Dēng, and Mùróng Yǒng all raised armies and contended for power.
In the first month of the fourteenth year,
rebel bandits from Péngchéng again proclaimed a false reign title at Huángqiū.
Liú Láozhī defeated and eliminated them.
In the third month,
Zhāng Dào broke through Héxiāng and Tàishān.
Xiàng Qīnzhī attacked and drove them away.
In the third month, on the day of Jiǎyín, in the fifth year of Lóng'ān of Emperor Āndì,
shooting stars of a red color,
numerous, traveled westward,
passing through Qiānniú, Xū, Wēi, Tiānjīn, Gédào,
and penetrating Tàiwēi and Zǐgōng.
The prognostication said:
"Stars represent the common people.
Their numerous westward travel
is an omen of many generals flowing westward.
Passing through the Son of Heaven's court
indicates a weak ruler and strong ministers,
and that the feudal lords' armies cannot be controlled."
In the fifth month of that year,
Sūn Ēn invaded Wújùn,
and killed the Internal Administrator.
In the sixth month,
he reached Jīngkǒu.
Thereupon, both inside and outside the capital, martial law was declared,
camps and formations were garrisoned,
and Liú Yù pursued and defeated him.
In the seventh month of the first year of Yuánxīng,
there was a great famine,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
Six or seven tenths of the population east of Zhèjiāng became refugees,
the households in Wújùn and Wúxīng were halved,
and tens of thousands more fled westward.
In the tenth month,
Huán Xuán sent generals to attack Liú Guǐ,
defeating and driving him away.
Guǐ fled to Qīngzhōu.
Cloud Qi
In the twelfth month, on the night of Rénzǐ, in the first year of Yǒngxīng of Emperor Huìdì,
there was a red qi stretching across the sky,
with a rumbling and hidden sound.
In the tenth month, on the day of Dīngchǒu, in the second year,
a red qi appeared in the north,
extending across the sky from east to west.
The prognostication said:
"Both are omens of a great war.
The rumbling and hidden sound
is an omen of anger."
After this,
the four seas were in turmoil,
and armies clashed throughout the nine regions.
In the twelfth month, on the day of Jiǎshēn, in the first year of Guāngxī,
there was a white qi like a rainbow,
descending from mid-sky northward to the ground,
visible for five nights before disappearing.
The prognostication said:
"A great war will arise."
The following year,
Wáng Mí arose in Qīng and Xú,
Jí Sāng caused chaos north of the Hé (Yellow River),
and their poison spread throughout the land.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Yǐhài, in the third year of Yǒngjiā of Emperor Huáidì,
〔三二〕there was a white qi like a sash,
two appearing from both north and south,
rising from the ground to the sky,
and piercing through Cān and Fá.
The prognostication said:
"Great wars will arise throughout the realm."
In the third month of the fourth year,
Sīmǎ Yuè arrested Miáo Yìn and others.
Also,
the three regions were in turmoil,
with incessant warfare.
In the third month of the fifth year,
Sīmǎ Yuè died at Qīngpíngchéng.
Shí Lè attacked and defeated his forces,
with over one hundred thousand dead.
In the sixth month,
the capital was burned and destroyed,
and the Emperor was taken captive.
In the tenth month, on the night of Jǐsì, in the first year of Jiànxīng of Emperor Mǐndì,
a red qi shone in the northwest.
The Governor of Jīngzhōu, Táo Kǎn, attacked Dù Tāo's faction at Shíchéng,
and was defeated in battle.

In the first year of Tàikāng of Jìn Wǔdì,
after the pacification of the Sūn氏,
a total of twenty-three commanderies and states were newly established:

(Xíngyáng, Shàngluò, Dùnqīu, Línhuái, Dōngguǎn, Xiāngchéng, Rǔyīn, Chángguǎng, Guǎngníng, Chānglí, Xīnyě, Suí Jùn, Yīnpíng, Yìyáng, Pílíng, Xuānchéng, Nánkāng, Jìn'ān, Níngpǔ, Shǐpíng, Lüèyáng, Lèpíng, Nánpíng.)
The Sīlì province was abolished and Sī Zhōu was established.
Furthermore, four new provinces, Liáng, Qín, Níng, and Píng, were separately created,
and Wú's Guǎng Zhōu was retained,
making a total of nineteen provinces:

There were one hundred seventy-three commanderies and states.
(Twenty-five retained from Wú,
eleven newly established by Shǔ and retained,
twenty-one established by Wèi and retained,
ninety-three ancient ones from Hàn,
and twenty-three newly established.)
These were regarded as the states of ceremonial attire,
possessing all the lands of Yīn and Zhōu.
As for the immensity at the beginning of heaven and earth,
and the clarity in the era of Xī and Nóng,
they were used to nurture the common people,
without contention over territories.
With jade rings and common arrows,
barbarian furs and carriages driven by wind,
southern pheasants presenting tribute,
and the east wind entering the musical scale,
it illuminates the highest virtue,
how could any distance not be reached?
Thus, the constellations adorn the heavens,
and mountains and rivers mark the earth.
The vastness of Duānyè is demarcated,
and the cities and towns are divided by Xiáohán.
Looking up and looking down,
all things return to it.
Therefore, the banks of the Luò and Xiányáng,
are just like Qín and Hàn.
Jìn borders the Hexī region,
sharing the knowledge of Yáo and Yǔ.
In this new capital,
residing in this Hàojīng,
things that even five-foot tall children can recite by heart,
are not recorded by official historians.
In the past, Bāoxīshì was born in Chéngjì,
and became the Son of Heaven,
making his capital in Chén.
Shénnóngshì made his capital in Chén,
and separately established a settlement in Qūfù.
Huángdì was born in Shòuqīu,
and made his capital in Zhuólù.
Shàohào began in Qióngsāng,
and moved his capital to Qūfù.
Zhuānxū began in Qióngsāng,
and moved his town to Shāngqīu.
Gāoxīn ascended the throne,
and established his capital in Bó.
Xún Qīngzǐ said:
“If you do not ascend a high mountain,
you will not know the height of the sky;
if you do not approach a deep ravine,
you will not know the thickness of the earth.”
How great is the Kun Trigram,
from which all things derive life!
It carries Kūn and Huá mountains without falling,
and can tilt rivers and seas without leaking.
Consulting the oracle, the king,
rides and stops his chariot,
gazes at Mount Gòu and carves inscriptions,
and views Zēngchéng as a spectacle.
When the times met with gradual decline,
and the path encountered erosion,
King Píng moved east,
scattering like stars and splitting like beans.
When Dangtú commanded the imperial chariot,
the land was divided like melons and stood like tripods.
Shìzǔ Wǔ Huángdì received the remnants of a thousand years,
and accepted the abdication from eight Yáo.
The former kings' hometowns,
and the entire realm came to submit.
This can truly be spoken of.
When Huì Huáng was unexpected,
the central plains were entirely abandoned.
During Yǒngjiā, they crossed south,
and the imperial court was established in Jiànyè,
possessing two-ninths of the world.
In the past, Dà Yǔ observed the muddy Hé and received the green characters.
Within the whole world, this can be spoken of.
Heaven has seven stars;
earth has seven markers.
Heaven has four cardinal points;
earth has four great rivers.
Beyond the eight directions,
it is called the Eight Extremities.
The earth is not full in the southeast;
heaven is not full in the northwest.
The vastness of the Eight Extremities
is two hundred million thirty-one thousand three hundred lì from east to west,
and two hundred million thirty-one thousand three hundred lì from north to south.
From earth to heaven
is half the number of the Eight Extremities;
from below it is also so.
In the past, Huángdì ordered Shù Hài to measure from the eastern extremity
to the western extremity,
five hundred million ten thousand nine thousand eight hundred and eighty steps.
The imperial historian notes that
the circumference of the entire heavens is one million seventy thousand nine hundred thirteen lì,
with a diameter of three hundred fifty-six thousand nine hundred seventy lì.
What is called north-south is the warp;
east-west is the weft.
Heaven has twelve stations,
where the sun and moon reside;
earth has twelve terrestrial branches,
where kings and lords establish their states.
Some obtained their surnames through birth,
some were granted land for their merits,
such as Qí, Yóu, Yān, and Qí,
all within these regions.
In ancient times, Huángdì 黃帝 traveled everywhere under Heaven.
He governed an area ten thousand *lǐ* 里 in every direction,
obtaining ten thousand territories, each a hundred *lǐ* 里 in size.
This is what the *Zhōu Yì* 周易 refers to when it says,
“Leading forth the myriad things,
all myriad states are in peace.”
In ancient times, during the reign of Dì Yáo 帝堯,
he harmonized the myriad states,
establishing eight families as a *lín* 鄰 (neighborhood),
three *lín* 鄰 as a *péng* 朋 (group),
three *péng* 朋 as a *lǐ* 里 (village),
five *lǐ* 里 as an *yì* 邑 (town),
ten *yì* 邑 as a *dū* 都 (city),
ten *dū* 都 as a *shī* 師 (division),
and a *zhōu* 州 (province) had twelve *shī* 師.
The Xià Hòu Shì 夏后氏 (Xià Dynasty) extended eastward to the sea,
westward to the shifting sands (*liúshā* 流沙),
southward to the Jiāng 江 (Yangtze River),
and north and south their influence and teachings reached
as far as the steps of Shù Hài 豎亥.
None failed to follow and obey.
At Túshān 塗山, he assembled his ministers,
and ten thousand states presented jade and silk.
Thereupon, within the nine *zhōu* 州,
the Five Domains (*wǔfú* 五服) were established.
The Son of Heaven's own domain
was the five hundred *lǐ* 里 of the Diànfú 甸服 (Imperial Domain).
Within one hundred *lǐ* 里, a total tax was paid;
within two hundred *lǐ* 里, reaped grain was paid;
within three hundred *lǐ* 里, straw was paid;
within four hundred *lǐ* 里, grain was paid;
within five hundred *lǐ* 里, hulled rice was paid.
Beyond the Diànfú 甸服, for five hundred *lǐ* 里, was the Hóufú 侯服 (Feudal Lords' Domain).
Within one hundred *lǐ* 里, official residences were provided;
within two hundred *lǐ* 里, appointments were given;
within three hundred *lǐ* 里, feudal lords resided.
Beyond the Hóufú 侯服, for five hundred *lǐ* 里, was the Suífú 綏服 (Pacification Domain).
Within three hundred *lǐ* 里, civil education was supervised;
within two hundred *lǐ* 里, military defense was strengthened.
Beyond the Suífú 綏服, for five hundred *lǐ* 里, was the Yàofú 要服 (Reaching Domain).
Within three hundred *lǐ* 里, barbarians resided;
within two hundred *lǐ* 里, those subject to punishment resided.
Beyond the Yàofú 要服, for five hundred *lǐ* 里, was the Huāngfú 荒服 (Wild Domain).
Within three hundred *lǐ* 里, savage tribes resided;
within two hundred *lǐ* 里, exiles resided.
Reaching to the four seas,
the Five Domains (*wǔfú* 五服) were completed,
extending to five thousand *lǐ* 里.
When the virtue of Xià 夏 declined,
it encountered the chaos of Yǒuqióng 有窮.
Shàokāng 少康 brought about a restoration,
and did not lose the old ways.
From after Kǒng Jiǎ 孔甲,
up to Jié 桀,
the feudal lords annexed each other,
and those that could survive numbered over three thousand states.
Compared to Túshān 塗山,
seven-tenths had been lost.
Chéng Tāng 成湯 defeated Jié 桀 at Jiāo 焦,
and moved the tripods (*dǐng* 鼎) to Bó 亳.
Yī Zhì 伊摯, Zhòng Huǐ 仲虺, and others
greatly illuminated the constitutional laws.
The royal system for ranks and emoluments
had five grades: Gōng 公, Hóu 侯, Bó 伯, Zǐ 子, Nán 男.
The Son of Heaven's territory was one thousand *lǐ* 里 square.
A Gōng 公 or Hóu 侯 had territory one hundred *lǐ* 里 square;
a Bó 伯 had seventy *lǐ* 里;
a Zǐ 子 or Nán 男 had fifty *lǐ* 里.
Those with less than fifty *lǐ* 里
did not reach the Son of Heaven directly,
but were attached to the feudal lords,
and were called Fùyōng 附庸 (dependencies).
Within the four seas were nine *zhōu* 州,
each *zhōu* 州 being one thousand *lǐ* 里 square.
In each *zhōu* 州 were established thirty states of one hundred *lǐ* 里,
sixty states of seventy *lǐ* 里,
and one hundred twenty states of fifty *lǐ* 里,
totaling two hundred ten states.
Famous mountains and great marshes were not enfeoffed,
the rest were used as intermediate lands for the Fùyōng 附庸.
For the eight *zhōu* 州,
each *zhōu* 州 had two hundred ten states.
Within the Son of Heaven's domain,
there were nine states of one hundred *lǐ* 里,
twenty-one states of seventy *lǐ* 里,
and sixty-three states of fifty *lǐ* 里,
totaling ninety-three states.
Famous mountains and great marshes were not distributed,
the rest were used to reward scholars,
and as intermediate lands.
In total, the nine *zhōu* 州 contained
one thousand seven hundred seventy-three states.
The prime ministers of the Son of Heaven,
and the Fùyōng 附庸 of the feudal lords,
were not included in this count.
Within one hundred *lǐ* 里 of the Son of Heaven was for supporting officials;
within one thousand *lǐ* 里 was for official use;
beyond one thousand *lǐ* 里, regional lords (*fāngbó* 方伯) were established.
Five states formed a *shǔ* 屬,
and a *shǔ* 屬 had a chief (*zhǎng* 長);
ten states formed a *lián* 連,

There were eight *zhōu* 州,
eight *bó* 伯,
fifty-six *zhèng* 正,
one hundred sixty-eight *shuài* 帥,
and three hundred thirty-six *zhǎng* 長.
The eight *bó* 伯, each with their dependents, belonged to two elders of the Son of Heaven,
who divided the realm into left and right,

Within one thousand *lǐ* 里 was called *diàn* 甸 (imperial domain);

The Son of Heaven sent his grandees to be three inspectors (*sānjiān* 三監),

Within the Son of Heaven's domain,
the inner territories

the outer territories

Wǔ Wáng 武王 returned to Fēng 豐,

He established only five ranks,

Zhōu Gōng 周公 and Kāng Shú 康叔 established themselves in Lǔ 魯 and Wèi 衞,

For land that was not rotated, each family received one hundred *mǔ* 畝;

Five families formed a *bǐ* 比,

At that time, governance achieved great peace,
and policies were such that punishments were rarely needed.
The population was thirteen million seven hundred eleven thousand four hundred thirty-three.
This was the peak of the Zhōu dynasty.
When it declined,
rites, music, expeditions, and punitive actions originated from the feudal lords;

At the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period,

The *Sīmǎ Fǎ* extensively describes the Three Dynasties,

three *fū* made a *wū*,
three *wū* made a *jǐng*.
A *jǐng* was one *lǐ* square,
consisting of nine *fū*,
shared by eight families.
One man and one woman received one hundred *mǔ* of private land
and ten *mǔ* of public land,
totaling eight hundred eighty *mǔ*.
The remaining twenty *mǔ* were for dwellings.
They helped each other coming and going,
assisted each other in watch and guard,
and mutually aided in sickness.
When the people received land,
for superior land, each man received one hundred *mǔ*;
for medium land, each man received two hundred *mǔ*;
for inferior land, each man received three hundred *mǔ*.
They cultivated it annually,
from their own residence.
If a family had extra men,
they also received land according to their number, just like this.
Scholars, artisans, and merchants received land,
but five mouths were equivalent to one farmer's mouth.
There were both tribute (*fù*) and tax (*shuì*).
Tax referred to one-tenth of the public land yield and the income from commerce, crafts, and natural resources.
Tribute supplied chariots, horses, armor, weapons, and followers for service.
People received land at twenty years old
and returned it at sixty.
They had to plant a mixture of five grains,
to guard against drought and disaster.
No trees were allowed in the fields,
to prevent hindering the five grains.
Mulberry and paper mulberry trees were planted around dwellings,
vegetables were in garden beds,
melons, gourds, and fruits were planted along boundaries.
Chickens, dogs, and pigs were raised in their proper season.
Villages had *xù* (schools),
and districts had *xiáng* (schools).
The *xù* were to elucidate teachings,
and the *xiáng* were to practice rites.
According to the *Sīmǎ Fǎ*,
officials established armies of six divisions,
and the military system was based on the *jǐngtián* (well-field) system.
It stipulated that an area one *lǐ* square was a *jǐng*;
ten *jǐng* made a *tōng*;
ten *tōng* made a *chéng*;
a *chéng* was ten *lǐ* square.
Ten *chéng* made a *zhōng*;
ten *zhōng* made a *tóng*;
a *tóng* was one hundred *lǐ* square.
Ten *tóng* made a *fēng*;
ten *fēng* made a *jī*;
a *jī* was one thousand *lǐ* square.
Thus, four *jǐng* formed an *yì*;
four *yì* formed a *qiū*;
a *qiū* had sixteen *jǐng*,
one warhorse,
and three oxen.
Four *qiū* formed a *diàn*;
a *diàn* had sixty-four *jǐng*,
four warhorses,
one war chariot,
twelve oxen,
three armored soldiers,
and seventy-two infantrymen.
This was called the system of the chariot-unit.
One *tóng*, one hundred *lǐ* square,
covered ten thousand *jǐng* in total.
After deducting mountains, rivers, ravines, banks, city walls, settlements, gardens, parks, and roads, three thousand six hundred *jǐng*,
the fixed area for taxation was six thousand four hundred *jǐng*,
yielding four hundred warhorses
and one hundred war chariots.
This was the largest territory for a *qīng* or *dàfū*;
it was called a "household of one hundred chariots."
One *fēng*, three hundred sixty-six *lǐ* square,
covered one hundred thousand *jǐng* in total.
The fixed area for taxation was sixty-four thousand *jǐng*,
yielding four thousand warhorses
and one thousand war chariots.
This was considered the largest for a feudal lord;
it was called a "state of one thousand chariots."
The Son of Heaven's *jī* was one thousand *lǐ* square,
covering one million *jǐng* in total.
The fixed area for taxation was six hundred forty thousand *jǐng*,
yielding forty thousand warhorses
and ten thousand war chariots,
with seven hundred twenty thousand infantrymen.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven was called the "lord of ten thousand chariots."
Qín Shǐhuáng, having gained his ambition over all under Heaven,
investigated the failures of Zhōu,
and concluded that the discussions of private scholars,
the incessant warfare among the feudal lords,
and the mutual invasions by the Four Barbarians
had led to its weakening and usurpation.
Therefore, he abolished the Five Orders of nobility.
When the Hàn arose,
it was alarmed by Qín’s isolation and failure,
and thus partitioned territories and enfeoffed lands,
establishing two ranks of nobility.
More than one hundred meritorious ministers were enfeoffed as Hóu.
At that time, the common people suffered under Qín and Xiàng,
and the population was decimated.
A great Hóu commanded no more than ten thousand households,
while a small one had five or six hundred households.
However, the imperial princes and younger brothers were greatly honored,
and nine kingdoms were grandly established.
In antiquity, there was a division of land but no division of people.
If it was great, it spanned provinces and linked commanderies;
if small, it comprised over ten cities.
The difference in scale was based on the number of households,
and the extent of the enfeoffed territory was largely determined by distance.
The so-called division of people began with the Hàn dynasty.
From Yànmén eastward,
extending to Liáoyáng,
was Yàn and Dài.
South of Chángshān,
where Tàiháng turns left,
crossing the Hé and the Jì,
gradually reaching the sea,
was Qí and Zhào.
Where Gǔ and Sì flow together,
encompassing Guīméng,
was Liáng and Chǔ.
To the east, bordering the Jiāng and Hú,
reaching close to Kuàijī,
was Jīng and Wú.
To the north, bordering the Huái River,
largely comprising Lú and Héng,
was Huáinán.
On the sunny side of the Hàn River,
extending to Jiǔyí,
was Chángshā.
The feudal lords bordered each other,
encompassing the three borders,
and externally connected with the Hú and Yuè.
The Son of Heaven himself possessed the three Hé regions, Dōngjùn, Yǐngchuān, and Nányáng,
from Jiānglíng westward to Bāshǔ,
northward to Yúnzhōng,
and westward to Lǒngxī,
along with the Jīngshī Nèishǐ,
making a total of fifteen commanderies.
Emperor Wén adopted Jiǎ Shēng’s proposal to divide Qí and Zhào.
Emperor Jǐng used Cháo Cuò’s strategy to reduce Wú and Chǔ.
Emperor Wǔ implemented Zhǔ Fùyán’s policy,
issuing the Order of Grace Promotion,
allowing the feudal kings to divide their households and territories to enfeoff their sons and younger brothers.
Without actually dismissing or promoting,
the vassal states naturally fragmented.
From this time onward,
Qí was divided into seven,
Zhào into six,
Liáng into five,
and Huáinán into three.
The imperial princes who were initially enfeoffed as rulers of great states had no more than ten-plus cities.
Although Chángshā, Yàn, and Dài retained their old names,
they all lost their northern and southern borders.
From Emperors Wén and Jǐng, who allowed the people to rest,
to the second year of Yuánshǐ of Emperor Píng,
the number of households was 12,233,062,
and the population was 59,594,978.
Its territory measured 9,302 lì from east to west,
and 13,368 lì from north to south.
Generally, there was one Tíng for every ten lì,
and a Tíng had a chief.
Ten Tíng formed one Xiāng,
and a Xiāng had one Sānlǎo,
one Yǒuzhì Sèfū, and one Yóujiǎo.
A Xiàn generally measured one hundred lì square;
if the population was dense, it was reduced,
if sparse, it was expanded;
Xiāng and Tíng were likewise.
These were all Qín institutions.
Guāngwǔ Zhongxīng did not exceed the previous system.
As the King of Dōnghǎi, Qiáng, observed propriety in his conduct,
he was therefore generously given a large enfeoffment,
simultaneously enjoying Lǔ Jùn with twenty-nine counties.
The rest, described as favored grants,
were merely granted one commandery.
By the third year of Yǒngshòu of Emperor Huán,
there were 10,677,960 households,
and 56,486,856 people.
This was also an increase in population.
In the first year of Jiàn'ān of Emperor Xiàn,
Cáo Cāo was appointed Zhèn Dōng Jiāngjūn,
and enfeoffed as Fèitíng Hóu.
In the third year of Huángchū of Emperor Wén of Wèi,
a system was first established whereby the sons of enfeoffed kings were made Xiāng Gōng,
the sons of succeeding kings were Tíng Hóu,
and the sons of Gōng and Hóu were Tíng Bó.
In the first year of Zhāngwǔ of Liú Bèi,
he also enfeoffed various kings with commanderies and states,
sometimes adopting auspicious names from afar,
without inspecting the land's actual produce.
There were 200,000 households
and 900,000 people (males and females).
In the fifth year of Chìwū of Sūn Quán,
he also took auspicious names from the central states to enfeoff various kings.
There were 523,000 households
and 2,400,000 people (males and females).
When Emperor Wén of Jìn was the King of Jìn,
he ordered Péi Xiù and others to establish the system of Five Orders.
Only Fú, the Duke of Ānpíng Commandery, had an estate of ten thousand households,
with institutions like the Wèi kings.
For the rest, a Xiàn Gōng's estate had one thousand eight hundred households,
covering seventy-five lì;
a great state Hóu's estate had one thousand six hundred households,
covering seventy lì;
a secondary state Hóu's estate had one thousand four hundred households,
covering sixty-five lì;
a great state Bó's estate had one thousand two hundred households,
covering sixty lì;
a secondary state Bó's estate had one thousand households,
covering fifty-five lì;
a great state Zǐ's estate had eight hundred households,
covering fifty lì;
a secondary state Zǐ's estate had six hundred households,
covering forty-five lì;
a Nán's estate had four hundred households,
covering forty lì.
In the first year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Wǔ,
he enfeoffed the various kings with commanderies as states.
An estate of twenty thousand households constituted a great state,
with three armies (upper, middle, lower),
totaling five thousand soldiers;
an estate of ten thousand households constituted a secondary state,
with two armies (upper, lower),
totaling three thousand soldiers;
an estate of five thousand households constituted a small state,
with one army,
totaling one thousand five hundred soldiers.
The kings did not reside in their states,
but held office in the capital.
The system of Five Orders was abolished.
Gōng and Hóu with estates of ten thousand households or more were great states;
those with five thousand households or more were secondary states;
those with fewer than five thousand households were small states.
In the first year of Tàikāng,
after the pacification of Wú,
there were a total of 2,459,840 households,
and 16,163,863 people.
And the various states south of the Yangtze each shared one-third of the tribute.
When Emperor Yuán crossed the Yangtze,
in the first year of Tàixīng,
it was first stipulated that they should share one-ninth.
Sīzhōu.
According to the Yǔ Gòng, this was the land of Yùzhōu.
By the time of Emperor Wǔ of Hàn,
the Sīlì Xiàowèi was first established,
whose jurisdiction included the three Fǔ and the various Hé commanderies.
Its boundaries included the three commanderies of Jīngzhào, Féngyì, and Fúfēng from Yōngzhōu in the west;
the two commanderies of Hédōng and Hénèi from Jìzhōu in the north;
and the two commanderies of Hóngnóng and Hénán from Yùzhōu in the east,
making a total of seven commanderies.
Its status was superior to that of the Mù and Bó,
with a silver seal and a green ribbon.
When Guāngwǔ made Luòyáng his capital,
the Sīlì's jurisdiction was no different from that of the Former Hàn.
When the Wèi clan received the abdication,
they immediately made the Hàn palace their capital.
The Sīlì's jurisdiction included Hénán, Hédōng, Hénèi, Hóngnóng, and Píngyáng from Jìzhōu,
making a total of five commanderies,
and established Sīzhōu.
Jìn continued to reside in the Wèi capital,
then returned the three Fǔ to Yōngzhōu,
divided Hénán to establish Xíngyáng,
divided Jīngzhào from Yōngzhōu to establish Shàngluò,
abolished Dōngjùn to establish Dùnqiū,
and thus officially named it Sīzhōu,
with the Sīlì Xiàowèi governing it.
The Zhōu governed twelve commanderies,
one hundred counties,
and 475,700 households.

Towards the end of Huìdì's reign,
the entire territory of Yǎnzhōu was lost to Shí Lè.
Later, Shí Jìlóng changed Chénliú Jùn to Jiànchāng Jùn,
belonging to Luòzhōu.
At this time, the remaining populace crossed south,
and Yuándì established a provisional Yǎnzhōu,
residing in Jīngkǒu.
Míngdì appointed Xī Jiàn as Inspector,
residing in Guǎnglíng,
establishing Púyáng, Jìyīn, Gāopíng, Tàishān, and other commanderies.
Later it was renamed Nányǎnzhōu,
sometimes returning to the south of the river,
sometimes residing in Xūyí,
or in Shānyáng.
Later, land was first allocated to form its territory,
regularly residing in Guǎnglíng,
across the river from Jīngkǒu to the south.
In the fourth year of Xiánkāng (338 CE),
Chénliú Jùn was established within the borders of Běiqiáo.
Āndì divided the five counties of Jiànlíng, Línjiāng, Rúgāo, Nínghǎi, and Pútáo from Guǎnglíng Jùn to establish Shānyáng Jùn,
belonging to Nányǎnzhōu.
Yùzhōu.
According to the Yǔ Gòng, it was the land of Jīng and Hé.
The Zhōu Lǐ states:
"South of the Yellow River is Yùzhōu."
Yù means "to be at ease,"
implying that it received the qi of moderation and harmony,
and its nature and disposition were tranquil and at ease.
The Chūnqiū Yuán Mìng Bāo says:
"The star Gōujíng corresponds to Yùzhōu."
Its geographical boundaries stretched
from Huà Shān in the west,
east to the Huái River,
north from the Jì River,
and its southern boundary was Jīng Shān.
When Qín unified all under heaven,
it established the seven commanderies of Sānchuān, Hédōng, Nányáng, Yǐngchuān, Dàng, Sìshuǐ, and Xuē.
Hàn changed Sānchuān to Hénán Jùn,
and Wǔdì established thirteen provinces.
Yùzhōu retained its old name,
with Hénán and Hédōng commanderies belonging to Sīlì,
and Nányáng belonging to Jīngzhōu.
Before this,
Sìshuǐ was renamed Pèi Jùn,
Dàng Jùn was renamed Liáng,
Xuē was renamed Lǔ,
Rǔnán Jùn was established by dividing Liáng and Pèi,
and Huáiyáng Jùn was established by dividing Yǐngchuān.
Later, Hàn Zhāngdì renamed Huáiyáng to Chén Jùn.
Wèi Wǔ divided Pèi to establish Qiáo Jùn,
and Wèi Wén divided Rǔnán to establish Yìyáng Jùn.
When Wǔdì received the Mandate of Heaven,
he again divided Yǐngchuān to establish Xiāngchéng Jùn,
divided Rǔnán to establish Rǔyīn Jùn,
and combined Chén Jùn with Liáng Guó.
The province governed ten commanderies and kingdoms,
eighty-five counties,
with 116,796 households.

During the Disorder of Yǒngjiā,
Yù Zhōu fell into the hands of the Shí clan.
When Yuán Dì crossed the Yangtze River,
he established Xiāngchéng Jùn and Fánchāng Xiàn by relocating Chūngǔ Xiàn.
Chéng Dì then established Yù Zhōu by relocating it between the Yangtze River and the Huái River,

At that time, Huáinán was incorporated into the North,

Huáinán, Lújiāng, and Ānfēng were all subordinate to Yù Zhōu.

Xiàowǔ changed Qíchūn Xiàn to Qíyáng Xiàn,

which belonged to Nán Yù Zhōu.
Also, Jìnxī Jùn was established in the southern part of Hàn Lújiāng Jùn.
Jì Zhōu.
According to Yǔ Gòng and Zhōu Lǐ, it was all land within Hé'nèi.
Shùn established twelve mu,
and this was one of them.
The Chūnqiū Yuánmìng Bāo states:
"The constellation Mǎo Bì scattered to form Jì Zhōu,
which was divided into Zhào Guó."
Its land had both dangers and ease.
It was the capital of emperors and kings;
when there was disorder, Jì was peaceful;
when it was weak, Jì was strong;
when it was barren, Jì was abundant.
Because Jì Zhōu was broad from north to south,
Shùn divided the area west of Wèi to form Bìng Zhōu,
and the area north of Yān to form Yōu Zhōu.
The Zhōu people followed this.
When Hàn Wǔ Dì established thirteen prefectures,
this region was still called Jì Zhōu by its old name,
and it remained unchanged through the Later Hàn dynasty to the Jìn dynasty.
The prefecture administered thirteen commanderies and states,
eighty-three counties, [二四]
and three hundred twenty-six thousand households.

After Huì Dì,
Jì Zhōu fell to Shí Lè.
Shí Lè usurped the title in Xiāngguó in the second year of Tàixīng,
calling himself Zhào.
Later, he was overthrown by Mùróng Jùn,
and the Mùróng clan was in turn overthrown by Fú Jiān.
In the eighth year of Xiàowǔ's Tàiyuán era,
Fú Jiān was defeated,
and his territory fell to Mùróng Chuí.
Mùróng Chuí usurped the title in Zhōngshān,
which was known as Hòuyān.
Hòuyān was eventually destroyed by Wèi.
Yōu Zhōu.
According to Yǔ Gòng, it was within the domain of Jì Zhōu.

and this was one of them.

After Emperor Huì,
Yōuzhōu fell to Shí Lè.
Then, in the fifth year of Yǒnghé of Emperor Mù,
Mùróng Jùn usurped the title at Jì,
which was known as Former Yàn.
In the seventh year,
Jùn moved the capital to Yè.
After Jùn died,
his son Wěi was destroyed by Fú Jiān.
When Jiān was defeated,
the territory again fell to Mùróng Chuí,
which was known as Later Yàn.
After Chuí died,
Bǎo moved to Hélóng.
Píngzhōu.
According to Yǔ Gòng, this region was part of Jìzhōu,
and in the Zhōu dynasty, it was within Yōuzhōu.
In the Hàn dynasty, it belonged to the right Běipíng Commandery.
At the end of the Later Hàn,
Gōngsūn Dù styled himself Governor of Píngzhōu.
And his son Kāng, and Kāng’s son Wén Yì, all held Liáodōng independently,
and the nine types of Eastern Yí all submitted to them.
Wèi established the Eastern Yí Commandant,
residing at Xiāngpíng,
and divided the five commanderies of Liáodōng, Chānglí, Xuántú, Dàifāng, and Lèlàng to form Píngzhōu.
Later, it was reunited into Yōuzhōu.
After Wén Yì was destroyed,
there was a Protector of the Eastern Yí Commandant,
residing at Xiāngpíng.
In the tenth month of the second year of Xiánníng,
the five commanderies and kingdoms of Chānglí, Liáodōng, Xuántú, Dàifāng, and Lèlàng were separated to establish Píngzhōu.
It governed twenty-six counties,
with eighteen thousand one hundred households.

When Píngzhōu was first established,
Mùróng Huì was made its Inspector.
During the chaos of Yǒngjiā,
Huì was supported by the masses.
And his grandson Jùn moved the capital to Jì.
Later, Mùróng Chuí's son Bǎo again moved to Hélóng,
and the territory from Yōuzhōu to south of Lú Púzhèn fell to Wèi.
Mùróng Xī stationed the Inspector of Yōuzhōu at Lìzhī,
the Inspector of Qīngzhōu at Xīnchéng,
the Inspector of Bìngzhōu at Fánchéng,
the Inspector of Yíngzhōu at Sùjūn,
and the Inspector of Jìzhōu at Féirú.
Gāo Yún stationed the Governors of Yōu and Jì at Féirú,
and the Inspector of Bìngzhōu at Báiláng.
Later, he was usurped by Féng Bá.
Bá usurped the title at Hélóng,
which was known as Later Yàn,
and was finally destroyed by Wèi.
Bìngzhōu.
According to Yǔ Gòng, this was the territory of Jìzhōu.
Shùn established twelve Mu,
and this was one of them.
Zhōu Lǐ states: "The region due north is called Bìngzhōu,
and its guardian mountain is Shān."
Chūnqiū Yuánmìng Bāo says:
"The constellation Yíngshì flows into Bìngzhōu,
and is divided into the state of Wèi."
The zhōu was not named after the Wèi River,
nor was it named after a mountain,
but was called Bìng,
probably because it was located between two valleys.
Emperor Wǔ of Hàn established thirteen zhōu,
and Bìngzhōu retained its old name without change,
governing the ten commanderies of Shàngdǎng, Tàiyuán, Yúnzhōng, Shàngjùn, Yànmén, Dài, Dìngxiāng, Wǔyuán, Xīhé, and Shuòfāng.
A separate Shuòfāng Inspector was also established.
In the eleventh year of Jiànwǔ of the Later Hàn,
Shuòfāng was abolished and merged into Bìngzhōu.
At the end of Emperor Líng's reign,
the Qiāng and Hú caused great disturbances,
and the five commanderies of Dìngxiāng, Yúnzhōng, Wǔyuán, Shuòfāng, and Shàngjùn all dispersed through migration.
In the eighteenth year of Jiàn'ān,
it was abolished and merged into Jìzhōu.
In the twentieth year,
Xīnxīng Commandery was first established in the deserted land below the frontier.
Later, Lèpíng Commandery was again established by separating part of Shàngdǎng.
In the first year of Huángchū of Wèi,
Bìngzhōu was re-established.
The area north of Jǐng Líng was abandoned,
and Jìn continued this without change.
Bìngzhōu governed six commanderies and kingdoms,
forty-five counties,
with fifty-nine thousand three hundred households.
