Emperor Huì changed Xīnxīng to Jìnchāng Commandery.
In the first year of Yǒngxīng,
Liú Yuánhǎi usurped the title at Píngyáng,
proclaiming Hàn.
Thereupon, all of Bìngzhōu's territory became Yuánhǎi's.
Yuánhǎi then stationed the Inspector of Yōngzhōu at Píngyáng,
and the Inspector of Yōuzhōu at Líshí.
When Liú Cōng attacked and captured Luòyáng,
he established left and right Sīlì,
each governing over two hundred thousand households.
For every ten thousand households, an Nèishǐ was appointed.
In total, there were forty-three Nèishǐ.
The left and right advisors to the Chányú each oversaw six types of non-Hàn people.
He also established five zhōu: Yīn, Wèi, Dōngliáng, Xīhéyáng, and Běiyǎn,
to appease those newly annexed.
Liú Yào moved the capital to Cháng'ān,
and the territory east of Píngyáng fell to Shí Lè.
Lè pacified Shuòfāng,
and also established Shuòzhōu.
Between the reigns of Emperors Huì and Huái,
Líshí County became deserted.
Lè established Yǒngshí Commandery in its place,
and also separately established Wǔxiāng Commandery.
Under Fú Jiān, Yáo Xīng, and Hèlián Bóbó,
Bìngzhōu was moved and established in Hédōng.
Yáo Xīng also called Hédōng the two zhōu of Bìng and Jì.
Yōngzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng, it was the land of Hēishuǐ and Xīhé.
Shùn established twelve mu,
and it was one of them.
Due to its mountainous terrain
it was named Yōng.
It is also said that it was in the northwest position,
where the yang could not reach,
and the yin qi was blocked and obstructed.
〔二七〕The Rítuals of Zhōu state: "To the west is Yōngzhōu."
This likely included the land of Yǔ's Liángzhōu.
From the time King Wǔ of Zhōu conquered Yīn,
he made his capital at Fēnghào,
and Yōngzhōu became the royal domain.
When King Píng moved the capital eastward to Luòyì,
he granted the land of Qí and Fēng to Qín Xiānggōng,
thus it became Qín territory.
Qín established its capital there for generations,
until Shǐhuáng ultimately unified the Six States.
When Qín fell,
Hàn again made its capital there.
When Emperor Wǔ established thirteen zhōu,
its western part became Liángzhōu,
and the rest was all under Sīlì,
not being governed by a zhōu.
Later, when Emperor Guāngwǔ of Later Hàn made Luòyáng his capital,
Yōngzhōu was re-established in Guānzhōng.
Later it was abolished,
and Sīlìxiàowèi was re-established,
governing the Sānfǔ as before.
During Emperor Xiàn's time, Yōngzhōu was again established,
and from the Sānfǔ to the Western Regions, all belonged to it.
When Emperor Wén of Wèi ascended the throne,
he divided Héxī into Liángzhōu,
Lǒngyòu into Qínzhōu,
changed Jīngzhàoyǐn to Tàishǒu,
removed the "left" and "right" from Féngyì and Fúfēng respectively,
and still made the Sānfǔ subject to Sīlì.
In the early Jìn, Yōngzhōu was established in Cháng'ān,
governing seven jùn and guó,
thirty-nine xiàn,
and ninety-nine thousand five hundred households.

Governed nine xiàn,

When Emperor Huì ascended the throne,
he changed Fúfēngguó to Qínguó.
The capital was moved.
〔二九〕After Jiànxīng,
Yōngzhōu was lost to Liú Cōng.
When Liú Yào moved the capital to Cháng'ān,
he changed the dynastic title to Zhào,
and stationed the mu of Qín and Liáng zhōu at Shàngguī,
the mu of Shuòzhōu at Gāopíng,
the cǐshǐ of Yōuzhōu at Běidì,
and the mu of Bìngzhōu at Púbǎn.
When Shí Lè conquered Cháng'ān,
he re-established Yōngzhōu.
After the Shí clan was defeated,
Fú Jiàn usurped and occupied Guānzhōng,
and again made Cháng'ān his capital,
this was Former Qín.
Thereupon, a Sīlìxiàowèi was established in Yōngzhōu,
the cǐshǐ of Yùzhōu was stationed at Xǔchāng,
the cǐshǐ of Qínzhōu at Shàngguī,
the cǐshǐ of Jīngzhōu at Fēngyáng,
the cǐshǐ of Luòzhōu at Yíyáng,
and the cǐshǐ of Bìngzhōu at Púbǎn.
During Fú Jiān's time,
Sīlì was divided into Yōngzhōu,
Jīngzhào was divided into Xiányáng Commandery,
and the cǐshǐ of Luòzhōu was stationed at Shǎnchéng.
After the destruction of Yàn,
Yōuzhōu was divided to establish Píngzhōu,
stationed at Lóngchéng,
the cǐshǐ of Yōuzhōu was stationed at Jìchéng,
the cǐshǐ of Hézhōu at Páohǎn,
the cǐshǐ of Bìngzhōu at Jìnyáng,
the cǐshǐ of Yùzhōu at Luòyáng,
the cǐshǐ of Yǎnzhōu at Cāngyuán,
and the cǐshǐ of Yōngzhōu at Púbǎn.
Thereupon, Luòzhōu was moved to Fēngyáng,
Dōngyùzhōu was established at Xǔchāng,
the cǐshǐ of Jīngzhōu was stationed at Xiāngyáng,
and the cǐshǐ of Xúzhōu at Péngchéng.
Later, Yáo Cháng destroyed the Fú clan,
this was Later Qín.
When Cháng's son Xīng conquered Luòyáng,
he stationed the mu of Bìng and Jì zhōu at Púbǎn,
the mu of Yùzhōu at Luòyáng,
the cǐshǐ of Yǎnzhōu at Cāngyuán,
divided Sīlì to govern the five northern commanderies,
and established the cǐshǐ of Yōngzhōu at Āndìng.
When Yáo Hóng was destroyed by Liú Yù,
its territory soon fell to Hèlián Bóbó.
Bóbó usurped the title at Tǒngwàn,
this was Xià.
He established a Yōuzhōu mu at Dàchéng,
and also pacified Liú Yìzhēn at Cháng'ān,
sending his son Guī to govern it,
calling it Nántái.
He stationed the mu of Shuòzhōu at Sānchéng,
the cǐshǐ of Qínzhōu at Xìngchéng,
the cǐshǐ of Yōngzhōu at Yīnmì,
the cǐshǐ of Bìngzhōu at Púbǎn,
the mu of Liángzhōu at Āndìng,
the cǐshǐ of Běiqínzhōu at Wǔgōng,
and the mu of Yùzhōu at Lǐrùn.
〔三０〕The cǐshǐ of Jīngzhōu was stationed at Shǎn,
and the names of its zhōu and jùn are all unknown.
However, since Emperor Yuán crossed the Yangtze,
the zhōu he established were all remotely controlled.
Initially, Wèi Gāi was appointed cǐshǐ of Yōngzhōu,
stationed at Cuózéng,
which was soon abolished.
Shǐpíng Commandery was established as a temporary measure,
residing temporarily in Wǔdāngchéng.
When displaced people from Qínguó arrived in Jiāngnán,
Tángyì was renamed Qín Commandery,
and Wèishì County was temporarily established and belonged to it.
During Emperor Kāng's time,
Yǔ Yì was the cǐshǐ of Jīngzhōu,
and he moved his station to Xiāngyáng.
Thereafter, many displaced people from Qín and Yōng moved south to Fán and Miǎn,
and Emperor Xiàowǔ first established a temporary Yōngzhōu at Xiāngyáng,
and then established seven commanderies: Jīngzhào, Shǐpíng, Fúfēng, Hénán, Guǎngpíng, Yìchéng, and Běihénán,
all belonging to Xiāngyáng.
Xiāngyáng formerly belonged to Jīngzhōu.
Liángzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng, it was the western boundary of Yōngzhōu.
When the Zhōu declined,
its territory was occupied by the Dí.
When the Qín rose, the Měiyáng Gānquán Palace
was originally a place where the Xiōngnú cast gold figures to sacrifice to Heaven.
Since the Xiōngnú had lost Gānquán,
they also had Xiūtú and Húnyé Wáng and others reside in the land of Liángzhōu.
These two kings later surrendered their territory to the Hàn.
The Hàn established Zhāngyè, Jiǔquán, Dūnhuáng, and Wǔwēi Commanderies.
After that, Jīnchéng Commandery was also established,
and these were called the five commanderies of Héxī.
The Hàn renamed the Zhōu's Yōngzhōu as Liángzhōu,
probably because the land was located in the west,
and was often cold and cool.
The terrain extended obliquely to the northwest,
between the Southern Mountains.
To the south, it was separated by the Western Qiāng;
to the west, it connected to the Western Regions.
At that time, it was known as "severing the Xiōngnú's right arm."
During the reign of Xiàndì,
Liángzhōu frequently experienced unrest,
and the five commanderies of Héxī were far separated from the provincial capital.
Thus, it was separately designated as Yōngzhōu.
Later, based on ancient classics, the Nine Provinces were re-established,
and Guānyòu was merged to form Yōngzhōu.
During the Wèi dynasty, it was again divided to form Liángzhōu.
The Cìshǐ concurrently held the post of Wùjǐ Jiàowèi,
protecting the Western Regions,
following the Hàn precedent.
This remained unchanged until the Jìn dynasty.
It administered eight commanderies,
forty-six counties,
and thirty thousand seven hundred households.
Jīnchéng Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered five counties,
and two thousand households.)
Yúzhōng, Yǔnjiē, Jīnchéng, Báitǔ, Hàoqǐng.
Xīpíng Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered four counties,
and four thousand households.)
Xīdū, Línqiāng, Chángníng, Ānyí.
Wǔwēi Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered seven counties,
and five thousand nine hundred households.)
Gūzāng, Xuānwēi, Jícì, Cāngsōng, Xiǎnměi, Líqián, Fānhé.
Zhāngyè Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered three counties,
and three thousand seven hundred households.)
Yǒngpíng, Línzé (Hàn Zhāowǔ county,
renamed to avoid the taboo name of Wéndì.) [三一]
Wūlán (Hàn named it after Wūlán.)
Xī Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered five counties,

Rìlè, Shāndān, Xiāntí, Wànsuì, Lánchí (Also called Lánjuéchí.)

Administered nine counties,

Fúlù, Huìshuǐ, Ānmí, Xīngmǎ, Yuèguàn, Biǎoshì, Yánshòu, Yùmén, Shātóu.
Dūnhuáng Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered twelve counties,
and six thousand three hundred households.)
Chāngpú, Dūnhuáng, Lónglè, Yángguān, Xiàogǔ, Guǎngzhì, Yíhé, Míng'ān [三二], Shēnquán [三三], Yīwú, Xīnxiāng, Gānqí.
Xīhǎi Commandery (Originally belonged to Zhāngyè.
In the second year of Xīngpíng during the reign of Hàn Xiàndì,
Zhāng Yǎ, the Grand Administrator of Wǔwēi, requested its establishment.
Administered one county,
and two thousand five hundred households.)
Jūyán (The marsh is in the southeast,
what the Shàngshū called Liúshā.)
In the fifth year of Yuánkāng,
Huìdì divided the five counties of Yíhé, Yīwú, Míng'ān, Shēnquán, and Guǎngzhì from Dūnhuáng Commandery,
and Shātóu county from Jiǔquán.
He also separately established Huìjī and Xīnxiāng.
In total, eight counties formed Jìnchāng Commandery.
During the Yǒngníng era,
Zhāng Guǐ became the Cìshǐ of Liángzhōu.
Stationed in Wǔwēi,
he submitted a memorial requesting to gather the displaced people from Qín and Yōng in the northwest of Gūzāng,
and establish Wǔxīng Commandery,
administering counties such as Wǔxīng, Dàchéng, Wūzhī, Xiāngwǔ, Yànrán, Xīnzhàng, Píngdí, and Sījiān.
He also divided the territory of Xīpíng to establish Jìnxīng Commandery,
administering counties such as Jìnxīng, Bāohǎn, Yǒnggù, Línjīn, Línzhàng, Guǎngchāng, Dàxià, Suìxīng, Hǎntáng, and Zuǒnán.
At this time, the Central Plains were overrun,
and Yuándì moved to the south of the Jiāng.
Guǐ then seized and occupied Héxī,
proclaiming the legitimate reign of Jìn.
This was known as the Former Liáng.
When Zhāng Shí reigned,
he divided the two counties of Língjū and Zhīyáng from Jīnchéng,
and also established Yǒngdēng county.
These three counties combined formed Guǎngwǔ Commandery.
Zhāng Mào divided Wǔxīng, Jīnchéng, Xīpíng, and Āngù to establish Dìngzhōu.
Zhāng Jùn divided Wǔwēi, Wǔxīng, Xīpíng, Zhāngyè, Jiǔquán, Jiànkāng, Xīhǎi, Xī Commandery, Huánghé, Jìnxīng, and Guǎngwǔ—a total of eleven commanderies—to form Liángzhōu [三四].
Xīngjìn, Jīnchéng, Wǔshǐ, Nán'ān, Yǒngjìn, Dàxià, Wǔchéng, and Hánzhōng formed Hézhōu.
Dūnhuáng, Jìnchāng, Gāochāng, the Protectorate of the Western Regions, the Wùjǐ Jiàowèi, and the Grand Protector of Yùmén—three commanderies and three camps—formed Shāzhōu.
[三五]Zhāng Jùn was granted the title of Governor of Liángzhōu,
administering the three provinces.
Zhāng Zuò also renamed Dūnhuáng Commandery as Shāngzhōu.
During the Yǒngxīng era,
Hànyáng county was established to guard pastoral lands.
Zhāng Xuánjìng renamed it Qílián Commandery.
Zhāng Tiānxī also separately established Línsōng Commandery.
When Tiānxī surrendered to the Fú clan,
his territory was soon seized by Lǚ Guāng.
After Lǚ Guāng made Gūzāng his capital,
following Guō Nún's prophecy,
he renamed Chāngsōng as Dōngzhāngyè Commandery.
When Lǚ Lóng surrendered to Yáo Xīng,
his territory was divided into three.
Wǔzhāo Wáng established the Western Liáng,
proclaiming his reign in Dūnhuáng.
Tūfà Wūgū established the Southern Liáng,
proclaiming his reign in Yuèdū.
Júqú Méngxùn established the Northern Liáng,
proclaiming his reign in Zhāngyè.
They separately occupied the five commanderies of Héxī.
Qínzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng, it was originally part of Yōngzhōu.
The Wèi first divided Lǒngyòu to establish it.
The Cìshǐ concurrently held the post of Hùqiāng Jiàowèi.
It was temporarily abolished in the interim.
In the fifth year of Tàishǐ,
the five commanderies of Lǒngyòu from Yōngzhōu, and Jīnchéng from Liángzhōu, and Yīnpíng from Liángzhōu,
a total of seven commanderies, were merged to establish Qínzhōu,
with its seat in Jìchéng.
In the third year of Tàikāng,
Qínzhōu was abolished
and merged with Yōngzhōu.
In the seventh year,
it was re-established,
with its seat in Shàngguī.
It administered six commanderies,
twenty-four counties,
and thirty-two thousand one hundred households.
Lǒngxī Commandery (Established by Qín.
Administered four counties,
and three thousand households.)
Xiāngwǔ, Shǒuyáng (Bird-Rat Mountain is to the east.),
Líntáo, Díyù.
Nán'ān Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered three counties,
and four thousand three hundred households.)
Huándào, Xīnxīng, Zhōngtáo.
Tiānshuǐ Commandery (Established by Hàn Wǔdì.
Xiàomíng renamed it Hànyáng.
Jìn restored it to Tiānshuǐ. [三六]
Administered six counties,
and eight thousand five hundred households.)
Shàngguī, Jì (Former seat of Qínzhōu.),
Shǐchāng, Xīnyáng, Xiǎnchén (Hàn Xiǎnqīn county.),

Lüèyáng Commandery (Originally named Guǎngwèi.
Renamed during the Tàishǐ era.
Administered four counties,
and nine thousand three hundred twenty households.)
Línwèi, Píngxiāng, Lüèyáng, Qīngshuǐ.
Wǔdū Commandery (Established by Hàn.
Administered five counties,
and three thousand households.)
Xiàbiàn, Héchí, Jǔ, Wǔdū, Gùdào.
Yīnpíng Commandery (Established during the Tàishǐ era.
Administered two counties,
and three thousand households.)
Yīnpíng, Píngguǎng [三七].
Huìdì divided Díyù, Líntáo, and Héguān from Lǒngxī,
and also established six new counties: Táoyáng, Suípíng, Wǔjiē, Shǐxīng, Dìwǔ, and Zhēnchóu.
These nine counties combined formed Díyù Commandery,
belonging to Qínzhōu.
Zhāng Jùn made it belong to Liángzhōu,
and also established Wǔshǐ Commandery with Díyù county.
The Jìn court south of the Jiāng divided Liáng to form Qín,
temporarily residing in Liángzhōu, and also established Díchí as Northern Qínzhōu.
Liángzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng, it was the land of Huáyáng and Hēishuǐ.
Shùn established twelve mù,
and this was one of them.
As for Liáng,
it refers to the strong and unyielding (qiángliáng) nature of the metal element qì in the West,
hence the name.
The Zhōulǐ Zhífāngshì combined Liáng with Yōng.
The Hàn dynasty did not establish a zhōu name,
treating the area as Yìzhōu.

In the sixth year of Jiàn'ān (201 CE),
Liú Zhāng changed Yǒngníng to Bādōng Commandery,
and separated Diànjiāng from Bā Commandery to establish Bāxī Commandery.
When Liú Bèi occupied Shǔ,
he further divided four counties from Guǎnghàn: Jiāmēng, Fúchéng, Zītóng, and Báishuǐ,
renaming Jiāmēng as Hànshòu,
and also establishing Hàndé County,
to form Zītóng Commandery;
he detached Dàngqú, Xuānhàn, and Hànchāng counties from Bā Commandery to establish Dàngqú Commandery,
which was soon abolished,
and these counties were then assigned to Bāxī Commandery.
In the third year of Tàishǐ (267 CE),
Yìzhōu was divided,
and Liángzhōu was established in Hànzhōng.
Hànshòu was renamed Jìnshòu,
and Xīndū Commandery was also established from Guǎnghàn.

In the ninth month of the sixth year of Tàikāng (285 CE),
Xīndū Commandery was abolished and merged into Guǎnghàn Commandery.
Huìdì again divided Bāxī to establish Dàngqú Commandery,
administering Dàngqú, Hànchāng, and Xuānhàn three counties,
and also assigned Xīnchéng, Wèixīng, and Shàngyōng, a total of four commanderies, to Liángzhōu.
Soon after, the commanderies and counties of Liángzhōu were lost to Lǐ Tè.
During the Yǒngjiā period, it was again divided and belonged to Yáng Màosōu.
The Jìn people who had migrated to Liáng and Yì
then established Nán Yīnpíng and Běi Yīnpíng commanderies in these two zhōus.
After Huán Wēn pacified Shǔ,
Jìnchāng Commandery was established for the displaced people of Bā and Hàn,
governing ten counties: Chánglè, Ānjìn, Yánshòu, Ānlè, Xuānhàn, Níngdū, Xīnxīng, Jíyáng, Dōngguān, and Yǒng'ān;
Yìchāng and Jìnxīng two counties were also established,
belonging to Bāxī Commandery;
Suìníng Commandery was established southeast of Déyáng's border;
and Jiàngé County was established in Jìnshòu,
belonging to Liángzhōu.
Later, Xiàowǔdi divided the northern border of Zītóng to establish Jìnshòu Commandery,
administering Jìnshòu, Báishuǐ, Shàohuān, and Xīng'ān four counties;
Zītóng Commandery was moved to Zītóng,
and Jiàngé County was abolished;
Nán Hànzhōng Commandery was also separately established,
and Jīnshān Commandery was formed by dividing Bāxī and Zītóng.
During Āndì's time,
Xīnbā and Wènyáng two commanderies were again established,
and there were also Běi Xīnbā, Huáyáng, Nán Yīnpíng, and Běi Yīnpíng four commanderies.
Later, Bāqú, Huái'ān, Sòngxī, Báishuǐ, Shàngluò, Běi Shàngluò, Nán Dàngqú, Huáihàn, Xīnxīng, and Ānkāng ten commanderies were also established.
Yìzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng and Shùn's twelve mù, this entire region was within Liángzhōu.
The Zhōu dynasty merged Liáng into Yōng,
thus it was also part of Yōngzhōu.
The Chūnqiū Yuánmìng Bāo says:
"Cānfá flows into Yìzhōu,
and the word Yì means 'difficult' or 'narrow'."
This refers to the rugged and difficult terrain of the area,
also, it is said that the territory was expanded (jiāngrǎng yì dà),
hence the name.
When Qín Huìwáng first conquered Shǔ,
he established a commandery
and appointed Zhāng Ruò as the Administrator of Shǔ.
When Shǐhuáng established thirty-six commanderies,
the name Shǔ Commandery remained unchanged.
In the early Hàn, there were Hànzhōng, Bā, and Shǔ.
In the sixth year of Gāozǔ (201 BCE),
Guǎnghàn was established by dividing Shǔ,
making a total of four commanderies.
Wǔdì opened up the Southwest Barbarians,
and further established Jiànwéi, Zāngkē, Yuèxī, and Yìzhōu four commanderies,
making a total of eight commanderies,
and then established Yìzhōu to govern them,
Yìzhōu likely began at this point.
During the Later Hàn,
Míngdì established Yǒngchāng Commandery for the newly submitted territories.
Āndì also established three commandery-dependent commanderies for various routes: Shǔ, Guǎnghàn, and Jiànwéi.
Língdì then established Wénshān Commandery from Wénjiāng, Cánlíng, and Guǎngrǒu three counties.
In the first year of Chūpíng, in the reign of Xiàndì (190 CE),
Liú Zhāng established Yǒngníng Commandery by dividing Bā Commandery.
Yǒngníng was renamed Bādōng,
Bā Commandery was renamed Bāxī,
and Fúlíng Commandery was also established.
In the twenty-first year (216 CE),
Liú Bèi established Gùlíng Commandery by dividing Bā Commandery.
In the first year of Zhāngwǔ of Shǔ (221 CE), Gùlíng was again renamed Bādōng Commandery,
Bāxī Commandery was renamed Bā Commandery,
Zītóng Commandery was established by dividing Guǎnghàn,
Jiāngyáng Commandery was established by dividing Jiànwéi,
Shǔ Commandery's dependent commandery was renamed Hànjiā Commandery,
and Jiànwéi's dependent commandery was renamed Zhūtí Commandery.
In the second year of Jiànxīng, in the reign of Liú Shàn (224 CE),
Yìzhōu Commandery was renamed Jiànníng Commandery,
Guǎnghàn dependent commandery was renamed Yīnpíng Commandery,
Yúnnán Commandery was established by dividing Jiànníng and Yǒngchāng,
Xīnggǔ Commandery was established by dividing Jiànníng and Zāngkē,
and Dōng Guǎnghàn Commandery was established by dividing Guǎnghàn.
During the Jǐngyuán era of Wèi (260-264 CE),
Shǔ was pacified,
and Dōng Guǎnghàn Commandery was abolished.
In the second year of Tàishǐ, in the reign of Wǔdì (266 CE),
Yìzhōu was divided to establish Liángzhōu,
with Hànzhōng belonging to it.
In the seventh year (271 CE),
Yìzhōu was again divided to establish Níngzhōu.
Yìzhōu administered eight commanderies,
forty-four counties,
and one hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred households.

After Huìdì,
Lǐ Tè usurped the title in Shǔ,
calling himself Hàn,
and the commanderies and counties of Yìzhōu were all lost to Tè.
Lǐ Xióng also established Shěnlí and Hànyuán two commanderies by dividing Hànjiā and Shǔ two commanderies.
At this time, although the commanderies and counties of Yìzhōu were lost to the Lǐ clan,
the government east of the Jiāng River still nominally controlled them.
When Huán Wēn destroyed Shǔ,
its territory again belonged to Jìn.
Hànyuán and Shěnlí were abolished, and Nán Yīnpíng, Jìnyuán, Níngshǔ, and Shǐníng four commanderies were established.
In the second year of Xián'ān (372 CE),
Yìzhōu was again lost to the Fú clan.
In the eighth year of Tàiyuán (383 CE),
it again belonged to Jìn.
In the second year of Lóng'ān (398 CE), Jìnxī, Suìníng, and Jìnníng three commanderies were also established.
Níngzhōu.
During the Hàn and Wèi dynasties, it was part of Yìzhōu.
In the seventh year of Tàishǐ (271 CE),
Emperor Wǔ, seeing that Yìzhōu was vast,
divided Jiànníng, Xīnggǔ, Yúnnán from Yìzhōu, and Yǒngchāng from Jiāozhōu,
combining these four commanderies to form Níngzhōu.
It administered forty-five counties,
with eighty-three thousand households.
Yúnnán Commandery (established by Shǔ.
Administered nine counties,
with nine thousand two hundred households.) Yúnpíng, Yúnnán, Lóngdòng, Qīnglíng, Gūfù, Xiélóng, Yèyú, Suìjiǔ, Yǒngníng.
Xīnggǔ Commandery (established by Shǔ.
Administered eleven counties,
with six thousand two hundred households.) Lǜgāo, Gōudīng, Wǎnwēn, Lòuwò, Wúdúo
Jiànníng Commandery (established by Shǔ.
Administered seventeen counties,
with twenty-nine thousand households.) Wèi, Kūnzhé, Cúnmiè, Xīndìng, Tán, Mǔdān, Tónglài, Lòujiāng, Mùmá, Gǔchāng, Liánrán, Qínzàng, Shuāngbó, Yúyuán, Xiūyún, Língqiū, Diānchí.
Yǒngchāng Commandery (established by Hàn.
Administered eight counties,
with thirty-eight thousand households.) Bùwéi, Yǒngshòu, Bǐsū, Yōngxiāng, Nánfú, Xītáng, Āiláo, Bónán.
In the third year of Tàikāng (282 CE),
Emperor Wǔ again abolished Níngzhōu and incorporated it into Yìzhōu,
establishing the Southern Yi Commandant to protect it.
In the second year of Tài'ān (303 CE),
Emperor Huì re-established Níngzhōu,
and also separated seven counties west of Jiànníng to form Yìzhōu Commandery.
In the second year of Yǒngjiā (308 CE),
Yìzhōu Commandery was renamed Jìnníng.
From Zāngkē, Píngyí and Yèláng commanderies were established.
Later, Lǐ Shòu separated Xīnggǔ, Yǒngchāng, Yúnnán, Zhūtí, Yuèxī, and Héyáng, six commanderies from Níngzhōu, to form Hánzhōu.
In the fourth year of Xiánkāng (338 CE),
Zāngkē, Yèláng, Zhūtí, and Yuèxī, four commanderies, were separated to establish Ānzhōu.
Eight years later,
Níngzhōu was again abolished and merged,
with Yuèxī returned to Yìzhōu,
and Yǒngchāng Commandery was abolished.

Xúzhōu Cìshǐ garrison Jǔchéng,
Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ garrison Dōnglái,

Xúzhōu.

It is perhaps derived from the meaning of "leisurely and gentle,"

In the tenth year of Tàikāng,
the four counties of Jǔ, Gūmù, Zhū, and Dōngwǔ from Qīngzhōu's Chéngyáng Jùn were subordinated to Dōngguǎn.
In the first year of Yuánkāng,
Lánlíng Jùn was established by partitioning Dōnghǎi.
In the seventh year,
Dōng'ān Jùn was again established by partitioning Dōngguǎn,
Huáilíng Jùn by partitioning Línhuái,
and Tángyì Jùn was established from Tángyì.
During the chaos of Yǒngjiā,
Línhuái and Huáilíng were both lost to the Shí clan.
After Emperor Yuán crossed the Jiāng (Yangzi River),
Xúzhōu retained only half its territory,
so four commanderies were temporarily established: Huáiyáng, Yángpíng, Jìyīn, and Běijìyīn.
Furthermore, for the people of Lángyá Guó who followed the Emperor across the river,
Huáidé Xiàn and Lángyá Jùn were established to administer them.
At that time,
the displaced people from Yōu, Jì, Qīng, Bìng, Yǎn five provinces and the region north of the Huái River in Xúzhōu, led by their chiefs, crossed the Jiāng and Huái Rivers.
The Emperor established temporary commanderies and counties to govern them.
The northern border of Hǎiyú in Wú Jùn was partitioned,
and seven counties—Tán, Qú, Lìchéng, Zhùqí, Hòuqīu, Xīxí, and Xiāngbēn—were established,
temporarily residing in Qǔ'ā.
Nán Dōnghǎi, Nán Lángyá, Nán Dōngpíng, Nán Lánlíng, and other commanderies were established using Jiāngchéng.
Línhuái, Huáilíng, Nán Péngchéng, and other commanderies were established by partitioning Wǔjìn,
subordinated to Nán Xúzhōu.
Dùnqīu Jùn was also established, subordinated to Běi Xúzhōu.
Emperor Míng also established Nán Pèi, Nán Qīnghé, Nán Xiàpī, Nán Dōngguǎn, Nán Píngchāng, Nán Jìyīn, Nán Púyáng, Nán Tàipíng,
Nán Tàishān, Nán Jìyáng, Nán Lǔ, and other commanderies,
subordinating them to Xú and Yǎn two provinces.
Initially, some resided south of the Jiāng,
some north of the Jiāng,
and some considered Yǎnzhōu as the governing province.
Xī Jiàn was the Grand Governor of all military affairs in Qīng and Yǎn two provinces and the Inspector of Yǎnzhōu,
and was additionally appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu,
stationed in Guǎnglíng.
After Sū Jùn was pacified,
he returned from Guǎnglíng to garrison Jīngkǒu.
Zhōnglí Jùn was also established within the former Jiǔjiāng Jùn of Hàn,
subordinated to Nán Xúzhōu.
North of the Jiāng, Yōu, Jì, Qīng, Bìng four provinces were also temporarily established.
During the reign of Emperor Mù,
the seven counties of Nán Dōnghǎi were moved out to reside in Jīngkǒu.
In the seventh year of Yìxī,
the region north of the Huái River was first divided into Běi Xúzhōu,
while the region south of the Huái remained simply Xúzhōu.
It governed eleven commanderies: Péngchéng, Pèi, Xiàpī, Lánlíng, Dōngguǎn, Dōng'ān, Lángyá, Huáiyáng, Yángpíng, Jìyīn, and Běijìyīn.
Xūyí Jùn was established from Xūyí,
governing three counties: Kǎochéng, Zhídú, and Yángchéng.
Hǎilíng and Shānyáng two commanderies were also established by partitioning the territory of Guǎnglíng.
Later, Yōu and Jì were combined with Xúzhōu,
and Qīng and Bìng were combined with Yǎnzhōu.
Jīngzhōu.
According to the Tribute of Yǔ, Jīng and the land of Héngyáng,
when Shùn established twelve mu,
this was one of them.
The Rítuals of Zhōu states:
"The due south is called Jīngzhōu."
The Chūnqiū Yuánmìng Bāo says:
"The constellation Zhěn disperses to form Jīngzhōu."
Jīng
means strong,
referring to its impetuous and strong qi.
It also means to be alert,
referring to the frequent banditry of the Southern Mán barbarians;
their people, if there is dao, submit later,
if there is no dao, they become strong first,
so constant vigilance is necessary.
It is also said to be named after Jīngshān.
During the Warring States period,
this land belonged to Chǔ.
When Qín took Yān Yǐng of Chǔ to form Nán Jùn,
and also took the land of Wūzhōng to form Qiánzhōng Jùn,
and established Nányáng Jùn north of the Hàn River in Chǔ.
After the destruction of Chǔ,
Qiánzhōng was partitioned to form Chángshā Jùn.
Hàn Gāozǔ partitioned Chángshā to form Guìyáng Jùn,
renamed Qiánzhōng to Wǔlíng Jùn,
and partitioned Nán Jùn to form Jiāngxià Jùn.
Emperor Wǔ again partitioned Chángshā to form Línglíng Jùn.
When the thirteen provinces were established,
it was named Jīngzhōu after the old name,
governing seven commanderies: Nán Jùn, Nányáng, Línglíng, Guìyáng, Wǔlíng, Chángshā, and Jiāngxià.
Later, in the thirteenth year of Jiàn'ān,
during Emperor Xiàn's reign of the Later Hàn,
Wèi Wǔ obtained all the land of Jīngzhōu.
He partitioned the area north of Nán Jùn to establish Xiāngyáng Jùn,
again partitioned the western border of Nányáng to establish Nánxiāng Jùn,
and partitioned the area west of Zhījiāng to establish Línjiāng Jùn.
After his defeat at Chìbì,
the area south of Nán Jùn belonged to Wú.
Wú then divided Jīngzhōu with Shǔ.
Thus, Nán Jùn, Línglíng, and Wǔlíng to the west belonged to Shǔ,
Jiāngxià, Guìyáng, and Chángshā three commanderies belonged to Wú,
and Nányáng, Xiāngyáng, and Nánxiāng three commanderies belonged to Wèi.
The name Jīngzhōu
was then established doubly, north and south.
Shǔ partitioned Nán Jùn
to establish Yídū Jùn.
After Liú Bèi's death,
the territories of Yídū, Wǔlíng, Línglíng, and Nán Jùn four commanderies all reverted to Wú.
Emperor Wén of Wèi established Wèixīng and Xīnchéng two commanderies from the remnants of Hànzhōng.
Emperor Míng partitioned Xīnchéng to establish Shàngyōng Jùn.
Sūn Quán partitioned Jiāngxià to establish Wǔchāng Jùn,
and again partitioned Cāngwú to establish Línhé Jùn,
and partitioned Chángshā to establish Héngyáng and Xiāngdōng two commanderies.
Sūn Xiū partitioned Wǔlíng to establish Tiānmén Jùn,
and partitioned Yídū to establish Jiànpíng Jùn.
Sūn Hào partitioned Línglíng to establish Shǐ'ān Jùn,
and partitioned Guìyáng to establish Shǐxīng Jùn,
and again partitioned Línglíng to establish Shàolíng Jùn,
and partitioned Chángshā to establish Ānchéng Jùn.
Jīngzhōu governed fifteen commanderies: Nán Jùn, Wǔchāng, Wǔlíng, Yídū, Jiànpíng, Tiānmén, Chángshā, Línglíng, Guìyáng, Héngyáng, Xiāngdōng, Shàolíng, Línhé, Shǐxīng, and Shǐ'ān.
Nányáng, Jiāngxià, Xiāngyáng, Nánxiāng, Wèixīng, Xīnchéng, and Shàngyōng seven commanderies belonged to Wèi's Jīngzhōu.
When Emperor Wǔ pacified Wú,
he partitioned Nán Jùn to form Nánpíng Jùn,

Xiāngzhōu
Yángzhōu.
According to the Yǔ Gòng, this was the land between the Huái River and the sea.
When Shùn established the twelve Mù,
this was one of them.
The Zhōu Lǐ states:
"The southeast is called Yángzhōu."
The Chūnqiū Yuánmìng Bāo states:
"Qiānniú (the Ox constellation) flowing forms Yángzhōu,
which is divided into Yuègúo."
It is believed that the temperament of the land south of the Yangtze River is vigorous and forceful,
and its nature is light and uplifted (yáng).
It is also said
that the region has many waterways,
and the water waves rise (yáng).
In ancient times, it was a country of the wilderness domain.
During the Warring States period, its territory was divided by Chǔ.
When Qín Shǐhuáng united all under heaven,
he established the three commanderies of Zhāng, Kuàijī, and Jiǔjiāng there.
Xiàng Yǔ enfeoffed Yīng Bù as the King of Jiǔjiāng,
who possessed all its land.
The Hàn dynasty renamed Jiǔjiāng to Huáinán,
and then enfeoffed Bù as the King of Huáinán.
Six years later,
Yùzhāng Commandery was established by partitioning Huáinán.
Eleven years later,
after Bù was executed,
Imperial Prince Cháng was established as the King of Huáinán,
and Liú Bì was enfeoffed as the King of Wú,
and these two kingdoms acquired all the land of Yángzhōu.
In the sixteenth year of Emperor Wén,
Lújiāng and Héngshān Commanderies were established by partitioning Huáinán.
In the fourth year of Emperor Jǐng,
Imperial Prince Fēi was enfeoffed as the King of Jiāngdū,
and also received Zhāng and Kuàijī Commanderies,
but not Yùzhāng.
Emperor Wǔ renamed Jiāngdū to Guǎnglíng,
enfeoffed Imperial Prince Xū as king, and assigned it to Xúzhōu.
In the second year of Yuánfēng,
Zhāng was renamed Dānyáng,
and Huáinán was renamed Jiǔjiāng again.
Later, Emperor Shùn of Hàn partitioned Kuàijī to establish Wú Commandery.
Yángzhōu administered the six commanderies of Kuàijī, Dānyáng, Wú, Yùzhāng, Jiǔjiāng, and Lújiāng,
and Liù'ān was abolished and merged into Lújiāng Commandery.
In the Xīngpíng era of Emperor Xiàn,
Sūn Cè partitioned Yùzhāng to establish Lúlín Commandery.
Sūn Qúan further partitioned Yùzhāng to establish Póyáng Commandery,
and partitioned Dānyáng to establish Xīndū Commandery.
Sūn Liàng also partitioned Yùzhāng to establish Línchuān Commandery,
and partitioned Kuàijī to establish Línhǎi Commandery.
Sūn Xiū also partitioned Kuàijī to establish Jiàn'ān Commandery.
Sūn Hào partitioned Kuàijī to establish Dōngyáng Commandery,
partitioned Wú to establish Wúxìng Commandery,
partitioned Yùzhāng, Lúlín, and Chángshā to establish Ānchéng Commandery,
and partitioned Lúlín to establish Lúlín Nánbù Dūwèi.
〔一八〕Yángzhōu administered fourteen commanderies: Dānyáng, Wú, Kuàijī, Wúxìng, Xīndū, Dōngyáng, Línhǎi, Jiàn'ān, Yùzhāng, Póyáng, Línchuān, Ānchéng, and Lúlín Nánbù.
The land of Lújiāng and Jiǔjiāng west of the river, from north of Héféi to Shòuchūn, all belonged to Wèi.
When Jìn pacified Wú,
Ānchéng was assigned to Jīngzhōu.
From Dānyáng, the eleven counties of Xuānchéng, Wǎnlíng, Língyáng, Ānwú, Jīng, Guǎngdé, Níngguó, Huái'ān, Shíchéng, Línchéng, and Chūngǔ were partitioned to establish Xuānchéng Commandery,
with its seat in Wǎnlíng.
Xīndū was renamed Xīn'ān Commandery,
Lúlín Nánbù was renamed Nánkāng Commandery,
Jiàn'ān was partitioned to establish Jìn'ān Commandery,
and Dānyáng was further partitioned to establish Pílíng Commandery.
Yángzhōu altogether administered eighteen commanderies,
one hundred seventy-three counties,
and three hundred eleven thousand four hundred households.

In the first year of Yuánkāng [元康], during the reign of Emperor Huì [惠帝],
the responsible officials submitted a memorial, stating that
the territories of Jīngzhōu [荊州] and Yángzhōu [揚州] were vast and distant,
making administration particularly difficult.
Therefore, Yúzhāng [豫章], Póyáng [鄱陽], Lúlíng [廬陵], Línchuān [臨川], Nánkāng [南康], Jiàn'ān [建安], and Jìn'ān [晉安] from Yángzhōu [揚州],
and Wǔchāng [武昌], Guìyáng [桂陽], and Ānchéng [安成] from Jīngzhōu [荊州] were detached.
These ten commanderies were combined,
and named Jiāngzhōu [江州], after the name of the Jiāngshǔi [江水] (Yangzi River).
In the first year of Yǒngxīng [永興],
Xúnyáng [尋陽] from Lújiāng [廬江] and Cháisāng [柴桑] from Wǔchāng [武昌] were separated to establish Xúnyáng Jùn [尋陽郡],
which was attached to Jiāngzhōu [江州]. Wūjiāng [烏江] and Lìyáng [歷陽] from Huáinán [淮南] were separated to establish Lìyáng Jùn [歷陽郡].
Also, because Zhōu Qǐ [周玘] initiated a righteous uprising to suppress Shí Bīng [石冰],

Yángxiàn [陽羨] from Wúxīng [吳興], along with the northern rural areas of Chángchéng Xiàn [長城縣], were detached to establish Yìxiāng [義鄉], Guóshān [國山], Línjīn [臨津], and Yángxiàn [陽羨], a total of four counties.
Furthermore, Yǒngshì [永世] from Dānyáng [丹楊] was separated to establish Pínglíng [平陵] and Yǒngshì [永世],
making a total of six counties.
Yìxīng Jùn [義興郡] was established
to commemorate Qǐ's [玘] achievements,
and all were attached to Yángzhōu [揚州].
Furthermore, since Pílíng Jùn [毗陵郡] was enfeoffed to Pí [毗], the heir apparent of the King of Dōnghǎi [東海王世子],
to avoid the taboo of Pí's [毗] name,
it was renamed Jìnlíng [晉陵].
In the first year of Yǒngjiā [永嘉], during the reign of Emperor Huái [懷帝],
Péngzé Xiàn [彭澤縣] from Yúzhāng [豫章] was attached to Xúnyáng Jùn [尋陽郡].
When Emperor Mǐn [愍帝] ascended the throne,
to avoid his given name, Jiànyè [建鄴] was renamed Jiànkāng [建康].
When Emperor Yuán [元帝] crossed the Yangtze River,
he established the capital in Yángzhōu [揚州],
and the Grand Administrator of Dānyáng [丹楊 Tàishǒu] was changed to Yǐn [尹].
Jiāngzhōu [江州] also established Xīncài Jùn [新蔡郡].
Xúnyáng Jùn [尋陽郡] also established Jiǔjiāng [九江] and Shàngjiǎ [上甲] counties.
Soon after, Jiǔjiāng Xiàn [九江縣] was abolished and merged into Xúnyáng [尋陽].
At this time, Sīzhōu [司州], Jìzhōu [冀州], Yǒngzhōu [雍州], Liángzhōu [涼州], Qīngzhōu [青州], Bìngzhōu [并州], YǎNzhōu [兗州], Yùzhōu [豫州], Yōuzhōu [幽州], and Píngzhōu [平州] had all fallen.
The territory south of the Yangtze River only included Yángzhōu [揚州], Jīngzhōu [荊州], Xiāngzhōu [湘州], Jiāngzhōu [江州], Liángzhōu [梁州], Yìzhōu [益州], Jiāozhōu [交州], and Guǎngzhōu [廣州].
Of Xúzhōu [徐州], more than half was retained,
while Yùzhōu [豫州] only had Qiáochéng [譙城].
In the first year of Tàiníng [太寧], during the reign of Emperor Míng [明帝],
Yǒngjiā Jùn [永嘉郡] was established from Línhǎi [臨海],
administering four counties: Yǒngníng [永寧], Āngù [安固], Sōngyáng [松陽], and Héngyáng [橫陽].
Yángzhōu [揚州] then administered eleven commanderies: Dānyáng [丹楊], Wújùn [吳郡], Wúxīng [吳興], Xīn'ān [新安], Dōngyáng [東陽], Línhǎi [臨海], Yǒngjiā [永嘉], Xuānchéng [宣城], Yìxīng [義興], and Jìnlíng [晉陵].
[二二]
Since the chaos and disunion in the Central Plains,
the remaining populace moved south.
Provisional administrative offices were established in Guǎnglǐng [廣陵] and
Dāntú [丹徒], which was not the original territory.
When the Hú [胡] invaders encroached south,
all the people of Huáinán [淮南] crossed the Yangtze River.
In the early years of Emperor Chéng [成帝],
Sū Jùn [蘇峻] and Zǔ Yuē [祖約] caused turmoil in the Jiānghuái [江淮] region.
The Hú [胡] invaders then arrived in great numbers,
and even more people moved south.
Therefore, provisional Huáinán Jùn [淮南郡] and various counties were established south of the Yangtze River.
Also, provisional Sōngzī Jùn [松滋郡] was established in Xúnyáng [尋陽],
nominally under Yángzhōu [揚州].
In the fourth year of Xiánkāng [咸康],
provisional Wèijùn [魏郡], Guǎngchuān [廣川], Gāoyáng [高陽], Tángyì [堂邑], and other commanderies were established,
along with their subordinate counties, all residing in the capital region (Jīngyì [京邑]).
Língyáng [陵陽] was renamed Guǎngyáng [廣陽].
In the second year of Níngkāng [寧康], during the reign of Emperor Xiàowǔ [孝武],
Lèchéng Xiàn [樂成縣] was established from Yǒngníng Xiàn [永寧縣] of Yǒngjiā Jùn [永嘉郡].
At this time, the people of Shàngdǎng [上黨] moved south,
and provisional Shàngdǎng Jùn [上黨郡] was established with four counties,
residing in Wúhú [蕪湖].
Soon after, Shàngdǎng Jùn [上黨郡] was reduced to a county.
Xiāngchéng Jùn [襄城郡] was also abolished and became Fánchāng Xiàn [繁昌縣],
both attached to Huáinán [淮南].
In the eighth year of Yìxī [義熙], during the reign of Emperor Ān [安帝],
Xúnyáng Xiàn [尋陽縣] was abolished and merged into Cháisāng Xiàn [柴桑縣].
Cháisāng [柴桑] remained a commandery.
Later, Shàngjiǎ Xiàn [上甲縣] was abolished and merged into Péngzé Xiàn [彭澤縣].
Formerly, Jiāngzhōu [江州] supervised Jìnglíng Jùn [竟陵郡] of Jīngzhōu [荊州].
When Hé Wújí [何無忌] became the Cìshǐ [刺史],
he memorialized that Jìnglíng [竟陵] was far from the provincial capital,
three hundred *lǐ* [里] from Jiānglíng [江陵].
The households of Suí'ān Jùn [綏安郡], established by Jīngzhōu [荊州], were entering its territory,
and he wished to use this commandery to assist in the defense of the riverbanks.
He returned Jìnglíng Jùn [竟陵郡] to Jīngzhōu [荊州].
Furthermore, Hóngnóng [弘農] of Sīzhōu [司州] and Sōngzī [松滋] of Yángzhōu [揚zhou], two commanderies, were provisionally located in Xúnyáng [尋陽],
with mixed populations,
and both should be subject to supervision.
Emperor Ān [安帝] agreed.
Later, Sōngzī Jùn [松滋郡] was abolished and became Sōngzī Xiàn [松滋縣],
and Hóngnóng Jùn [弘農郡] became Hóngnóng Xiàn [弘農縣],
both attached to Xúnyáng Jùn [尋陽郡].
Jiāozhōu [交州].
According to Yǔgòng [禹貢], this area was part of Yángzhōu [揚州],
which was the land of Nányuè [南越].
After Qín Shǐhuáng [秦始皇] conquered and pacified Yángyuè [揚越],
he sent 500,000 convict soldiers to guard the Wǔlǐng [五嶺].
From north to south,
the path into Yuè [越] necessarily passed through the mountain ridges (Lǐngjiào [嶺嶠]).
At that time, there were five such places,
hence the name Wǔlǐng [五嶺].
Later, he sent Rèn Xiāo [任囂] and Zhào Tuò [趙佗] to attack Yuè [越],
conquering the land of Lùliáng [陸梁].
Thus, Nányuè [南越] was pacified,
and it was made into three commanderies: Guìlín [桂林], Nánhǎi [南海], and Xiàng [象].
These were not within the limit of thirty-six commanderies,
so a Nánhǎi Wèi [南海尉] was appointed to govern them,
which was known as the single *wèi* [尉] of the southeast.
In the early Hàn [漢] dynasty,
the three commanderies of Lǐngnán [嶺南], along with Chángshā [長沙] and Yúzhāng [豫章], were enfeoffed to Wú Ruì [吳芮] as the King of Chángshā [長沙王].
In the eleventh year,
Nánwǔ Hóu [南武侯] Zhī [織] was enfeoffed as the King of Nánhǎi [南海王].
When Lù Jiǎ [陸賈] returned from his mission,
he appointed Zhào Tuò [趙佗] as the King of Nányuè [南越王],
and the three southern commanderies of Chángshā [長沙] were detached to enfeoff him.
In the sixth year of Yuándǐng [元鼎], during the reign of Emperor Wǔ [武帝],
Lǚ Jiā [呂嘉] was suppressed.
His territory was established as seven commanderies: Nánhǎi [南海], Cāngwú [蒼梧], Yùlín [鬱林], Hépǔ [合浦], Rìnán [日南], Jiǔzhēn [九真], and Jiāozhǐ [交阯].
These were originally the lands of the three commanderies during the Qín [秦] dynasty.
In the Yuánfēng [元封] period,
Dān'ěr [儋耳] and Zhūyá [珠崖] were also established as two commanderies,
and a Jiāozhǐ Cìshǐ [交阯刺史] was appointed to supervise them.
In the fifth year of Shǐyuán [始元], during the reign of Emperor Zhāo [昭帝],
[二三] Dān'ěr [儋耳] was abolished and merged with Zhūyá [珠崖].
In the third year of Chūyuán [初元], during the reign of Emperor Yuán [元帝],
[二四] Zhūyá Jùn [珠崖郡] was again abolished.
Later, Mǎ Yuán [馬援] of the Later Hàn [漢] pacified the Jiāo Bù [交部] region,
and for the first time established cities, towns, wells, and settlements.
In the ninth year of Yǒnghé [永和], during the reign of Emperor Shùn [順帝],
[二五] Zhōu Chǎng [周敞], the Grand Administrator of Jiāozhǐ [交阯 Tàishǒu], requested that it be established as a province (Zhōu [州]).
The court deliberated but did not permit it.
Instead, Chǎng [敞] was appointed as Jiāozhǐ Cìshǐ [交阯刺史].
Emperor Huán [桓帝] separated and established Gāoxìng Jùn [高興郡].
Emperor Líng [靈帝] renamed it Gāoliáng [高涼].
In the eighth year of Jiàn'ān [建安],
Zhāng Jīn [張津] was the Cìshǐ [刺史],
and Shì Xiè [士燮] was the Grand Administrator of Jiāozhǐ [交阯 Tàishǒu].
They jointly memorialized to establish it as a province,
and Jīn [津] was then appointed as Jiāozhōu Mù [交州牧].
In the fifteenth year,
the seat was moved to Pānyú [番禺].
An imperial edict stated that border provinces were to be granted *shǐchíjié* [使持節] (imperial envoys with credentials),
and commanderies were to be provided with drums and wind instruments (gǔchuī [鼓吹]),
to emphasize the importance of fortresses and towns.
Additionally, the nine bestowals (jiǔxī [九錫]) and the six-row dance (liùyì [六佾]) were added.
In the fifth year of Huángwǔ [黃武] of Wú [吳],
Nánhǎi [南海], Cāngwú [蒼梧],
and Yùlín [鬱林] were detached to establish Guǎngzhōu [廣州],
[二六] and Jiāozhǐ [交阯], Rìnán [日南], Jiǔzhēn [九真], and Hépǔ [合浦] formed Jiāozhōu [交州].
Dài Liáng [戴良] was appointed Cìshǐ [刺史],
but due to the turmoil, he could not enter.
Lǚ Dài [呂岱] pacified the region,
and it was re-merged into the Jiāo Bù [交部].
In the fifth year of Chìwú [赤烏],
Zhūyá Jùn [珠崖郡] was re-established.
In the seventh year of Yǒng'ān [永安],
Guǎngzhōu [廣州] was again established from the former three commanderies.
Under Sūn Hào [孫晧],
Xīnchāng [新昌], Wǔpíng [武平], and Jiǔdé [九德] were also established as three commanderies.
Shǔ [蜀] appointed Lǐ Huī [李恢] as the Grand Administrator of Jiànníng [建寧 Tàishǒu],
remotely holding the title of Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ [交州刺史].
When Jìn [晉] pacified Shǔ [蜀],
Huo Yì [霍弋], the Grand Administrator of Jiànníng [建寧 Tàishǒu] of Shǔ [蜀], was remotely granted the title of Jiāozhōu [交州],
allowing him to expediently select and appoint senior officials.
After the pacification of Wú [吳],
Zhūyá [珠崖] was abolished and merged into Hépǔ [合浦].
Jiāozhōu [交州] administered seven commanderies,
fifty-three counties,
and 25,600 households.
Hépǔ Jùn [合浦郡] (established by Hàn [漢].
Administered six counties,
2,000 households.):
Hépǔ [合浦], Nánpíng [南平], Dàngchāng [蕩昌], Xúwén [徐聞], Dúzhì [毒質], Zhūguān [珠官].
Jiāozhǐ Jùn [交阯郡] (established by Hàn [漢].
Administered fourteen counties,
12,000 households.):
Lóngbiān [龍編], Gōují [苟𧜞], Wànghǎi [望海], Qú [𥕟], Xīyú [西于], Wǔníng [武寧], Zhūyuān [朱鳶], Qǔyáng [曲昜], Jiāoxīng [交興], Běidài [北帶], Jīxú [稽徐], Āndìng [安定], Nándìng [南定], Hǎipíng [海平].
Xīnchāng Jùn [新昌郡] (established by Wú [吳].
Administered six counties,
3,000 households.):
Mílíng [麋泠] (the place where the woman Zhēng Cè [徵側] held sway as ruler,

Jiāníng [嘉寧], Wúdìng [吳定], Fēngshān [封山], Línxī [臨西], Xīdào [西道].
Wǔpíng Jùn [武平郡] (established by Wú [吳].
Administered seven counties,
5,000 households.):
Wǔníng [武寧], Wǔxīng [武興], Jìnshān [進山], Gēnníng [根寧], Ānwǔ [安武], Fú'ān [扶安], Fēngxī [封溪].
Jiǔzhēn Jùn [九真郡] (established by Hàn [漢].
Administered seven counties,
3,000 households.):
Xūpǔ [胥浦], Yífēng [移風], Jīnwú [津梧], Jiànchū [建初], Chánglè [常樂], Fúlè [扶樂], Sōngyuán [松原].
Jiǔdé Jùn [九德郡] (established by Wú [吳].
In the Zhōu [周] period, it was the land of Yuècháng Shì [越常氏].
Administered eight counties,
no households recorded.):
Jiǔdé [九德], Xiánhuān [咸驩], Nánlíng [南陵], Yángsuí [陽遂], Fúlíng [扶苓], Qǔxū [曲胥], Pǔyáng [浦陽], Dūxiáo [都洨].
Rì’nán Jùn (Qín established Xiàng Jùn,
which Hàn Wǔdì renamed.
It administered five counties,
with six hundred households.)
Xiànglín (South of this, there are four kingdoms.
Their people all say they are descendants of Hàn people.
There is now a bronze pillar,
which was also erected by Hàn to mark the boundary here.
They pay tribute in gold as tax.)
Lúróng (where Xiàng Jùn was located.)
Zhūwú, Xījuǎn, Bǐjǐng.
Guǎngzhōu.
According to the Yǔgòng, this was part of Yángzhōu.
At the end of Qín, it was the territory occupied by Zhào Tuó.
During the reign of Hàn Wǔdì,
this area became Jiāozhǐ Jùn.
In the fifth year of Huángwǔ of Wú [226 CE],
Nánhǎi, Cāngwú, Yùlín, and Gāoliáng — four commanderies of Jiāozhōu — were separated to establish Guǎngzhōu,
but it was soon restored to the old system.
In the sixth year of Yǒng'ān [263 CE],
Guǎngzhōu was again established by separating it from Jiāozhōu.
Hépǔ Běibù was established by separating it from Hépǔ,
and a Dūwèi was put in charge.
Sūn Hào separated Yùlín to establish Guìlín Jùn.
In the middle of Tàikāng [280-289 CE],
after Wú was pacified,
Jīngzhōu, Shǐ'ān, Shǐxīng, and Línhè — three commanderies — were brought under its administration.
It administered a total of ten commanderies,
sixty-eight counties,
and forty-three thousand one hundred twenty households.
Nánhǎi Jùn (established by Qín.
It administered six counties,
with nine thousand five hundred households.)
Pānyú, Sìhuì, Zēngchéng, Bólúo, Lóngchuān, Píngyí.

It administered six counties,

Línhè, Xièmù, Féngchéng, Fēngyáng, Xīng'ān, Fùchuān.

It administered seven counties,

Shǐ'ān, Shǐyáng, Pínglè, Lìpǔ, Cháng'ān, Xīpíng, Yǒngfēng.
Shǐxīng Jùn (established by Wú.
It administered seven counties,

Qǔjiāng, Guìyáng, Shǐxīng, Hánkuāng, Zhēnyáng, Zhōngsù, Yángshān.

Guǎngxìn, Duānxī, Gāoyào, Jiànlíng, Xīnníng, Měnglíng, Zhāngpíng, Nóngchéng, Yuánxī, Línyǔn, Dūluó, Wǔchéng.
Yùlín Jùn (Qín established Guìlín Jùn,
〔二七〕Hàn Wǔdì renamed it.
It administered nine counties,

Bùshān, Ālín 〔二八〕, Xīnyì, Jìnpíng, Shǐjiàn, Yùpíng, Lǐngfāng, Wǔxī, Ānguǎng.
Guìlín Jùn (established by Wú.
It administered eight counties,
with two thousand households.)
Tánzhōng, Wǔfēng, Sùpíng, Yángpíng, Lónggāng, Jiáyáng, Wǔchéng, Jūnténg.
Gāoliáng Jùn (established by Wú.
It administered three counties,
with two thousand households.)
Ānníng, Gāoliáng, Sīpíng.

It administered five counties,

Níngpǔ, Liándào 〔三０〕, Wú'ān, Chāngpíng 〔三一〕, Píngshān.
After Wǔdì, Gāoxìng Jùn was abolished.
In the first year of Yǒngjiā of Huáidì [307 CE],
Línhè, Shǐxīng, and Shǐ'ān — three commanderies totaling twenty counties — were again made into Xiāngzhōu.
Yuándì separated Yùlín to establish Jìnxīng Jùn.
Chéngdì separated Nánhǎi to establish Dōngguān Jùn,
and the two commanderies of Shǐxīng and Línhè were returned to Jīngzhōu.
Mùdì separated Cāngwú to establish Jìnkāng, Xīnníng, and Yǒngpíng — three commanderies.
In the middle of Tàihé during Āidì's reign [366-371 CE], Xīn'ān Jùn was established.
Āndì separated Dōngguān to establish Yì'ān Jùn.
