and changed the era name to Hóngchāng (弘昌).
Previously,
when Qǐfú Gān'guī (乞伏乾歸) was in Jìnxīng (晉興),
he had sent his heir apparent Chìpán (熾磐) as a hostage.
Later, Chìpán (熾磐) escaped and returned,
but was captured by pursuing cavalry.
Lìlùgū (利鹿孤) ordered him to be killed.
Tán (檀) said:
"For a subject and son to escape and return to his lord and father
is a common principle since ancient times.
Thus, Wèi Wǔ (魏武) praised Guān Yǔ (關羽) for fleeing,
and Qín Zhāo (秦昭) pardoned Qǐngxiāng (頃襄) for departing.
Although Chìpán (熾磐) fled and rebelled,
his filial heart is commendable;
he should be fully pardoned to demonstrate a vast and profound magnanimity."
Thereupon, he pardoned him.
At this time,
Chìpán (熾磐) again fled to Yúnjiē (允街).
Tán (檀) returned his wife and children to him.
Yáo Xīng (姚興) sent an envoy to appoint Tán (檀) as Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guǎngwǔ (廣武公).
Tán (檀) greatly fortified Lèdū (樂都).
Yáo Xīng (姚興) sent his general Qí Nán (齊難) to lead troops to welcome Lǚ Lóng (呂隆) at Gūzāng (姑臧).
Tán (檀) withdrew the two garrisons of Chāngsōng (昌松) and Wèi'ān (魏安) to avoid them.
Xīng's (興) Inspector of Liángzhōu (涼州), Wáng Shàng (王尚), sent his Master of Records Zōng Chǎng (宗敞) to establish friendly relations.
Chǎng's (敞) father, Xiè (燮),
during the time of Lǚ Guāng (呂光), went from Grand Administrator of Huánghé (湟河) to be a Minister in the Department of State Affairs.
He met Tán (檀) at Guǎngwǔ (廣武),
and holding his hand, said:
"Your spirit is grand and outstanding,
your lofty *qì* (氣) reaches the clouds.
You are a hero destined for this age,
and will surely clear the world's troubles.
I only regret that I am old and will not live to see it,
so I entrust Chǎng (敞) and his brothers to you."
At this time,
Tán (檀) said to Chǎng (敞):
"I, with my ordinary talent,
was mistakenly praised by your esteemed late father.
I always feared that I would tarnish the clear discernment of that great man.
Since I have come into my family's inheritance,
I have secretly held you, a *jūnzǐ* (君子), in my heart.
The *Shī* (詩) says: '
Hidden in my heart, how can I ever forget it.'
I did not expect to see you today."
Chǎng (敞) said:
"Your Majesty's benevolence rivals that of Wèi Zǔ (魏祖),
remembering my late father.
Even Zhū Huī (朱暉) looking after Zhāng Kān's (張堪) orphan,
or Shū Xiàng (叔向) comforting the sons of Rǔ Qí (汝齊),
could not surpass this."
As the wine flowed freely,
they spoke of their lives.
Tán (檀) said:
"You are a match for Lǔ Zǐjìng (魯子敬); I only regret that I cannot accomplish great things with you."
At that time, the Wèi armies entered Zhōngshān,
Mùróng Bǎo fled to Jì,
and Mùróng Xiáng again usurped the title.
Just then, Liú Zǎo arrived from Yáo Xìng.
Xìng's Grand Astrologer, Gāo Lǔ, sent his nephew, Wáng Jǐnghuī, with Zǎo to deliver a jade seal,
along with prophetic diagrams and secret texts,
which said:
"The virtuous prosper,
the unvirtuous perish.
Virtue receives Heaven's mandate,
soft yet becoming firm again."
There was also a rhyme that said:
"A great wind rises, stirring up dust,
'Eight wells, three knives' suddenly appear.
The four seas boil, Zhōngshān declines,
only the virtuous person occupies the Sāntái."
Thereupon, Dé's officials debated, considering Mùróng Xiáng's usurpation in Zhōngshān,
and the Wèi armies' strength in Jìzhōu.
Unsure of Bǎo's fate,
they consequently urged Dé to assume the imperial title.
Dé did not comply.
Soon after, Mùróng Dá fled from Lóngchéng to Yè,
claiming that Bǎo was still alive,
and the general consensus then ceased.
Shortly thereafter, Bǎo appointed Dé as Chancellor
and concurrently Governor of Jìzhōu,
entrusting him with authority over the southern regions.
Dé's elder brother's son, Lín, fled from Yìtái to Yè,
and persuaded Dé, saying:
"Now that Zhōngshān is lost,
Wèi will surely take advantage of the victory to attack Yè.
Although provisions have been accumulated,
the city is large and difficult to defend.
Moreover, the people's morale is shaken,
making it impossible to fight.
Before the Wèi army arrives,
lead the multitude south across the river,
unite with Lǔyáng Wáng Hé,
hold Huátái, gather troops, and accumulate grain.
Wait for an opportunity to act;
this is the best plan.
Although Wèi has captured Zhōngshān,
their stay will not be long;
they will merely plunder and return.
People are reluctant to relocate,
and naturally, disorder will arise.
Then, you can demonstrate your might to support them,
and Wèi will face enemies both internally and externally.
This will give those who miss their homeland something to rely on,
and by widely extending benevolence and trust,
you can gather the remaining populace.
You can then capture it in one fell swoop."
Previously,
Mùróng Hé had also urged Dé to move south.
Therefore, Dé agreed to it.
In the second year of Lóng'ān,
he led forty thousand households and twenty-seven thousand chariots
from Yè, preparing to move to Huátái.
They encountered a storm,
and their boats sank.
The Wèi army was close,
and the multitude was afraid,
debating whether to retreat and defend Líyáng.
That evening, the ice floes froze solid.
That night, they crossed the river.
At dawn,
the Wèi army arrived, but the ice melted,
as if by divine intervention.
They then renamed Líyáng Ford to Tiānqiáo Ford.
Upon arriving at Huátái,
a propitious star appeared in Wěijī.
White jade,
shaped like a seal, was found in the Zhāng River.
Thereupon, Dé, following the precedent of Yān Yuán,
declared the first year of his reign,
granted a general amnesty throughout his territory for all offenses down to death,
and established government officials.
He appointed Mùróng Lín as Sīkōng and concurrently Shàngshūlìng,
Mùróng Fǎ as Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn,
Mùyú Bá as Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè,
Dīng Tōng as Shàngshū Yòu Púyè,
with other appointments and enfeoffments varying by rank.
Earlier,
a qílín had been seen in Héjiān,
and Mùróng Lín believed it was a good omen for himself.
By this time,
he secretly plotted rebellion.
The matter was discovered,
and he was granted death.
That summer,
the Wèi general Hèlà Lú led his troops to submit to him.
At this point,
Mùróng Bǎo fled south from Lóngchéng to Líyáng,
and sent his Zhōnghuángménlìng, Zhào Sī, to summon Mùróng Zhōng to welcome him.
Zhōng had originally been the primary advocate for Dé assuming the imperial title.
Hearing this, he disliked it,
seized Sī and imprisoned him,
and dispatched a swift messenger to report the situation.
Dé said to his subordinates:
"Gentlemen, you previously, for the great plan of the state,
urged me to assume regency.
I also, seeing that the successor emperor had fled,
and that both men and spirits lacked a master,
temporarily yielded to the general consensus
to satisfy the hopes of the multitude.
Now, Heaven is regretting its calamity,
and the successor emperor has returned.
I shall prepare my carriage to respectfully welcome him,
apologize at the imperial court,
and then retire to my private residence, wearing a simple cap.
What do you all think?"
His Huángmén Shìláng, Zhāng Huá, stepped forward and said:
"In an era of contention,
only a heroic talent can succeed;
in times of shifting alliances,
how can a coward prevail!
If Your Majesty treads the path of womanly benevolence,
abandoning the enterprise granted by Heaven,
once power and authority are lost,
your head and body will not be safe.
What room for retreat and deference will there be!"
Dé said:
"I believe that the ancients' method of 'seizing by force and holding with virtue' is not sufficient.
That is why I have been hesitating midway,
feeling regretful and undecided."
Mùyú Hù requested to ride swiftly to inquire about Bǎo's true situation.
Dé wept and dispatched him.
Hù then led several hundred brave men
and followed Sī northward,
intending to assassinate Bǎo.
Initially,
after Bǎo dispatched Sī,
he learned that Dé had assumed power,
became afraid, and fled northward.
Hù arrived but found nothing,
so he seized Sī and returned.
Dé, finding Sī knowledgeable in precedents,
intended to employ him.
Sī said:
"In the past, Guān Yǔ was highly regarded by Cáo Gōng,
yet he did not forget the kindness of his former lord.
Although I am a lowly servant who has suffered mutilation,
and have received the nation's favor and grace,
even dogs and horses have feelings,
let alone a human!
I beg to return to my former lord
to demonstrate my humble integrity."
Dé insisted on detaining him.
Sī angrily said:
"When the Zhōu House declined,
Jìn and Zhèng supported it;
when Hàn faced the calamity of the Seven Kingdoms,
it truly relied on the King of Liáng.
Your Highness is a close relative, an uncle,
and holds a high position,
yet you fail to lead the other lords in upholding the royal house,
and instead rejoice in the collapse of the foundation, acting like Zhào Lún.
Although I cannot achieve the effectiveness of Shēn Xū crying out in Qín,
I still aspire to the example of Jūnbīn who refused to live in Wáng Mǎng's era."
Dé was enraged
and had him executed.
The Jìn Nányáng Tàishǒu, Lǘqiū Xiàn, and Níngshuò Jiāngjūn, Dèng Qǐfāng, led an army of twenty thousand to attack,
with their forces encamped at Guǎnchéng.
Dé dispatched his Zhōngjūn, Mùróng Fǎ, and Fǔjūn, Mùróng Hé, to resist them.
The royal army suffered a defeat.
Dé was angry that Fǎ did not pursue the Jìn army thoroughly,
and executed his Fǔjūn Sīmǎ, Jìn Kuī.
Previously,
after Fú Dēng was defeated by Yáo Xìng,
Dēng's younger brother, Guǎng, led his tribe to surrender to Dé,
was appointed Guānjūn Jiāngjūn,
and settled in Qǐhuóbǎo.
At that time, Huòxīng guarded Dōngjǐng,
and some said that Qín would rise again.
Guǎng then declared himself King of Qín,
and defeated Dé's general, Mùróng Zhōng.
At that time, Dé had just made Huátái his capital,
situated between Jìn and Wèi,
with fewer than ten cities,
and his forces numbered no more than several tens of thousands.
After Zhōng lost his army,
many wavering individuals defected to Guǎng.
Dé then left Mùróng Hé to guard Huátái,
and personally led his forces to attack Guǎng,
executing him.
Chāo held a New Year's Day court for his officials in the Dōngyáng Hall.
When the music began,
he sighed that the musical performances were incomplete,
regretting that he had sent musicians to Yáo Xīng.
Thereupon, he discussed launching an invasion.
His Commander of the Army, Hán Chāng, remonstrated, saying:
"The former emperor, seeing the old capital lost,
gathered his strength in Sān Qí.
If the time is not yet right,
even the wisest should refrain from action.
Now that Your Majesty has inherited and upholds the established rules,
you should close the passes, nurture your soldiers,
and await an opportune moment.
You should not create enmity with your southern neighbor
and widely sow grievances."
Chāo said:
"My plan is already set.
I will not discuss it with you."
Thereupon, he dispatched his generals Húgǔ Tí and Gōngsūn Guī and others to lead cavalry to invade Sùyù.
They captured it,
seized the Administrator of Yángpíng, Liú Qiānzài, and the Administrator of Jìyīn, Xú Ruǎn,
plundered extensively, and departed.
They selected two thousand five hundred men and women,
and handed them over to the Grand Music department for training.
At that time, Gōngsūn Wǔlóu was a Household Attendant and Grand Minister,
leading the General of the Left Guard,
and solely controlled the court's affairs.
His elder brother Guī was Champion General and Duke of Chángshān.
His uncle Tuí was a Military Guard and Duke of Xīnglè.
All of Wǔlóu's relatives were assisting him on both sides,
and inside and outside the court, all the dukes and officials feared them.
Chāo, discussing the merits of the Sùyù campaign,
enfeoffed Húgǔ Tí and others as dukes of commanderies and counties.
Mùróng Zhèn remonstrated, saying:
"Your subject has heard that rewards are offered for merit,
and one is not enfeoffed without merit.
Now Gōngsūn Guī has brought disaster and extended the war,
harming the common people,
yet Your Majesty enfeoffs him.
Is this not unacceptable?
Truly, loyal words are harsh to the ear,
and are not spoken by those who are not close.
Although your subject is foolish and unworthy,
I am a humble relative and vassal of the state.
I shall presumptuously offer my foolish sincerity.
I only ask Your Majesty to consider it."
Chāo was enraged
and did not reply.
From then on, all officials kept silent,
none daring to speak.
The Grand Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, Wáng Yǎn, flattered Wǔlóu,
was promoted to Minister of Personnel,
then went out to be Administrator of Jìnán,
and then returned to be Left Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
People at the time had a saying about him:
"If you want to become a marquis,
serve Wǔlóu."
Chāo again sent Gōngsūn Guī and others to lead three thousand cavalry to invade Jìnán,
captured Administrator Zhào Yuán,
plundered over a thousand men and women, and departed.
Liú Yù led his army, intending to campaign against him.
Chāo summoned his officials to the Dōngyáng Hall,
to discuss repelling the royal army.
Gōngsūn Wǔlóu said:
"The Wú soldiers are light and swift,
and their advantage lies in battle.
Their initial charge is valiant and sharp,
and cannot be contended with directly.
We should occupy Dàxiàn,
preventing them from entering.
If we prolong the days and extend the time,
their锐气 will be blunted.
We can slowly select two thousand elite cavalry,
follow the coast southward,
cut off their grain transport,
and separately order Duàn Huī to lead the army from Yǎnzhōu
to descend along the mountains to the east.
Attacking them from front and rear
is the best strategy.
Alternatively, order each governor and magistrate
to secure themselves by relying on natural defenses.
Beyond what is required for their stores,
burn and destroy everything else.
Cut down the grain sprouts
so the enemy has nothing to provision themselves with.
Fortify walls and clear the fields
to await their opportune moment.
This is the middle strategy.
Allowing the bandits to enter Dàxiàn
and then marching out of the city to engage them
is the worst strategy."
Chāo said:
"The capital is prosperous,
and the population is numerous,
not something that can be guarded by entering quickly.
The green sprouts are spread across the fields,
not something that can be quickly cut down.
Even if we cut down the sprouts and guard the city
to preserve our lives,
that is something I cannot do.
Now, relying on the strength of five provinces,
with mountains and rivers as defenses,
ten thousand chariots of war,
and ten thousand iron cavalry,
even if they cross Dàxiàn
and reach the plain,
we can slowly crush them with elite cavalry.
This is a sure capture."
Hèlàilú strenuously remonstrated,
but he did not listen.
He then turned to Wǔlóu and said:
"The emperor will not use our plan;
destruction is but days away."
Mùróng Zhèn said:
"If it is as His Majesty instructs,
it will indeed be more convenient to use cavalry on the open plain.
We should go out to Dàxiàn and engage them.
If we fight and do not win,
we can still retreat and defend.
We should not allow the enemy to enter Dàxiàn,
thereby creating our own predicament.
In the past, Chéng'ān Jūn did not defend the pass of Jǐngxíng,
and was ultimately defeated by Hán Xìn.
Zhūgě Zhān did not hold the strategic heights of Shùmǎ,
and was eventually captured by Dèng Ài.
Your subject believes that the timing of heaven is not as good as the advantage of terrain.
Blocking and defending Dàxiàn
is the best strategy."
Chāo did not listen.
Zhèn left
and said to Hán Chāng:
"The emperor is neither able to cut down the sprouts and defend the strategic heights,
nor willing to move the people to escape the invaders.
He is exactly like Liú Zhāng!
This year the state will be destroyed,
and I will surely die for it.
You, gentlemen of the Central Plains,
will again become tattooed barbarians!"
Chāo heard this and was greatly enraged.
He arrested Zhèn and imprisoned him.
Then he deployed the two garrisons of Jǔ and Liángfù,
repaired the city walls,
selected soldiers and horses,
and accumulated strength to await them.
Jǔqú Méngxùn
was a Hú person from Lúsui, Línsōng.
His ancestors were formerly Xiōngnú Zuǒjūqú,
and thus took the official title as their surname.
Méngxùn was broadly learned in all histories,
quite understood astronomy,
was heroic and outstanding with brilliant strategies,
and was humorous and good at adapting to circumstances.
Liáng Xī and Lǚ Guāng both admired and feared him,
so he often indulged in drinking to conceal himself.
It so happened that his paternal uncles Luóchóu and Qūzhōu followed Lǚ Guāng to campaign in Hénán.
Guāng's vanguard was greatly defeated.
Qūzhōu said to his elder brother Luóchóu:
"Our lord is senile and arrogant,
his sons form factions and contend against each other,
and slanderers cast their eyes about.
Now the army is defeated and generals are dead,
this is precisely the day when the wise and brave are suspected.
How can we not be afraid!
Our brothers have always been feared by him.
Rather than dying in a ditch,
why not gather the troops and head west to Xīpíng,
emerge from Tiáodiào,
raise our arms and give a great shout,
and Liángzhōu will be easy to conquer!"
Luóchóu said:
"What you say is reasonable,
but our family has for generations been loyal and filial,
and recognized by the region.
Rather let others betray me,
than I betray others."
Soon after, they were both killed by Guāng.
More than ten thousand relatives and tribal members gathered for the funeral.
Méngxùn wept and said to the crowd:
"In the past, when the Hàn dynasty's fate was in decline,
our ancestor assisted Dòu Róng
and secured Héyòu.
King Lǚ is confused and senile,
tyrannical and lawless.
How can we not uphold our ancestors' ambition to bring peace to the times,
and let our two fathers have regrets in the Yellow Springs!"
The crowd all cheered, "Long live!"
Thereupon, he beheaded Guāng's Zhōngtián Hùjūn Mǎ Suì and Línsōng lìng Jǐng Xiáng to seal the alliance.
Within ten days,
the crowd numbered over ten thousand.
They encamped at Jīnshān,
and together with his cousin Nánchéng, they elevated Guāng's Jiànkāng Tàishǒu Duàn Yè to be Shǐchíjié, Dàdūdū, Lóngxiáng Dàjiāngjūn, Liángzhōu Mù, and Jiànkāng Gōng.
They changed Lǚ Guāng's Lóngfēi second year to Shénxǐ first year.
Yè appointed Méngxùn as Zhāngyè Tàishǒu
and Nánchéng as Fǔguó Jiāngjūn,
entrusting them with military and state affairs.
Yè intended to send Méngxùn to attack Xī Jùn.
Everyone had doubts.
Méngxùn said:
"This commandery holds the strategic pass of the mountains,
it must be taken."
Yè said:
"What you say is correct."
So he dispatched him.
Méngxùn diverted water to flood the city.
The city collapsed,
and he captured Tàishǒu Lǚ Chún and returned.
Thereupon Wáng Dé surrendered Jìnchāng,
and Mèng Mǐn surrendered Dūnhuáng to Yè.
Yè enfeoffed Méngxùn as Línchí Hóu.
Lǚ Hóng left Zhāngyè
and intended to flee east.
Yè discussed attacking him.
Méngxùn advised:
"Do not block a retreating army,
do not pursue a desperate foe.
These are the warnings of military strategists.
It is better to let him go
and plan for later."
Yè said:
"If one lets the enemy escape for a day,
regret will be too late."
So he led his troops to pursue him
and was defeated by Hóng.
Yè relied on Méngxùn to escape
and sighed:
"I failed to heed Zǐfáng's words
and have come to this!"
Yè built Xī'ān City
and appointed his general Zāng Mòhái as Tàishǒu.
Méngxùn said:
"Mòhái is brave but lacks strategy,
knowing only how to advance and forgetting how to retreat.
This is what is called building a tomb for him,
not building a city."
Yè did not follow.
Soon after, it was defeated by Lǚ Zuǎn.
Méngxùn feared that Yè could not tolerate him,
so he always concealed his intelligence to avoid him.
Yè presumptuously claimed the title of King of Liáng,
appointing Méngxùn as Shàngshū Zuǒchéng
and Liáng Zhōngyōng as Yòuchéng.
Lǚ Guāng sent his two sons Shào and Zuǎn to attack Yè.
Yè requested help from Tūfà Wūgū.
Wūgū sent his younger brother Lùgū and Yáng Guǐ to assist Yè.
Shào, seeing Yè's army was strong,
wanted to pass through Sānmén Guān and go east along the mountains.
Zuǎn said:
"Going along the mountains shows weakness,
a path to defeat.
It is better to form up and charge them;
they will surely be intimidated by us and not fight."
Shào then led his army south.
Yè was about to attack them.
Méngxùn advised:
"Yáng Guǐ, relying on the strength of his barbarian cavalry,
has ambitions to usurp.
Shào and Zuǎn's troops are in a death trap,
they will surely fight desperately for survival.
If we do not fight, we will have the security of Mount Tài;
if we fight, we will face the danger of piled eggs."
Yè said:
"What you say is correct."
So he held his troops and did not fight.
Shào also found it difficult,
and they each led their troops back.
Yè feared Méngxùn's heroism and might,
and subtly wished to distance himself.
So he appointed Méngxùn's paternal cousin Yìshēng as Jiǔquán Tàishǒu
and Méngxùn as Línchí Tàishǒu.
Yè's Ménxià Shìláng Mǎ Quán was brilliant and spirited,
with military prowess surpassing others.
Yè replaced Méngxùn with Quán as Zhāngyè Tàishǒu,
greatly trusting and valuing him,
and often condescending towards Méngxùn.
Méngxùn also feared and resented him,
so he slandered him to Yè, saying:
"The world is not worth worrying about;
only Mǎ Quán is to be feared."
Yè then killed him.
Méngxùn said to Nánchéng:
"Duàn Yè is foolish and ignorant,
not a talent for resolving chaos.
He believes slander and loves sycophants,
lacking clear discernment.
The only ones to be feared were Suǒ Sì and Mǎ Quán;
now they are both dead.
Méngxùn wishes to eliminate Yè and enthrone you, what do you think?"
Nánchéng said:
"Yè is a lonely sojourner,
established by us.
Having our brothers is like fish having water.
Since people trust me,
betraying him would be inauspicious."
So he stopped.
Méngxùn, being feared by Yè,
felt uneasy internally,
and requested to be Xī'ān Tàishǒu.
Yè also, knowing Méngxùn had great ambitions,
feared a sudden change,
and so agreed.
Méngxùn Qí and Nánchéng jointly offered sacrifices at Lánménshān.
Méngxùn secretly sent Sīmǎ Xǔ Xián to inform Yè, saying:
"Nánchéng intends to rebel.
He promised that if he were to take a holiday, he would stage a rebellion.
If he asks to offer sacrifices at Lánménshān,
my words will be proven true."
When the appointed day arrived,
it was indeed so.
Yè arrested Nánchéng
and ordered him to commit suicide.
Nánchéng said:
"Méngxùn intends to rebel.
He had already informed me earlier,
but out of brotherly affection,
I endured and did not speak.
Fearing that his followers would not obey him
as long as I was alive,
he arranged a date with me to offer sacrifices on the mountain,
and then turned around and falsely accused me.
If I die this morning,
Méngxùn will surely launch his rebellion this evening.
I beg you to feign my death
and publicize my crimes.
Méngxùn will certainly rebel,
and I will roll up my sleeves and attack him.
There will be nothing that is not victorious."
Yè did not comply.
When Méngxùn heard of Nánchéng's death,
he told the衆(zhòng) (people), saying:
"Nánchéng was loyal to Duàn Gōng,
but was wrongfully slaughtered.
Can you all avenge him?
Furthermore, with the military chaos in the province,
it seems that Yè is incapable of bringing peace.
The reason I initially supported him
was because I regarded him as Chén Shèng and Wú Guǎng.
Yet, he believes slander and is overly suspicious,
wrongfully harming loyal and good people.
How can we sleep peacefully and watch
while the common people suffer in misery?"
Nánchéng had always been benevolent and trusted,
so everyone was indignant and tearfully followed him.
By the time they reached Dīchí,
their numbers exceeded ten thousand.
Zhèn Jūn Zāng Mòhái led his followers to join him.
Many Qiāng and Hú people raised troops in response.
Méngxùn set up camp at Hóuwù.
Yè had previously suspected his Right General Tián Áng
and imprisoned him.
At this point,
he apologized and pardoned him,
making him and Wǔwèi Liáng Zhōngyōng attack Méngxùn.
Yè's general Wáng Fēngsūn said to Yè:
"The Tián clan of Xīpíng
has had rebels for generations.
Áng is outwardly respectful but inwardly cruel,
ambitious and cunning;
he cannot be trusted."
Yè said:
"I have suspected him for a long time,
but without Áng, there is no one who can attack Méngxùn."
Since Fēngsūn's words were not heeded,
when Áng reached Hóuwù,
he led five hundred cavalry to defect to Méngxùn.
When Méngxùn arrived at Zhāngyè,
Áng's nephew, Chéng'ài, cut open the gate to let him in.
All of Yè's attendants dispersed.
Méngxùn loudly called out:
"Where is Zhènxī?"
A soldier said:
"He is here."
Yè said:
"I am a lonely wanderer,
pushed forward by your esteemed family.
Please grant me a few more days of life
to go south of the mountains.
Perhaps I can return east
and see my wife and children."
Méngxùn then beheaded him.
Yè was
a native of Jīngzhào.
He was widely read in historical records
and possessed literary talent.
He served as Dù Jìn's secretary
and followed him on campaigns to the frontier.
He was a cultured and upright elder,
without other schemes or strategies.
His authority was not enforced,
and his subordinates acted on their own initiative.
He particularly believed in divination, prognostication, shamans, and auspicious signs,
and was therefore misled by treacherous flatterers.
In the fifth year of Lóng'ān (401 CE),
Liáng Zhōngyōng, Fáng Guǐ, Tián Áng, and others supported Méngxùn as Cìshǐchíjié, Dàdūdū, Dàjiāngjūn, Liángzhōu Mù, and Zhāngyè Gōng.
He pardoned those within his territory
and changed the era name to Yǒng'ān.
He appointed his cousin Fúnú as Zhèn Jūn Jiāngjūn, Zhāngyè Tàishǒu, and Hépíng Hóu.
His younger brother Ná was appointed Jiànzhōng Jiāngjūn and Dōugǔ Hóu.
Tián Áng was appointed Zhènnán Jiāngjūn and Xī Jùn Tàishǒu.
Zāng Mòhái was appointed Fǔguó Jiāngjūn.
Fáng Guǐ and Liáng Zhōngyōng were appointed Zuǒ Yòu Zhǎngshǐ.
Zhāng Zhì and Xiè Zhènglǐ were appointed Zuǒ Yòu Sīmǎ.
He promoted worthy talents,
and both civil and military officials were pleased.
At that time, Yáo Xīng sent his general Yáo Shuòdé to attack Lǚ Lóng at Gūzāng.
Méngxùn sent his secretary Lǐ Diǎn to meet Xīng,
to establish friendly relations.
Méngxùn, seeing that Lǚ Lóng had already surrendered to Xīng,
and that the two commanderies of Jiǔquán and Liángníng had rebelled and surrendered to Lǐ Xuánshèng,
sent Jiànzhōng Ná and Mùfǔ Zhǎngshǐ Zhāng Qián to meet Shuòdé at Gūzāng,
requesting troops to welcome them
and lead the people of the commandery to migrate eastward.
Shuòdé was greatly pleased,
appointing Qián as Zhāngyè Tàishǒu
and Ná as Jiànkāng Tàishǒu.
Qián urged Méngxùn to migrate eastward.
Ná secretly said to Méngxùn:
"The Lǚ clan still exists,
and Gūzāng has not yet been taken.
Shuòdé's provisions will be exhausted, and he will return soon;
he cannot stay long.
Why should we abandon our homeland
and be controlled by others!"
Fǔguó Mòhái said:
"Jiànzhōng's words are correct."
Méngxùn then executed Zhāng Qián
and subsequently issued a decree, saying:
"I, being of meager virtue,
have improperly taken on the present fortune,
unable to widely promote great plans
and quell all the rebels,
allowing the 'peach worms' to flap their wings in the Eastern Capital
and the 'great boars' to cross the western frontiers.
War chariots have frequently moved,
and weapons have not been sheathed.
Farmers have lost their livelihood for three seasons,
and the common people's households lack grain for food.
Therefore, all unnecessary corvée duties may be abolished
to concentrate efforts on the southern fields.
Clear regulations shall be established
to fully utilize the land's potential."
At that time, Liáng Zhōngyōng, as Xī Jùn Tàishǒu,
fled west to Lǐ Xuánshèng.
Méngxùn, hearing of this,
laughed and said:
"My bond with Zhōngyōng is deep, as if we were one body,
yet he did not trust me.
He simply overestimated himself;
how could I blame him!"
He then returned his wife and children entirely.
Méngxùn issued an order, saying:
"To support the elderly and ask for their advice.
Jìn Wén Gōng accepted the words of commoners,
which is why he was able to attract and honor extraordinary talents
and achieve the beauty of peaceful times.
How much more so should I, who possess meager virtue
and lack profound wisdom,
not strive to hear honest words to reflect upon myself!
All officials, both inside and outside,
shall each seek out and promote worthy and outstanding individuals,
and widely present humble opinions,
to rectify my shortcomings."
He sent Fǔguó Zāng Mòhái to attack the northern barbarians in Shānběi,
inflicting a great defeat upon them.
Yáo Xīng sent his general Qí Nán, leading forty thousand men, to welcome Lǚ Lóng.
Lóng advised Nán to attack Méngxùn,
and Nán agreed.
Mòhái defeated their vanguard,
whereupon Nán made an alliance and returned.
Méngxùn's paternal uncle Zhōng Tián Hùjūn Qīnxìn and Línsōng Tàishǒu Kǒng Dú were both arrogant, extravagant, and oppressive,
causing suffering to the common people.
Méngxùn said:
"Those who disrupt my state are these two paternal uncles!
How can I govern the people properly?"
He ordered both to commit suicide.
Méngxùn attacked Dí Luòpán at Fānhé
but did not succeed.
He relocated over five hundred households
and returned.
Méngxùn 孟遜 sent his general to transport provisions to the Huáng Hé 湟河.
He personally led his troops to attack and capture Qǐfú Chìpán's 乞伏熾磐 Guǎngwǔ 廣武 Commandery.
As the supply of provisions was cut off,
he moved from Guǎngwǔ 廣武 to Huáng Hé 湟河,
crossing Hàowěi 浩亹.
Chìpán 熾磐 sent his general Qǐfú Tuíníyín 乞伏魋尼寅 to resist Méngxùn 蒙遜.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 attacked and slew him.
Chìpán 熾磐 again sent his generals Wáng Héng 王衡, Zhéfěi 折斐, Qū Jǐng 麴景, and others, leading ten thousand cavalry to hold Lèjiě Lǐng 勒姐嶺.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 fought as he advanced,
utterly defeating them,
capturing Zhéfěi 折斐 and over seven hundred others.
Qū Jǐng 麴景 fled back.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 appointed his younger brother, Hànpíng 漢平, as General for Quelling the Barbarians (Zhéchōng Jiāngjūn 折衝將軍) and Administrator of Huáng Hé 湟河 (Huánghé Tàishǒu 湟河太守).
Then he withdrew.
The Jìn 晉 Governor of Yìzhōu 益州, Zhū Língshí 朱齡石, sent an envoy to pay respects.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 sent his palace attendant Huáng Xùn 黃迅 to return the courtesy to Yìzhōu 益州,
and thereupon presented a memorial which stated:
"Heaven has sent down disaster,
the Four Seas are in disarray.
The brilliant light is constrained in the southern frontiers,
and the common people are submerged among the barbarian enemies.
Your Majesty, through successive sagely reigns, has accumulated glory,
your Way surpasses that of Zhōu 周 and Hàn 漢.
Where your pure influence reaches,
the eight directions are at peace.
Although your servant lives with unbound hair on the borderlands,
and his talent is not that of a contemporary luminary,
he has been mistakenly acclaimed as the leader by the remaining people of Héyòu 河右.
Your servant's ancestors,
for generations, have enjoyed grace and favor.
Though they experienced hardships and dangers,
they held fast to righteousness without faltering.
They turned their heads towards the morning sun,
and their hearts were devoted to the royal house.
Last winter, the Governor of Yìzhōu 益州, Zhū Língshí 朱齡石, sent an envoy to your servant,
and only then did I fully learn of the court's kind inquiries.
I heard that General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chēqí Jiāngjūn 車騎將軍) Liú Yù 劉裕 is preparing his horses and brandishing his halberds,
taking the Central Plains as his concern.
This can be called Heaven assisting the great Jìn 晉,
giving birth to a truly exceptional aide.
Your servant has heard that Shàokāng 少康 rose to revive the great Xià 夏,
and Guāngwǔ 光武 restored the Hàn 漢 dynasty;
both brandished swords and rose,
with not even a single troop,
yet they were able to achieve merits matching Heaven,
and have the praise of 'Chēgōng' 車攻 sung.
Your Majesty occupies the entire territory of Chǔ 楚,
and commands the elite forces of Jīng 荊 and Yáng 揚,
yet you can sit idly and comfortably,
abandoning the two capitals to benefit the barbarians!
If the six armies were to turn north,
with a date for restoration,
your servant requests to lead the armies of Héxī 河西 as the right wing vanguard for Jìn 晉."
Chìpán 熾磐 led thirty thousand troops to attack Huáng Hé 湟河.
Hànpíng 漢平 fought bravely and held fast,
sending Commander Wěi Rén 隗仁 to launch a night attack on Chìpán 熾磐,
slaying several hundred heads.
Chìpán 熾磐 was about to withdraw,
first sending away the old and weak.
Hànpíng's 漢平 Chief Clerk Jiāo Chǎng 焦昶 and General Duàn Jǐng 段景 secretly sent a letter inviting Chìpán 熾磐.
Chìpán 熾磐 then advanced again to attack Hànpíng 漢平.
Hànpíng 漢平 accepted Chǎng's 昶 and Jǐng's 景 suggestion,
bound himself and surrendered.
Rén 仁 led over a hundred brave men to occupy the top of the south gate tower,
not descending for three days.
Outnumbered,
he was captured by Chìpán 熾磐.
Chìpán 熾磐 was enraged,
and ordered his execution.
Duàn Huī 段暉 remonstrated, saying:
"Rén 仁 faced difficulty and danger,
fighting without regard for his life;
this is loyalty.
He should be pardoned,
to encourage those who serve their lord."
Chìpán 熾磐 then detained him and returned.
After five years in Chìpán's 熾磐 custody,
Huī 暉 again earnestly pleaded for him,
and he was then allowed to return to Gūzāng 姑臧.
Upon his arrival,
Méngxùn 蒙遜 grasped his hand and said:
"You,
are my Sū Wǔ 蘇武!"
He was appointed Administrator of Gāochāng 高昌 (Gāochāng Tàishǒu 高昌太守).
He was praised for his governance, which combined severity and benevolence,
though he was somewhat criticized for his love of wealth.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 went west to sacrifice at Jīn Shān 金山,
sending Jūqú Guǎngzōng 沮渠廣宗 to lead ten thousand cavalry to attack the Wūtí 烏啼 barbarians,
achieving a great victory and returning.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 went west to Tiáodiào 苕藋,
sending General of the Vanguard (Qián Jiāngjūn 前將軍) Jūqú Chéngdū 沮渠成都 to lead five thousand cavalry to attack the Bēihé 卑和 barbarians.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 led his central army of thirty thousand to follow him,
and the Bēihé 卑和 barbarians led their people to surrender.
He then proceeded west along the sea,
reaching Yánchí 鹽池,
and offered sacrifices at the temple of the Queen Mother of the West (Xīwángmǔ Sì 西王母寺).
There was a mysterious stone divine map in the temple.
He ordered his Gentleman of the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Shìláng 中書侍郎) Zhāng Mù 張穆 to compose a rhapsody for it,
and inscribed it in front of the temple,
then went to Jīn Shān 金山 and returned.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 issued a decree saying:
"Recently, since spring, there has been a scorching drought,
harming the seasonal crops.
The green fields and verdant plains
have suddenly become parched earth.
Is it because the administration of justice has been imbalanced,
and there are unredressed grievances below?
Or is it that the labor service is excessive and taxes are heavy,
bringing down the condemnation of Heaven?
Upon internal reflection, there are many shortcomings;
this is my fault.
Does not the Shūjīng 書經 say: 'When the common people have faults,
the blame falls on me alone'?
Let there be a great amnesty for all crimes down to those punishable by death."
The next day, heavy rain fell.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 heard that Liú Yù 劉裕 had destroyed Yáo Hóng 姚泓,
and was extremely angry.
Liú Xiáng 劉祥, a Palace Cadet in the Department of the Palace Gate (Ménxià Xiàoláng 門下校郎), spoke about this matter to Méngxùn 蒙遜.
Méngxùn 蒙遜 said:
"You hear that Liú Yù 劉裕 entered the Pass,
and dare to look so proud!"
Then he killed him.
His cruelty and violence were like this.
He turned to his attendants and said:
"In ancient times, when an army marched,
it would not violate the location where the Jupiter station (Suìzhèn 歲鎮) was.
The Yáo 姚 clan were descendants of Shùn 舜,
and scions of Xuānyuán 軒轅.
Now the Jupiter star is in Xuānyuán 軒轅,
and Yù 裕 destroyed them;
he will not be able to long hold Guānzhōng 關中."
Méngxùn 蒙遜 was defeated by Lǐ Shìyè 李士業 at Xiānzhī Jiàn 鮮支澗,
and again gathered his scattered soldiers, intending to fight.
General of the Vanguard (Qián Jiāngjūn 前將軍) Chéngdū 成都 remonstrated, saying:
"Your servant has heard that Gāozǔ 高祖 suffered the defeat at Péngchéng 彭城,
but ultimately established the great Hàn 漢.
It is advisable to withdraw the army to plan for the future."
Méngxùn 蒙遜 followed his advice,
fortified Jiànkāng 建康, and returned.
His subordinates presented a memorial saying:
"Establishing offices and dividing responsibilities
is how the state is governed and the times are aided;
diligently performing one's duties in office
is how all government affairs are made clear and bright.
Those in office should make selflessness their duty,
and those entrusted with responsibility should make forgetting themselves their achievement.
Since the imperial framework first shook,
and warhorses were bred in the fields,
public and private affairs have been improvised,
with no time for old customs.
However, many court officials violate regulations
and do not follow the established rules;
some keep public documents at home,
signing them while lying down;
others, whether a matter is right or wrong,
pass it by looking blankly.
This has led to promotions and demotions being suspended in the imperial court,
and discussions of policy being put aside in this sagely era.
The pure and the turbid flow together,
the competent and the incompetent are mixed,
people have no desire to compete,
merely passing the days aimlessly.
How can this be the way of serving the emperor,
worrying about public affairs and forgetting private ones!
Now the imperial transformation is daily more prosperous,
and peace and stability prevail far and wide.
It is fitting to sternly uphold the principles
and restore the old regulations."
Méngxùn 蒙遜 accepted it,
and ordered General Who Quells the South (Zhēngnán Yáo Aì 征南姚艾) and Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Shàngshū Zuǒchéng 尚書左丞) Fáng Guǐ 房晷 to compile regulations for the court.
They were implemented for ten days,
and all officials became disciplined and serious.
Tàishǐlìng Zhāng Yǎn (太史令 張衍) spoke to Méngxùn (蒙遜), saying:
"This year, to the west of Línzé (臨澤) city, there will be a defeat of troops."
Méngxùn (蒙遜) then dispatched his heir, Zhèngdé (政德), to station troops at Ruòhòu Wù (若厚塢).
Méngxùn (蒙遜) went west to Báibàn (白岸),
and said to Zhāng Yǎn (張衍):
"I am destined to achieve something this year,
but the Grand Duke Júpiter (Tàisuì 太歲) is in Shēn (申),
and the month also begins with Shēn (申),
so I cannot go west yet.
I should first inspect the south,
await their return,
be the host and not the guest,
to accord with Heaven's will.
The plan is to act opportunistically;
do not reveal it."
So he attacked Hàowěi (浩亹),
and a snake coiled in front of his tent.
Méngxùn (蒙遜) laughed and said:
"Previously it was a flying snake (téngshé 騰蛇),
now it coils in my tent.
Heaven's will desires me to turn back my army and first secure Jiǔquán (酒泉)."
He burned his siege equipment and returned,
encamping at Chuānyán (川巖).
He heard that Lǐ Shìyè (李士業) was raising an army to attack Zhāngyè (張掖).
Méngxùn (蒙遜) said:
"This falls into my plan.
But I fear that if he hears of my army's return,
he will not dare to advance.
Military affairs are about expediency."
So he publicly announced throughout the western border
that he had captured Hàowěi (浩亹)
and would advance into Huánggǔ (黃谷).
Shìyè (士業) heard this and was greatly pleased,
advancing into Dūdú Jiàn (都瀆澗).
Méngxùn (蒙遜) secretly led his army to meet him,
defeating Shìyè (士業) at Huàichéng (壞城),
and then advanced to conquer Jiǔquán (酒泉).
The common people settled down as before,
and the army committed no private plunder.
He appointed his son Màoqián (茂虔) as the Grand Administrator (tàishǒu 太守) of Jiǔquán (酒泉),
and all of Shìyè's (士業) former officials were promoted according to their talent.
In the fifth year of Āndì (安帝)'s Lóng'ān (隆安) era (401 CE), Méngxùn (蒙遜) proclaimed himself Governor (Zhōumù 州牧).
In the eighth year of Yìxī (義熙) (412 CE), he usurped the throne.
Eight years later, the Sòng (宋) dynasty received the abdication.
He died in the tenth year of Yuánjiā (元嘉) (433 CE),
at the age of sixty-six,
having been on the usurped throne for thirty-three years.
His son Màoqián (茂虔) succeeded him.
Six years later,
he was captured by Wèi (魏),
and the state was extinguished after a total of thirty-nine years.
The imperial historian (shǐchén 史臣) states: Méngxùn (蒙遜) emerged from a barbarian (yí zōu 夷陬) region,
and dominated the frontier.
When Lǚ Guāng (呂光) was immoral,
he deeply harbored a grudge of enmity;
he supported Duàn Yè (段業) to save the times,
using him as Chén Shèng (陳勝) and Wú Guǎng (吳廣) used others.
When he raised troops at Báijiàn (白澗),
Southern Liáng (Nánliáng 南涼) sued for peace;
when he led an army out of Dānlǐng (丹嶺),
the northern barbarians submitted.
However, he forgot righteousness for profit,
harbored evil and destroyed kin.
Although he could control a corner of the realm,
he was also endowed with various wicked virtues.
Eulogy (Zàn 贊) says: Guāng (光) suspected the heroic,
Yè (業) was jealous of the wise of the time.
He drank and hid himself,
concealed his wisdom to preserve himself.
When his vicious heart was indulged,
his false achievements were proclaimed.
He displayed these treacherous schemes,
and contended fiercely in his era.
Collation Notes (Jiàokān Jì 校勘記)
Memoir (Zàijì 載記) 30: Hèlián Bóbó (赫連勃勃)
Hèlián Bóbó (赫連勃勃), courtesy name Qūjié (屈孑),
was a descendant of Xiōngnú (匈奴) Right Virtuous King (Yòuxiánwáng 右賢王) Qùbēi (去卑),
and of the same clan as Liú Yuánhǎi (劉元海).
His great-grandfather, Wǔ (武),
was enfeoffed as Lord of Lóufán (Lóufán Gōng 樓煩公) during Liú Cōng (劉聰)'s reign, by virtue of being of the imperial clan.

He was appointed General Pacifying the North (Ānběi Jiāngjūn 安北將軍), Supervisor of all Xiānbēi (鮮卑) Military Affairs (Jiān Xiānbēi Zhūjūnsì 監鮮卑諸軍事), and Commander of the Dīnglíng (丁零) (Dīnglíng Zhōnglángjiāng 丁零中郎將).
He held sway over Sìlú Chuān (肆盧川).
He was defeated by Dài (代) King Yīlú (猗盧),
and subsequently went beyond the frontier.
His grandfather, Bàozǐ (豹子), gathered his tribes
and again became a powerful figure among the various tribes.
Shí Jìlóng (石季龍) sent an envoy to appoint him General Pacifying the North (Píngběi Jiāngjūn 平北將軍), Left Virtuous King (Zuǒxiánwáng 左賢王), and Dīnglíng (丁零) Chányú (單于).
His father, Wèichén (衞辰), moved inside the frontier.
Fú Jiān (苻堅) made him Western Chányú (Xīdānyú 西單于),
supervising all the Hu (胡) barbarians west of the Hé (河),
and stationed him at Dàilái Chéng (代來城).
When Jiān's (堅) state fell into chaos,
he acquired the land of Shuòfāng (朔方),
with thirty-eight thousand skilled archers.
Later, a Wèi (魏) army attacked him.
Chén (辰) ordered his son Lìsìtí (力俟提) to resist,
but he was defeated by Wèi (魏).
The Wèi (魏) people crossed the river in triumph,
captured Dàilái (代來),
seized Chén (辰) and killed him.
Bóbó (勃勃) then fled to the Chìgān (叱干) tribe.
Chìgān Tā dòu fú (叱干他斗伏) sent Bóbó (勃勃) to Wèi (魏).
Tā dòu fú's (他斗伏) nephew, Ālì (阿利), who was previously garrisoned at Dàluò Chuān (大洛川),
heard that Bóbó (勃勃) was to be sent away,
and rushed to remonstrate, saying:
"Even a bird that seeks refuge with a person
should be saved and exempted from harm,
let alone Bóbó (勃勃) whose state is broken and family destroyed,
and who pledges allegiance to us?
Even if we cannot accommodate him,
we should still let him go where he wishes.
To seize him and send him away now
is deeply not the act of a benevolent person."
Tā dòu fú (他斗伏) feared being blamed by Wèi (魏),
and did not heed him.
Ālì (阿利) secretly dispatched brave warriors to intercept Bóbó (勃勃) on the road,
and sent him to Yáo Xīng (姚興)'s Gāopíng Gōng (高平公) Mòyì Yú (沒奕于).
Yì Yú (奕于) gave him his daughter in marriage.
Bóbó (勃勃) was eight chi (八尺) five cun (五寸) tall,
and his waist measured ten circumference (shí wéi 十圍).
He was eloquent and intelligent,
and had a fine bearing.
Xīng (興) saw him and was impressed,
treating him with great deference,
appointing him General of Agile Cavalry (Xiāojì Jiāngjūn 驍騎將軍),
and also Grand Master of Carriages (Fèngchē Dūwèi 奉車都尉).
He often participated in major military and state deliberations,
and his favor exceeded that of veteran officials.
Xīng's (興) brother Yōng (邕) said to Xīng (興):
"Bóbó (勃勃) is inherently unkind,
difficult to be intimate with.
Your Majesty's favor is excessive;
your servant is secretly perplexed by it."
Xīng (興) said:
"Bóbó (勃勃) has the talent to save the world;
I intend to utilize his skills,
and together with him pacify the world.
What is wrong with that?"
So he made Bóbó (勃勃) General Pacifying the Far (Ānyuǎn Jiāngjūn 安遠將軍),
enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yángchuān (Yángchuān Hóu 陽川侯),
and sent him to assist Mòyì Yú (沒奕于) in guarding Gāopíng (高平).
He assigned him the Three Cities (Sānchéng 三城), the mixed barbarians (zá yí 雜夷) of Shuòfāng (朔方), and thirty thousand troops from Wèichén's (衞辰) tribe,
to serve as a scout for attacking Wèi (魏).
Yáo Yōng (姚邕) strenuously advised against it.
Xīng (興) said:
"How do you know his nature?"
Yōng (邕) replied:
"Bóbó (勃勃) is arrogant towards his superiors,
cruel to his subordinates,
greedy and violent, without kin,
and readily changes allegiance.
To favor him excessively
will ultimately lead to disaster on the frontier."
Xīng (興) then stopped.
A short while later,
he made Bóbó (勃勃) Bearer of the Imperial Staff (Chíjié 持節), General Pacifying the North (Ānběi Jiāngjūn 安北將軍), and Duke of Wǔyuán (Wǔyuán Gōng 五原公).
He assigned him the Xiānbēi (鮮卑) of Sānjiāo (三交)'s five tribes and over twenty thousand miscellaneous barbarian (zá lǔ 雜虜) households,
to garrison Shuòfāng (朔方).
At this time, Dù Lún (杜崘), a Xiānbēi (鮮卑) from Hexi, offered eight thousand horses to Yáo Xīng (姚興).
He crossed the river and arrived at Dàchéng (大城).
Bóbó (勃勃) detained him,
summoned thirty thousand of his followers, pretended to hunt in Gāopíng Chuān (高平川),
attacked and killed Mòyì Yú (沒奕于), and incorporated his troops,
swelling his forces to tens of thousands.
In the third year of Yìxī (義熙) (407 CE),
he usurped the title of Heavenly King (Tiānwáng 天王) and Grand Chányú (Dà Dānyú 大單于),
pardoned all within his territory,
proclaimed the era name Lóngshēng (龍昇),
and appointed a hundred officials.
Considering himself a descendant of the Xiōngnú (匈奴) Xià Hòushì (夏后氏),
he named his state Dàxià (大夏).
He made his eldest brother Yòudì Dài (右地代) Chancellor (Chéngxiàng 丞相) and Duke of Dài (Dài Gōng 代公),
his second brother Lìsìtí (力俟提) Grand General (Dàjiāngjūn 大將jūn) and Duke of Wèi (Wèi Gōng 魏公),
Chìgān Ālì (叱干阿利) Grand Censor (Yùshǐ Dàfū 御史大夫) and Duke of Liáng (Liáng Gōng 梁公),
his younger brother Ālì Luóyǐn (阿利羅引) General Pacifying the South (Zhēngnán Jiāngjūn 征南將軍) and Colonel Director of Retainers (Sīlì Xiàowèi 司隸校尉),
Ruòmén (若門) Minister of the Imperial Secretariat (Shàngshūlìng 尚書令),
Chìyǐ Jiàn (叱以鞬) General Pacifying the West (Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn 征西將軍) and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè 尚書左僕射),
Yǐdòu (乙斗) General Pacifying the North (Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn 征北將軍) and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Shàngshū Yòu Púyè 尚書右僕射),
and the rest were appointed in order.
